registrationNotes: Designed for Cypress Presbyterian Church, North Carolina USA, in celebration of its 190th anniversary. As the founder elders of Cypress Presbyterian Church were called Cameron, Keith and Johnstone, the colours in this tartan are based on those in the Cameron, Keith and Johnstone tartans.

name: Battle of Prestonpans (1745) Heritage Trust, The
registrationNotes: This is a corporate and commemorative tartan to be worn by all who work for the Battle of Prestonpans (1745) Heritage Trust, to conserve, interpret and present the hope, ambition and victory arising from the battle fought in Prestonpans on 21st September 1745.

name: Riley-Utter Union (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the use of Keith Riley and Kathleen Utter, their immediate family and descendants.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of Kathleen 'Sequoia' Utter and Keith 'Fisher' Riley and for their family and descendants. The colours chosen represent their virtues and their love of nature.

name: Glencross (Moniaive) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the designer and his family. Those who share the Glencross surname, or variations thereof, and wish to wear this tartan are invited to contact the designer for his consent.
registrationNotes: Designed to commemorate the designer’s Dumfriesshire surname which originates from the lands of Glencrosh near Moniaive.

name: Mangles, Peter and Annette (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is intended for the specific use of Peter and Annette Mangles, their immediate family and their descendents. Developed for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: Designed as a family tartan by Peter and Annette Mangles. The colours represent Liverpool, where the couple first met, and red, black and grey represent the city of Aberdeen and the granite used there.

name: Hage-West (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Jamie West and his family.
registrationNotes: Designed by Jamie Hage, born Jamie Vincent West, to celebrate his Irish heritage. The black, green and yellow colours are based on West family colours.

name: Centennial-King George Lodge No.171
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Masonic Lodge, Centennial-King George Lodge No. 171, within the Grand Lodge of British Columbia and Yukon. Prepared for weaving by Fraser & Kirkbright Weaving Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed by Earl Kitchener Ward of Langford, British Columbia, in 1958. It is believed that this was the official tartan for the British Columbia Centennial celebrations in 1958, although it appears that the tartan was never registered and there is no documentary evidence of its use during the centennial celebrations. The tartan was adopted at the time, and is currently still used, as the altar cloth for the Freemason's Lodge: Centennial-King George Lodge No. 171, within the Grand Lodge of British Columbia and Yukon.

name: Langara College
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the corporate use of Langara College only. Permission to weave or use it should be sought from Langara College or the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was developed for Langara College, located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Langara College started in 1965 as part of Vancouver City College and in 1970, it opened its West 49th Avenue campus. On 1 April 1994, Langara College was established as an independent public college under the Provincial College and Institute Act. Today, Langara is one of BC's leading under-graduate institutions providing University Studies, Career Studies, and Continuing Studies programs and courses to more than 21,000 students annually.

name: Simon and Friends (Hamburg) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended solely for the use of Sven Simon, his family and friends. Developed for weaving by Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed by Donald McKenzie and Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd for Sven Simon, his family and friends, to celebrate nature and friendship. Colours: light brown is for the earth (Terra); gold symbolises thoughts and ideas; green represents a new beginning, black individuality, and white purity.

name: Thomas Newcomen's Combustion Engine
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the invention of the steam engine by Thomas Newcomen in 1712 and the importance of combustion engines (first external, now internal) in the last three centuries. Colours: black recalls the iron from which the engines and boilers are made as well as the coal and oil that they burn, its dominance in the tartan gives a dark industrial appearance; red represents fire; white represents steam and smoke and blue represents the air (oxygen) required for combustion as well as water.

name: Ch. Supt. Everett and Mrs Julene Summerfield Dress
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the sole use of Everett and Julene Summerfield and their immediate family. The use of this tartan is controlled by MacIsaac Kiltmakers and/or members of the Summerfield family and written permission should be sought before weaving.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to commemorate Everett and Julene Summerfield's life-long commitment to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) and to demonstrate their pride in their name. Blue represents the many waters and skies which the family has known; red recalls the red serge of the RCMP and the Canadian flag; green represents family links with Cape Breton Island; yellow is a reminder of the wheat fields in Alberta and Saskatchewan; black and white are reminders of good and bad times as well as representing the strength and loyalty of the family.

name: Alaskan Scottish
registrationNotes: Designed in 1991 by Alice Dillbeck for the Alaskan Scottish Club, a non-profit organization established to promote the Scottish culture, heritage and teachings to the people of Alaska. Colours: rose reflects a winter sunset on Denali’s (Mount McKinley) lofty top, a summer offer of shooting stars, and wild rose hips; green suggests magnificent forests, short stalk sedge, lingonberry, and saxifrage; gold recalls the great North Star, the miners’ golden dream, tamarack, birch, and aspen mirrored in a stream; white the ice, the snow, the lights of the Auroras; blue is for the sky, forget-me-nots, the open sea, the deep cold azure of lakes, the glaciers’ mysterious hue and for the Scottish origins of many Alaskans.

name: ChuMac (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Alex Chubays and his family. Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: Designed by Alex Chubays for himself and his family. Colours: green is used to represent hope; white for 'something new'; red for passion, yellow for optimism; and purple for love.

name: Keilar (2013)
registrationNotes: The name Keilar or Keillor (and its many other spelling variants) originates in the county of Forfarshire / Angus. The Keilar spelling of the designer’s name developed after family members migrated to Australia in the 19th century. The tartan uses green and gold, representing the national colours of Australia; green also represents the farm country around Inverkeilor. Blue and white represent the Scottish flag. The addition of a red stripe to the blue and white represents the colours of the Australian flag. This tartan is intended for anyone with the name Keillor, whatever the spelling.

name: Sanley-Cantamessa (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn or used only by members of the Sanley Cantamessa family.
registrationNotes: Inspired by his wife’s Scottish ancestry, the designer has created this tartan for himself, his immediate family and his heirs to wear. Black and white have been chosen for their religious significance, red to recall the Sanley blood in the family and blue as the favourite colour of the designer’s wife.

name: Ryder Cup, The
restrictions: Yes. A corporate tartan intended for the sole use of Ryder Cup Europe LLP. Developed for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland. Community design registration no. 002225037-0001 in the Office for Harmonization in the Internal Market in the European Union by Ryder Cup Europe LLP, 23 April 2013.
registrationNotes: The exclusive Ryder Cup Tartan has been designed to celebrate the 40th Ryder Cup Match, which will take place at Gleneagles, Scotland in 2014. Inspired by the landscape of Scotland and the colours of the iconic Ryder Cup logo, the Ryder Cup Tartan reflects the unique quality and drama of the most treasured trophy in golf.

name: Australian Defence Force Academy, The
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the past, present and future graduates of the Australian Defence Force Academy. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills Co Ltd and Ingles Buchan Textiles Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Australian Defence Force Academy (ADFA) is a tri-service military academy that provides military and tertiary academic education for junior officers of the Australian Defence Force, alongside regular military training. The Academy trains officers from all three services. Colours: red is for the Australian Army and recalls the sacrifice made by the "Diggers" who have died or been wounded; dark blue is for the Royal Australian Navy; light blue represents the Royal Australian Air Force; white represents the tri-service nature of the Academy; green and gold are Australia's national colours.

name: Staines (2013)
registrationNotes: Designed by Terence Anthony Staines and intended to be worn by anyone bearing the Staines surname.

name: Cullen (Christian Hill) (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed by John P M Cullen II for the Cullen family of Christian Hill, descendants of Jerome Cullen (born in Ballymote, County Sligo Ireland) and Elizabeth MacDonald Cullen (whose family is from the Isle of Lewis, Scotland). Colours: blue is for the Cullen family tradition as Police Officers; light blue is for the family's Scottish heritage; dark yellow/gold is for the family's military service; green is for their Irish heritage; black is to mourn those who were lost.

name: Rams Timeless
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the corporate use of Colorado State University only and all use must be licensed and authorised by Colorado State University.
registrationNotes: The Rams Timeless tartan was designed by Ajay Li, an interior design student, as the official tartan for Colorado State University (CSU). Three alternative designs in CSU’s branded colours (two specific tones of green, plus gold and pumpkin) were selected from the 76 designs submitted by 17 Design and Merchandising students, and CSU Rams everywhere voted for their preferred tartan. More information about the contest is at http://www.colostate.edu/tartan/.

name: Rikaco Vintage
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Dinos Inc, Japan and their customers. Developed for weaving by Joshua Ellis & Co Ltd, Batley.
registrationNotes: The Rikaco Vintage tartan is based on the modern Cooper tartan, which is fused with an unlikely colouration. The melange grey ground gives a contemporary characteristic to a popular and traditional pattern.

name: East Tennessee State University
designer: Cannon, Michael & ETSU Digital Media Dept
restrictions: Yes. The East Tennessee State University Tartan is intended for the corporate use of East Tennessee State University only. For permission to weave or use this tartan in any way, contact the Director of Marketing and Special Events, Office of University Relations, East Tennessee State University, Box 70717, Johnson City, Tennessee 37614, USA.
registrationNotes: Designed by Michael Cannon, Collegiate Tartan Apparel, and the East Tennessee State University (ETSU) Digital Media Department. ETSU was founded in 1911 for the education of teachers in Southern Appalachia and has evolved into a dynamic university offering degrees in fields ranging from medicine to Appalachian studies. The university celebrated its centennial in 2011 with festivities throughout the year, many of which highlighted the Scottish traditions of the region. The ETSU marketing/merchandising and digital media faculty created three designs incorporating the traditional school colours along with new, bright shades. These were presented to students, staff, and the community, who voted overwhelmingly for this, the school's official tartan.

name: Christopher Newport University
restrictions: Yes. The Christopher Newport University Tartan is intended for the corporate use of Christopher Newport University only. For permission to weave or use this tartan in any way, contact the Christopher Newport Alumni Society at Office of Alumni Relations, Christopher Newport University, 1 Avenue of the Arts, Newport News, VA 23606 or email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: Designed by Michael Cannon, Collegiate Tartan Apparel, for Christopher Newport University (CNU). CNU was founded in 1960 as Christopher Newport College, a branch of the College of William & Mary in Williamsburg, Virginia, and was named for the 17th-century English mariner who helped establish the Jamestown Colony. The University became independent in 1977 and gained university status in 1992. Collegiate Tartan Apparel presented several tartan designs using the official CNU colours of blue and silver to an alumni focus group which selected three designs. All members of the Christopher Newport Alumni Society were then given the opportunity to vote for the design which they felt best represented their alma mater.

name: Mullikin (2013)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Scarlett Mullikin for her family and for others who share the surname Mullikin. The colours used in the tartan are Mullikin family colours, with the red representing home, blue representing water, green representing the beauty of the meadows and hills, and navy representing family devotion, strength and bravery.

name: Fremsaeter, Jenny (Personal)
registrationNotes: Created by the designer in memory of Jenny Fremsaeter, his mother, who was related to the families Syltevik, Blomberg, Brandal, Homlong, and Vonen families in the Storfjord and Geiranger districts of western Norway. The colours used in the tartan represent the soil and grass fields, the peat burned in the winter, the sea, flowers and the colour of the house they lived in.

name: Caie (2013)
restrictions: Yes. Developed for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: Designed by Brian, Graeme and Kevin Caie for the wedding of Graeme. The family name originates in the North East of Scotland, with this particular branch of the family coming from Cove Bay near Aberdeen (though the name is also found in Torry and Footdee). The family is happy for anyone to wear this tartan, and invite prospective users to get in touch with Graeme Caie by emailing [email protected].

name: Asheville Firefighters, The
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use by the Asheville Firefighter Pipes and Drums. Others wishing to use it should seek permission from the Asheville Firefighters Pipes and Drums.
registrationNotes: The Asheville Firefighters Tartan was designed to be worn by the Asheville Firefighters Pipes and Drums, which was formed in 2010 to honour fallen comrades, and to instill pride and ownership in the Asheville Fire Department. The colours were selected to match the colours of the Asheville Fire Department badge.

name: Chestico
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan can be sought from: Chestico Museum & Historical Society PO Box 144, 8095 Route 19 Port Hood, Nova Scotia, Canada B0E 2W0 phone: 902-787-2244 web: chesticoplace.com email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: Port Hood (Seastago or Chestico in Gaelic) is a small fishing village on the west coast of Cape Breton Island in Nova Scotia, Canada. The tartan was designed in 1993 by Mary, Ann and Rachel Smith as a tribute to the community. It is managed and promoted by the Chestico Museum & Historical Society and its registration as a District tartan is supported by the Municipality of the County of Inverness. The brown in the tartan recalls the original name for Chestico, ‘Mi’kmaq’, which translates as 'sand bar'.

name: Hampden-Sydney College
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the corporate use of Hampden-Sydney College only. Permission to weave or produce the tartan in any form should be sought from: W Glenn Culley Jr, Vice President for Business Affairs and Finance, Hampden-Sydney College, Business Office, College Road, Hampden-Sydney, VA 23943.
registrationNotes: Hampden-Sydney College was founded in 1775. The tartan uses the College's official colours, 'Garnet & Grey'. These colours were originally worn by the 'Hampden-Sydney Boys', a company of millitia formed in 1776. The colours were officially adopted by the College when intercollegiate athletics were introduced in the 1890s.

name: Tiger of Sweden
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended as a corporate tartan for Tiger of Sweden.
registrationNotes: Ronnie Junior McDonald, designer at Tiger of Sweden, created this tartan for Tiger of Sweden's Spring 2014 collection. The design is based on McDonald's own family tartan but the colours have been updated to create a softer Scandinavian feeling. The tartan will be used in kilts, blazers, trousers and suits.

name: Coats (New Zealand)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for those directly descended from James and Hellen Coats and other family members who migrated to New Zealand from Scotland between 1850 and 1900.
registrationNotes: Created for and chosen by the descendants of James and Hellen Coats, who arrived at Port Chalmers, Dunedin, New Zealand on 6 July 1863. The tartan's design and colours depict the family's migration to New Zealand. Blue represents Scotland; green is for family roots in Lanarkshire; the voyage from Scotland to New Zealand is represented by two strips of grey representing the sea with a strip of brown through the middle for the ship; gold represents the city of Dunedin, and black represents New Zealand.

name: Williams, Edmund (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to use this tartan should contact the designer at: [email protected] Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: The colours in this tartan are based on the Scottish landscape, particularly the hills, where the designer spends a lot of his time.

name: Flodden
restrictions: Yes. Designed for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Flodden 1513 Ecomuseum Ltd, a company established to coordinate the heritage and legacy of the Battle of Flodden and to mark its 500th anniversary. The tartan uses white, Tudor green, golden yellow and red to represent the dyed colours of the uniforms worn by the English and Scottish troops. Woven in Selkirk by A Elliott Fine Fabrics Ltd.

name: Gracey (2013)
restrictions: Yes. Developed for weaving by House of Tartan.
registrationNotes: Designed by Blair Urquhart of House of Tartan for all those who share the Gracey name, many of whom can trace their ancestry to Argyll. The tartan has been approved by a significant number of Graceys around the world, with positive comments about the design and approval collected by Facebook.

name: Moggach (Strathspey)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Matthew Moggach and his immediate family. Prepared for weaving by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts Ltd for Matthew Moggach and his family. Pattern elements of the Strathspey and Douglas setts were incorporated, and the colours have been chosen to represent the granite of Aberdeenshire.

name: Round Table Sweden
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of current or former members of Round Table Sweden. Prepared for weaving by Cargokilts, South Africa.
registrationNotes: The Round Table Sweden (RTS) tartan was developed by Egbert Harmse at Cargokilts (SA) for the Central Tablers' Meeting in Stirling, Scotland, in January 2013 and is intended to be worn at meetings and functions arranged by Round Table associations around the world. The tartan has a falu-red base; falu-red is a Swedish deep red paint well-known for its use on wooden cottages and barns. The red-brown represents the rich soil and the potato fields, from which brännvin or schnapps has been produced for generations. The design also uses blue and yellow, traditional colours of RTS.

name: Woodward, R Glenn (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to use this tartan should seek written permission from the designer, Glenn Eugene Woodward or Aarron Phillip Gregory Woodward. There shall be no modifications to this design when woven, published, created, displayed, artistically created for public or private display without personal review and subsequent specific permission from the above mentioned males.
registrationNotes: Designed by R Glenn Woodward to unite and bond past, present and future generations of his family. The colours black, blue, purple and red represent the family's blood lineage; green represents the earth.

name: Process Safety Solutions Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of employees of Process Safety Solutions Ltd. Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed by Blair Urquhart of House of Tartan for Process Safety Solutions Limited, a safety systems design specialist in the oil and gas sector, to celebrate and promote the development of their Training and Skills Centre in Aberdeen. Red, grey and black are the company colours and green is the company's Managing Directors last name.

name: Binder (2013)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the designers and their immediate family. Others may wear this tartan with authorisation from the designers.
registrationNotes: Designed by Anja and Michael Binder, Austrians who have settled in Scotland. The tartan uses the red, white and red of the Austrian Flag, and blue and white for the Saltire. Green combines the two countries, the two thin blue lines represent the Blue Danube and the sea, and black stands for the tartan’s formal purpose.

name: Bertea, A H (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Alex Bertea, his family and friends.
registrationNotes: Designed by Alex Bertea as a family tartan. The red and white colours are taken from the arms of Florence, Italy and Switzerland to represent his family's ancestry.

name: Charlotte Fire Department
designer: Slater, Foulk, Kline & Alexis Malcolm Kilts
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Charlotte Fire Department Pipes and Drums members, Charlotte Fire Department, 500 Dalton Ave, Charlotte, NC 28204.
registrationNotes: Designed by Hannah Slater, Lance Foulk, Joseph Kline & Alexis Malcolm Kilts for the Charlotte Fire Department Pipes and Drums with a black base to represent the Fire Department’s unbroken commitment of service day or night to the city; red represents the fire service; green and gold represent the City of Charlotte, its prosperity and people; blue represents truth and humility; and white represents service and sacrifice.

name: McCruden, Raymond (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the designer and his immediate family. Others wishing to wear this tartan should seek permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate Mr McCruden's 60th birthday and as a legacy for his family. Colours: navy,one of the colours in the Robertson tartan, Robertson being his mother's maiden name; lovat green for his father’s Irish family connection; blue for his Scottish family connection; white for the cross on the Scottish Saltire.

name: Seacliff Academy
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Seacliff Global Education Society. Those seeking permission to use or weave this tartan should contact Seacliff Global Education Society.
registrationNotes: The Seacliff Academy tartan was developed to establish a brand identity for private schools of that name founded by the Seacliff Global Education Society.

name: Kinloch Anderson Rowanberry
restrictions: Yes. Available to the general public exclusively through Kinloch Anderson. Kinloch Anderson to select supplier to commission weave the tartan. All products using the fabric or the tartan design to be supplied by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Kinloch Anderson Rowanberry Tartan is one of the Kinloch Anderson collection of tartans, all of which are based on the sett of the original Kinloch Anderson tartan. It introduces four shades of red and a golden yellow overcheck. In Scotland the rowan tree’s berries are red whereas in Asia there are some species where the berries are a golden yellow. The tree is famed for its hardiness and ability to survive in the mountains as well as its long and interesting history and mythology. In Scotland it is called rudha-an, meaning 'red one'.

name: Vetoclock
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the use of Vetoclock.
registrationNotes: Vetoclock is an organisation that provides a remote diagnostics veterinarian service. This tartan was created to celebrate the new headquaters of Vetoclock in Scotland.

name: Special Air Service
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of serving and former of the Special Air Service, and such persons as approved by the Committee of the Special Air Service Regimental Association. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of McNaughton Holdings of Perth.
registrationNotes: The official Regimental tartan for the Special Air Service Regiment, approved by the various bodies within the regimental structure.

name: Beechgrove Garden, The
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Knockando Woolmill Co LTD.
registrationNotes: Designed to commemorate the restoration of the Knockando Woolmill garden by the BBC's "Beechgrove Garden" television programme. The tartan is based on the McColl sett after the original programme presenter Jim McColl. It incorporates purple, white and the greens from the Beechgrove Garden logo.

name: MacSween Hunting (Lochs, Isle of Lewis) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson with the MacSween Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use.
registrationNotes: Designed by Kinloch Anderson and Donald, Rory and Stuart MacSween. The colours and design of the MacSween tartan reflect the family's origins in the Isle of Lewis and its service in the UK Armed Forces. Black and green represent the Royal Green Jackets Regiment and the dark sea of the Minch, the sand colour represents 22 Special Air Service Regiment's operations in Oman's Qara mountains and desert during the Dhofar War. The ancient red represents a family link to the Seaforth and Cameron Highlanders and to the City of Liverpool.

name: Hasegawa (Akasaka) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Hitoshi Hasegawa, his family and their descendants.
registrationNotes: Designed by Hitoshi Hasegawa for his family and their descendants. The family name Hasegawa means the "long river valley" in Japanese and the blue lines in the design signify the river running through the dark green mountains. Akasaka, meaning the "red slope", is a district of Minato, Tokyo and is represented by the red line.

name: elCorte
registrationNotes: Designed by Anemone Tontsch and George Urquhart to celebrate elCorte, a community of tango enthusiasts based in Nijmegen in the Netherlands their tango home. The tartan is in the official elCorte colours and will be worn to identify a ‘family’ member.

name: Steve Walls Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave must be sought from the family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created in memory of Steve Walls, a proud Scot who represented Scotland in Cheerleading and Dance, and was well-known for wearing kilts. The tartan incorporates green - the colour of The New Golf Club, St Andrews, of which he was a past captain; red and yellow for Scotcheer, the company Steve founded to promote Scottish Cheerleading throughout the world; blue and white for the Saltire and Dundee FC. The tartan will be used by friends and family and potentially by Scottish Cheerleading squads.

name: Centeno-Oxford (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for members of the Centeno-Oxford family, immediate relatives of the designer and his wife and friends of the family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the birth of the designer's daughter on 11/11/2007. It combines the colours of the Castillian last name Centeno (green and yellow) for the father, and the family name of the mother (Oxford, Royal Blue).

name: Inspiration
registrationNotes: The Inspiration tartan has been created to inspire all individuals to make a difference in the world. The red represents the bloodshed of people who have died in the struggle for peace; blue represents the Scottish skies and green represents the mountains. The black and white symbolise the various cultures, religions and people who are all woven together, like the threads of the tartan; interlinked to make up the diversity of this great planet. The yellow represents inspiration, emerging from the dark colours that have hidden its light.

name: Stephen F Austin State University
restrictions: Yes. For permission to weave or produce this tartan, please contact: Stephen F Austin State University, Director of Licensing and Trademarks, P.O. Box 13010, Homer Bryce Stadium, Nacogdoches, TX 75962
registrationNotes: The Stephen F Austin (SFA) State University tartan was created by fashion merchandising student Kelcie Brown to represent the university and its traditions. The university opened in 1923 in Nacogdoches, Texas, and is named for Stephen Austin, the “Father” of Texas. The design uses the SFA colours of purple and white with accents of grey and black to represent the university’s “Purple Pride!”.

name: Flowers of the Forest, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Christine Macleod and the National Trust for Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the death of King James IV, many of his nobles and over 10,000 men of Scotland during the battle of Flodden on the 9th September 1513. The large square represents the four corners of the kingdom from which thousands of men from all sectors of society were sent to die on Flodden field. Three inner lines of red represent the sword, dagger and ring associated with King James IV. The steel blue and turquoise check represents the turquoise ring, given to James by Anne of Brittany as a token of the alliance between Scotland and France.

name: Scottish Ballet
restrictions: Yes. A corporate tartan intended for the exclusive use of Scottish Ballet. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed by Lochcarron of Scotland for Scottish Ballet. The colour palette features the Scottish Ballet purple, complemented with a dark grey and incorporating a gold highlight to represent the gold roof of Scottish Ballet’s Tramway headquarters.

name: Guildry of Stirling
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Guildry Brethren (past, present & future) and those associated with the Guildry of Stirling. Permission to weave should be sought from the incumbent Dean of The Guildry of Stirling.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Dean Robin Iffla to celebrate the Guildry of Stirling’s remarkable longevity, and was ratified by the Council on 14th August 2013. The design is based in part on the Black Watch tartan, and recognises the association of the Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders with the City of Stirling. The design also incorporates green for the Guildry of Stirling.

name: Shedor (2013)
restrictions: Yes. If worn or woven, the Shedor name should be associated with this tartan.
registrationNotes: The Shedor family live in Algonquin and wish to create a tartan for their name. The threadcount and colours have been selected by the eldest son, Chase Shedor, and this pattern is intended for use by all current and future generations of Shedors.

name: Buschke (Skye) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the Buschke family or persons legally associated with them, i.e. legal descendants or relatives of the family of retired Major Thomas H. Buschke Senior and Ingrid Buschke, subject to a decision of the family council. All rights reserved
registrationNotes: Created in honour of Major Buschke to celebrate his 77th birthday and for members of the Buschke family and subsequent generations, to commemorate the family’s love of Skye. The tartan reflects the rugged natural beauty of the Highlands and Islands, with blue representing the sky over the Hebrides, the lochs and the sea; white for the clouds, falls and cotton grass; green and brown for the hues of the breas, moorlands and the heather; black for the volcanic rock like the Old Man of Storr, and gold and light red for Scotland's Highland flora such as Tormentil, Yellow Rattle, Rosebay Willowherb, and Bell Heather.

name: Shawn Jones Afghan Memorial, The
registrationNotes: Created by the designer for himself and for other individuals who, like him, have served in Afghanistan since 2001.

name: Spencer (2013)
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created to celebrate the designer’s Celtic roots and his Australian heritage. The colours reflect Australia (green and gold), Queensland (red), the New England region of northern New South Wales (blue, white and red), and Coorparoo (sporting colours are blue).

name: Fred Perry
restrictions: Yes. This is a Corporate tartan created solely for the use of Fred Perry Ltd. Weaving of this tartan is controlled by Fred Perry Ltd.
registrationNotes: This vibrant signature tartan for the Fred Perry global label celebrates that famous British figure in the world of Lawn Tennis and his becoming Wimbledon Champion in 1936. Against a dark blue sky, this design combines one of the traditional Fred Perry colourways with the familiar green and white of lawn tennis courts.

name: Noble (South Africa) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. A personal tartan intended for Alan Noble and his immediate family. Please contact Alan Noble or Houston Kiltmakers for permission to use this tartan.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Alan Noble in South Africa, created for his son's wedding in Scotland.

name: McGuirk (2013)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Andy & Nick McGuirk, Camelon, Falkirk, intended for use by all McGuirk family members.

name: Du Lion
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Office of the Governor General of Canada, the Lieutenants-Governors of the provinces, the Commissioners of the territories and the entire viceregal community in Canada. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: Originally designed as a fashion tartan created to celebrate the designer's meeting with Canada's Heralds of Arms and the principal artist of the Canadian Heraldic Authority in Ottawa in June 2013. The design represents the lion on the flag of the Governor General of Canada: a crowned lion in gold (Or) holding a maple leaf in red (Gules) on a background in blue (Azure). "Du Lion", was formally adopted as the official tartan of the Office of the Governor General of Canada on 13 June 2017, the same year that Canada celebrated her 150th birthday. This tartan may be used and enjoyed by the entire viceregal community across Canada.

name: Schwarzen Keiler, Die
restrictions: Yes. Intended solely for use by members of Die Schwarzen Keiler.
registrationNotes: Designed by Ralf Sichert and Alexander Sommerer for use by a medieval re-enactment group called “Die Schwarzen Keiler” (The Black Boars). The black and dark green boxes stand for the wood and meadows in Franconia and the black boars within them, from which the group’s name has been taken.

name: Alexander-Johnstone (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Immediate family members may wear this tartan but anyone else wishing to use it should contact the designer.
registrationNotes: Designed by Chris Alexander to celebrate his wedding and to create a unique family tartan for use in years to come. The colours are a combination of those contained in the Alexander and Johnstone tartans.

name: MatchPoint
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the MatchPoint Group. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: MatchPoint, a company set up in 1992 provides hospitality across the range of major sports and arts events throughout the UK, Mainland Europe Asia and Australia. One of three MatchPoint Tartans designed to mark their 21st birthday and reflect the international footprint of MatchPoint after 21 years in business. The blue, red, white and gold colours represent the offices in Edinburgh, Hong Kong, London, Melbourne and Sydney.

name: Matchpoint Hunting
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the MatchPoint Group. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: MatchPoint, a company set up in 1992 provides hospitality across the range of major sports and arts events throughout the UK, Mainland Europe Asia and Australia. One of three MatchPoint Tartans designed to mark their 21st birthday and reflect the international footprint of MatchPoint after 21 years in business. The blue, red, white and gold colours represent the offices in Edinburgh, Hong Kong, London, Melbourne and Sydney.

name: MatchPoint Dress
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the MatchPoint Group. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: MatchPoint, a company set up in 1992 provides hospitality across the range of major sports and arts events throughout the UK, Mainland Europe Asia and Australia. One of three MatchPoint Tartans designed to mark their 21st birthday and reflect the international footprint of MatchPoint after 21 years in business. The blue, red, white and gold colours represent the offices in Edinburgh, Hong Kong, London, Melbourne and Sydney.

name: Timmins (2013)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer to wear, use or weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: Designed by Paul Timmins and intended to be worn by anyone bearing the Timmins surname. Colours: the blues represent the Royal Air Force and the Royal Navy; green represents the land; purple represents heather; red and yellow added to complete the design.

name: Kellogg College University of Oxford
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only by fellows, students and alumni of Kellogg College and those invited to do so by the President of the College. Intended to be reproduced and used only with the written agreement of the President of Kellogg College.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Kellogg College, University of Oxford, for the Burns Supper 2013. This is the Kellogg College tartan to be worn only by fellows, students and alumni of the College and those invited to do so by the President of the College. The colours are taken from the College Coat of Arms – in particular the thread of gold represents an ear of wheat, recalling the College's close association with the W K Kellogg Foundation.

name: Spirit of Romania
restrictions: Yes. Intended as a universal tartan for anyone to wear. Only to be woven with the registrant's written permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan incorporates the colours of the flags of Romania and Scotland.

name: Boxer Beauty
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to use this sett for commercial purposes should contact the designer first.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the Boxer dog, which is known for its handsome looks, playfulness, and warmly affectionate nature. The Boxer can be all white, brindle (black on brown or brown on black), and fawn (various shades of ginger, caramel, strawberry blonde), with or without white 'flash' throughout the coat.

name: Leaf Peeper
registrationNotes: Inspired by the October foliage of New Hampshire's White Mountains region, this tartan is named after the tourists who swarm the area to see the foliage and who are nicknamed "Leaf Peepers" by the locals. The colours are those of the sugar maple, oak, birch and elm trees of the Mount Washington Valley in October, as they change from yellow/gold and red to brown, while the pines remain green throughout the season. The hints of white are for the snow that frequently appears at the summits of the higher elevations at that time of year.

name: Hayama Shirt Honten, The
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Goto Yokohama Office,Co. Ltd. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Hayama Shirt Honten Tartan was exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson to celebrate the opening of Goto Yokohama Office, Co. Ltd. The design was based on a reduced sett of the Kinloch Anderson Tartan to show synergy between the two companies. Goto Yokohama Office, Co. Ltd corporate colours of red and white were introduced into the design along with a soft green shade taken from Kinloch Anderson’s seasonal trend colours.

name: Lunch with an Old Bag (Fundraising Committee)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Lunch With an Old Bag Committee. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use.
registrationNotes: The Lunch with an Old Bag Charity(LWOB) tartan is designed to reflect the values of Lunch with an Old Bag and the challenges affecting young people in Scotland today. Bringing together many of Scotland’s most glamorous and stylish ladies, known affectionately as ‘Old Bags’, this event was so named in order to address the unnecessary labelling of young people who can so easily and unfairly be assigned to categories they do not fit, and to raise funds for the many programmes run by The Prince’s Trust to help young people move into education, employment, training and/or self-employment. A rich, vibrant pink breaks through the boxes, brightens the grey areas and breaks the regimented black and white, signifying what LWOB is all about: challenging stereotypes, dispelling labels, and raising funds to transform young lives.

name: Wojtek Memorial Trust
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be used and marketed according to the wishes of the Polish Ex-Combatants Association, 11 Drummond Place, Edinburgh EH3 6PJ. Any tartan fabric and products which feature the tartan may not be made or sold unless specific permission has been requested to and granted by the Association.
registrationNotes: The Wojtek Memorial Trust Tartan commemorates Wojtek the Bear (1942–1963) was a Syrian brown bear cub found in Iran and adopted by soldiers of the 22nd Artillery Supply Company of the Polish II Corps. The tartan is based on the sett of the Roxburgh tartan because Wojtek visited Springwood Park, Kelso owned by the Duke of Roxburgh when he arrived in Scotland. The vibrant red colour of the Roxburgh tartan reflects the Polish flag whilst the red “ribbon-like lines” are a reminder of the red and white ribbons soldiers bought from local women to sew onto their uniforms to identify themselves as the Polish Army. The colours of the Polish flag and the Scottish flag sit together in the design to represent the special relationship between Scotland and Poland. The two shades of green reflect the countryside of the Scottish Borders and the Leslie tartan trews which were worn by the King’s Own Scottish Borderers Regiment. The single sand over-check is a reminder of the desert lands of the Middle East and of Wojtek’s soft brown fur. Within the tartan design it is symbolically placed in the heart of the Scottish Borders green, representing where both the Polish soldiers and Wojtek found friendship and a new homeland.

registrationNotes: A 111th anniversary tartan celebrating the teddy bear, which originated from a Mississippi bear hunt on 14th November 1902, where Teddy Roosevelt refused to shoot a bear tied to a willow tree. The tartan represents Roosevelt's hunt and the resultant political cartoon (printed two days later in the Washington Post) which inspired the creation of 'Teddy's Bear'. Colours: 26 grey threads represent Roosevelt the 26th US President whose image is hewed in grey granite of Mount Rushmore; six black threads recognizes Roosevelt's 1906 Nobel Peace Prize, with black and beige together representing the American Black Bear; brown portrays the traditional colour of the teddy bear, with 32 threads referring to Mississippi as the 32nd largest US state; green represents the willow tree; white is a tribute to Roosevelt's renaming of the White House in 1901. The geometry is created from the two relevant dates; 14th November 1902 as 14, 11, 19 and 2 threads; 16th November 1902 as 16, 11, 19 and 2 threads.

registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for the Scottish Team at the 2014 Commonwealth Games Scotland. The tartan is inspired by the four seasons, spring, summer, autumn and winter, represented by turquoise for spring, coral for summer, caramel for autumn and navy for winter. The turquoise reflects the blue waters of Vatersay Bay, Barra, and the blue of the Saltire. The coral is made up of soft red and fuchsia to reflect the colour of heather on the Scottish mountains and hills in summer. The caramel represents the bracken in autumn in the Scottish Highlands. The narrow navy stripe represents the dark days of winter and reflects the Commonwealth Games Scotland corporate tartan which is predominately blue.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the 350th anniversary of the formation of the Royal Marines. Colours: blue represents the intimate connection of the Corps with the Royal Navy, and the colour of the facings on the uniform for over 100 year; red represents ‘Drummer Red’, the old historic colour of the British Army, worn by the infantry of the Corps from early times down to the introduction of scarlet in 1876; green represents ‘Light Infantry Green’ as was worn on the shako by the infantry of the Corps for some years and is perpetuated in the bugle strings of the RMLI; and yellow represents ‘Old gold’, closely associated with the early history of the Corps, as it was the distinctive colour of the dress and ensigns of the Duke of York and Albany's Maritime Regiment of Foot from which the Corps originates.

Orange also represents the Celtic Goddess Danu, who symbolises love, youth and rebirth through children, and grey reflects the colour of the Northern Scottish rocks, representing invincibility of spirit and resilience of character.

name: Earthrise
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2014. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 5003477.
registrationNotes: The tartan commemorates the 45th anniversary of the world-famous Apollo 8 ‘Earthrise’ photograph, taken from lunar orbit by astronaut William Anders on 24th December 1968. The photograph was captured only with a collaborative effort by all three Nasa crew members. The tartan celebrates the colour image which was declared by wilderness photographer Gallen Rowell as "the most influential environmental photograph ever taken". The geometry in the tartan depicts the Earth rising above the Moon's horizon. Numbers in the threads have numerical significance; 10 dark blue threads are a reminder of the reading of Genesis 1 verses 1-10, which was read out aloud and beamed back to Earth as part of a Christmas Eve message; 68 black threads represent the year 1968. The 3 black stripes pay tribute to the crew: Commander Frank Borman, Command Module Pilot James Lovell and Lunar Module Pilot William Anders. The tartan's 6 colours and thread count of 147 threads recognise the mission length of 6 days, or 147 hours. Colours: the colours represent the Earth, Space and the Moon.

registrationNotes: Virginia Arts Festival commissioned this design from Alastair Dunn of R G Hardie & Co Ltd (Glasgow). The tartan was the inspiration of James Hixon, Chairman of the Board. The Virginia International Tattoo in Norfolk, VA, was established in 1997 as part of the world-renowned Virginia Arts Festival. Its mission is to honour the US military, celebrate American freedom and patriotism, educate youth, attract visitors to Coastal Virginia, strengthen international relations and enhance the quality of life for the people of Coastal Virginia. Colours: the blue, ‘Festival Blue’, represents the Virginia Arts Festival and pays tribute to those who bring the arts to life; the red, white and blue threads represent the patriotic themes and the performances of the Tattoo; the blue shades represent the Virginia Flag and the Norfolk Seal; and the grey stripes recall the naval ships and airforce planes.

The tartan has been endorsed by the Mayor of Ballarat.

name: South Carolina, University of

registrationNotes: Garnet and black are the official colours of the University of South Carolina (USC). They were first used by the football team in a game against Furman University on Christmas Eve 1892. In 2010, Marianne Bickle, PhD, Director at the USC Centre for Retailing, started the process of establishing USC’s own tartan incorporating the school’s colours. The students, faculty, staff and alumni chose the final design from a pool of three finalists during the spring semester of 2013. An important element of the tartan’s production is its philanthropic nature, as a portion of the proceeds from sales of the tartan will be used to fund student scholarships.

name: YMCA
restrictions: Yes. Copyright of this tartan belongs to YMCA Scotland and it cannot be woven or offered for sale in any country without their express permission.
registrationNotes: This 21st century tartan is a variation of the ancient Breacan nan Cleirach, the tartan of the Clergy - which was possibly worn in the Scottish Highlands by men of the church as early as the 1750s. The YMCA tartan incorporates the colours of the world organisation and at its core is the 1844 founding date of the YMCA represented with 18 threads of black and white and 44 threads of blue. Combined with that 1844 beginning, the blue of the oceans links over 45 million members around the globe and celebrates the values, strengths and aspirations of the world's largest 'clan' - the YMCA.

name: Lermontov Bicentenary

The tartan has been created to commemorate the bicentenary of the birth of Mikhail Yuryevich Lermontov - a Russian Romantic writer, poet and painter who is considered the supreme poet of Russian literature alongside Pushkin and the greatest figure in Russian Romanticism and his influence on later Russian literature is still felt in modern times.

name: Lawrence's Seven Pillars of Khaki
restrictions: Yes. Available for wear by anyone providing official merchandise is purchased from authorised outlets. The design may only be used or woven with the permission of the designer, Lady Theresa Jenkins-Teague. This is a registered design #4033956 and the design has been trademarked for use in classes 6, 9, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 28, #UK00003045982, with the UK Intellectual Property Office.
registrationNotes: The Lawrence’s Seven Pillars of Khaki Tartan has been designed by Lady Theresa Jenkins-Teague to commemorate Lawrence of Arabia. The orange brown represents Wadi Rum and Lawrence’s famous raid on Aqaba as well as the warm internal hues and tones of Clouds Hill, Lawrence’s secluded Dorset retreat. Red represents Lawrence’s birthplace at Tremadoc and his Welsh ancestry. The cross of Saint George is contrived in the sett to demonstrate Lawrence’s admiration for ‘Richard the Lionheart’ and his thesis on Crusader Castles. Blue and green represent his Irish connections and his two periods of service in the RAF. The sett shows seven distinct bands of Khaki which pay homage to Lawrence’s literary masterpiece, ’The Seven Pillars of Wisdom’.

name: Scotland's Grace
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2014. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6104319.
registrationNotes: The tartan was inspired after the designer witnessed an unusually bright double rainbow, during a heavy cloudburst in full sunshine, appearing over Arbroath east coast of Scotland on 9th May 2014. The sett reflects the seven colours of the spectrum and portrays Alexander's Dark Band, the optical phenomenon associated with rainbows and named after Alexander of Aphrodisias (the celebrated Peripatetic philosopher from Ancient Greece) who first described it in AD 200. The grey pivot represents the second bow occasionally seen in the cloud. As rainfall can be a common occurrence in Scotland the designer wanted to celebrate the dramatic Scottish cloudscapes, sunlit rainbows and rains - which when gracing the land bring forth stunning natural beauty. The blue in the weave pays tribute also to Scotland's streams, rivers and lochs. The tartan is intended for any individual or group wishing to be represented by a rainbow-themed tartan.

restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2014. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. The Declaration 1320 ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3138756.
registrationNotes: The tartan commemorates the most treasured document in Scotland's history - the 'Declaration of Arbroath' dated 6th April 1320 - a letter from the Scottish Earls and Barons in support of King Robert the Bruce and his battle for Scottish independence. The tartan is designed to visually portray both the Royal Standard of Scotland (the Lion Rampant) - and - the National Flag of Scotland (the Saltire). When printed or worn on the square the red and yellow represents the Lion Rampant, and when printed or worn on the bias the white and blue - the white cross - visually becomes the Scottish Saltire, known also as St. Andrew’s Cross. In the tartan thirteen red threads and twenty yellow threads represent the year 1320, the year the Declaration of Arbroath was sealed. Visit the registrant's website for the full rationale and numeracy within the tartan: www.theTartanArtisan.com/theDeclaration1320.

registrationNotes: Another design for Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd, a company based in the Highlands of Scotland. The tartan was inspired by an old bothy blanket. The palette of colours represent the warm heathery tones found on the highland hills.

name: Green Thistle
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. Only to be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: Another design for Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd, a company based in the Highlands of Scotland. The tartan was inspired by an old bothy blanket. The palette of colours represent the lively earthy tones of the highland landscape.

name: Qatar Airways
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Qatar Airways, on behalf of Edinburgh Airport. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Edinburgh Airport as a gift to Qatar Airways, the Qatar Airways Tartan celebrates the new route, from Edinburgh to Doha. The City of Edinburgh Tartan was selected as the starting point for the new design, to mark the growing relationship between Edinburgh Airport and Qatar Airways. A gradation of tonal grey shades has been used as the backdrop for the tartan and is highlighted with a strong white overcheck. The burgundy tone, which is synonymous with the Qatar Brand, adds a sense of depth and richness to the overall appearance of the design.

name: Wallenberg, Nicolas (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Nicolas Wallenberg, Baron of Sauchie. Based on the 1797 Bruce Tartan this asymmetric design incorporates the French Tricolour and the yellow and blue of the Swedish flag representing the Baron’s lineage. The blue and white also represent the Scottish Saltire together with the traditional Scottish colours of green and heather. The personal significance of the numeral 6 is reflected in each Tricolour band being made up of six threads.

name: Wallenberg, Nicolas Dress (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal and private dress version of the Barony of Sauchie family tartan with the design dedicated to the Baron's late mother.

name: International Bear Pride
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is to be solely manufactured by Kilted Bros, LLC.
registrationNotes: Based on the colours of the International Bear Brotherhood flag, this tartan is the first in the Equality series of kilts for Kilted Bros, LLC.

name: CREATeGlasgow

registrationNotes: CREATe is the Research Councils UK Centre for copyright and New Business Models based at the University of Glasgow. CREATe investigates the future of creative production in the digital age, in particular the role of copyright. This tartan represents CREATe's research and brand identity. Colours: black: for the project's monochrome branding; red: for UK partner universities; light purple represents creativity and diversity of project themes; dark blue represents regulation and law; green represents enterprise and inventiveness; light yellow represents technology and intellect.

name: Buchanhaven Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by the Knockando Woolmill Company Ltd unless written permission is granted by the Directors
registrationNotes: Designed by John Gillespie, Knockando Woolmill Company Ltd, for Buchanhaven Heritage Society (BHS) to celebrate their success in purchasing and refurbishing the old school in Buchanhaven to use as a Heritage and Community Centre. The tartan is based on the Ferguson sett and the colours chosen by the local community are: blue for the North Sea; red for the local granite; green and gold from the local school tie; silver for the herring.

name: King, Garry (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For exclusive family use.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Garry King and his family using colours of significance to the family.

name: Roseate Sunrise
registrationNotes: A vivid, bright pattern, complimented by a strong purple tone to represent the morning sunrise at dawn, with a small dash of green and red to represent the colour of roses.

name: Caisteal Leòdhais
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Celtic Clothing, Isle of Lewis unless permission is granted. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright belongs to Kathleen Mary Fiona Ferdinando, owner of Celtic Clothing, Isle of Lewis.
registrationNotes: The Caisteal Leòdhais (Lews Castle) tartan was designed to capture the mystical spirit of the Outer Hebrides, the rich culture of the islanders and the storied history of Lews Castle. Colours: purple and green are for the islands of Lewis and Harris; black represents the peat that fuelled life on the islands for many centuries; brown represents the Harris Tweed industry and the brown stone of the Castle; light blue is for Stornoway Harbour; golden yellow is for the Castle’s regal air.

name: St Margaret's School for Girls, Aberdeen
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for St Margaret's School for Girls, Aberdeen. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The St Margaret's School for Girls, Aberdeen tartan is based on the Aberdeen district sett. Elements of the Drummond tartan have been included within the design to acknowledge Queen Margaret, the school’s namesake, and her marriage into the Scottish Drummond Clan. Colours: blue, red and green represent the three houses of the school; Kildrummy, Crathes and Dunnottar; light blue and golden yellow reflect the school’s crest and brand colours.

name: Loretto School
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Loretto School. Restricted availability, please contact Loretto School regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Loretto School tartan is based on the Musselburgh district tartan. Elements of the MacThomas and MacDonald tartans have been included within the design to acknowledge the school’s founder, Reverend Thomas Langhorne and the headmastership of Dr Hely Hutchinson Almond. Colours: red represents the iconic red jacket worn by the pupils; blue, green, pink and purple represent the four houses of the school; Mackintosh; Langhorne, Greenlees and Tristram.

registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Daniel Kieck for him and his family.

name: Manac
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: Based on the 1965 Quebec Tartan, the Manac corporate colours of red, white and black predominate. 50 red threads commemorate the company's 50th Anniversary and 66 black threads represent 1966, the year the company was founded. On the black square, the French Tricolour marks the bloodline of the Dutil family who left France for The New world circa 1737. The white line on grey symbolises the roads of North America on which the Manac trailers operate. The red and white have greater significanance as they form the colours of both Canada's National flag and the French Arms of Forge les Eaux (Dutille's home town) and the company's original Quebec home town St. Georges.

name: Haus of RvR
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Haus of RvR. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Haus of RvR Tartan was commissioned, in 2015, by entrepreneur Ramone Turnquest and is the signature tartan of the Haus of RvR brand. The design is based on the Caledonia Tartan sett and is inspired by a rich ancestral history of toil, survival and freedom, as well as the luxurious surroundings of the Caribbean. A palette of blue, black and straw gold, originally derived from the colours of the Bahamian and Swedish flags, has been softened and tempered to reflect the conservative but sophisticated feel of the luxury brand.

name: O'Connor, Hugh (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Hugh O’Connor and his family based on the O'Connor/Ochiltree tartan and using colours of significance to the family.

name: Goldwire (2015)

registrationNotes: This tartan may be used by all those with the surname Goldwire and its variants. The name Goldwire is believed to be an occupational name for a filigree maker/jeweller hence the many intricate interwoven gold lines in the design.

name: Reeves (2015)

registrationNotes: A tartan celebrating the union of the Scottish and Australian family houses of Dykes and Reeves. registrationNotes: Designed by Michael Ross and David Waterton-Anderson for the Military and Hospitaller Order of Saint Lazarus of Jerusalem which dates from the early 12th century and was established by Papal Bull in 1255. Its purpose then was the care of lepers among pilgrims and the Crusader orders in the Holy Land and Europe. The Order continues uninterrupted as a charity and as an Order of Chivalry. The tartan is based on the Order's coat of arms of a green cross on white with gold side-stripes representing the gold fimbriation on the Order's cross, set on black representing the cloak, all on the Order's dress colours of dark green.

name: Garvock (2015)

Geometry: The yellow pivot (with the red) represents great grandmother Margaret Cameron; the four black quadrants (surrounding the green pivot) represent four generations all named James Millar Garvock; green represents Garvock hill the suggested origin of the Garvock family name in the parish of the same name in Kincardineshire.

name: Laurel Cadre, The

registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for The Laurel Cadre, a fraternal organization to be used to identify their members at historical recreation events, Highland games, and other social events, such as weddings. name: Scotland's Charity Air Ambulance
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is the copyright of SCAA and must not be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any form without their express permission.
registrationNotes: Robert the Bruce was crowned King of Scotland in 1306 in Scone and the 18th century Bruce tartan gives the inspiration for this 21st century tartan for the Scone-based Scotland's Charity Air Ambulance (SCAA) - the first of its kind in Scotland. The two predominant elements are blue and white for Scotland's national flag and the white on red - the universal colours of medical aid. Separating those two symbolic elements are the grey and green of the Scottish lansdscape over and through which SCAA flies its rescue missions in all weathers. Donated to SCAA by the Scottish Tartans Authority.

name: Equity Vision Ltd
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for Equity Vision Ltd.

name: Zimmermann, Martin (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Martin Zimermann, his family and descendants using colours of significance to the family.

name: Blueheart
restrictions: Yes. Anyone who identifies with the global movement against human trafficking is welcome to wear or display the Blueheart tartan. Liberation Kilt Co. holds exclusive rights to the Blueheart tartan and all derivatives thereof, which may only be reproduced (woven, printed etc) under license. For more information contact [email protected]. Digital images of the Blueheart tartan are protected by an Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs (CC BY-NC-ND) license, which means you may download and share them with others as long as you credit Liberation Kilt Co.; however you cannot change them in any way or use them commercially. More info at creativecommons.org. Registration No: 4040928. Date of registration: June 22 2015.
registrationNotes: Modern slavery affects every country, with an estimated 40–50 million people enslaved worldwide. Human trafficking alone generates an estimated $150 billion annually for traffickers. The Blueheart tartan serves as a powerful symbol of solidarity in the fight against modern slavery. The light blue lines represent the collective heartbeat of victims, a reminder of their resilience and hope. The black lines intersect to form a cage, signifying the harsh reality of entrapment and exploitation. This tartan is officially endorsed by the United Nations’ Blue Heart Campaign, an international initiative dedicated to raising awareness about the plight of human trafficking victims. The campaign, coordinated by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), aims to inspire action and promote global solidarity in the fight against modern slavery. The Blueheart tartan offers individuals a meaningful way to show their support and commitment to eradicating this profound human rights violation.

name: Russian Arctic Convoy
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the Russian Consul General, Edinburgh or his designated agents.
registrationNotes: With echoes of the MacLeod and MacKenzie tartans from the clanlands bordering Loch Ewe, departure point for so many of the World War II Arctic Convoys to Archangel and Murmansk, the Russian Arctic Convoy tartan encapsulates the essential colours remembered by convoy veterans. Colours of dread, death and destruction but colours too of bravery, hope and survival. White brings a multitude of memories: ice flows, wind-whipped wave-tops, snow and ice-encrusted superstructures and today the classic white berets of the surviving veterans. Grey is for the sea and the sky, for allied battleships and the ever-threatening German U-Boats. Black is for line upon line of German bombers and their devastating cargoes whilst silver is the most chilling sight of all, the bubbles in the wake of an oncoming torpedo. Brightening the hopes of many thousands of those Arctic mariners however, was the red in the White Ensign of the escorting Royal Naval vessels; the red of the merchantmen's own flag, the Red Duster, and the red in the Russian national flag.

registrationNotes: Edinburgh International Film Festival (EIFF) is the world’s longest continually running film festival, and in 2016 celebrates its landmark 70th edition. By way of commemoration, EIFF has collaborated with Edinburgh College of Art (ECA) and Bute Fabrics to create a bespoke, unique tartan which represents key elements pertaining to the festival and its long-standing cultural heritage, as well as celebrating the Scottish roots of an internationally renowned and respected institution. Incorporating the red, black and white of the EIFF logo, the colour, form and structure of the tartan also assimilates the elements below: The aspect ratio of 70mm film, serving as a commemoration of our landmark 70th edition while also representing our commitment to the heritage, artistic integrity and technical skill of cinema exhibition and projection. The vertical white broken weave represents the perforations of film stock. The asymmetry of the black rectangular frame is reminiscent of the cinema screen. The vertical red weave juxtaposed with the black rectangular frame is reminiscent of traditional red velvet cinema tabs framing the cinema screen. The pattern in repeat is reminiscent of strips of film. The two tone gold represents the light emitted from a projector.

name: Old Glory (1824)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2016. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Designs Nos. 5003476 and 6104315 (representing the US Flag flying), 4045683 and 6104316 (representing the US Flag hanging). US PTO Registered Patent No. D878,059.
registrationNotes: Created to honour the Flag of the United States of America, the tartan was inspired by the first American flag to be nicknamed "Old Glory". Owned and named as such by the 19th-century New England sea captain William Driver (1803-1886) the original 24 star flag, made in 1824, passed into legend and bequeathed its name to all American flags. The tartan commemorates the 100th anniversary of President Woodrow Wilson's Proclamation on 30th May 1916 establishing Flag Day 14th June as the official anniversary of the Flag Resolution of 1777. This Resolution was monumental in announcing the adoption by the Second Continental Congress of the stars and stripes as the official Flag of the United States. Colours and geometry: red stands for hardiness and valour; white symbolizes purity and innocence; blue represents vigilance, perseverance and justice. 100 blue threads commemorates the one hundredth anniversary of the Proclamation; 13 alternating red and white stripes represent the original thirteen British colonies that declared independence from the Kingdom of Great Britain becoming the first states in the Union; 5 white stripes in both the warp and weft cross on the blue field creating 25 accents, 24 of which represent the stars (or states) of the Union from the original Old Glory flag; the 25th becomes a memorial to Captain Driver himself representing the white anchor added to Old Glory in 1861 signifying Driver's maritime career at sea. Visit the registrant's website for the full numeracy and rationale within the tartan: www.theTartanArtisan.com/OldGlory1824.

restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Lévesque family.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Pascal Lévesque, his family and descendants using colours of significance to the family.

name: Gaffney (2016)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a tribute to the 59 year marriage of Terence Gaffney and Kathleen Pitman and to be worn by the family and their descendants.

name: Day (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed for use by the descendants of Nathanial Day, his son and grandson who emigrated to Canada c1881.
