registrationNotes: Designed using colours taken from the WaterAid logo. WaterAid will be working with Slanj to develop a range of high quality products for merchandise and uniforms.

name: Pilkington (2016)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may be worn by all of the Pilkington by name with permission from the registrant. Permission should be sought from the registrant to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: Ken MacDonald and David Pilkington principally designed this tartan for the wedding of David Douglas Pilkington of Gourock and Angela Mary Gaffney of Greenock, and to found a family tartan for their descendants. The colours were chosen due to their significance to the family and for their combined aesthetic qualities.

name: SABA
restrictions: Yes. For permission to wear/use this tartan, please contact [email protected] or [email protected]. Designed and prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed by Alan Trivett with Lisa and Russell Morton, to celebrate the fourth year of operations of the Scottish American Business Alliance (SABA), the Houston Texas group that assists Scottish companies establish entities in Texas. The Tartan will be unique to SABA members, the organisations it helps, and individuals that support its aims and clients.

name: Kansas State University
restrictions: Yes. The Kansas State University Tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from: Kansas State University University Licensing Office Kansas State University 785-532-6269 The tartan can only be produced under licence. All rights to the Kansas State University Tartan are held by Kansas State University under the US Copyright Act. All rights reserved. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: In March of 2016 Kansas State University students, alumni, faculty, staff, and friends voted to select the Official Kansas State University Tartan. The winning tartan was designed by Apparel and Textiles undergraduate students Virginia Davis and Do Young Lydia Lee under the instruction of Kelsie Doty. Colours: royal purple, the official Kansas State University colour along with white, silver, black and grey.

name: Gibson, Robert (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for use by Robert James Britain Gibson, his immediate family and descendants. Anyone wishing to weave this tartan should seek permission from Robert James Britain Gibson.
registrationNotes: Designed by Amanda Gibson as a personal tartan for Robert James Britain Gibson when he reached the age of 21, to reflect his Scottish ancestry.

name: Glasgow Warriors
restrictions: Yes. This tartan can only be purchased through Glasgow Warriors Rugby Club or Slanj Kilts of Glasgow.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed for and incorporating Glasgow Warriors team colours. The tartan has been designed for a range of merchandise for both players and supporters.

name: Jones (2016)
registrationNotes: Jestin Jones designed this tartan inspired by his family's history. It may be worn by all those sharing the Jones surname.

name: Loch Ness in Scotland
restrictions: Yes. May only be used via Loch Ness Centre & Exhibition and their licensees Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The exclusive Loch Ness in Scotland tartan has been designed to celebrate the 35th anniversary of The Loch Ness Centre & Exhibition. The colours are inspired by the beautiful landscape surrounding the loch, the mysterious waters of the loch itself, Scotland and the corporate colours of the iconic company logo. The tartan reflects Scotland's famous landscape and the name was chosen specifically to tie in with the Loch Ness Centre's International Trademark and branding.

name: International Cricket Council
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the International Cricket Council. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the International Cricket Council (ICC) to commemorate its Annual Conference, held in Edinburgh on 27th June – 2nd July 2016. The tartan design was based on the Stirlingshire District tartan sett as it was in Alloa, Stirlingshire that the first recorded cricket match in Scotland took place in 1785. The colours of the tartan are based on the ICC’s global blue and field green of its logo. Red has been introduced to represent a cricket ball and the 3 lines are representative of the cricket stumps.

name: Bruma
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his immediate family and descendants. May not be worn/woven without the written permission of the designer. Commercial sale not allowed.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding in Scotland of the designer and his wife on the 17th May 2016. Bruma, the Portuguese word for mist is associated with the island of Madeira, Portugal, the designer’s home. The red crossed lines symbolise the cross of the Knights Templar or "Order of Christ" based on 16th century Portuguese discoveries, and the subtle colour shades represent Madeira.

name: Green Alaskan
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the majestic colours of the Alaskan landscape.

name: Belladrum Estate
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Belladrum Estate. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. All tartan cloth created using this design must be woven in Scotland
registrationNotes: Belladrum Estate stretches over 1150 acres, and is positioned just a few miles North West of Inverness. This Estate has been in Joe Gibbs' family since 1857, save for a short interlude, and prior to that these lands were once owned by the Frasers of Belladrum. The estate tartan colours have been influenced by the surrounding landscape, ancient green forests and native lichens. Then coupled with a contrasting russet red, a colour that signifies the passion and pride many generations have had for the Belladrum Estate. This Estate is also home to Belladrum Tartan Heart Festival which has been staged annually since 2004. A modern vibrant version of this tartan has been woven, inspired by the vibrancy of the festival held annually on the Estate. This version will be used to promote the Tartan Heart Festival.

name: SAL Cubiska Stenen
restrictions: Yes. The Tartan is intended for use by SAL Cubiska Stenen, its members past, present and other persons affilated with SAL Cubiska Stenen, efforts and workings of said Lodge.
registrationNotes: SAL Cubiska Stenen is a Masonic Lodge working in the St Andrew Degrees within the Swedish Order of Freemasons. The Lodge recieved its Charter in 1777 and traces its origins to 18th Century Scottish Freemasonry. The affiliation with the legend of St Andrew, Scotland and Scottish traditions Past and Present is predominant, and this tartan is intended to be a reminder and a visual relationship between SAL Cubiska Stenen and its origin.

name: McNair (2016)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Martin McNair for himself and his family.

name: Hubbard (2016)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed to commemorate the descendants of George Hubbard who arrived in America in the year of 1633.

name: Brock University Alumni Association
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be reproduced or replicated without consent from the Brock University Alumni Association. Permission must be sought from Brock University Alumni Association to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: The Brock University Alumni Association tartan designed by alumnus David MacKenzie is predominantly red and blue with stripes of yellow and white. The tartan was designed in honour of Brock’s 50th anniversary as a distinctive yet traditional symbol, to identify and rally our university’s students, alumni, faculty, staff and retirees. The tartan provides a way to celebrate Brock University and raise awareness about its namesake, Major-General Sir Isaac Brock, and uses colours common to both.

name: Pompili, Antonio and Alessandro (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn by those authorised by the copyright holder. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder.
registrationNotes: Designed for Antonio Pompili, baron of Fullarton, and Alessandro Pompili, baron of Denny, incorporating the major colours from their Scottish coats of arms granted by Lord Lyon King of Arms, those arms being based on their Italian family equivalent. Only to be used by their families, heirs and successors.

name: Jensen, Sven (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Sven Jensen and his family.
registrationNotes: Designed by Sven Jensen for his and his family's use during Highland Games and other formal events. Sven is an active Major in the United States Marine Corps and designed this tartan after returning from his 4th combat tour in the Iraq and Afghanistan wars.

name: Martinez, Clément (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and those to whom he gives permission. May only be woven by Scottish or French weavers.
registrationNotes: Designed for Clément Martinez, using colours of personal significance to him.

name: Tolmie
restrictions: Yes. Those wishing to produce and use the tartan are requested to advise the registrant and/or the Clan MacLeod Society of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Tolmie sept is one of the MacLeods of Lewis and is a sept "of the blood" who were once the MacLeods of Gairloch. In discussion with past president of the Clan MacLeod Society of Scotland, Lt Col (retired) Ruari Halford-MacLeod, it was agreed that the MacLeod of Lewis tartan should be the basis of the Tolmie tartan. In recognition of the superiority of MacLeod of MacLeod, and as it is a principal colour of the arms of Kevin John Tolmie, the background is green rather than gold. After the arms granted in 2014 the Tolmie tartan was the next logical step.

name: Tainsh (2016)
registrationNotes: The designer has traced his Scottish ancestors back to the 1500s and as the last of his direct line, created this tartan to honour his family. The colours used are all contained in the ribbons of the war medals inherited from his grandfather and they also symbolise the journey and sadness leaving family in Scotland to emigrate (black for sadness, red for family/bloodline, white for the snow, blue for the sky and sea and yellow and green for sun, sand and fields.) The blue and white and green and yellow also representative the flags of Scotland and Australia. The tartan is representative of the designer’s passion for history, family, the natural elements of his birthplace and adopted country and traditions.

name: Monroig, Eric (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Eric Monroig, his immediate family and descendants. Anyone wishing to weave this tartan should seek permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for Eric Monroig, his family and descendants. Colours: red and yellow represent the designer's Catalan origins; green and blue represent the Scottish landscape.

name: Crombie, Harry (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Designed by Kinloch Anderson for the exclusive use of Harry Crombie and family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: Harry Crombie, born and raised in Edinburgh, traces the Crombie side of his family back several generations in Edinburgh. With a strong affinity to Loch Tay and the surrounding areas, the design was based using the district tartans of Edinburgh and Perthshire. Colours representing the thistle and St Andrews Cross were incorporated to give a vibrant and modern take on the traditions of his heritage, creating a personal tartan for private and corporate use.

name: Ferguson (Tarlogie)
registrationNotes: Based on the Ferguson of Atholl tartan, the designer has included an additional white line to specifically identify this tartan with his family, the senior native Fergusons of Ross and northern Scotland. The tartan is intended for anyone to use, especially Fergusons and their sept clans of MacAdie, Keddie etc.

name: Inman (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed using colours of significance to the Inman family. This tartan may be used by all those sharing the Inman surname or its derivatives.

name: Oakland Centre
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Oakland Centre. Any persons wishing further information in regards to the design and/or use of this tartan should contact the designer: [email protected].
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Warpweftweave in conjunction with service users at Oakland Centre, Dundee, a day-care centre run by Dundee City Council which provides a wide range of activities for older people. The project started as an activity created to encourage service users to celebrate St Andrew’s day and honour their "Scottishness" in a creative and meaningful manner. A total of ten different designs were created, either individually or as part of a group. The winning design was created by a group of three service users who called themselves “The Tuesday Terrors". They felt the colours they chose (red, black and natural white) were a good contrast. The group did not want too many colours in their tartan as they wanted it to be straightforward and unfussy.

name: Malone (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed using colours of significance to the Malone family. This tartan may be used by all those sharing the Malone surname.

name: Thomas McGurran
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Thomas McGurran Publishing Company owners and their descendants.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed for the Thomas McGurran Publishing Group representing the owners' joint heritage.

name: Wattenhofer (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed primarily for André Pierre Wattenhofer and his family, this tartan may be worn by anyone with the Wattenhofer surname.

name: Hummelt, Katherine (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Katherine Hummelt and her family.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Katherine Hummelt to celebrate her love of Scotland.

name: Wolves Wod Kindred
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is restricted to the oathed members of Wolves Wod Kindred or oathed members of Wolves Wod Kindred's affiliate kindreds.
registrationNotes: Wolves Wod Kindred is an Asatru religious group from Evansville, Indiana, USA. They are a faith that honours their god/goddesses, ancestors, and community. This tartan is representative of their history as an Asatru Kindred, to honour their roots and hope for the future, and is an enduring symbol of love and loyalty to the group’s faith and to one another.

name: Solberg-Bell Hunting
restrictions: Yes. The Solberg-Bell Hunting tartan is reserved for the exclusive use of Rev. Col. Douglas Evan Solberg-Bell; his wife Briani Patricia Alberta Solberg-Bell; and family and friends of the designer and any designated heir, at the discretion of the designer or designated heir. There are no restrictions at present regarding who may weave this tartan, save that it be at the personal request of the designer or designated heir.
registrationNotes: Solberg-Bell Hunting was developed using the Solberg-Bell (Personal) tartan (STR Ref #11124) as a base. It further commemorates the loss, in 2016, of Dashiell Edwin Tillman Solberg-Bell, the sole heir of the Solberg-Bell name, Arms, and privileges.

name: Isle of Raasay
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven under authorisation from Isle of Raasay Community Council.
registrationNotes: In addition to a Community Art Project to produce a large wall hanging for the village hall, it was decided to design a tartan for Raasay. The winning design was chosen from a range of tartan designs which the community considered and voted on. A piece of the woven tartan has been added to the wall hanging.

name: Scotstown
registrationNotes: This tartan and its colours represent the life and history of Scotstown, a city in Le Haut-Saint-François Regional County Municipality in the Estrie region of Quebec, Canada.

name: SYHA Hostelling Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to weave this tartan should seek permission from SYHA Hostelling Scotland. Not to be used for the commercial gain of a third party without prior consent from SYHA Hostelling Scotland.
registrationNotes: SYHA Hostelling Scotland tartan, inspired by the Scottish Highlands and Islands, incorporates the natural beauty of the great outdoors through use of forest greens, light blue to represent lochs, rivers and coastline, and a touch of SYHA earthy red denoting warmth and hospitality. The tartan will be used for soft furnishings within the SYHA network.

name: Porsche Bank Austria
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan should be sought from Porsche Bank Austria. Prepared for weaving by The Kilt Hire Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: Porsche Bank Austria decided that they would celebrate their 50th anniversary in Edinburgh and commemorate their event with a tartan. They wanted a tartan that connected their company with Scotland. Blue is taken from their company logo, ancient red for the ambers of the whisky and green represents the lush scenery found in the Highlands of Scotland.

name: RCACA
restrictions: Yes. For wear and use by members of the RCACA and the Royal Canadian Armoured Corps. Permission of the President of the RCACA must be obtained for any other use. Permission to weave must be obtained from the President of the RCACA.
registrationNotes: The Royal Canadian Armoured Corps Association (RCACA) tartan was donated by the outgoing Association President, Lieutenant Colonel (Honourary) Bernard Ciaronni in October 2016. The tartan was commissioned on 13 August 2015, the 75th anniversary of the Royal Canadian Armoured Corps (RCAC). Its design evokes both the modern Corps and its cavalry predecessors.

name: Weait (2016)
restrictions: Yes. Although this tartan may be worn/used/woven by those with the Weait surname, additional use is by permission only.
registrationNotes: Designed by Richard Weait, this tartan is intended to be hand woven for family gifts. It may be used by others sharing the Weait surname.

name: Henry, David G (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright lies with the designer. The design has been registered with the United States Copyright Office.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan using colours that are of significance to the designer and his family, as they represent university and organisational affiliations.

name: Hynett, William (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holder William A Hynett OBE. Cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder William A. Hynett OBE.
registrationNotes: This personal tartan for William Hynett OBE is based on the Clan Gordon, whose ancestral home later became Gordonstoun, the school which he attended. The surrounding area has a number of strong family ties. The colours represent those of the flag of the United Kingdom, which William has served both locally in Grampian and more broadly through the Royal Navy. The colours of the flag of Chile are also represented to denote continuing maternal family links. Finally, the centre element of light blue and pink is to represent his great pride in his two children.

name: Scottish Bear (Mathan Albannach)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan should be sought from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by the applicant for his own personal use which uses the nickname given to him by his friends and family. The tartan uses colours of personal significance to the designer.

name: Britten-Norman
registrationNotes: In celebration of the Islander’s 50th anniversary, Britten-Norman has commissioned a tartan to mark the aircraft’s long service to Scottish aviation and its role in the rugged and beautiful terrain of the Highlands and Islands. The tartan is based upon the Royal Stewart, with the broad blue representing the sky and the central silver band flanked with two lines of red representing the aircraft and its twin engines. The pale blue accent is to represent Britten-Norman’s service to military flying units around the world, first among which is the Army Air Corps. Woven in white against navy blue is the morse code for IW, representing Bembridge Airport on the IoW, the venue for the Islander's maiden flight.

name: Skarpathiotakis, George (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of George Skarpathiotakis, his family and descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for George Skarpathiotakis, his family and descendants. Colours: blue represents Greece; white is for the 5 lines in Greek flag; gold represents children; black represents the family's Cretan heritage and to remember their ancestors. The thin yellow line represents those who stayed in Greece; the thicker line represents those who emigrated to Canada.

name: McCarter (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed with the help of family members in Scotland, Australia, USA and Canada, this tartan may be worn by all those with the McCarter surname.

name: Currens (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed for the Currens family, this tartan incorporates colours of significance to the family. The tartan may be worn by anyone with the Currens surname.

name: Daly (2016)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for Rory Daly and his family. It may be worn by others sharing the Daly surname.

name: Glackin-McColgan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the family.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the joining together of the Glackin and McColgan families into a new one.

name: Northern Kentucky University
restrictions: Yes. The University of Northern Kentucky Tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from: Marketing & Communications Northern Kentucky University [email protected] 859-572-6948 The tartan can only be produced under licence. The design right for the Northern Kentucky University Tartan is held by Northern Kentucky University under the U.S. Copyright Act- 17 U.S.C. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: Northern Kentucky University students, faculty, staff, alumni, and supporters were challenged by the Office of Marketing and Communications to select an official NKU Tartan to supplement and enhance the University’s apparel and accessory options. More than 2,000 people voted in an online poll conducted in the summer of 2016, overwhelmingly selecting a black-on-gold pattern over a gold-on-black alternative. The Northern Kentucky University Tartan will be woven into fabrics appropriate for a variety of uses, including apparel, accessories, decorative items, and more. NKU’s official colors were changed from gold and white to black and gold as part of a comprehensive rebranding that began in 2014.

name: Loch Linnhe
registrationNotes: Based on Mr McArthur Fox's other Loch tartans using their features to produce a variant which is related to the general character of tartans from that area with a traditional look. This tartan can be used for dress by any individual or for dancers, pipe bands or other social groups.

name: Dogrobes
restrictions: Yes. The IP of this design is owned by Araminta Campbell and is licensed to Dogrobes only for use as woven fabric, prints and and branding and cannot be used by anyone else. Can only be woven with the joint permission of Araminta Campbell and Dogrobes Ltd.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Dogrobes Ltd to be designed by Araminta Campbell using the corporate colours for use in products and branding.

name: Tricotisse
restrictions: Yes. Can only be worn or used with the permission of the designer. Can only be woven with the permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan features colours taken from the logo of the Tricotisse company for weaving and knitting products and education. Blue is for the sky, white for the pure cotton fibre, black for the loom and light brown for the weaving shuttle.

name: L'Abeille du Cercle de Fermières Sainte-Geneviève-de-Sainte-Foy
registrationNotes: Created to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the foundation of the Cercle de Fermières Sainte-Geneviève-de-Sainte-Foy. Colours: blue is for Quebec and the preservation of the group’s craft heritage; yellow and black are for the bee (l’abeille), the group’s symbol; burgundy is for the shuttle thread in its [logo]; green represents the preservation of nature. The tartan is intended to be worn by members at formal representations.

name: Gettelman (2016)
registrationNotes: Designed as a family tartan for the Gettelmans of the eastern United States in preparation for the wedding of the designer. Can be worn by anyone with the Gettelman surname or anyone who identifies as a member of the Gettelman family.

name: Balmoral Hotel Edinburgh
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Balmoral Hotel. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Balmoral team wanted their new tartan to tie in with the inspiration behind the décor in the hotel and showcase a modern, elegant twist on tartan design. The yarn colours selected incorporate three different shades of green as well as purple and yellow. These colours reflect the stunning views of Arthur’s Seat, the Old Town and Princes Street Gardens which can be seen from The Balmoral. The colours also complement the hotel lobby which was designed with Edinburgh and Scotland in mind by Rocco Forte Hotels’ Director of Design, Olga Polizzi. This is the second tartan associated with the hotel and is called ‘The Balmoral Hotel Edinburgh’ tartan, it will showcase modern Scottish tartan design to the local, national and international guests who will visit the hotel over many years to come.

name: Maciver of Strathendry Castle Dress (Personal)
registrationNotes: A dress tartan for the Macivers at Strathendry Castle to compliment their existing hunting tartan. The family originally comes from the Outer Hebrides and the design has been based on an historical tartan fragment from the region with appearance altered to closely resemble the existing Maciver tartans.

name: Al Suwaidi of Abu Dhabi (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Houston Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: Designed by Dr Hamed Bin Mohamed Khalifa Al Suwaidi and Ken MacDonald, this tartan is made up of the traditional Pan-Arab colours that form the UAE's flag which was adopted on 2nd December 1971. The colours (red, green, white and black) combine to form and symbolize Arab unity. The designer who originally created the UAE flag was inspired by verses of a poem describing the citizens acts as white representing peace and honesty, plains as green representing hope goodness and agriculture, battles as black representing strength of mind, courage and power and swords as red representing bravery and sovereignty. Each colour was selected precisely to reflect an important concept to the natives of the country and hence, the choice of the same colours has been used in the design of this piece. The tartan was designed in a symmetrical manner to give equality and importance to each choice of colour and what it symbolizes. The red colour was chosen to be a little more dominant and significant on the design because it resembles the original and authentic flag of Abu Dhabi, the Capital Emirate and the largest city in the UAE.

name: Utah Valley University
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed by Micah Martin and Jacob Oldroyd for the Utah Valley University using the official University colours. The tartan will be used to create products for the university students, faculty members and staff e.g. kilts, scarves, hats, blankets. Kilts shall also be made for the official graduation pipe band.

name: Hebridean Celebration
restrictions: Yes. Can only be reproduced with the express written permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan designed with inspiration drawn from the landscape of the Outer Hebrides from Barra to the Butt of Lewis. The green with black overcheck is similar to the Morrison Hunting (a clan from the north of Lewis) and also represents the black peat cuttings through the green moors. The blue with white overcheck is similar to the Macneil of Barra and also represents the blue seas with white crests on the waves that surround the islands. The purple and rusty brown checks represent the other colours of the moors - the russets of autumnal bracken and grasses and purples of the summer heathers, thistles and wild thymes.

name: Sutherland de Albergaria Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used with permission from Stephen Sutherland de Albergaria.
registrationNotes: Designed and registered on behalf of Stephen John Sutherland de Albergaria as a dress version of the family tartan.

name: MIT1951
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by graduates of MIT and their immediate families.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) (Cambridge, USA) Class of 1951's 65th reunion.

name: Forget Family (Red)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Forget family.
registrationNotes: A red version of the Forget Family (Yonne) (STR Ref: 10694) tartan.

name: Southern Lakes
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from Hilary Johnstone.
registrationNotes: Shona Johnstone designed this tartan inspired by the lakes and tussock hills, the snow of winter and the dark shadows of the peaks in the Southern Lakes district of New Zealand.

name: Malone, Keagan Allen (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his son Keagan Allan Malone and descendants. Permission to wear or use this tartan must be sought from Keagan Allen Malone, or his immediate family.
registrationNotes: Designed by Jeffrey Allen Malone for his son inspired by colours of significance to their family.

name: Heart of Oak
restrictions: Yes. This weaving of this cloth will be at the discretion of the designer and cannot be woven without his permission. Copyright lies with the designer.
registrationNotes: The idea for this design came from a currently serving member of the Royal Canadian Navy (RCN) who wished to have a tartan created. The tartan is not something that has been proposed as something the Navy would adopt for wear by its members. Rather, that the tartan would stand as a symbol of appreciation by members and supporters of the RCN. It is open to any and all that wish to show support for members, veterans, friends and family of the RCN.

name: Muylle, Jelle (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and his family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in 2003 by Jelle Muylle on the occasion of his marriage to Beatrice Dower. The design was inspired by the colours of the national flags of Belgium and Scotland. It celebrates both Jelle's nation of origin and the country he has chosen to make his home.

name: Gray, Thomas (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of Thomas Gray, his family and those to whom he gives permission to wear/use it. Designed and prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd., Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed for Thomas Gray and his family from Bucksburn, this tartan commemorates the strength of connection the Gray family enjoyed in the Sclattie and Newhills parishes in the history of Aberdeenshire.

name: Dunoon Burgh Hall Trust
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by the designer or another independent Harris Weaver.
registrationNotes: Designed as part of a community project led by Dunoon Burgh Hall Trust in 2015/16, participants drew the landscape choosing colours that reflected the Cowal Peninsula: yellow represents broom and daffodils; purple for heather and rhododendrons; grey for lichen, rocks and the weather; navy for the river Clyde and the sky and green for the moss. The design was woven this year and launched at the Cowal Highland Gathering in August 2016.

name: Scottish-Shop Switzerland
restrictions: Yes. Supplied by request from Scottish-Shop Switzerland GmbH.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed to represent the Scottish-Shop in Switzerland.

name: Coast & Glen (Fishbox) Ltd
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of Coast & Glen Ltd. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. This tartan must be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: Coast & Glen Ltd was founded in 2012, with the introduction of its sub-brand Fishbox in 2014. This tartan has been created using both brand corporate colours as the core colour palette. The yarn counts represent the founding years of the business, the specific fishing areas of Scottish waters that are used to source all produce and the Scottish ports they work with.

name: Komissarov, Dmitry (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For exclusive use of the Komissarov family. Commission weave with Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. This tartan must be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: A family tartan created for the Komissarov family, to celebrate their strong affinity with Scotland. The red and purple have been chosen to represent Dmitry and Maria, the mother and father, with the grey and navy repeats representing their five children. restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2016. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6014261. Scotch Whisky Tartan ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3158697. 1494 ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3204936.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate Scotch Whisky, the tartan also pays tribute to the ‘Spiritual home of Scotch’ (Lindores Abbey, Fife), remembering the first written record of whisky production in the Exchequer Rolls of Scotland 1st June 1494. “To Friar John Cor, by order of the King, to make aqua vitae VIII bolls of malt.” — Exchequer Rolls 1494–95, Vol x, p. 487. Considered to be the industry's founding document, it records Brother Cor, a ‘Grey Monk’ of the Tironensian Order, being charged with the commission of making "acqua vitae" by King James IV. The tartan was created to tell this story. Colours and Geometry: Blue is the pure Scottish water used to make the spirit, the three stripes representing the ‘Holy Burn’, the water source used by the Monks of Lindores Abbey; Dark Grey represents John Cor and the robes of the Tironensian Order; Russet Brown represents the traditional oak cask used for maturation, the shade between the brown and ochre alluding also to the copper pot still; Ochre represents the ‘eight bolls of malt’, the shade between the ochre and grey representing the yeast; Yellow and Amber combine to represent the Scotch Whisky itself, with yellow shades in the tartan representing the ancient barley fields surrounding Lindores Abbey in 1494. The Scotch Whisky tartan is designed to harmonise with ‘The Angels' Share’ (tartan reference 11497), the White not only representing the glint in the whisky glass but also the Angels, said to have their own interest in Scotch. Visit the registrant's website for the full numeracy and rationale within the tartan: www.theTartanArtisan.com/ScotchWhisky.

restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of members of The Weaver Incorporation of Dundee part of the Nine-Trades Incorporation of Dundee. This tartan may not be used for any other purpose. registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to match garments worn by members of The Weaver Incorporation of Dundee, and will be made into hand-woven neckerchiefs and scarves. Colours: the dark blue, light blue and silver grey are used in gentlemen’s regalia, and the simple yellow threads represent the Incorporation's insignia. The sett was designed for hand-loom weaving.

name: Isle of Eriskay
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale or woven unless with the Specific authorisation of the copyright holders Co Chomunn Eirisgeidh Ltd, Rubha Ban, Isle Of Eriskay HS8 5JJ.
registrationNotes: The tiny Hebridean island of Eriskay has many claims to fame - the haunting Eriskay Love Lilt, the ancient breed of Eriskay ponies, the seamless Eriskay jersey; the real 1941 Whisky Galore island and the first Scottish footfall of Bonnie Prince Charlie in 1745. It is the last of these that forms the Royal Stewart basis of the Eriskay Tartan whose colours mirror those of the landscape, seas and sands of the island. One final touch is the pink for the sea bindweed that is uniquely present on Eriskay. Legend has it that it grew from the seeds inadvertently dropped on the beach when Bonnie Prince Charlie pulled out his ‘kerchief’.

name: Children's Village
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Kinokuni Children’s Village School.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Kinokuni Children’s Village School in Japan founded in 1992 and which celebrates its 25th anniversary in 2017. It was inspired by the philosophy of Scottish educators, A S Neill of Summerhill School in Norfork and John Aitkenhead of Kilquhanity House School near Dumfries, the core of which was ‘to make children happy.’ Colours: the two green are from the school emblem; blue is from the McNeil of Barra tartan, said to have been worn by John Aitkenhead in his everyday life; white and yellow are added as an attractive accent. The tartan will be used for school goods.

name: Jarosz, Andrew Leslie, baron of Kirkliston (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Andrew Leslie O.W. Jarosz, his family, heirs and successors.Use by others by the express permission of the owner. Cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of Andrew Leslie O.W. Jarosz or his designated agents.
registrationNotes: Based on an early Montgomerie tartan, this was designed in 2005 by Romilly Squire, then Deputy Secretary of the Standing Council of Scottish Chiefs, for Andrew Leslie O. W. Jarosz, Kirkliston, a gentleman and hereditary clansman of the Clan Montgomerie (confirmed in 2005 by the Chief, the Rt. Hon Archibald George Montgomerie, 18th Earl of Eglinton and 6th Earl of Winton). In 2002 he became Baron of Kirkliston (in the County of West Lothian), officially recognised by The Lord Lyon King of Arms in 2003.

name: Perth County

registrationNotes: The (Canadian) Perth County Tartan was created to commemorate the 150th Anniversary of Canada in 2017. Colours; the shades of green represent the strong agricultural presence in Perth County; blue represents the many rivers and creeks that flow through the fertile farmland; red is for the blood sacrificed by the early settlers and veterans who gave their lives so that their descendants could prosper; gold signifies the industrious nature of the people of Perth County.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the Scottish heritage and identity of Skyscanner Ltd. The bold and bright colours represent the striking image of the corporate organisation, each of which has a specific yarn count representing the organisation's journey.

name: Manual, The

registrationNotes: The Manual is the influential online “Essential Guide for Men” and this tartan was commissioned by its colourful Editor-in-Chief Cator Sparks. The green on grey is for The Manual’s corporate colours and that Big Apple red of its New York base, combines with the city’s road grid, bustling with the famous yellow cabs. Green is also from the old city arms of Portland, Oregon – the 2012 birthplace of The Manual - and the pink is for that city’s nickname ‘The City of Roses’.

name: Pauley (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Permission to weave the Pauley Tartan must be sought from Matthew Pauley or one of his agents with the authority to make such approval decisions.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Pauley family from Canada using colours of significance to represent their heritage and nationality. This tartan may be used by others with the Pauley surname.

name: Hankyu

registrationNotes: Violet is the company's signature colour, the song of the violet is played daily at the opening time of all Hankyu Department Stores. Beige and orange reflect gracefulness, and grey the stores' sophisticated and fashionable atmosphere which provides a peaceful space for customers. Blue reflects both sea and sky, and pink represents the cherry blossoms loved by Japanese people. Green reflects the forest green that provides customers with a relaxing space, with yellow reflecting the relaxing beauty of nature.

name: Blackcraig Castle
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Thompson family unless permission given. May only be woven with permission from the Thompson family.
registrationNotes: Designed by Christopher and Linzi Thompson, this tartan was created to mark the family’s renovation of Blackcraig Castle and also for the wedding of their eldest son, Christopher. The earthy tones were chosen to represent the countryside in which the castle is situated and the flash of blue to represent the family and its Scottish roots. Once woven, the tartan will be made into garments such as kilts, trews and dresses for use by the family.

name: Livingston (MacLea) - Curcio (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of family members. Others wishing to wear/use this tartan should seek prior consent. Copyright rests with the designers.
registrationNotes: Designed by Gary and Jennifer Livingston as a personal family tartan based on the Livingson tartan. The additional white stripes represent Jennifer's Italian ancestry and the blue stripe represents their American heritage, specifically Gary's Scottish ancestors' participation in the founding of the United States.

name: Cobourg
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holders. Not to be offered for sale or woven without the specific approval of the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: Lying in Northumberland County on the north shore of Lake Ontario in Canada, the "Feel good" town of Cobourg's civic hall - named after his mother Queen Victoria - was opened in 1860 by Edward VII when Prince of Wales. To link with that event, the Cobourg tartan is inspired by the 1853 Balmoral tartan designed by Victoria's husband Prince Albert. Teamed with that classic design is a distinctive element from the Northumberland Check - a simple shepherd's plaid that has enjoyed cross-border popularity in Scotland for very many centuries. The colours are from Cobourg's town logo.

name: Edinburgh Festival Fringe
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or printed on commercial products without the express permission of the copyright holders The Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society.
registrationNotes: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe began in 1947 when eight groups arrived in Edinburgh hoping to perform at the newly formed Edinburgh International Festival but were refused entry to the programme. Rather than being discouraged from performing, they went ahead and performed on the fringe of the Festival anyway and so the Edinburgh Festival Fringe was born. 2017 marks the 70th anniversary of these eight groups’ defiance and the Edinburgh Festival Fringe is now the largest arts festival in the world. The Fringe is a truly open access festival where, in the spirit of the original eight, no one is denied entry, making it the largest platform on earth for creative freedom. This tartan commemorates and celebrates 70 extraordinary years of defying the norm, and pays tribute to the eight groups and to the bright, bold, creative spirit of the Fringe against Edinburgh’s wonderful historic backdrop. The denim blue block with 70 threads represents the city and 70 years, the eight bright yellow lines are the Fringe flame ignited by those eight groups and, when combined with the reds and greens, come together to create a bold, exciting tartan which represents this extraordinary festival. The tartan will be used in and on a variety of promotional items.

name: Colours of Flanders
registrationNotes: This tartan is a tribute to the colours of the ancient province of Flanders before the French revolution.

registrationNotes: An official tartan designed for the City of Long Beach. Each of the following colours is significant to the City itself. Yellow features prominently each day with 350 days of sunshine per year and throughout the 9 miles of sandy coastline; green showcases the vibrancy of life in the 162 citywide parks; red represents the sunrise and sunsets which streak through the sky; situated on the coast, blue represents the surrounding ocean and the city’s title of the "Aquatic Capital of the US."

name: Van Ritchie (2017)
registrationNotes: A family tartan based very loosely on an existing Ritchie pattern, and evolved, incorporating the designers' favourite colours.

registrationNotes: A new tartan design for the Glenlivet USA representing the brand's rich Scottish heritage while nodding to its evolution in modern times. The design draws from colours represented in the refreshed brand palette, focusing on its characteristic dark taupe colour, shot through with sky blue and dark blue that represent the broad product portfolio. In designing the tartan, the brand desired to focus on its roots while allowing for a modern overlay that reflects the refreshed, contemporary brand design.

registrationNotes: The Peak District National Park was the first UK national park established in 1951. The tartan will be used in garments, soft furnishings and specially designed products.

name: Darien Venture, The
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with authorisation from Great Scot International, Charlotte, North Carolina, USA. email; [email protected].
registrationNotes: Designed by Gordon Kirkbright and Peter Wilson this tartan is inspired by the failure of the Scottish plan to establish a trading colony in the Panama Isthmus in the late 1600's. The Darien Venture was a scheme which saw brave men and women risk and/or lose their lives with some never seeing their homeland again. The dream of a transoceanic trade route was to be fulfilled some two centuries later by a descendant of one of the survivors, who settled in the Carolinas. The colours represent blue for the Saltire, red for the Panamanian flag, purple for the Scottish heather and gold for the Golden Isle which sits at the mouth of the bay of New Caledonia in Darien.

registrationNotes: Approved and supported by The Royal British Legion, in celebration of the poppy, a symbol of remembrance and hope worn by millions of people as part of modern British life, culture and heritage. A percentage of the sales of “Remember Me” tartan products is donated to The Royal British Legion to help and support those who are proud to wear the poppy, and to help those in need. Colours: red, green and black represent the poppy and remembrance and white represents hope and the future of the living.

name: Stuart Nicol Transport

name: Loganair 2017

registrationNotes: A new tartan for Loganair, Scotland and the UK’s longest serving airline trading under its original name. Loganair is a truly unique operation offering an incredibly diverse route network to the Highlands and Islands. This includes the iconic Barra with the only scheduled service in Europe to a beach airport and the World’s shortest commercial flight between Orkney’s Westray and Papa Westray. Loganair wanted a tartan that was clean and simple and able to reflect its Scottish history.

name: Blake, Steven (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and his family.
registrationNotes: This tartan constitutes a personal design which incorporates colours representing the designer’s family (white), those that he has identified with throughout his life (red, black, and yellow), and those which represent his ancestral countries (among them the United Kingdom and France).

name: HMS Forth

registrationNotes: First Sea Lord, Admiral Sir George Zambellas asked Rachel Johnstone-Burt to be the sponsor of the first of the new River Class vessels, HMS Forth, commissioned by the Royal Navy and due to come into service later in 2017. As the ship's sponsor, it is expected that a gift is given to the ship and as HMS Forth was built in Scotland by a Scottish workforce, it was felt appropriate that it should bear the name of a Scottish river. The designer felt that the gift should be Scottish and that HMS Forth having her own tartan would be an appropriate gift for her and her future ship's companies.

name: Tschischka, Sabine and Marcus (Personal)

name: Fascaray

registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the fictional Hebridean island of Fascaray, setting of the novel 'Hame' by Annalena McAfee. Its colours are drawn from the natural world of the region: sea mist grey; the eggshell blue of frozen burns; green for native pines and lichen; mauve for heather; brown for peat; and sapphire blue for summer seas.

name: Dundee Scottish Pipe Band (Illinois)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by USA Kilts, Wesley Williams and Faye Williams for the Dundee Scottish Pipe Band (DSPB) founded in 2010 in Dundee Illinois, and is based on the Dundee district tartan (SRT ref. 1029). The colours chosen reflect the energy of DSPB: orange reflects a band focused on youth education and achievement, while maintaining a friendly environment; green reflects their energy and vigour; blue represents their commitment and loyalty to both the individuals within the band and the unit as a whole, working together to achieve a united goal of success.

name: Fair Trade
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar in the UK and World Fair Trade members outside the UK. Prior written consent is required from the owner and copyright holder of the tartan Tania Pramschufer.
registrationNotes: The Fair Trade tartan was created by Tania Pramschufer, Director, Hand Up Events with the World Fair Trade Organisation (WFTO) in mind, to support fair trade weavers, crafts makers and designers around the globe, to promote the wider fair trade movement and to serve as a legacy to Scotland as a Fair Trade Nation. Hand Up Events exists to platform and promote fair trade through events and networking to benefit fair trade producers around the world. The tartan launched on World Fair Trade Day 2017 with Rudi Dalvai, President of the World Fair Trade Organisation in attendance at Fair Trade Fiesta. The aim of this tartan is to develop products using the tartan with WFTO members.

name: Royal Regiment of Fusiliers
restrictions: Yes. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 11 July 2017, registration number: 6015205.
registrationNotes: The Royal Regiment of Fusiliers was formed with the amalgamation of the four English fusilier regiments which were: The Royal Northumberland Fusiliers, The Royal Warwickshire Fusiliers, The Royal Fusiliers (City of London Regiment) and The Lancashire Fusiliers. This tartan celebrates all past, present and future Fusiliers attached to this Regiment. Encompassing important and historical colours associated with the regiment: red and white signify the distinctive Hackle, worn by all ranks in the Regiment and handed down from the Royal Northumberland Fusiliers, the Hackle was awarded in recognition for the defeat of the French at the Battle of St Lucia in 1778; navy blue represents the beret; gold represents the cap badge and black signifies continual respect for the fallen.

registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the history and pride of Benton High School in St Joseph, Missouri. The tartan is named after the school mascot, Bentley (a red cardinal bird), and uses school colours of red, white and black.

registrationNotes: The Saint Andrew's Society of Los Angeles was founded in 1930 and is the oldest organisation in Southern California devoted to the promotion of Scottish culture. The colours in the design are those found in the Society’s emblem, which is recognized by the Lord Lyon King of Arms, at Edinburgh, and represent the Flag of Saint Andrew, four golden images ( St Andrew, Fleur de Lys and the California Grizzly Bear) and motto, "Scotia Semper Patria".

name: Hall

registrationNotes: Designed for Hall, a small village in the north of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT), that sits on the border of New South Wales. Colours: dark blue represents the ACT, Canberra flag and the association to the Australian National Flag; lime green represents the colours worn today by the “Canberra Raiders” Rugby League Team in addition to the original referred colours, light blue represents the protected native species “The Royal Blue Bell” the floral emblem of the ACT; yellow represents the flag of the ACT on which the Coat of Arms is displayed; blue and yellow represent the traditional heraldic sporting colours of the ACT and the Hall Primary School established in 1911; black represents the Viking emblem displayed by the Canberra Raiders; white symbolically represents the Southern Cross Constellation, unique to and viewed only in the Southern Hemisphere.

registrationNotes: Members of the Second Battalion, The Royal Australian Regiment currently wear the Australian Tartan however due to the re-role of the Second Battalion, The Royal Australian Regiment it was decided that a new tartan specific to the unit would be created and implemented to further distinguish members of the Second Battalions Pipes and Drums.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Rangeley, Maine, inspired by the 45th parallel and its sporting history, the deep forest that meets the big lakes and the reflection of the clouds on the water; the hills and dales, the black bear and the salmon.

name: Sherlock Holmes
restrictions: Yes. Please contact Tania Henzell to wear/use/weave this tartan. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar. Copyright: Tania Henzell trading as Tattimole. Tania Henzell [email protected] Design Application Number 6009771 Class: 05 and 32 Registered 26/03/2017
registrationNotes: The Sherlock Holmes tartan has been created to show his followers that a tartan has been designed in his name. The creator of Sherlock Holmes was Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, who was born in Scotland with Irish ancestry, hence the blue and green in the tartan. The lighter blue with the brown edging represents the Reichenbach Falls in Switzerland, the gold strip to show that Sherlock Holmes was one of the leading detectives of London. The tartan will be used to sell merchandise worldwide to all his fans and Sherlock Holmes societies.

registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the beauty of the natural colours in the New Forest: green represents oak leaves, moss, lichen, grass where the New Forest ponies graze; dark green represents yew, fir, holly and gorse; grey represents silver birch and donkeys; purple represents heather; russet red represents red deer, New Forest ponies, ferns and autumn leaves.

name: Keep Calm and Carry On
restrictions: Yes. Copyright Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 2 June 2017, registration number: 6013331.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the quintessential Britishness of the ‘stiff upper lip’- renowned for remaining resolute and calm in the face of adversity and unsure times. Which was arguably put to its greatest test during WWII. ‘Keep Calm and Carry On’ Tartan is designed to praise the Great British tenaciousness of remaining positive during dark times. Black represents uncertain and worrying times and with the power of optimism the blackness turns to a lighter shade of grey. Followed by positive green, symbolising renewal, growth, calm and harmony. Red, white and blue represent the colours of Great Britain. The tartan also pays tribute to the Ministry of Information (MOI - 1939 dissolved in 1946) essential in Great Britain’s Victory during WWII, not to be forgotten. Achieving extraordinary success with their morale boosting public posters across Britain. The poster "Keep Calm and Carry On" was to be used upon invasion, thus never seen by the public. Since then, “Keep Calm and Carry On” has become a popular personal mantra. In an uncertain world with modern-day anxieties people are still drawn to the calming Britishness of this simple message ‘Keep Calm and Carry On’. Making it still so very relevant to our lives today.

name: Seyfarth, Christel (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal tartan created for Christel Seyfarth and her family. The design detail reflects her Scandinavian heritage and her strong affiliation with Scotland.

name: Roy (2017)

registrationNotes: Based on the Robertson tartan that was recorded in 1819 – a clan with which the Roys are historically connected – this design celebrates both the Scottish and Canadian branches of the family. Red is for the Maple leaf and Claire Roy – a much loved and mourned red-haired member of the ‘clan’ - and together with white and blue represents David Roy’s naval career. White is for the snows of Canada and the Cairngorms; grey is for the Canadian Shield and the skies of Blackpool, Margaret’s adopted home; the green is for Granny and Grandad Roy’s love of gardening. The thread count of 50 commemorates the year the first Roy graduated from University – John Roderick in 1950 from St. Andrew’s. Finally the yellow represents the common characteristics of the Roy family DNA – curiosity, intellect, humour, and joy. May be used by descendants or those sharing the Roy Surname.

name: House of Elrick

As part of the Estate revitalisation a tartan has been designed to reflect the unique heritage of the site since 1720.
