registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Scottish National Team, approved by the Scottish Football Association and voted for by the Tartan Army.

name: Tall Ships
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Simon Fuller, Tall Ships Landing Developments Inc. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: Dockside Living - The 1000 Islands Shoppe, situated within The Tall Ships Landing Coastal Resort, Brockville, Ontario, Canada, commissioned this design to honour the majestic tall ships and has now become the home of the official “Tall Ships” tartan. Colours: Almalfi navy evokes the romance of the sea and sky with the freedom to explore; scholar green embodies the pioneer spirit of adventure and discovery; red damask is reminiscent of the demanding and rewarding experiences that build courage and leadership; golden yellow of the rope detail symbolises the time honoured traditions inherent in the age of sail. A tartan was chosen as Scottish tartans are a symbol of clan kinship, a great representation of the bonds of fellowship created through seamanship amongst the crew of a tall ship. A traditional and timeless design, much like the tall ship. A classic tartan to encapsulate the spirit of a sailor.

name: Rapalje-Dieb
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills.
registrationNotes: This tartan is one of four designs for the members of the Dutch folk band ‘Rapalje’, known for their Scottish, Irish and Dutch folk music. Dieb den Boer, fiddler with the band, designed the original purple version for himself in 1998. In 2005, using the same sett, he designed this brown version to replace the original design. In 2009 he created versions for his fellow band members: green for William; red for Maceál and blue for David. The colours are based on those found in the Scottish highlands. The Rapalje tartan has become the trademark of the band and is worn at every one of their concerts around the world.

name: Liverpool Plains
restrictions: Yes. May not be offered for sale, reproduced or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder/designer: F J Lawson, Crofter's Weaving Mill.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Liverpool Plains, an extensive agricultural area covering about 1.2 million hectares of the north-western slopes of New South Wales in Australia. Designed to reflect the districts, natural beauty and the diversity of primary production in the area on the unique self mulching black soil plains. Colours: rust is for the sorghum that is ready to harvest; black is for the fertile alluvial soils cloddy and cracked; yellow is for the sunflowers and canola, so cheerful and bright; blue is for the artesian basin that irrigates the plains and for rivers that run between the hills engulfed in a eucalypt haze; white is for the soft buds of cotton that are yet to be baled; green is for the pastures that leap out of the ground after bountiful rains. All of these elements are woven together on the Liverpool Plains.

name: Wee Scottish
registrationNotes: For the use of the 'Wee Scottish Group' on Facebook who follow the 'Wee Scottish Lass' on YouTube. This tartan is intended as a trade mark for the YouTube channel and all its fans.

name: Claesson-Molcroft, Daniel (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn by those authorised by the copyright holder Daniel Molcroft. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or printed without the express permission of the copyright holder Daniel Molcroft.
registrationNotes: This tartan is based on the Leslie Clan tartan with the Swedish flag prominently placed between the requested beige bands. In the centre of the dark blue ground lies a single pink for the couple's young daughter Chloe, flanked by a narrow gold for Hjoker, the family's Golden Retriever, a gold which also doubles for Daniel's great love of Scotch Whisky. Finally the light green is for the wild celery plant, better known as Angelica - Daniel's partner.

name: O'Buckley (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A tartan for use by all with the O'Buckley surname, created using family colours and those of their Irish homeland.

name: Western Catholic Union
restrictions: Yes. To be woven only through Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts.
registrationNotes: The three colours of the tartan were chosen because they represent the primary colours in the company logo. Gold symbolises both the cross (faith) and the anchor (hope); red represents the heart (charity) and navy blue is used in the handshake (good fellowship). The sett is based on the existing Clergy sett.

name: King George Lodge Masonic
restrictions: Yes. For use by freemasons in good standing who are members of King George Lodge No. 59, GRA, AF & AM or those who have been licenced to wear it. Please contact the designer to weave this tartan. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the King George Lodge No. 59, located in Calgary, Alberta. Colours: red represents allegiance to country and crown; white represents the purity to which all masons aspire; dark blue represents Grand Lodge and Monarch; light blue represents the craft lodge; gold signifies that the lodge has celebrated its centennial.

name: Pride of Anfield
restrictions: Yes. Please seek the designer's permission to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: As a Liverpool Football Club supporter, the designer wanted to pay tribute to the club by designing a tartan using colours synonymous with the famous footballing institution.

name: Grangemouth Rugby Club
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of players, members and supporters of Grangemouth Rugby Club.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to be worn by the players, families and supporters of Grangemouth Rugby Club. The club was formed in 1929 and has prided itself on having a strong sense of community and family. This tartan will allow members to show their affiliation to the club at many occasions.

name: Pendleton (2017)
restrictions: Yes. May not be worn without permission from the designer, Glenn Pendleton or his descendants.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed to honour the family's long tradition of military service, those who have passed, friends, family and brothers-in-arms as well as those who are serving or will in the future. Black, red, white, blue and green are all colours of significance to the family.

name: Scottish Open Golf
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is not to be used by any other company or person without the permission of the European Tour. Please contact Samantha Purssell for permission – [email protected]
registrationNotes: The European Tour decided it was time for the Scottish Open, one of the major golf tournaments on its schedule, to have its own unique tartan. The three shades of blues represent both Scotland's national colours and the colours chosen by European Tour for the Scottish Open golf event.

name: Cahill (2017)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is designed for use by the descendants of Michael Cahill and Elizabeth O'Connell who settled in New York in the 1880s. Permission to weave should be requested from the designer.
registrationNotes: Green represents the family’s ancestral home of Ireland, blue and silver are the ancient colours of the Cahill name and the red, white and blue stripe represent the family's new home in the United States of America.

name: Colchester, Nova Scotia
designer: Lloy, Deana A, Red Label Kilts
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used with written permission from Colchester Highland Games and Gathering Directors. May only be woven with permission from Colchester Highland Games and Gathering Directors and Deana A Lloy, Red Label Kilts 16 Woodill St. Sydney, NS.
registrationNotes: A tartan to commemorate the very first Colchester Highland Games & Gathering, Colchester County, Nova Scotia, held on 9 September 2017. Colours: red is for the clay loam soil of Colchester County; green is for the land; blue is for the Fundy Bay, rivers and high tides; yellow is for the daffodil on the County flag and to represent Acadians; black is taken from the Mi'kmaw flag.

name: Sole Sisters
registrationNotes: Sole Sisters Women's Race Series, located in Nova Scotia, includes the largest women's only 5K in Canada. The tartan is intended for use in medals, kilts, scarves etc.

name: Knight (2017)
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: The pattern was commissioned as a 60th birthday gift for Peter John Knight, and is based on the Gunn tartan. The tartan may be used by anyone with the Knight surname.

name: Memory of Armentières
registrationNotes: In commemoration of WW1, the designer wanted to create a tartan paying tribute to the city of Armentières, France. The colours represent the city's coat of arms and the two crosses of war awarded to the city. Black is taken from the Flemish flag, as Armentières was situated in what was once French Flanders.

name: Héritage Eduen
restrictions: Yes. Please consult the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan. .
registrationNotes: The Héritage Eduen tartan pays homage to the Celtic people who lived in Burgundy, France. The colours were chosen for their strong symbolic connection with the Burgundy culture. The tartan has been designed for inhabitants of the region bringing together Saône and Loire, Côte d'or, Yonne and Nièvre.

name: Team Rubicon USA
restrictions: Yes. Only for use by registered volunteers and paid employees of Team Rubicon USA.
registrationNotes: Team Rubicon is an international disaster response non-profit organisation that unites the skills and experiences of military veterans with first responders to rapidly provide relief to communities in need. Founded in 2010 with the expressed goal of quickly responding to large-scale disasters, Team Rubicon has deployed thousands of volunteers across the United States and world to provide relief to communities in need. Colours: grey represents the grey shirts worn by members; brown represents military veterans; black represents helping people in their darkest hour; red represents the fire that dwells within all organisation volunteers; white is the purity of heart and purpose of the organisation; the thin black line breaking the white is to remember the fallen members of all armed services.

name: Saint Andrew's Society of Sacramento
restrictions: Yes. Only those proven members of the Society and their immediate family members may wear/use this tartan.
registrationNotes: Saint Andrew’s Society of Sacramento was organised in 1983 as a non-profit charitable society. The mission of the society is to promote and perpetuate Scottish culture by providing grants and scholarships to support education, music, arts, and other charitable activities. The Brotherhood of its members is informed by their proven lineage to Scotland. On 30 January 2015, Lord Lyon King of Arms granted the society arms. The tartan is a representation of the colours found in the arms.

name: Powell (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by and for the family of Shane and Janice Powell, Surrey. It may be worn by others sharing the Powell surname.

name: Arnprior, Ontario (Two Rivers)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan resides with the Friends of the Arnprior and District Museum of Arnprior, Ontario Canada. Permission to reproduce this tartan in any form resides with The Friends of the Arnprior and District Museum.
registrationNotes: Designed by Donalda Stevens and Janice Herwig, this tartan was created to celebrate Canada's 150th birthday and references the following: the town's Scottish origins as a town named after a hamlet in Stirling, Scotland; the colours of the founders' tartans and the importance of the Buchanans, MacNabs, and McLachlins to the town's development; the colours of the town's traditional symbol and the current colour palette used by the town in its newer logo (represented by the lighter blue) - to unite past and present. The phrase "Where the Rivers Meet" is a key part of the town's image, with the dark blue representing the mighty Ottawa River and the lighter one, the Madawaska River, which intersects the Ottawa. The green represents the white pine forests, a vital element of the town's history as a major centre of the lumber trade. Parallel lines evoke the bridge and the railway tracks, key elements in the town's development.

name: Montreal 1642
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Montreal 1642 tartan is a gift to the City and citizens of Montreal on the 375th anniversary of its founding. The 1642 tartan represents Scots and the city's civic and military organisations. The design uses colours which represent the founding peoples of Montreal; white and blue represent the St Andrew's flag of the Scots; green represents the Irish, red represents the St. George's cross of the English and the French are represented by the blue of St. Jean and the white of the Fleur de Lys. The interlocking shades of the tartan express the peaceful integration of these original founding peoples with those of other nations and cultures from around the world.

name: Mollison (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Mollison family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: This tartan is based on the Aberdeenshire district sett, in recognition of the Mollison family connection to Aberdeen, with several family descendants having served in various official positions within the city since the 15th Century. The colours of green, blue and yellow have been taken from the Dyce Tartan, also in acknowledgement of family ties to the area.

name: Wells Variation (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer.
registrationNotes: A variation on the Wells (Personal) tartan (STR ref. 4592).

name: Bryson (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Others wishing to wear/use this tartan should seek permission from Guy Bryson: [email protected]. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed by father and son, Guy and Dean Bryson for family descendants to wear. The inspiration for the design is centred around the four cherry red stripes, which represent the four children of Guy and Margie Bryson. Other colours of significance to the family are blue, grey, black and yellow which also feature in the design.

name: Basel Tattoo Choir
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for the Basel Tattoo Choir. Restricted availability, please contact Basel Tattoo/Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The Basel Tattoo Choir tartan was designed to be an additional complement to the original Basel Tattoo tartan (STR ref. 5971). The tartan will be used to make uniforms for the in-house Basel Tattoo Choir. The new pattern for the design was submitted with a brighter colour of green, with an increased amount of bright blue and a reduced amount of burgundy red. The final design has a totally different sett, colourway and threadcount.

name: Alloway Rose
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of the designer and owner, and may not be used, woven, copied, reproduced or displayed in any way without her written consent.
registrationNotes: The designer created this tartan for her business, Alloway Rose which offer unique handmade jewellery and gifts inspired by Robert Burns poetry.

name: REME Corps
registrationNotes: Designed for the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers (REME) Corps. The Corps Colours are dark blue, yellow and red, a combination of the colours taken from the existing colours of the Royal Army Ordnance Corps (RAOC), Royal Army Service Corps (RASC) and Royal Engineers (RE) respectively when the REME were first formed.

name: Williams, Robert (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For use by descendants of A S Forsythe of Oust.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Robert Williams and for the descendants of A S Forsythe, Oust near Thurso in Scotland prior to their emigration to the United States.

name: Orillia
restrictions: Yes. Lochcarron of Scotland hold exclusive production rights. Restricted with the approval by the City of Orillia.
registrationNotes: William Waddell and Chuck Penny designed this tartan for the City of Orillia, which shares its 150th Anniversary with the 150th Anniversary of Canadian Confederation and with the 40th Anniversary of the Orillia Scottish Festival. The basis of the tartan includes the official colours of the City of Orillia: blue for the lake and green for the abundant woodland. A broad yellow stripe signifies sunshine, as there is a common reference to Orillia as "The Sunshine City". The red and white bordering the yellow represent the colours of the Canadian Flag.

name: Cirrus Logic
restrictions: Yes. For the use of persons authorised by Cirrus Logic Corporation.
registrationNotes: The four colours of the tartan represent several core values of the company. Black, noted for its sturdiness, symbolises integrity, with the surrounding shades of grey representing the global teams that make up the wholeness of Cirrus Logic’s award winning corporate culture. The simplicity of ivory unifies each unique individual for a culture that rocks, and the blue represents the colour of the company logo.

name: Edinburgh Marathon Festival
restrictions: Yes. To be woven through Geoffrey (Tailor) Ltd.
registrationNotes: The sett is based on the existing Edinburgh District tartan. The colours are from the Edinburgh Marathon Festival logos and represent the Saltire blue, the white, grey and sage from heathers, and the orange for the fiery nature of the Scottish people.

name: Lareymondie (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the designer, his family and descendants based on family colours.

name: Dark Sky
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Dale Stevenson or with Dale Stevenson's permission.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Dark Sky Observatory in Dalmellington using colours that reflect the night sky.

name: Tartan Day Society of Washington State, The
registrationNotes: Designed for the Tartan Day Society of Washington State. Colours: green represents the official colour of Washington, known as the "Evergreen State"; blue represents the Pacific Ocean and Puget Sound; red, white and blue represent the colours in the United States flag.

name: Johnson, Bradley P & Gayle L (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Can only be worn with permission of the copyright holder. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven or produced in any commercial form with the express permission of the copyright holder.
registrationNotes: Based on a 1725 tartan thought to have been worn by the Campbells from an even earlier date to mark Bradley Johnson's Scottish links, this design also celebrates his Scandinavian forebears by incorporating family colours with the Norwegian, American and Scottish flags.

name: Johnson, Bradley P & Gayle L Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Use of this tartan restricted to those approved by the copyright holder. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder.
registrationNotes: A “Dress” version of the Bradley P & Gayle L Johnson (Personal) tartan.

name: Chatwin, Craig Stuart (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for Craig Stuart Chatwin. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed for Craig Stuart Chatwin and worn at his wedding to Kirsty Ann Lee on 30 September 2017. The red and yellow are taken from the Cameron of Erracht tartan worn by the father of the bride. The red parallel lines through the blue replicate the red parallel lines through the green in the Cameron of Erracht tartan. Red symbolises the link between the families resulting from the marriage with yellow depicting the joy from their union. The parallel lines symbolise the journey through life taken by the couple. White represents the traditional colour of marriage with black chosen to balance the design and reflect a gift, being based on the coal traditionally given at Hogmanay.

name: Fidgett (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created as a 50th birthday present for the designer's husband.

name: Greenwards Primary School
restrictions: Yes. For use by those who have an association with Greenwards Primary School, either past or present. The weaving of this tartans should only be carried out in the design of materials associated with the school e.g. as part of the school uniform.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to fit the corporate image of the school. It will be used as an important image to represent the school's identity and to become a feature of the school uniform. It has been designed in the school's colours with grey providing the background colour and the tartan check has been selected to go from green to gold to represent the school's reward system.

name: Goose Watch (Anser albifrons flavirostris)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or printed without the express permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: Created for an exhibition, this tartan was inspired whilst on a ‘goose walk’ organised by RSPB Loch Lomond. The source of the inspiration came from observing the white-fronted geese (Anser albifrons flavirostris) who travel from their breeding ground in Greenland to the beautiful Loch shores each winter. The colours chosen are symbolic of those of the birds to which they relate and white was given more prominence in homage to their name. The tartan will be used to celebrate the beauty of the geese and to help raise their profile as an endangered species. RSPB (Scotland) endorse the application for this design and it is envisaged that its creation will assist with the continuing efforts to conserve nature and the surrounding scenery that will protect the future survival of these striking birds.

name: Caledonian Bloom
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Highland Kilt Connections. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan evoking the colours of a floral bloom in Scotland.

name: Spirit of Speyside Whisky Festival
restrictions: Yes. May only be used by Spirit of Speyside Whisky Festival Ltd or Knockando Woolmill. May only be woven with the express permission of Spirit of Speyside Whisky Festival Ltd.
registrationNotes: Spirit of Speyside Whisky Festival collaborated with Knockando Woolmill to create a new Festival tartan. The grey base and pops of colour hint at Speyside's rich whisky history. Red represents a sherry cask finish and the golden hue represents a bourbon cask finish.

name: McSchmid
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of family members.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Laura McNaught as a wedding gift for her husband to share and celebrate her Scottish roots. The tartan name is a combination of two surnames. The predominant blue and turquoise colours are reminiscent of the beautiful sea around the island of Menorca and the flash of orange reflects the sun setting on the sea.

name: Isle of Arran Distillers Ltd, The
restrictions: Yes. Can only be worn/used/woven with the express permission of the Isle of Arran Distillers Ltd. See above No
registrationNotes: Designed in 2016 to mark the 21st anniversary of the opening of the distillery at Lochranza, the tartan's colours are influenced by the flora of the Isle of Arran. The colours also feature on the labels and packaging of the various malt whiskies distilled at Lochranza. The background colour is a muted blue with soft white, lichen green, deep wine, soft purple and copper.

name: Symbiosis
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Symbiosis Pharmaceutical Services and its employees. May not be woven without written permission of the designer or the company CEO.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for the Stirling based company Symbiosis Pharmaceutical Services using colours included in the company's artwork.

name: Fleet Air Arm
restrictions: Yes. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 11 July 2017, registration number: 6015202.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the squadrons of the Royal Navy’s Fleet Air Arm. Encompassing important colours associated with the Fleet Air Arm crest: light blue, gold, white, red, and green. Navy blue signifies the Royal Navy and black represents continual respect for the fallen. Although the term Fleet Air Arm did not actually come into being until 1924, the Admiralty was investigating kites and balloons for spotting as early as 1903, the first Naval aviator completed his flying training in 1910 and the first launch from a Royal Navy battleship was achieved by January of 1912. From those early formative years of naval aviation to current operations their naval personnel and aircraft have played a leading role. Flying from ships deployed worldwide, the aircraft of the Fleet Air Arm provide the UK with influence over land and sea, and assist in the wide range of roles undertaken by the Royal Navy from disaster relief to landing Royal Marines onto a hostile shore.

name: Single Malt Club China
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for the Single Malt Club China. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned in recognition of the Single Malt Club China’s long standing relationship with Scotland and its whisky industry. A cool colour palette of greens and blues form the base of the design and are inspired by the distinctive architectural details, found within the interior of the Single Malt Club China. The green colour also represents the natural landscape of Scotland. Purple is a noble colour in Chinese tradition and stands for authority, prestige, profound and spirit and the three formation purple overcheck that runs through the centre of the design also reflects the thistle, Scotland’s national flower.

name: Bromhead (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for Stephen Bromhead. Permission required for use - please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd/Stephen Bromhead in this regard. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan is based on a combination of the Mackintosh clan tartan and the Graham of Montrose clan tartan as the customer's mother's maiden name is Mackintosh and his wife's maiden name is Graham. The red is taken from the Mackintosh tartan and the white over-check from the Graham of Montrose tartan. The tartan is therefore relevant to the Scottish ancestry of this married couple now living in Australia.

name: Mitchell, George (Personal)
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to use, wear or weave this tartan should seek permission from the owner of the design.
registrationNotes: Based on the colours of the Scottish flag with the addition of gold and red.

name: Daugherty (2017)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the registrant's written permission.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the marriage of Jonathan Daugherty of Arkansas to Katie Lynn Fry. This tartan is available to anyone of that surname or variations thereof.

name: Mexicana
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the registrant's written permission.
registrationNotes: A design for the people of Mexico, of Mexican descent, or those associating with Mexico worldwide, based on the colours of the national flag of Mexico.

name: Hello Kitty Navy
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Sanrio Company Ltd and Hello Kitty. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland
registrationNotes: With navy representing trust, white for honesty, red for vigour and the signature Hello Kitty pink, this tartan represents the true value of Hello Kitty's character.

name: Hall, W A B (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Mr W A B Hall and his immediate family only or anyone as authorised. Prepared for weaving by the House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd as authorised by Touchdown Tartans Ltd. All enquiries must be made through Touchdown Tartans Ltd.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Walter Ambrose Brebner Hall in honour of his mother and father’s names and his given name. The colours, used in the family business, were chosen to complement each other.

name: Hardbattle, Tom (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan which represents the Hardbattle family's association with Scotland and Botswana. Colours: purple for Scotland the family's adopted home; green for new life and rebirth; gold for the sands of the Kalahari desert; blue for the sky above.

name: Morrow (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for David Morrow. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson / David Morrow regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The Morrow (2017) tartan was based on the Ayrshire district tartan due to family connections with the district. The tartan has intentionally maintained a similar design and uses colours of significance to represent the Morrow family’s heritage.

name: Hitmillgreen
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan must be sought from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan created to express the designer’s great love for Scotland. The name Hitmill is the English translation of the designer’s Dutch surname Slagmolen and the word green was added to indicate one of the main colours found in the tartan.

name: Joicey, North (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants who bear the Joicey surname.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed to honour the designer's Father, Corporal Thomas Joicey, Grandmother, Anne Egginton (Wylie-Wilkie) and Grandfather John (Jack) Egginton using colours of significance to the family.

name: Kinloch Anderson Blue Loch
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Kinloch Anderson Blue Loch tartan is an exclusive design. It is one of the Kinloch Anderson Collection of house tartans, all of which are based on the sett of the original Kinloch Anderson tartan. The colour shades include the blue and white of the Scottish saltire and other blues which reflect Scotland’s lochs and rivers, whilst the sky blue with gold over check symbolize a fine Scottish summer’s day.

name: Amway NAGC Scotland 2017
restrictions: Yes. Rights to wear and weave the tartan should be sought from Janielle Moss Meeting Planner II | North America Meetings & Events 7575 Fulton Street, E, Ada, MI 49355 [email protected]
registrationNotes: To reward their top sales performers achievements, Amway decided to create a trip to Scotland and a Corporate tartan to celebrate.

name: Mihulka (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Restricted to people who can prove they are a direct descendant of the family name Mihulka.
registrationNotes: A family tartan for Steven Mihulka which incorporates both his Scottish and Polish heritage. The design is therefore based on the Lamont tartan from his mother’s side with the addition of the red and white Polish colours to represent his father’s side of the family. Grey has been added for a modern twist along with yellow and purple in a “nod” to the Scottish Rugby team.

name: Gott Hop
registrationNotes: Designed by the founders of GOTT HOP, Luis Gustavo Gomes and José Wilker Tarradt de Araujo. The tartan being predominantly black (monochromatic), is the most classic colour used to express luxury, elegance and sophistication representing the brand true to its heritage. The monochromatic shades of black also expresses the beliefs of the founders also known as; ‘for all few’. Numerology is one of the key components responsible for the tartan’s geometry and the number 8 being an inspiration around the Gott Hop concept and vision. It is the sum of 4 strategies (unique, brewing, drinkwear and for all few who value experiences) and 4 key elements (luxury, innovation, precision and legacy). Furthermore, the tartan was designed with; 8 different lines, using 4 different colours by 2 people.

name: Prestoungrange, Baron of Lochnaw (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. See registration notes below.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Baron of Lochnaw together with Prestoungrange his heirs and successors; also a tartan for Wills & Hine family members from the Baronies of Prestoungrange and Dolphinstoun; also may with permission be worn by those presently dwelling on the former feudal lands of the Baron of Lochnaw.

name: Lenaghan (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the designer’s grandparents. It is intended for use by any of the descendants of Francis and Mary Lenaghan, both of Hilden, County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

name: Veltman-West (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the marriage of Kirstin Veltman and Dorothy West using colours of personal significance to both.

name: Malts of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Malts of Scotland. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Glasgow District tartan was used as the starting point of the design because of the connection of Malts of Scotland with the distilleries in this area. Malts of Scotland have a long standing connection to Islay, specifically with their new whisky, the Dark Side of Islay. Black and shades of grey have been used according to the Brand Identity but also because of the peat found within this area. Red is the colour of the Malts of Scotland, it represents the blood of the dragon and whisky as the life blood of Scotland.

name: Moyer, Glen (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Glen Moyer and his family. Permission may be sought, and must be obtained by contacting Glen Moyer or a direct family member. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. Only to be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed for Glen Moyer. The colours that feature in this design reflect his connections with Texas, his birthplace and his strong affiliation and ancestral link with Scotland. Using the prominent blues as found on the Texas flag, a dark navy, and the Saltire, a medium sky blue, these have been arranged with a third blue, a deep cobalt colour which is Glen's personal signature colour. The red strike through represents his Scottish genealogy through his father, by using his fathers favourite colour. The white strike though represents his connection with his mother. Both further reflect the two flags of his heritage. The specific yarn counts used in the design all hold a personal meaning.

name: Caledonian Maasai
restrictions: Yes. Please consult the designer/owner for written permission to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by Scottish and Maasai cultures.

name: Nasir, Amirali Bakirali (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the applicant and his descendants using the following colours: blue and green which represent Marylebone in London and holidays in Scotland, red represents Hong Kong, white represents the Bauhinia flower, blue-green the Pacific Ocean and yellow represents the rays of the sun.

name: Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Mr Rutherford, British Columbia, Canada and his immediate family. Permission is required from the designer and or his descendants, before anyone outside their immediate family may use this tartan.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan featuring the following colours: white and blue as a tribute to bratach na h-Alba, dark red which represents fortitude and yellow which represents constancy and faith with which family lineage has endured and prospered.

name: Obama Family
restrictions: Yes. Please consult the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: The Obama Family tartan was commissioned by the Hunter Foundation to commemorate the visit of former US President Barack Obama when he flew in to Scotland on 26 May 2017 to play golf at St Andrews. He went on to speak at a prestigious dinner in Edinburgh and was presented with a kilt and trews made by Slanj Kilts. The red, sky blue and white colours in the tartan are taken from the flag of Chicago where Mr Obama lives and works, navy blue represents the Hawaiian flag where Mr Obama was born and green represents the Kenyan flag to honour Barack Obama Senior’s family roots.

name: Blundell (2017)
registrationNotes: Designed as a tribute and as a wedding present marking the unification of two families, one from Scotland and one from England, this tartan is based around the colours of the groom’s local football team.

name: Lodge Royal Alfred 420SC
restrictions: Yes. Only members or past members of the Lodge or those authorised in writing by the Worshipful Master sitting at that time, may wear this tartan. The right to weave this tartan in any way belongs solely to the designer and his heirs and then only under written request from the Worshipful Master sitting at that time.
registrationNotes: Lodge Royal Alfred No. 420 on the roll of the Grand Lodge of Scotland, was first formed in 1862 and granted its Royal Charter by H.R.H. Prince Alfred, 3rd Duke of Edinburgh in 1870. The blue celebrates its origins as a naval Lodge, the rich burgundy and gold are the colours of the aprons worn in Lodge and the green is for the Grand Lodge of Scotland. The black is symbolic of Africa.

name: So Stobo
registrationNotes: A tartan commissioned for Stobo Castle. Colours: blue represents the sky; green represents the countryside; bright pink is one of Stobo Castle’s brand colours. It will be used to create items to sell in our Spa Shop and potentially within staff uniforms.

name: Red Thistle
registrationNotes: Designed as a tribute to The Red Thistle Dancers, a Scottish Country and Highland Dance performance group based in the San Francisco Bay Area, who take as their namesake, the California native red thistle. This tartan is based on the California State tartan, birthplace of The Red Thistle Dancers in 1973. Colours: Highland Green for the Scottish Highlands of Highland Dancing, Parchment for the Scroll of Honour awarded to the Directors of The Red Thistle Dancers by the Royal Scottish Country Dance Society. Reds and crimsons for the California red thistle native species (Cirsium occidentale and Cirsium arizonicum).

name: Clark, Robert McGavin (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. See registration notes below.
registrationNotes: Based on the basic Clark tartan, and designed for the descendants of Robert McGavin Clark (1833-1877) who emigrated in 1856 and whose descendants helped build New Zealand. The fourth white stripe of the basic Clark tartan has been replaced with green, symbolising the verdant nature of New Zealand. Inside this band are two threads of black, honouring those in the family who passed before their time, many owing to the harsh conditions of their new home. This black stripe notably commemorates the premature passing of William Robert Clark (1859-1921), as well as his grandson Robert Alexander Clark (1950-2016) and his wife Kyra Alicesandy Ward (1963-2007). Each of the two black bands of the basic Clark tartan have been inlaid with two threads of red, in honour of two members of the family who passed away outside New Zealand. Robert McGavin Clark the elder, who returned to Edinburgh in 1877 to pay visit to his mother Margaret Clark née McGavin, and who died shortly thereafter while with her. And his grandson, Robert McGavin Clark the younger (1895-1917) who died in battle in Belgium during the Great War.

name: Maison de Moggy
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of Maison De Moggy Ltd. Please contact Maison De Moggy Ltd directly to enquire about its use on a permission basis. This tartan must be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: Maison de Moggy was one of the first cat cafés in Scotland, with its first premises in the country's capital Edinburgh. This design reflects the companies strong sense of pride in its Scottish place of origin. Using distinct brand colours the tartan sett detail has embedded details about its founding year, the company's unique assets and its founding location in the heart of Edinburgh.

name: College of Dental Surgeons of Alberta
restrictions: Yes. 'For the exclusive use of the College of Dental Surgeons of Alberta and its members. 'This design may be reproduced only with the permission of either the College of Dental Surgeons of Alberta or the designer, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: 'This tartan is intended for the use of the College of Dental Surgeons of Alberta (CDSA) and its members. The design features Alberta's provincial colours of deep blue for the lakes, gold for sunshine along with the colours of the CDSA; leaf green, sky blue and white. A black background is provided for contrast allowing this design to be worn at both formal and informal occasions.

name: Walter Marchbank Haulage 75
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use by the Company Directors, Marchbank Family and others as authorised by them. All enquiries must be made through Touchdown Tartans Ltd. Prepared for weaving by the House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd as authorised by Touchdown Tartans Ltd. All enquiries must be made through Touchdown Tartans Ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan commissioned by the Company Directors to celebrate 75 years in the Haulage Industry in 2017. The colours used represent the traditional livery used on the Walter Marchbank Haulage Trucks.

name: Kim-Dean (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the new family name Kim-Dean.

name: North Woods Rovers
restrictions: Yes. Can only be worn by or woven for members of the North Woods Rover crew and decendants upon becoming Rovers Knights.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the North Woods Rovers scouts. Colours: red and white represent the legend and flag of St George, the patron saint of all scouts; blue is taken from the US flag; green represents the forests surrounding the North Woods Rovers and grey represents the sword, knighthood and the vow to follow chivalrous ways and the scout law.

name: Dartmouth, City of Lakes
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with written permission from Deana Lloy, Red Label Kilts.
registrationNotes: Dartmouth consists of 23 beautiful lakes and is world known for its rich history of paddling and rowing. Colours: yellow represents 3 rowing clubs on Lake Banook; red is for red clay identifies the rich history of the Shubanacadie Canal and the 3 main lakes it feeds into; blue represents the harbour which separates the two adjoining cities; grey represents the tragedy of the Halifax explosion in 1917, lives lost, people injured and thousands left homeless on that grey day in history, the Starr Manufacturing Company known for its production of metal ice skates and also identifies the oil stacks of Woodside where the flame no longer burns.

name: Dinwiddie, Alistair John (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Alistair Dinwiddie, his family, relations and decendants. Permission may be sought by contacting Alistair Dinwiddie or other direct family member. Only to be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan designed to give an identity to the family's long roots and traditions both in south west Scotland and in many other parts of the world. Colours; green represents the family's farming origins in Dumfriesshire, light blue for the many ministers and connections in the Church of Scotland and red represents the African flame tree or the Pohutukawa tree in New Zealand, symbolising the vitality and strength of the family and its members across the world.

name: Rocky Mountaineer
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for the Great Canadian Railtour Co. Ltd. (Rocky Mountaineer). Restricted availability. Please contact Rocky Mountaineer regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Rocky Mountaineer.
registrationNotes: The Rocky Mountaineer is the largest, privately owned rail company in the world. It operates out of Vancouver taking global travellers throughout the majestic Rocky Mountains of western Canada.

name: Sorel-Tracy
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Atelier de Tissage Sorel-Tracy.
registrationNotes: Designed by Anne Bérard, Micheline Gauthier, Pascale Leclerc and Gislaine Massé of the Weaving workshop Sorel-Tracy within the context of the celebrations of the 375th anniversary of Sorel-Tracy, located at the confluent of the St. Lawrence and Richelieu rivers. The tartan is inspired by the history and the heritage of Sorel-Tracy an industrial capital town of steel. Colours: red and yellow represent fire, an essential component of metallurgical industry; blue represents water, the source of life. The city is laid out in the form of a quadrilateral surrounding the City Centre, the Carré Royal or Royal Square. The streets aligned North-South and East-West are set at right angles forming uniform batches and offer single aspects. The geometrical typical aspect of Old Sorel is used as the basic pattern for this tartan.

name: WooHa Brewing Company
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of WooHa Brewing Company Ltd. Permission to wear and use must be granted by WooHa Brewing Company at all times. This tartan is to be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: The WooHa Brewing Company is a Highland based bottle and KeyKeg conditioned craft beer manufacturer. To celebrate its Scottish origin this tartan has been specifically designed to capture the strong and striking brand colours of the company. Each yarn count and colour choice represents key elements of the company story.

name: Heineken
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Heineken. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson /Heineken regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Heineken tartan was based on The McEwan '1856' (STR ref 2880) tartan, as this relates to the acquisition of the brand from Scottish & Newcastle in 2007/08. Scottish & Newcastle Brewers resulted from the merger of William Younger and Co and McEwan's in 1931. The colours of the tartan are taken from the Heineken corporate colours of green, red, gold and black.

name: Powell-Wicks (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designers, however they wish the tartan to be available for others to use.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed by Bub Powell and Jeff Wicks to celebrate their love for each other using colours of significance to both.

name: Shark & Turtle Pub, The
restrictions: Yes. Copyright: Robert Byres, [email protected].
registrationNotes: The Shark and Turtle Pub is a bar in a private home where friends can relax and enjoy a bit of camaraderie. Colours: green represents turtles, grey represents sharks, blue represents the ocean; gold and black represent the United States Military Academy.

name: Volcano
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn /woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the volcanoes of Iceland. The island owes its very existence to its location on a mid-oceanic hot spot where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Volcanism is woven into,the mythology, history and everyday life of the Icelandic people.

name: Aurora Borealis
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: The dance of lights in the Aurora Borealis inspired this design.

name: Rift
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn /woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the Silfra Fissure in the Thingvellir Valley, Iceland. This rift was formed by the divergent tectonic drift of the Eurasian and North American continental plates and it contains exceptionally clear, cold and potable water. When snorkelling or diving, the landscape displays brilliant green and gold colours.

name: Atlantic Puffin
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the Atlantic puffin, a small and colourful bird sometimes known as the "clown of the sea", found along the coastlines of the North Atlantic Ocean. Iceland has the largest puffin population in the world.

name: Icelandic Lupines
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the fields of Lupines found in Iceland, where they were introduced in 1945 to combat topsoil loss. These somewhat aggressive plants display beautiful blue white and purple blooms.

name: Mountain Avens
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the National Flower of Iceland. Mountain Avens are small evergreen plants with creamy white flowers and they form large colonies on rocky slopes and moorland all over Iceland.

name: Icelandic Countryside
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: The colours and textures of the Icelandic countryside inspired this design.

name: Lagoon
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the "Blue Lagoon", a geothermal spa in Iceland. The colours represent the milky blue of the mineral-rich water, the black of the surrounding volcanic rocks, and the skin colours of the many people who visit to bathe there.

name: Gyrfalcon
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design represents the Gyrfalcon, the national bird of Iceland. It is the largest and most powerful falcon in the world and its plumage varies from white to grey to almost black. Gyrfalcons were worshipped by the Vikings and highly sought after by European kings and members of the aristocracy.

name: Orr (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed using colours of significance to the designer and his family.

name: Black and Lizars
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Black and Lizars Ltd. The tartan may only be woven or reproduced in print, digital media or any other format when in receipt of written consent from Black and Lizars Ltd IPR application 6014689 being processed
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed for Black and Lizars Ltd, a company that was established back in 1830 when John Lizars, at the age of 20, opened his first optical practice in Glasgow's Merchant City. Since then, Black and Lizars has become one of Scotland's largest independently owned optometrists with over 185 years' experience in delivering outstanding eye care. The tartan colours of Black and Deep Red represent the founders of the company (Messrs Black and Lizars), the dark grey is a solid and stable colour that embodies the company's heritage and long standing while the bright red signifies the company's pioneering spirit.

name: Blackwood
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for Blackwood, a maker of fine clocks and jewellery. The colours reflect the company logo - the raven and thistle, the name Blackwood and Scotland's unique landscape. The tartan will be used for kilts, and also for lining various items, for example the inside of cases holding products.

name: Cateran, The
restrictions: Yes. Designed as a marketing and promotional tool for Cateran Country in Perthshire. Please contact the designer to weave this tartan which should only be woven with the intention of using it within its context.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed as a marketing and promotional tool for Cateran Country in Perthshire. The Cateran Trail is a 64-mile circular trail that runs through Perthshire and the surrounding areas in Scotland and follows the traditional drove roads. The name Cateran is derived from the Caterans, cattle thieves who raided throughout the areas from Glenshee to Glen Isla, from the Middle ages to the 17th Century. The design and colours represent the plants and natural colours found within and reflect the history, culture and heritage of these areas, from whisky to wildlife and from glens to gorse.

name: Pride of LGBT
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holders. Contact - John Webster, John Morison Kiltmakers & Weavers, 63 High St., Edinburgh, EH1 1SR 0131 556 0666 [email protected]
registrationNotes: A watershed for the modern LGBT movement arose from a series of protests in New York in 1969 and to pay homage to all those involved, this tartan is based on the New York City tartan and incorporates the variety of bright colours used to identify that movement around the world.

name: Experience Scotland
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Experience Scotland. Permission to weave this tartan should be sought from Experience Scotland and Tartan Weaving Mill. Copyright: Tartan Weaving Mill.
registrationNotes: Created by Yves Lemarchand for the 25th anniversary of Experience Scotland, a company based in Penicuik, Scotland, specialising in events management since 1992.

name: Courteboeuf, Henri (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants. Others with the same name/names should seek his permission to wear/use/weave this tartan..
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for Henri Courteboeuf, his family and descendants using colours of significance to each family member.

name: Saudi Royal Terminals
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for IDesign based in London and Riyadh. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: This tartan is based on the sett of the Royal Stewart tartan, which is associated with the British Royal Family; there has been a long tradition of visits and exchanges between the Royal Families of the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia. Colours: brown and marble grey symbolise the desert sand of Saudi Arabia; royal blue emphasises the royal connection and green represents the national flag. The tartan will be used for interior decoration in Saudi Royal airport terminals.

name: Hick P & D (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Paula and Dave Hick.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed by Paula and Dave Hick to celebrate their love for each other using colours based on their experience wild camping in the Cairngorms.

name: Harmon, David R (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Use and wearing is restricted to the five USA families of Harmon, Potter, Waters, Knowles and Adams, and bloodlines with proof showing direct ties to any of these. Prepared for weaving by DC Dalgliesh, or if said mill is no longer established, by a Scottish weaver. Individuals not family members who have permission along with their spouses only are: Albert Hassinger, Richard Perdue and Ray Madrid. Others must obtain written permission from David Raymond Harmon or his representative upon death.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for the designer, his immediate family and descendants and for the five USA families of Harmon, Potter, Waters, Knowles and Adams which joined together to form his family. The tartan commemorates family heritage from Scotland, Ireland and Wales, the bonds shared and struggles endured to ensure a new life in the New World. It represents ties to those who came before and those who have yet to come.

name: Shevchenko, Denis (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed by Denis Shevchenko intended for members of the Shevchenko family, immediate relatives of the designer.

name: Shirley (2017)
registrationNotes: The designer used the Cameron of Erracht tartan, a tartan local to the area where he grew up near Roy Bridge in the Scottish Highlands, as a template for this tartan. The blues, black and white used in this new design are representative of the designer’s family bicycle racing team (the Glencroft Rabble) colours. The yellow represents success as well as helping to mirror Shirley family colours of blue and yellow.

name: Harley (2017)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan uses colours of significance to the designer and his family. A red line through the field of dark blue represents family roots in Canada and the blood line from Scotland; dark green represents the marriage(s) that brought together this family; thus yellow lines through the field of green represent the continuation of the family bloodline to the children and their dual citizenship; black commemorates past family members.

name: Highland Belle
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed for use by Yvonne Macrae, a couture dressmaker who lives, works and draws her inspiration from the Scottish Highlands to make made to measure bespoke ladies outfits and accessories.

name: Memories of Lille
registrationNotes: This tartan is an homage to Lille, the historic capital of Flanders, a city dear to the designer. It is inspired by the city’s emblem, a red and white fleur de lys, and the black and yellow colours in the flag of Flanders.

name: AMHT
restrictions: Yes. No-one other than those who have been sold material bearing this Tartan by the Aston Martin Heritage Trust may wear/use this Tartan. No-one other than those who have been given permission to weave this Tartan by the Aston Martin Heritage Trust may weave this Tartan. No-one other than those granted permission by the Aston Martin Heritage Trust may otherwise weave, wear or use this Tartan.
registrationNotes: The official tartan for Aston Martin Heritage Trust (AMHT) using Trust colours. The tartan is intended for AMHT merchandise and items.

name: Achadh na Cloiche
restrictions: Yes. Please consult the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by a house on the Gareloch owned by the designer’s parents. The three grey colours in the design reflect the name Achadh na Cloiche (Field of Stones).

name: Chandolin

registrationNotes: Lambert Zufferey offered this tartan to the Bourgeoisie de Chandolin (highest habited village in Europe from which he come from) to mark his participation in the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo 2017.

name: Kraków, City of
registrationNotes: Of 26 entries submitted by citizens of Edinburgh in a competition to design a tartan for Kraków, the winning design by Alex Imrie was voted for by the citizens of Krakow from a shortlist of 5 finalists. The competition was co-organised by partner cities Kraków and Edinburgh with the support of the Scottish-Polish Cultural Association and the Consulate of the Republic of Poland in Edinburgh. The winning design is presented to the Mayor of Kraków Jacek Majchrowski in September 2017, and evokes the city and spirit of Kraków and its enduring friendship with Edinburgh and Scotland.

name: Svedin, Martin (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Martin Svedin and his family.
registrationNotes: A gift from the designer to celebrate the 40th Birthday of Martin Svedin who has for many years been a proud supporter of Scottish produce within Sweden.

name: GREAT Campaign
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for GREAT Britain Campaign. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to support and enhance the GREAT Campaign. This is the Government’s International Marketing Campaign to showcase the very best of what Britain has to offer in business, tourism and education. The colours of the tartan reflect the Union Jack, the British flag, and also relate to the Brand image which has been created for this Campaign led by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office. The sett is based on the Royal Stewart tartan making a connection with the British Royal Family. The design also reflects aspects of the Royal Warrant Holders Association tartan which was designed by Kinloch Anderson in 1994.

name: Off Kilter Kilts
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan designed for the customers of "Off Kilter Kilts"

name: Isle of Gometra
restrictions: Yes. For use by family members of the designer, those with family connections with the Isle of Gometra and friends of the Isle of Gometra. Weaving must be authorised by the designer. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Gometra, the second largest and second most populous island in the Staffa Archipelago. It lies in Loch Staffa within the Loch Na Keal National Scenic Area near Staffa, the Treshnish Isles and Iona.

name: Arctic Fox
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan represents the changing colour phases of the thick fur coat of the Arctic fox, which are shades of brown in summer and white and bluish-grey in winter. Their eyes are often a deep golden yellow. The Arctic fox is native to Arctic regions of the Northern Hemisphere and is the only land mammal native to Iceland.

name: RAF 100
restrictions: Yes. Weaving is restricted to only those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. May only be used by Tartan Manor Ltd to produce various items, garments, clothing etc, all manner of products, for retail. No other person or company will have that right. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 August 2017, registration number: 6017029.
registrationNotes: The RAF 100 tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Royal Air Force since its formation in 1918. The design encompasses significant colours associated with the Royal Air Force: burgundy, dark blue, light blue, white, grey, and black. Burgundy, dark blue and light blue represent the colours of the RAF Stable Belt; grey represents the incredible RAF aircraft; white symbolises the impressive jet trails expelled from their mighty engines across the skies; black is for the continual respect for all fallen RAF comrades. RAF 100 is about celebrating the proud history of the RAF since 1918, and it is also about reaching out to a new generation, to inspire the next one hundred years of innovation.

name: Parker (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the wedding of Simon and Sarah in September 2018 in Inverness, Scotland. Colours: black is taken from the Black Watch tartan a tribute to a great Scottish Infantry battalion; grey is for conservative and sophisticated; purple is for wealth and ambition; white is for purity and perfection. it may be worn by anyone sharing the Parker surname.

name: People's Friend
restrictions: Yes. Wear and use must be authorised by the copyright holders, D C Thomson Ltd. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holders D C Thomson Ltd..
registrationNotes: Based on the Royal Stewart, this tartan encapsulates some of the symbols and sentiments that have kept The People's Friend a welcome visitor in so many homes around the world for almost 150 years. The bright red and white band represents the magazine's masthead whilst the adjoining grey celebrates Dundee - its city of origin on the northern bank of the ‘Silvery Tay’. The light blue and yellow are delicate pastels always seen in the historic cover illustrations of J Campbell Kerr and yellow, of course, is also the colour of friendship. The five pink lines on blue are for the five continents where your People's Friend is read each week and the sixteen tiny squares formed by them, mark the number of pages in the very first issue of the Friend back in 1869. Finally, the Royal Stewart symbolises the love and respect which Friend readers have so often extended towards our Royal Family.

name: Highland Lavender
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from Highland Lavender Farm, VA.
registrationNotes: A bespoke tartan for a small lavender farm and to celebrate its location on the blue ridge mountains as well as the designer’s Scottish heritage. These colours were chosen because they mimic the colours of the lavender plants themselves: the grey and green of the stem and leaves, the purple and white of the flowers.

name: Littlejohn (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Please notify the designer to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: Created to be worn at the designer’s wedding, this tartan uses colours of significance to his family.

name: Willien, David, Baron of Tulloch (Personal)

registrationNotes: The design is based on both the Davidson of Tulloch and the MacKay tartans of the 19th century with a central band of blue, white and red, representing the French Tricolour.

name: Symons

registrationNotes: This tartan has been created as part of The White Company's XM17 'Highland' Daywear collection. The colours used for the tartan are iconic for The White Company, neutrals and shades of white. The Tartan will be made into a 100% Merino Wool scarf which will be made in Scotland through the company's long standing partnership with Johnstons of Elgin.

name: Olann Aon Takihyo
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from the copyright holder.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Takihyo Company Ltd of Japan in partnership with House of Tartan Limited of Scotland. It is the first in a collection of contemporary tartans based on the traditional and classic. The tartan draws its name from the ancient Gaelic term for 'hair of sheep'; wool being the foundation of Scotland's renowned tartan industry.

name: Olann Dhà Takihyo

It is the second in a collection of contemporary tartans based on the traditional and classic. The tartan draws its name from the ancient Gaelic term for 'hair of sheep'; wool being the foundation of Scotland's renowned tartan industry.

name: Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is restricted for wear/use by Mr Rutherford, his immediate family and descendants. Permission to weave must be confirmed by the designer or his descendants before it may be woven.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan (Personal) (STR ref 11838) family tartan.

name: Axenoff (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the Axenoff family using black and gold which are the colours of the Axenoff Jewellery brand and incorporating the white, blue and red of the Russian national flag.

name: Valley Goon
restrictions: Yes. Permission to use, wear, weave this tartan must be granted from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan based on the applicant's ancestors, the Camerons using colours of significance to the group for whom the tartan was created.

name: David Philp Commercials
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Touchdown Tartans Ltd on behalf of the Directors of David Philp Commercials Ltd. For use by the Company Directors and as authorised by them. Prepared for weaving by the House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd as authorised by Touchdown Tartans Ltd. All enquiries must be made through Touchdown Tartans Ltd.
registrationNotes: David Philp Commercials (DPC) Ltd was established in the 1970s by David Philp Senior and the tartan was commissioned by David Philp Junior to represent the colours of the DPC Fleet.

name: Overgate
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Overgate Shopping Centre, Dundee.
registrationNotes: As part of their 2017 marketing strategy, Overgate Shopping Centre Dundee wanted to design their own brand of tartan to create a fresh visual appeal as well as adding a touch of Scottishness to a well-known shopping centre. The colours within the tartan design were selected by Overgate’s marketing team and are colours that are already present in there modern and fresh marketing brand. The design has been kept simple and fresh with varying widths of colour as used in the brand's logo.

name: Jute, Jam & Journalism
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the jute marketing campaign.
registrationNotes: warpweftweave studio was commissioned by Overgate Shopping Centre to design a unique tartan as a commemorative tribute to the once famous Dundee Juteopolis, as part of a yearlong marketing campaign. The tartan is to be woven entirely out of jute with various colours throughout to represent the three Js of Dundee; Jute, Jam and Journalism. Natural jute, the main colour of the design represents the jute industry of Dundee and secondary colours of orange, red, black and grey represent jam, marmalade and the newsprint of journalism respectively.

name: Charnley, William Francis (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for William Francis Charnley. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The Charnley, William Francis tartan is based on the sett of the Clan Douglas tartan due to shooting expeditions for many years with the Earl of Morton, who gave him some Clan Douglas (Ancient) tartan fabric to make trousers and a kilt, now proudly worn. His interest in fishing, shooting and stalking takes place in Inverness-shire and is reflected by the dark blue base of the tartan and the green overchecks. The colour black has been chosen because he likes wearing a black tie at formal events and particularly for his Pingus Dining Club. 3 gold lines have been included in the design because he was Master of the Drapers Company during 2016 – 2017 and the Drapers Company shield has 3 gold sunbeams. In addition, he has 3 gold bunches of grapes on his personal arms granted by the College of Arms.

name: Spirit of Northern France
restrictions: Yes. Please seek the designer's permission to wear/use/weave this tartan
registrationNotes: Designed as a tribute to the three ancient French provinces of northen France: Flandres, Hainaut and Artois, now in the modern department of Les Hauts-de France.

name: Arctic Tundra
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: The colours in this design represent the surprising number of flowering plants that grow low to the ground in the harsh climate of the Arctic Tundra of Alaska, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Scandinavia and Russia.

name: Reykjavík Reflections
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the pond in central Reykjavík which is surrounded by many notable buildings and beautiful homes and is frequented by people of all ages and numerous species of water birds. The designer was fortunate to be able to visit this lovely lake during the 22nd festival of “Culture Night” on August 19, 2017 and participate in the Reykjavík Marathon. The day was sunny with a clear blue sky and the reflections in the water were colourful. The evening concluded with an amazing display of fireworks at the Old Harbour.

name: Westfield State University - Westfield MA
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with the authorisation of Westfield State University.
registrationNotes: In 2019, the community of Westfield MA will celebrate 350 years since its founding; this tartan, designed by Gordon Kirkbright and Gerald Healy, symbolises the colours of the University and other educational establishments of the community.

name: Résilience Enfance
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan must be sought from the registrant.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the French Bikers Society, Résilience Enfance, formed to fight child abuse.

name: University of the West of Scotland
designer: University of the West of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the University of the West of Scotland. Weaving must be authorised by the University of the West of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The tartan incorporates colours drawn from elements used within the original Paisley University and College’s arms which were combined together to create the University of the West of Scotland during 2007. The Lord Lyon of Scotland, the heraldic authority for Scotland, devised the new Coat of Arms for the University of the West of Scotland drawing references from the former institutions together with new elements representing the University’s presence in Dumfries, the wider UK and global outlook. The Lord Lyon King of Arms, presented the University of the West of Scotland with the new Coat of Arms on the 10th May 2017.

name: UK Fire and Rescue Service
restrictions: Yes. May only be used by Tartan Manor Ltd to produce various items, garments, clothing etc, all manner of products, for retail. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to only those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 30 September 2017, registration number: 6019527.
registrationNotes: Approved and supported by the UK Fire and Rescue Service, the UK Fire and Rescue Service Tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the UK Fire and Rescue Service. Significant colours associated with the UK Fire and Rescue Service are: navy blue for the Fire Service uniform; red and yellow for the perilous fires that fire fighters battle against; grey for smoke; pale blue for the essential element of water used to save lives and properties; black for charcoal and also respect for fallen comrades.

name: Paisley Buddies
restrictions: Yes. Anyone is welcome to wear this tartan. If the tartan is to be used in any other way, please contact: [email protected] to discuss requirements. Please contact: [email protected] to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: Paisley, a one-time global textile hub, birthplace of the Paisley Pattern, and historical home of world-class weaving and thread-making industries. Now, the home of a vibrant, thriving cultural scene, making an impression on the world once again. This tartan commemorates Paisley’s ambitions to be UK City of Culture 2021. Designed by Ken MacDonald of Houston Kiltmakers, in collaboration with designers Gail McMillan and Sarah Hill of Renfrewshire Council, the Buddies of Paisley tartan is a contemporary celebration of the town’s textile history in the vibrant colours of the Paisley 2021 campaign branding.

name: Private Concierge Scotland, The
restrictions: Yes. This design is for the exclusive use of Private Concierge Scotland Ltd. Only with express permission from the company can this tartan be worn or used. This tartan must be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Private Concierge Scotland was founded on the 19th August 2016 in the Scottish capital, Edinburgh. The business prides itself on a 24/7 Scottish wide personal service, where attention to every thread of detail is their priority. The official corporate tartan design embodies all that the company stands for. Using the corporate colours the design sett has been carefully constructed to reflect the founding year, the length, breadth and height of Scotland.

name: Persevere Flint Grey
registrationNotes: Eagle & Fox was established in Leith and pulls 'Persevere' from the Leith coat of arms. Flint (the purple stone) refers to the accent colour found in the tartan and grey describes the main colourway of the tartan.

name: Fukae (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Fukae family KaMon, with elements of their Japanese and German heritage in the colours of the design.

name: Hanami
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 30 September 2017, registration number: 6019526.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate Hanami (blossom-viewing), a centuries-old Japanese tradition of welcoming the Spring. Hanami is the witnessing and adoration of the natural beauty of cherry blossom trees as they explode into bloom. The shades of pink, cerise and white of this Tartan pay tribute to the beautiful delicate petals on display. The leafy green colour represents the lush sepal and leaves. The pale yellow reflects the pollen coated stamen, and brown signifies the elegant branches and the sturdy tree trunk. Hanami has a brief blooming season, often seen as a metaphor for the ephemeral beauty of living. The love of cherry blossom runs deep in Japan, not only for its beauty, but also as an enduring expression of life, death and renewal.

name: Roach, John (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and his family.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer and his family, drawing on their Irish and Ukrainian heritage.

name: Colomines, Nicolas Dress (Personal)
