registrationNotes: A variation on the Nicolas Colomines (Personal) (STR ref. 4592) tartan.

name: Chalo Saint Mard
registrationNotes: As a genealogist, the designer wanted to create a Chalo Saint Mard descendants' family association for male and female lines of the family and a specific and complementary tartan for family members.

registrationNotes: A tartan designed using colours of significance to the designer's family.

name: Nicolau (2017)
registrationNotes: Designed to be woven into kilts and worn by the designer and his immediate family. The colours were chosen for symbolic reasons as well as being the favourite colours of family members. The threadcount uses numbers representing significant life events.

name: Engelhardt (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Any enquiries regarding the wearing, use or weaving of this tartan must go through Felix Georg Engelhardt or his family.
registrationNotes: The tartan colours characterise important locations for the family and are therefore especially apt as an emotional reference point conveying a sense of home. In addition to family colours, the geographic locations of Saxony, Leipzig, Zurich, Nova Scotia, Scotland, Canada and Switzerland are all represented in the colour pallet chosen by the designer.

name: Moriarty (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn/used by those directly related to the Moriarty family. Only to be woven with the designer's permission.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Richard Laurence Moriarty for the use of the family.

name: Hauser (2017)
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the Hauser family of Salzburg, Austria to reflect their close ties to Scotland. The colours, mainly blue, represent the water of the river in Salzburg, rainfall, cool weather and the Scottish Saltire.

name: Travelling the Road
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan must be sought from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for people travelling and moving about on the roads. Colours: black represents tarmac; the yellow stripes represent double yellow lines, likewise the red ones; the white lines represent the lines in the centre of the road and the green line represents verges and lay-bys.

name: Essence of Harris
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Essence of Harris. All enquiries seeking permission for use must be made direct to the company. This design must only be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: A tartan design created for the Isle of Harris company, Essence of Harris. This design has been inspired by the contrasting grey rocky landscape and idyllic blue waters that surround it. Using thread counts that reflect the year the company was founded and its GPS location, the design tells the story of the Essence of Harris.

name: Aaltonen, Roope (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Roope Aaltonen and his descendants (in current and all future generations) and immediate family (spouse, parents, siblings), and anyone else expressly authorised by Roope Aaltonen.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the use of Roope Aaltonen, his family and descendants.

name: Ward, Craig, Baron of Lundie (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is not to be offered for sale or woven unless authorised by Craig Ward, Baron of Lundie.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Craig Ward, Baron of Lundie to celebrate over 600 years since the Barony of Lundie was created.

restrictions: Yes. This tartan can only be used or worn with the express permission of the family of Detective Steven McDonald. This tartan must be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan for Detective Steven McDonald has been designed in his memory. The colours and thread counts specific to this design relate to his date of birth, his badge number whilst serving in the NYPD and his Irish-Scot descent.

name: Lantz, Teemu (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and descendants. Permission to weave this tartan should be sought from the designer, his family and descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer, his family and descendants.

name: Tsukuba Shuei
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Tsukuba Shuei School. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This private school is located in the cosmopolitan city of Tsukuba and is surrounded by the beauty of nature. The tartan has been created to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the school's establishment. Green represents the school colour, and the school's values of creation, independence and humanity are represented by navy, red and yellow.

name: Hedelius (2017)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of male members of the Hedelius family and/or their spouses.
registrationNotes: The purpose of this tartan is to create a bond with, and support for the Hedelius family’s interest in the centuries old conviction of an historical linguistic bond between the languages spoken in Scotland and the Nordic countries. This connection was hailed by the family’s ancestor, the Professor of Linguistics and Bishop Esaias Tegnér (1782-1846), who manifested in his greatest poetic achievement, set in northern Scotland, the much-translated Frithiofs saga (1825), based on an old Icelandic 8th Century saga celebrating the heroic Viking heritage of Frithjof, his life in Orkney and the Nordic countries, with lyric, dramatic and epic elements.

name: Takimoto Schools
restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn or used with the permission of D C Dalgliesh. Prepared for weaving by D C Dalgliesh.
registrationNotes: A tartan produced for school uniforms by Takimoto.

name: Slominski (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created as a gift with the tartan certificate presented to the hotel owner at the launch party of their first Scottish hotel. The tartan has been created to represent the partnership between Redefine/BDL Hotels and the hotel owner, the Slominski family. Red is used to represent the Polish flag; blue from the Scottish flag and white which is found in both. Yellow and emerald green are used to represent the brand colours of the hotel opening.

name: Little Frogs
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Little Frogs community. Weaving only through Little Frogs representatives.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Little Frogs, bilingual (French/English) daycare centres around Paris promoting early bilingualism. The colours are based on the company logo as well as the French and British flags.

name: Lemoine (2017)
restrictions: Yes. May not be worn/ used/ woven/ offered for sale without the express permission of the designer who is also the copyright holder. Weaving preferably undertaken in Scotland with 100% Scottish wool. Please contact the designer regarding use.
registrationNotes: Of French origin, the Lemoine family has been established in Scotland since the 19th century in Glasgow, Renfrewshire, Lanarkshire and Midlothian. This tartan is for the designer, Dimitri Lemoine, Christiane Lemoine-Vultaggio and their descendants using colours of significance to the family which also acknowledge the family’s Franco-Scottish roots.

name: Sacred Heart University
restrictions: Yes. The Sacred Heart University Tartan may not be reproduced in any form without permission from Sacred Heart University licensing. The design right for the Sacred Heart University Tartan is held by Sacred Heart University under the U.S. Copyright Act- 17 U.C. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Sacred Heart University, located in Connecticut, USA and founded in 1963 in the spirit of the Second Vatican Council by the Most Rev. Walter W. Curtis, Sacrae Theologiae Doctor. Central to the design, as it is to the university, is a cross which is comprised of sets of three lines representing the Holy Trinity with each of the three lines woven from six threads, an homage to 1963, the year of our founding. The primary colour of red represents the Sacred Heart of Jesus, which is the common thread that connects all we do and defines the institution, with grey and white as the secondary and tertiary colours.

name: Quinnipiac University
restrictions: Yes. The Quinnipiac University Tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from: Office of Brand Strategy and Integrated Communications Quinnipiac University [email protected] The tartan can only be produced under licence. The design right for the Quinnipiac University Tartan is held by Quinnipiac University under the U.S. Copyright Act- 17 U.S.C.
registrationNotes: Located in Connecticut, USA, Quinnipiac University is a private, co-educational, non-sectarian institution that was founded in 1924. In the spring of 2017, Quinnipiac University's Office of Brand Strategy and Integrated Communications created the official Quinnipiac University Tartan. The design features the three official university colours: Quinnipiac navy, York Hill sky blue and bobcat gold, as well as a touch of grey. The tartan is part of the broader University brand identity design and will be used on a variety of products including ties, scarves, flags, blankets, umbrellas and other merchandise.

name: University of the Incarnate Word
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from the University of the Incarnate Word, 4301 Broadway CPO - 357, San Antonio, TX 78209. The design right for the University of the Incarnate Word Tartan is held by the University of the Incarnate Word under the U.S. Copyright Act - 17 U.S.C. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: In 1869, San Antonio, Texas, suffered a cholera outbreak. In response to San Antonio's need for assistance, The Catholic Bishop of Texas, Claude M. Dubuis sent three French nuns, Sister Madeleine Chollet, Sister Pierre Cinquin, and Sister Agnes Buisson. They set up San Antonio's first hospital which is now called Santa Rosa. The building of the hospital led to an orphanage, which led to establishing a school in 1893. That school would later become what is now the University of the Incarnate Word (UIW) founded in 1996. The tartan depicts the UIW colors of red and black and its creation was a project of the UIW Fashion Design Program. The three white lines interwoven into the pattern, represents the three sisters who in 1869 founded the congregation of the Sisters of Charity of the Incarnate Word which still sponsors UIW today.

name: Moralez II, Joe F (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for Joe F Moralez for the sole use of his family. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: The Joe F Moralez II tartan is based on the sett of the “Edinburgh, City of” tartan (SRT ref 1086) to reflect great affection for the City. The navy blue and gold colours are taken from the badges of rank on naval Officers’ and Non-Commissioned Officers’ uniforms and represent the extensive family history of military service. The green and white threads reflect the family’s view that they are symbolic of hope, the desire to improve oneself and a search for knowledge. The black adds a degree of formality to the design. The tartan has been commissioned to honour the family members and to recall with pride their ancestors.

name: Arnot (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Arnot(t) family, recorded in Scotland since the 12th century. The design was inspired by family colours of red, white and black; purple and green for heather and brown for earth.

name: Van Cleemput, Marcel (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Marcel Van Cleemput and his family.
registrationNotes: Designed by Van Cleemput Marcel for his family, using the colours of local stones, brickwork, woods and former coal mines.

name: Toga Heritage
restrictions: Yes. This Tartan is intended to be worn and used by the company Toga Heritage and by its customers. No other use unless authorised by the company. To be woven only by the company Toga Heritage and its approved manufactureers.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Deborah DePasquale, Founder/Owner of Toga Heritage, a lifestyle company and purveyor of fine goods. The Tartan is intended to celebrate and honour the spirit and heritage of the City of Saratoga Springs, New York. It was designed using the company's brand guidlelines and colours reminiscent of the "Spa City".

name: Year of the Rat, The
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in graphic form without the express permission of the copyright holders - the Gold Brothers Ltd.
registrationNotes: The first of a series of 12 Chinese Zodiac tartans from the Gold Brothers Ltd, using the traditional colours and numbers associated with each.

name: M-Int Kobe
restrictions: Yes. Can only be used by those authorised by the copyright holders. Not to be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in graphic form without the express permission of the copyright holders the Kobe Shimbun Group.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by the Japanese company Kobe Shimbun Co Ltd of Kobe, the capital city of Hyogo Prefecture in Osako Bay on the main island of Honshu. The ‘new and fresh’ mint green is often associated with the younger generation and is the colour of the landmark Mint Kobe building in downtown Kobe City, rebuilt after the Great Hanshin earthquake of 1995. The Kobe Shimbun is a daily newspaper with its roots going back to 1898 and the black, white, beige and dark brown, anchor the design to the publication’s traditional newsprint origins of trees, paper and ink. The dark brown also symbolises the surrounding, heavily wooded Mount Kobo, a popular tourist area and symbol of the city of Kobe. Above all, this unusual asymmetric design, marries the company's long history and its role in today's Japan of exploring new ways of serving the public with its arts and cultural projects.

name: Club Kilt du Pays de Lorient
registrationNotes: Tartan created in 2017 for the association Club Kilt du Pays de Lorient, using colours intended to represent the cities of Lorient, Ploemeur, Hennebont and Port-Louis.

name: Black House Mill, The
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Black House Mill tartan has been inspired by the ancient Highland slate roof of an historic building on the Black Isle.

name: Friends of Cancer Research (UK)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of friends and associates of Cancer Research UK. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Selkirk Local Committee commissioned this design incorporating the Charity’s official colours. As a world leader in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of cancer, this tartan will help not only to raise awareness of CRUK but will also raise funds to carry on the important work both in Scotland and the rest of the UK.

name: Operation Encompass
restrictions: Yes. Those wishing to wear/use this tartan must be authorised by the copyright holder - Operation Encompass. Not to be offered for sale, woven or used in graphic form unless authorised by the copyright holder.
registrationNotes: Operation Encompass, the charity supporting children exposed to domestic abuse, was established in 2011 by retired police officer Sgt David Carney-Haworth and his wife Elisabeth, Head Teacher at Torpoint Infant School, Cornwall. This tartan, based on the International Police Association tartan, symbolises the partnership between a growing number of UK police authorities and their local schools. A partnership which enables the provision of timely care and support for the innocent and often silent victims of domestic abuse - the children. The design includes the iconic 'thin blue line'; the founder’s ‘sergeant’s stripes’; the traditional police force, blue and white checkered band and the colours of the co-founder's Infant School.

name: San Jose Police Emerald Society
restrictions: Yes. The use of this tartan is limited to San Jose Police Emerald Society members and associates and members of the San Jose Police Department. All others must receive written permission from the President of the Society: www.sjpes.org.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the San Jose Police Emerald Society, California; incorporated on 1 August, 2017. The Mission of the Society is to “Render Support and Keep Their Memory Alive”. That is to remember fallen colleagues. The colours and pattern of the tartan signify the following: blue represents the blood running through the veins of all police officers; black lines represent the sorrow bands worn on officers badges during times of mourning; silver lines represent the line officers doing the toughest job on the mean streets and the first ones to be put into harm’s way; green represents the Irish heritage of the Society with the culture, music, arts, fellowship and cheer accompanying it. All members of the Society, their friends and families are encouraged to wear this tartan.

name: Kinloch Anderson House
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is exclusive to Kinloch Anderson Ltd and authorisation for its use strictly belongs to the Company Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: This design uses shades of camel, brown, black and navy. It is based on the sett of the Kinloch Anderson tartan but has 6 colours and is a simpler version than the other tartans already in the Kinloch Anderson family of tartans. Great interest has been expressed in this design by Kinloch Anderson business contacts for menswear, ladieswear, childrenswear and leathergoods in many overseas countries. The Kinloch Anderson House tartan has been created to respond to the requirement for a classic, universally popular identity and to extend the tartan colour spectrum for the Kinloch Anderson Brand of clothing and accessory ranges.

name: Prokasova, Nadja (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Nadja Prokasova, her family and descendants.
registrationNotes: Designed by one of her three daughters as a 60th birthday present for Nadja Prokasova. Colours: green and purple represent lavender and the Scottish thistle, her favourite plants; blue is the colour of her eyes.

name: Midnight Sun, The
registrationNotes: This design celebrates the sun at the time of the Summer Solstice. At places north of the Arctic Circle or south of the Antarctic Circle, the sun is visible for 24 hours a day for a few days each year creating extended sunsets which transform gradually into sunrises. At midnight, the sun never sets.

name: Sprott (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Can be worn or used by anyone in a personal or family capacity. Any enquiries concerning commercial use should be addressed to the designer or his immediate family and their successors.
registrationNotes: The registrant designed this tartan as there is no recognised tartan for the name Sprott or its variants. The predominant greens are symbolic of the hills of Galloway (and also of Co. Down and Cumberland), which area is the heartland of those bearing the name Sprott. The other colours provide a design framework, or reflect other family associations, including Douglas and Cameron (Erracht). The tartan is intended for a range of garments and the colours to suit both modern and plant-based dyes.

name: Schiffmann (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Others wishing to wear/use/weave this tartan should contact the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the designer and his family.

name: Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums
designer: Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums Society
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of active or retired members of Edmonton Fire Rescue in Alberta Canada, I.A.F.F LOCAL 209 members and Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums Society members. Any exceptions must be given written permission from the Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums executive. Written permission to weave this tartan should be sought from the Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums Society executive.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan whose combined colours represent the uniform shoulder patches. 100 black threads represent the memory of all Edmonton fire rescue members and the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the Edmonton firefighters union; red represents the firefighters themselves; blue represents the City of Edmonton, it’s flag and its citizens; yellow represents the Chief Officers and grey represents the Captains. 16 red threads represent 2016, the year when the Edmonton Firefighters Pipes and Drums was established. The 3 red horizontal lines represent the Pipes and Drums phrase of Tradition, Honour, Pride. The 3 red vertical lines represent the mission, vision and core values of the fire service. The 5 red horizontal lines represent the 5 branches of Edmonton Fire Rescue and its members. The 6 blue threads represent 1906, the year when the Fire Department was established.

name: Highland Community College (Kansas)
registrationNotes: Highland Community College was established by a Scottish native, the Reverend Samuel Irvin, in 1858, making it the first college chartered in Kansas. The College mascot is a West Highland terrier.

name: Tynecastle Park
restrictions: Yes. All requests to wear/weave/use this tartan must go through Hearts Football Club: www.heartsfc.co.uk/contact
registrationNotes: This tartan, using the Club colours, has been designed to commemorate the opening of the new Heart of Midlothian Football Club stand and tartan merchandise will be available from the Club store.

name: Tukkerclan
registrationNotes: The Tukkerclan tartan was designed to celebrate the friendship between a group of football friends from Stranraer, Scotland and Enschede, Holland which started eleven years ago when two men gave up their tickets for a young man’s dying wish to go an Old Firm game. Many return trips were made and 2010 Dutch champions FC Twente Enschede set up coaching clinics for Stranraer youth three times over the last six years and played a friendly match in 2017 bringing with them 400 fans. FC Twente gained great popularity in Stranraer and the supporters’ club Tukkerclan Stranraer was established. The word Tukker refers to the inhabitants of the region of Twente. Colours: red is for FC Twente Enschede, black and green for the two clubs from which Twente was formed; blue is for Scotland/Stranraer and the three white lines represent Sportclub, boys and Scotland/Stranraer who carry this colour in their kit.

name: Ceide (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use weave this tartan must be sought from the Ceide family. Contact: Ramon Ceide, email: [email protected]. Prepared for weaving by Tartan Weaving Mill.
registrationNotes: The Ceide family from Girona has its origins in the Spanish region of Galicia. In the 1940s, after the Civil War, two members of the family moved to the Catalan province of Girona where they established two generations later. Some members of the family studied, lived and worked in Edinburgh and since then, have developed a close relationship with the city and with Scotland. Colours: the blues represent the Scottish and Galician flags as well as the sky and the sea; the four red lines represent the Catalan flag whilst black and white appear as extremes to the evolution from clear blues to darker blues.

name: Zangenberg, Claes, baron of Pittenweem (Personal)

registrationNotes: Based on the Royal Stewart tartan , the central white line on red represents the national flag of Denmark, the birthplace of Mr Zangenberg. Next to that central icon, the gold bands comprise six threads for the Stewart King, James VI who created the barony in 1609. Adding to the green, red and gold of the Baron's arms are two narrow pink lines for Claes and Yasar Zangenberg's young daughters, Olivia and Julia.

registrationNotes: Designed by David Brunckhorst and Alan Trivett for Emmanuel College, the oldest collegiate community at the University of Queensland. It was established more than 100 years ago by a Scotsman, the Reverand Dr Ernst Merrington, a graduate of Edinburgh and Harvard, and a Presbyterian clergyman who as Chaplain General became the ANZACS highest ranking chaplain at Gallipoli and the Western Front. The colours used are based on the corporate colours of the College.

name: Edinburgh’s Hogmanay

registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for the Underbelly Edinburgh Hogmanay celebrations. It will be used in various items of merchandise including staff uniforms.

name: Bean of Freeport Hunting
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for L.L. Bean Ltd. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The original ‘Bean of Freeport’ tartan was registered in 1988 for L.L.Bean Inc, Freeport, Maine, USA, who are outdoor sporting specialists, to commemorate their 75th Anniversary. This Bean of Freeport ‘Hunting’ tartan, has been designed as part of a collection in celebration of the 30th Anniversary of the original Bean of Freeport Tartan. Following a similar Sett to the original, however this has been simplified to a modern design. The colours have been kept in keeping with the original ‘Bean of Freeport’ tartan, with a strong emphasis to the rich dark green representing the outdoors for which L.L.Bean is known for, this colour is also known as ‘Bean Green’ and is used in their logo. The strong blue element, highlights the LL Bean association with sports enjoyed on the lakes, rivers and oceans of Maine. Black and red pay homage to their heritage and original tartan. Whilst the Yellow commemorates the founder L.L.Bean himself and his original ‘Bean Boot’ design with its distinctive yellow laces still made in Maine-one pair at a time-by expert craftspeople.

name: Bean of Freeport Dress
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for L.L. Bean Ltd. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The original ‘Bean of Freeport’ tartan was registered in 1988 for L.L. Bean Inc, Freeport, Maine, USA, who are outdoor sporting specialists, to commemorate their 75th Anniversary. This ‘Dress’ Bean of Freeport tartan, has been designed as part of collection in celebration of the 30th Anniversary of the original Bean of Freeport Tartan and follows a similar sett to the original, however has been simplified to a modern design. The strong white base represents the wintery landscape of Maine and is a particularly significant season within the L.L. Bean calendar for enjoying the outdoors. The green represents the rich dark green of the outdoors for which L.L. Bean is known for, this colour is also known as ‘Bean Green’ and is used in their logo. Black and red pay homage to their heritage and original tartan. Whilst the Yellow commemorates the founder L.L. Bean himself and his original ‘Bean Boot’ design with its distinctive yellow laces still made in Maine-one pair at a time-by expert craftspeople.

name: Bean of Freeport Fall
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for L.L. Bean Ltd. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson
registrationNotes: The original ‘Bean of Freeport’ tartan was registered in 1988 for L.L.Bean Inc, Freeport, Maine, USA, who are outdoor sporting specialists, to commemorate their 75th Anniversary. This Bean of Freeport Fall tartan, has been designed as part of collection in celebration of the 30th Anniversary of the original Bean of Freeport Tartan and follows a similar sett to the original, however has been simplified to a modern design. The orange colour in this Fall version signifies the change of season where the entire landscape of Maine turns to autumn and is of great significance to LL Bean being renowned outdoor specialists. The green represents the rich dark green of the outdoors for which L.L.Bean is known for, this colour is also known as ‘Bean Green’ and is used in their logo. The white signifies how the landscape is beginning to shift to winter snow. Brown represents further the change of the landscape where the brown trunks and branches of the trees become more prominent without their leaves. Whilst the Yellow commemorates the founder L.L.Bean himself and his original ‘Bean Boot’ design with its distinctive yellow laces still made in Maine-one pair at a time-by expert craftspeople.

registrationNotes: Designed for Timothy Joseph Maxwell Conway, this tartan may be worn/used by all those with the Conway surname.

registrationNotes: As a young boy the designer looked for his family's tartan and found to his dismay, there was none. After years of wearing another's tartan, he decided to create a tartan that all Patricks can call their own.

name: Laws, Julian (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for Julian Laws, his family and descendants. The colours reflect those of the family's mining company, and of the gold in the red dirt of Western Australia.

name: Galbiati, Luca Maria (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Luca Maria Galbiati and his friends.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Luca Maria Galbiati created as a special commemorative souvenir for him and his friends to keep in perpetuity.

name: Flores, Martin E (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Consent is needed from the designer or family representative to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan designed to commemorate the Flores/Florez surname which originated from the autonomous principality of Asturias in the Celt-Iberian northwest region of Spain. It is bordered by the Bay of Biscay/Mar Cantabrico to the north, and Castile and Leon to the south, Cantabria to the east, Galicia to the west. The Tartan is made up of 7 colours which symbolise the region. The blue square with the yellow cross represents the Victory Cross and the flag of Asturias; dark blue represents the lakes/Los Lagos and the Bay of Biscay; green is for the forest, prairies and meadows; red and yellow represent the Spanish national flag; white represents the fog and snow on Picos de Europa Mountains and black represents the coal mines in the principality.

name: Albuquerque Police Department
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Albuquerque Police Department.
registrationNotes: As the first bagpiper for the Albuquerque Police Department, the designer wanted a tartan that represented his department as well as law enforcement as a whole; those officers that have been lost in the line of duty; the officers and the leadership of the department as well as the community and the criminal element that they stand between (The Thin Blue Line).

name: Pannell, baron of Anstruther (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Only to be used by Ryan Patrick Pannell, and his wife, baron and baroness of Anstruther, their family, heirs and successors. May only be woven by weavers authorised by Ryan Patrick Pannell, baron of Anstruther.
registrationNotes: Designed for Ryan Patrick Pannell, baron of Anstruther, incorporating the colours of his grant of arms.

name: McBride, John D L (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan should not be woven without permission of the designer or his descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer and his family. The colours were chosen to represent Mr McBride's family ties to Scotland, Ireland, England and the United States. The tartan may be worn/used by anyone with the McBride surname (including variants) with permission of the designer or his descendants.

name: Moncrieff (2017)
restrictions: Yes. Any individual interested in using this tartan should contact: [email protected].
registrationNotes: The tartan was commissioned by the Moncrieff family on behalf of their father, James Moncrieff. It was created to celebrate his 60th birthday. Within the design there are five purple overchecks symbolising his five children. The white parallel overchecks represent their father and his signature white hair. This tartan may be worn/used by all those with the Moncrieff surname.

name: Silver Fern
restrictions: Yes. Weaving rights held by the House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd as authorised by “Askival of Strathearn”. Copyrighted design is owned by the designers. IPR Design No 6072252 Kilt with Fern leaf design in pleated area.
registrationNotes: The Silver Fern tartan has been designed by Nadia Savage and Marion Foster in black and silver colours for use by all New Zealanders who celebrate dual nationality and are proud of their Scottish heritage, New Zealanders who would enjoy wearing the kilt or anyone who loves what this kilt represents. The tartan is woven with the Silver Fern emblem associated with New Zealand incorporated in the pleats. Created by Nadia Savage as a gift to her New Zealand born partner, the grandson of Jock Veitch who completed his apprenticeship at Scottish Woollen, March Street Mills, Peebles, in their dye house at Caerlee Mills, in May 1922. Jock continued to work as a dyer in the mills until he left Scotland in February 1925, to travel to New Zealand, South Island. Almost 70 years later, in full circle, his grandson returned to the northern hemisphere and now resides in Scotland.

name: Church of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Church of Scotland Tartan was created in the year 2017, the colours chosen to reflect the Burning Bush, the Scottish Flag and the dynamic Scottish landscape.

name: Geyser
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: The Great Geysir, located in Iceland, first erupted in the 14th century and gave rise to the word “geyser”. Even though the Great Geysir no longer erupts regularly, the nearby Strokkur geyser erupts every 5 - 10 minutes to a height of some 15 to 20 metres. The beautiful blue-green colour of the superheated water of Strokkur and the golden yellow of nearby elemental sulphur inspired this design.

name: Longships
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the longships. Dark brown and black represent the lapstrake wooden hull of these boats. Dark red and gold represent dyes that were used to give colour to the sails, leatherwork and wooden shields. Green and blue represent the ocean. Longships were a type of ship invented and used by the Norsemen for trade, commerce, exploration, and warfare during the Viking Age between the 9th and 13th centuries.

name: Holmlund-Krantz (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Holmlund-Krantz family and those associated with the family.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the Holmlund-Krantz family.

name: Westpoint Homes
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Westpoint Homes Ltd, 3 Arthur Street, Clarkston, Glasgow, G&6 8BQ.
registrationNotes: Designed by Ellis Bird, a student at Ayr College, as part of a competition to design a tartan for the Laigh Meadows development in Fenwick Ayrshire which is home to the first acclaimed co-operative movement on record, the Fenwick Weavers Society, formed in 1761. Westpoint Homes wanted to ensure that the design for the interiors of the houses being built in Fenwick reflected the local heritage and the village's roots in Scotland's weaving industry. The winning design is intended for use in the Welcome Pack for new homeowners, and will be displayed in Fenwick show homes.

name: Tinkoff Bank
registrationNotes: A tartan for Tinkoff Bank, the world’s largest online bank using yellow a colour of significance for Oleg Tinkov, the bank’s founder and which symbolises the energy of the sun; and blue taken from the bank’s branding. The tartan is intended for use in interior decoration and clothing.

name: Thatcher (2017)
registrationNotes: A tartan that is a legacy to the family ancestors that originated from Scotland and Ireland. This tartan may be worn/used by all people with the surname Thatcher.

registrationNotes: This tartan is only for use of the immediate family of the designer, the Heil Family of Kemete. The name Kemete (= local German dialect, from Kemenate, a house with a fireplace, Caminata in Latin) is the traditional name of the ancestral home of the family. The autumnal colours in this tartan reflect the Highlands and Islands of Scotland.

name: Atlanta United

registrationNotes: Atlanta United, based in Atlanta, Georgia is a soccer club of the Eastern Conference of Major League Soccer in the USA. The colours in this tartan are official team colours arranged in the same order as their home jerseys.

registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer and his family. The colours were chosen to represent the family’s long history in Scotland and Canada. The greens are for the northern woods, blue for the Pacific waters, and the shade of yellow represents the hair of the women who made it all worthwhile.

name: Allen R & D (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer, his family and heirs. Permission is required to weave this tartan. Copyright rests with the designer and his heirs.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer and his fiancée to be worn on their wedding day and as a legacy for their descendants. Colours: blue and green represent their shared love of the Scottish countryside and water, the green similar to military uniforms, paying homage to the designer’s family military history; red, denotes the bloodline of family; yellow their love of sunshine and good times together; black acknowledges that we must make the best of darker times in our lives, with the white lines adding balance to all the colours.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Lodge Rosslyn of Switzerland based on traditional masonic colours: blue represents St John’s Freemasonry in general; green represents Scotland and the fellow craft degree; white is the basic colour of masonry, meaning the entered apprentice degree, as well as the principle of chivalry and to keep the order pure and unsullied; black represents the Master Masons degree. The white cross on red background represents the Swiss flag, the home country of Lodge Rosslyn.

registrationNotes: A dress version of the Maver (SRT Ref #10329) tartan.

registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Patrick L Scarborough, his family, and descendants to celebrate their Scottish heritage. registrationNotes: The third of three original tartans created by David Patrick that all Patricks can call their own.

name: Foster Brother Customs
registrationNotes: This is a custom tartan for a company called Foster Brother Customs. The colours were chosen to represent the company and its origins. The green, brown and black are commonly used in modern camouflage so were chosen to honour military both past and present. The earthy colours were also chosen to represent their origins from a rural farming community. The green for new crop and the brown for freshly farmed ground. The black and grey for the rocky hills in north western Oklahoma as well as their native rattlesnakes. Lastly, these colours generally represent the kinship their pioneering ancestors had with the land and each other.

name: Atlas Cranes UK Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Restricted to company use. Prepared for weaving by A. Elliot (Fine Fabrics) Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed for Atlas Cranes UK Ltd, a Scottish based company, to celebrate its forthcoming centenary in 2019. The main colours of orange and black are the company's brand colours, with other colours to signify the German and Bulgarian roots of the company and owner.

name: New York Outlanders
registrationNotes: Created for the New York Outlanders Downstate fan group, this tartan honours their state, their love of Scotland, and the family of one of the main characters of the television series, Outlander. The tartan was inspired by the Fraser of Lovat (STR Ref #1264) and the New York City (STR Ref #5085) tartans.

name: Cameron, Alison (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Alison Cameron, her family and descendants.
registrationNotes: Designed as a tribute to Alison Cameron by her husband. Her favourite colour is purple which forms the prominent colour of the design and in contrast with the various greys, symbolises her colourful personality but without being overstated. The tartan will act as a legacy for future generations.

name: Al-Ammari (2017)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan can only be woven through warpweftweave studio.
registrationNotes: Maryam, Alya and Abdallah Al-Ammari commissioned this tartan for their parents’ 25th wedding anniversary and for use by future generations. The colours are inspired by the Arabian Gulf, where their parents met and where the family grew up.

name: Tulloch (2017)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Dr Frank Tulloch & USA Kilts. The colours selected had significance to Dr Tulloch: blue for his association with blue water sailing; darker green for his interest in the outdoors and forests in North Carolina; lighter green a tribute to the Clan Ross of which Tulloch is a Sept; red and black a tribute to blood spilled by the Tullochs in the North American wars after the American Revolution and for family graduations from Davidson College; white represents clouds in the sky for the blue water sailors.

name: Parachute Regiment
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail, is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050720.
registrationNotes: The Parachute Regiment tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Parachute Regiment. Significant colours associated with the Parachute Regiment are: maroon which signifies their famous berets; pale blue is for Pegasus; the lighter maroon represents I Para; blue represents II Para; green represents III Para; white represents the clouds that the Regiment parachute through; black represents IV Para and continual respect for all fallen Parachute Regiment comrades.

name: Commonwealth Games Scotland, Team Scotland 2018
designer: House of Edgar and Commonwealth Games Scotland
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by Team Scotland 2018 team members or people who have been given authority from Commonwealth Games Scotland. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar.
registrationNotes: Commonwealth Games Scotland have created this tartan to be worn by Team Scotland 2018 at the Gold Coast 2018 Commonwealth Games. The colours used are from the Company and Team brand, incorporating green as an acknowledgement to Australia, hosts for the Games.

name: Page (2017)
restrictions: Yes. . Prepared for weaving through Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Page Family of Nowra, NSW Australia and their descendants. The colours were chosen due to their significance to the family. This tartan may be worn by anyone sharing the Page surname or who is part of the Page family.

name: Hands Across the Sea - North America
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a tribute to the people from Scotland who risked everything they possessed and who endured many hardships in pursuit of a better life in North America. The colours selected had significance to the designer; red, white and blue for the colours of the national flags of Canada and the USA; deep blue for dark times; bright red a tribute to the great achievements.

name: Tulchan Club & Estate
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with permission from Tulchan Club and Estate.
registrationNotes: The colours of the Tulchan Club and Estate tartan represents the rich sporting heritage of the estate.

name: Aquascutum 2017
registrationNotes: British heritage brand Aquascutum wanted to create their own interpretation of one of the most classic and recognisable British fabrics in the world. This collection was heavily inspired by British craftsmanship and in particular the Scottish highlands as they developed into Fair Isle knits and tweed textures. By personalising a traditional British design in an official capacity the designers wanted to both celebrate the rich culture of tartan and modernise it for a new audience. The colours chosen for this tartan came from their house club check which is synonymous with the brand. By using their house colours they will be able to use this tartan for Autumn Winter 2018 and future collections.

name: McFeron (2018)
registrationNotes: This tartan design is for the McFeron family; their descendants and relations; and any beholding an affinity for the McFeron family, regardless of geographic location. The colours selected had significance to the McFeron family: blue and white for their religious belief; green for their military service and sacrifice; orange for their fiery spirit of independence and adventure; purple for their Scottish heritage; black for their steadfastness of character and integrity.

name: Hookins (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
registrationNotes: A tartan for the designer and her family which is available for others to use.

name: Guilder (2018)

registrationNotes: Designed for the Guilder family using colours chosen by them.

name: Afternoon Tea / Vanilla Cream Tea

registrationNotes: Designed for the Gedling family to reflect their Scottish, Irish and English heritage, using colours of significance to the family.

name: Whiteside, Ann Lynn (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and her family. Those wishing to weave this tartan must seek written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for the designer and her family. Colours chosen were of significance to the designer: blue and black for her husband's eyes and hair; white for her own hair; green for the Georgia landscape; purple for the Scottish thistle.

name: Kinloch Anderson Sundial
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to commemorate the 150th Anniversary of the Kinloch Anderson company founded in 1868. The tartan name is in memory of the sundial monument which Councillor Kinloch Anderson donated to Inverleith Park in Edinburgh in 1890 and its restoration in 2018. The tartan colours were chosen because of their particular significance to the company: sandstone for the shade of the sundial; green for Inverleith Park where the sundial is located; blue for the Water of Leith that runs close to the company’s premises in Leith, Edinburgh; 3 golden yellow lines represent the three Royal Warrants held by the company and 6 red burgundy lines for the six generations of the family ownership and management.

name: Flint (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Please contact the designer or his authorised representative to weave this tartan. This pattern is not accompanied by a general public licence nor is it to be misconstrued in any way as having such.
registrationNotes: Designed for the Flint family from Black Mountain in the United States. The design was selected based on family history and ancestry c. 1635. The colours: light brown, white and red to symbolise the flint stone, which was often used for tools of both daily chore, as well as war; blue for their family love and beliefs; black is placed next to white, when mixed they turn grey, like stone, representing the common connection between all Flint families; yellow represents joy and kind-heartedness.

name: Kassapi, Mariana (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed to represent Mark Sweet's time spent studying at the Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania with many thin coloured lines used to signify his experience in computing. The colours used are of personal significance: bright blue for vibrancy in his life; red for hardship and strength; yellow from his university emblem; white for sincerity and trust; grey for his military service; greens for his home on the east coast of the USA.

In 2018 the design symbolised their seven years of marriage and two children and in turn the four family members of the family. The interwoven white and blue lines represent the continued lineage of their past.

registrationNotes: The designer was inspired by Ireland’s national flag. The colours chosen had personal significance and were deemed to represent Celtic colours, Ireland’s history and its lush green countryside and rolling hills.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Ann Cameron in June 2013 for Reverend Bonnie Fraser, Minister of Bridgeville United Church in Nova Scotia and members of the congregation to commemorate their 120th anniversary. The colours chosen were significant to the congregation: light blue for water and sky; green for the season of growth; white for Easter and Christmas; orange for Autumn; black for the printed word; yellow for the riches of life; red and royal blue for their religious beliefs; grey for the iron ore from local mines.

Cheesehearts was chosen to commemorate the cheese produced in Wisconsin and Green19 for the Packers’ player call. The colours used were deemed to be variants of the Packers' home and away jerseys.

Permission has been given by the designer for Deaf History Scotland to register the tartan and use it to raise awareness of heritage projects for the deaf community.

The designer used colours of personal significance: grey to represent the gloominess that some homeless people experience and ten bright colours for community support. Slanj Kilts will use the tartan on various products which will be sold through various homeless charities in the UK and around the world. Slanj pledged to give a percentage of the sales to different homeless charities in the United Kingdom.

name: Island Birth Surtsey
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn/woven with the designer's permission. This design may only be reproduced with the permission of the owner, Carol A L Martin.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the birth of Surtsey, the geologically youngest island on Earth. This tiny part of the Vestmannaeyjar Archipelago off the southern coast of Iceland was formed by a series of volcanic eruptions between November 1963 and June 1967. Surtsey was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2008. The colours used were inspired by the island of Surtsey.

name: JudoScotland

restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with JudoScotland.

JudoScotland is supported by sportscotland, the National Agency for Sport in Scotland, and represents members, clubs, individual disciplines and volunteers delivering the Olympic sport of Judo across Scotland.

name: Suffragette
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050721.
registrationNotes: This tartan marks the 6th February 2018, exactly 100 years since the 1918 Representation of the People Act was passed, which gave women over the age of 30 the right to vote. This tartan honours suffragettes and all of the key figures who worked for women to be given the right to vote, including Emmeline Pankhurst and Emily Wilding Davison. This tartan encompasses the colours of the suffragettes; namely green, white and purple. The suffragette colours had significance as the first letter of each colour represented the words ‘Give Women Votes’. Green represented ‘G’ for ‘Give’; white represented ‘W’ for ‘Women’; violet represented ‘V’ for ‘Votes’.

name: United Pipers for Peace
restrictions: Yes. Authorisation must be sought from the designer and the manager of the event "United pipers for Peace" https://www.unitedpipersforpeace.com/english, to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates July 7 and 8, 2018 when the “1918-2018 United Pipers for Peace” bring together more than 20 pipe bands in Amiens in France to pay tribute to the role, service and sacrifice of the soldiers and pipers who took part in the Battle of the Somme and the Great War. The tartan colours include red, white and black, which are the colours of the commemorative event and red for the poppy. Red, white and blue are also used to represent Amiens, where the event takes place.

name: Maclaine of Lochbuie Auld Sett
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the chief, his family and those of Mr James Greenfield, plus nominated officials of the Clan Maclaine of Lochbuie Society. May only be used with the written permission of the Lochbuie Clan Chief. May only be woven with the written permission of the Lochbuie Clan Chief.
registrationNotes: The design is taken from a joined and fringed plaid estimated to date from the 3rd or 4th quarter of the 18th century, hence the approximate date of 1780. The plaid belongs to Mr James Greenfield – a Maclaine of Lochbuie clansman and descendant of the 19th clan chief through the marriage of his daughter Mary to John Gregorson of Ardtornish. The family tradition is that she brought the plaid with her from Mull. Whilst this tartan pre-dates the other patterns associated with the clan, its use is restricted and it should not considered as an alternative or replacement for the current ‘red’ Maclaine of Lochbuie sett. The Auld Sett may only be woven/used with the permission of the chief of the Maclaines of Lochbuie.

name: Mercian Regiment
designer: Lawson, Margi of Tartan Manor Ltd.
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050726.
registrationNotes: This design celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Mercian Regiment. The Mercian Regiment, formed on 1st September 2007, was recruited from five English counties that formed the ancient kingdom of Mercia and known as ‘The Heart of England’s Infantry’. This Tartan encompasses some of the colours associated with the Mercian Regiment. Black is also for the continual respect for all fallen Mercian Regiment comrades.

The colours used were of personal significance to the designer, Robert Paterson: light and dark browns for layered sedimentary rock; green for the five national parks located within the Canadian Rockies; red for the Canadian Maple Leaf; white for snow covered peaks.

Down, and the Clyde in Lanark County, Ontario, where he has lived since 1961.

The colours selected were of personal significance: black and white for the Brittany Flag; blue and dark red for the lands in the Highlands; yellow for eternal faith and green for being in concordance with Nature.

name: Home-Start Glasgow North

registrationNotes: A tartan designed for Home-Start Glasgow North, which was established in 2001 to support and empower vulnerable parents with children under 5 living north of the River Clyde, helping them to grow in confidence, resilience and well-being, and assisting them to combat social exclusion by encouraging strong relationships within the family and in the wider community. name: Groix, l'île de
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Listing No 953, 56 - Morbihan, November 18th, 2017, Directorate of Legal and Administrative Information.
registrationNotes: Seven natives of Groix passionate about wearing the kilt decided to create the association "the kilt groisillon" and design a tartan for the island of Groix. This tartan, composed of six colours, represents the island of Groix: purple for garnets and heather, yellow for the gorse and broom, white and black for the Gwenn Ha (the Breton flag), blue for the Armor (coastal Brittany) and green for the Argoat (inland Brittany).

name: Godin, Anne (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Anne Godin, her family and descendants. Permission is required to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed to represent Anne Godin's journey of mastery though taekwondo. The colours used are of personal significance: white, yellow, green, blue and red represent each rank/belt before becoming a black belt. Black with 6 yellow lines has been selected to represent her 6th degree black belt. The burgundy lines are for her parents' and brother's support throughout her years. This tartan is a legacy for future generations.

name: Western Stag
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Western Stag company members and employees. For tartan details and permissions regarding use, please contact Richard Brook at: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Western Stag, a small business founded in 2018 that specialises in luxury candles, crafts, and homewares. The company’s ethos centres on supporting charitable causes, with proceeds from sales contributing to a range of charities. The tartan’s colour palette draws inspiration from Western Stag’s corporate logo alongside the natural landscapes of the Scottish Highlands, creating a design that balances brand identity with a strong sense of place and heritage.

name: Gildwell
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for Gildwell Property Ltd a Scottish property development company that convert unused commercial building in to residential homes and also develop new build properties on plots of land.

name: Halifax Regional Police
restrictions: Yes. For use only by persons specifically authorised by HRP. Prepared for weaving by Dianne Quimby or designated substitute approved by HRP.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Halifax Regional Police (HRP), the largest municipal police agency in Atlantic Canada (and Nova Scotia). Nova Scotia has a long and proud connection to Scotland and its traditions. HRP holds close many ceremonial aspects of those traditions. As an amalgamated police service in 1995 from former municipal police agencies, HRP's new tartan will be purposed to visibly celebrate the men and women of HRP. Inspector Don Moser lead the development of the HRP tartan and collaborated with Diane Quimby (designer) from the Royal Cape Breton Gaelic College. The HRP tartan concept is inspired by the organisational colours.

name: Chef Buchanan
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holder David Buchanan. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven unless specifically authorised by the copyright holder David Buchanan.
registrationNotes: With bright colours from David Buchanan’s clan tartan and its central blue & white ‘Saltire’, this vibrant design encapsulates the world-wide travel of David’s “Kilted Chef” persona. From luxury yachts in Monaco to sumptuous palaces in Qatar to village feasts in Bali, all promoting, preparing and presenting, the best of Scottish food and drink.

name: Lapierre-Sabourin (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Lapierre-Sabourin family and their descendants.
registrationNotes: Designed by Marc-André Lapierre & Chantal Sabourin, this tartan was created to celebrate the union of two families: Lapierre from Québec, Canada and Sabourin from Ontario, Canada. The colours chosen have personal significance: blue represents their Quebec roots while the green represents the Franco-Ontarian community; dark orange colour represents the groom's colour and the purple for the bride; white makes allusion to the creation of the tartan for their wedding. The intent is to use this design as their family tartan.

name: Lawson-Reid (Personal)
