registrationNotes: A family tartan created for the Lawson-Reid family that celebrates the uniting of two families through the wedding of Stuart Lawson and Jill Reid. The colours and thread counts of this tartan have been inspired by the personal heritage of the couple and dates of significance relevant to the new family.

name: Powell-Wicks Anniversary (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designers, however they wish the tartan to be available for others to use.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed by Bub Powell and Jeff Wicks for their 10 year anniversary. The design was derived from the original wedding tartan for Jeff and Bub called Powell-Wicks (Personal) with the reference 11856. The colour scheme and line placement stay the same, while the shades of each hue and size of said lines were adjusted.

name: Stafford-Johnston
registrationNotes: Created to honour a group of friends, known as the Stafford Johnstons. Brenda Gibson, a member of the group, specially dyed the yarns in order to weave the tartan by hand. The fabric will be made into cushions and presented to each couple in the group. The tartan design intends to reference the Johnston and the Wexford County tartans.

name: Canadian Veteran
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Veterans and individuals showing gratitude for their service. Permission must be sought from Harold H Lowe CD CRMC, the owner of the tartan to weave or reproduce in any form: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Harold Lowe, a retired Reserve Officer, who wanted to create an unofficial tartan to honour all Canadian Veterans. Dark blue represents the Royal Canadian Navy, dark green represents the Canadian Army and light blue represents the Royal Canadian Air Force. These colours are joined with the red and white as a symbol of Canada's flag. The black in the pattern recognises the Veterans who have passed.

name: Phoenix Rising
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2018. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6085119.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created as a tribute to the phoenix, an ancient mythological symbol which has endured for millennia, and across vastly different cultures. The phoenix, which is always characterised as a bird, dies in a magnificent fire of its own making burning into a pile of ash before being reborn and rising from its own demise as a newly resurrected phoenix. The colours and geometry in the tartan visualise the rising of the phoenix, and its rebirth from the ashes of its past life. Black represents the dying phoenix; the two greys represent the ash; yellow, red, purple and gold correspond to the brightly coloured plumage of the mythological bird. The Phoenix Rising tartan has a deep significance to the designer, who has arisen from the challenges of his own personal difficulties, and it is designed to express an enduring sense of hope, redemption and rebirth. The tartan represents the beginnings of a new life and is for all who have gained their own personal victory over life challenges and hard times.

name: Clark's Harbour
restrictions: Yes. For the use of the community of Clark's Harbour, Nova Scotia.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Leigh B Stoddard, the Mayor of Clark's Harbour, to celebrate the 100th Anniversary of Incorporation, 1919 - 2019 and to become the town's official tartan. The community is the southernmost town in the province of Nova Scotia, and thus one of the southernmost towns in Canada, being located roughly on a parallel with Bilbao, Spain and just north of Rome. The town is located on Cape Sable Island, and the main industry is lobster fishing.

name: Crouch (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the registrant.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the Crouch family in Texas in the United States that can also be worn by their descendants. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the Crouch surname.

name: Grundstein (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan must be granted by the designer or his direct descendants.
registrationNotes: Nehemiah and Godel Grundstein emigrated to London from Poland around 1910. Their sons anglicised their names to Grant and Gordon, some of whom had lost contact with each other, but recently their descendants have found each other after almost 100 years. This tartan has been designed by Bobby Gordon, Godel Grundstein's great grandson, to celebrate this reunion, and unite all other Grundstein's from around the world. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the Grundstein surname.

name: Atwal (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact Padeep Atwal to wear/use/weave this tartan: [email protected]
registrationNotes: Designed for Paldeep Atwal and his family. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the Atwal surname.

name: Cicerone Ensemble
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from Andreas Gilger: [email protected] to wear/use this tartan.
registrationNotes: edit

name: Scotts Bluff County
registrationNotes: A tartan for Scotts Bluff County in Nebraska. Colours used represent: tan from the sandstone of Scotts Bluff National Monument, named after slain frontier fur broker Hiram Scott, and for local hills; green for the grass of the prairie; gold for the harvest; purple for the Ulster Scots who were Hiram Scott’s fore-bears and for alfalfa and thistle bloom; a bit of scarlet in honour of the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

name: Change Mental Health
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Ingles Buchan. Enquiries should be directed to: Change Mental Health, Suite 4/1, Great Michael House, 14 Links Place, Edinburgh, EH6 7EZ. Email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: The Change Mental Health tartan was commissioned to celebrate the charity’s rich history and to raise mental health awareness. The charity was originally part of the National Schizophrenia Fellowship, set up in 1972, and then became an independent Scottish charity in 1984. The organisation adopted its current name, Change Mental Health, in 2022 following a rebrand from Support in Mind Scotland. The focal point of this design is the sequential inclusion of the charity’s heritage of a traditional blue and green that was prominent in its previous branding. Change Mental Health’s new branding pays homage to the past identity, carrying over the blue and green. The contrasting red on blue in the tartan was factored into the new branding, which is a major element from the Campbell of Cawdor clan tartan in recognition of the late Lady Campbell of Croy’s great support for this organisation.

name: Battles of Flanders Centenary
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the centenary of the end of the battles of Flanders in 1918 using black and red for the death and the blood of the soldiers; dark brown and brown for the clay of the ground and the mud of trenches; dark grey and azure for the sky changing Flanders; dark green and green for woods and meadows and red for poppies in Spring.

name: Edward Bransfield Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Authorisation to weave this tartan must be sought from the designer or members of the Remembering Edward Bransfield Committee.
registrationNotes: Edward Bransfield was an Irish Antarctica explorer. Bransfield was the first to land on and claim King George Island for the British Crown. He was arguably the first to discover the Antarctic Peninsula. Bransfield Strait, Island and Mount, all located in Antarctica, are named after him and the colours chosen represent these regions: white for ice and clouds; dark blue for the Antarctic Ocean; light blue for the icebergs; black for the volcanic rock and penguins; green for the algae and moss; orange for the lichen and penguins; red for the penguin rookeries.

name: Allen Associates
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from Allen Associates Limited to wear/use/weave this tartan..
registrationNotes: Allen Associates are a Scottish process design engineering company specialising in the delivery of projects across the distilling sector in both Scotland and internationally. They have worked with many of Scotland’s biggest brands. Towards the end of 2017 Allen Associates approached Glowfish Creative to create an Allen Associates tartan that both connected them with the industry and reflected their commitment to the sector. Their visits to many whisky distilleries made them realise that there are certain sights, colours and smells that link them all. However, it was always the distinctive copper stills which captured their imagination and being synonymous with Scotch whisky, their design uses a copper coloured thread as part of the weave. The overall theme of the tartan is dark grey to reflect the dark rainclouds that deliver the water from which, in part, all whisky is born. The design features fine lines of copper and orange threads to suggest the process of distilling the whisky we know and love. Allen Associates worked closely with Ken MacDonald at Houston Kiltmakers to develop the design and liaise with the weavers to incorporate a copper coloured metallic lurex thread.

name: Spirit of Peggy's Cove
restrictions: Yes. Copyright Patrick King Woollen Company (PKWC). May only be woven with written approval from (PKWC).
registrationNotes: A tartan inspired by Peggy's Cove, a small fishing community located on the Eastern shore of St. Margaret’s Bay in Nova Scotia. The three shades of blue represent the ever changing colours of the Atlantic Ocean. The tan colours represent the rock formations of this unique landscape carved by the migration of glaciers and the ocean tides. The white and red lines running through the tartan represents Peggy’s Point Lighthouse built in 1914 and is one of Nova Scotia’s most iconic tourist attractions.

name: Kinnamont-Pifer Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer and copyright holder to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of James Kinnamont and AshMarie Pifer. The Kinnamont family tartan: we grow, bonded through tribulation, strengthened by our creativity and independence with one blood, one family. The colours selected are of personal significance: red for the one blood of one family; green for growth in life and nature; purple for creativity and independence; grey for bonds through tribulation.

name: MacMaster (2018)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Dianne Quimby, Mabou, or designated substitute.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the designer and his family which may also be worn by other descendants of Donald (Weaver) MacMaster who settled in Cape Breton in Nova Scotia, Canada, in 1801. The colours were chosen to represent/reflect things of importance for that family: blue for scholarship; yellow/gold colour represents the value of the Gaelic language that is held by the MacMaster family; green for the island of Cape Breton; red for the strong family ties that exist within the MacMaster family; purple for the church and because there have been a high number of clergymen in the MacMaster family; brown is representative of a violin’s colour due to the family’s association with music. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the MacMaster surname.

name: McCune Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland. Copyright: Andrew Brookes Andrew Brookes Tailoring Ltd 60a George Street Edinburgh EH2 2LR IPR Pending
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Andrew Brookes and Marc McCune for Marc McCune's wedding to Laini Pawson. With strong roots in Glasgow, where the wedding took place, it was important to them to reference this in their colour choice. Using Scotland's national flag and the Glasgow Coat of Arms as inspiration, other colour influences, including the navy and white of St Andrew's Cross, were also included. The rest of the colours were deemed by them to represent the legends associated with the Glasgow Coat of Arms: ancient brown (there is the tree that never grew), Douglas blue (there is the bird that never flew) and ancient blue (there is the fish that never swam). Finally, Marc's marriage to Laini was considered by them to be the last nod to the Coat of Arms as it took place at Devonshire Gardens in Glasgow and not in a church (there is the bell that never rang).

name: Spirit Of Greenock
restrictions: Yes. Weaving and supply of merchandise must be through the designer and copyright holder.
registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the Scottish town of Greenock using various shades of blue and whites to represent the skies and water landscape, which the designer associated with Greenock.

name: Grantown East
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan should be sought from Karen Blessington
registrationNotes: Karen Blessington, one of the owners of the Ravack Estate, and Margaret Grant, designed a tartan for Grantown East, which pays homage to the beautiful scenery of the Highlands, the Grantown East station building, which is located on the Ravack Estate, and the railway. Purple for the lovely heather adorning the landscape. Green for the trees providing a habitat for the abundant wildlife in the area. Blue and white for their railway logo. Plum for the colourful windows in the Grantown East railway station building. Black lines for the railway track that transported thousands of people during its 105 years life before being closed to the last passengers on 2nd November 1968.

name: MS Society Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Permission from the MS Society Scotland must be sought to wear, weave or use this tartan: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan is dedicated to the memory of Margaret Theresa Kane, a great friend of this tartan’s designer, Moira Dalgetty. “Margaret was a much-loved person and teacher, a gifted seamstress and craftswoman who loved tartan. She is the inspiration for this tartan.” Over 11,000 people in Scotland had MS in 2018. It’s unpredictable and different for everyone. It’s often painful, exhausting and can cause problems with how people with this condition walk, move, see, think and feel. This tartan will be used to raise awareness and funds for this condition and allow the Society and its supporters to show their Scottish pride whilst taking part in events, speaking to Members of the Scottish Parliament and generally representing the MS Community visually.

name: Lochside
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from Michael S Fraser to wear/use this tartan. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakerrs.
registrationNotes: Michael and his wife purchased a ruined croft in the North West Highlands, near the small town of Lochinver in 1996. The couple and their four young boys set about renovating the place over a period of three years. The croft was de-crofted and the cottage, “Lochside Cottage”, remained a favourite destination for their family holidays. This tartan design was based on their family tartan Fraser Hunting (STA ref 1659) with the extra white line representing the hours they spent whitewashing the property to ensure it was maintained and the blue representing the small loch in front of the cottage with the sea also visible in the near distance.

name: Trinity Presbyterian Church, Little Rock
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use/weave this tartan must be granted by the Clerk of the Tartan of Trinity Presbyterian Church USA, as voted by the Session.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in September 2017 by Fiona Whitson of Edinburgh, Scotland to commemorate the 30th anniversary of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Little Rock in Arkansas, USA. The design was inspired by their church sanctuary, grounds and the stained glass over their Lord's table. Fiona created a fabric mural using colour combinations to suggest stained glass. The colours selected have personal significance for this Church: three yellow/gold lines together to represent the Trinity; red for the blood of Christ; blue for the water of their baptism; white for Christianity; grey for their human understanding; green for a commitment to grow in Christian love toward their neighbour and themselves.

name: Spirit of Ukraine
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the registrant's written permission.
registrationNotes: Suggested by ethnic Ukrainians in Canada to the designer, the Spirit of Ukraine tartan combines the colours in the national flag of the Ukraine.

name: International Mediators
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear or use this tartan must be sought from John Sturrock.
registrationNotes: The International Mediators Tartan, designed especially for the Edinburgh conference of the International Academy of Mediators in May 2018.

name: Hello Kitty Black
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of employees and customers of Sanrio Co. Ltd. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland
registrationNotes: This black tartan celebrates Hello Kitty. Black is for the kitty's eyes and whiskers with white for her face. Her ribbon is represented by the two reds and her clothes the blue.

name: Miracle-Ear
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from Miracle-Ear® to use this tartan. Prepared for weaving by by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan represents Miracle-Ear® who are dedicated to helping people hear. With 70 years of experience, Miracle-Ear® has over 1,400 locations all over the United States. This company understands that the sounds of life are a big part of what motivates people each day. This company customises the latest technology to each patient they serve to allow them to connect to each moment of their day. The Miracle-Ear family strives to bring their customers leading-edge technology and hearing solutions that improve lives, relationships and communities.

name: Woking Golf Club
restrictions: Yes. May only with worn/used/woven with permission from Mr Carl Bianco, Club Professional, Woking Golf Club, Pond Road, Woking, Surrey, GU22 0JZ
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created to recognise the high proportion of the membership of Woking who are Scottish or have strong links with Scotland. The colours chosen have significance to the club: the green and gold are the club colours and are worn on the club tie; the blue and white stripes represent the Saltire; the red and white represent the flag of St George’s as an acknowledgement of the geographical location of the club.

name: Ocean Worlds & Icy Moons Exploration
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Geoffrey (Tailor) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed on behalf of Charles Cockell, Professor of Astrobiology, School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Edinburgh. It is intended to be worn during science, exploration and outreach activities associated with icy worlds and planetary bodies with interior water bodies or oceans, such as Europa, Enceladus, Titan, Ceres and others. Colours: the ice blue depicts the water bodies and oceans of icy moons and ocean worlds; the white (peroxide) bars depict the crusts of icy worlds; the green lines depict the search for habitability and life in distant ocean worlds; the red line depicts hydrothermal activity and the possibility of core-ocean interactions and the influence of the cores on ocean chemistry and habitability.

name: Jordan, James, Cornwall (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Jordan Family.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to celebrate the Scottish ancestry of the Jordan family living in Cornwall. The yellow/gold and red colours have been taken from the Cornish Hunting tartan (STR ref. 765). The black acknowledges their Scottish ancestry beginning in the coal mines of Lanarkshire. The dark blue has been taken from the Clan Elliot (STR ref. 1102) tartan, with the light blue representing the coastal waters stretching from Cornwall and all around Scotland.

name: Jordan, James (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of James Jordan and his descendants, immediate family (spouse, parents, siblings), and anyone else expressly authorised by him.
registrationNotes: The personal tartan for James Jordan is a variation of the Jordan, James, Cornwall (2018) (Personal) tartan. The only slight variation from his family tartan is the exclusion of the gold section within the sett.

name: Royal Terrace Hotel
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Royal Terrace Hotel, Edinburgh.
registrationNotes: One of the many traditional elements of the design concept, with a modern twist. The tartan will be used within the Royal Terrace Hotel located at 18, Royal Terrace in Edinburgh, Scotland. The design takes into account the history of the building and the colours of heather, which are representative of the surrounding area in Scotland.

name: Calgary Dress
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission of the owners of the tartan, Calgary Highland Dancing Association 1984 email: [email protected].
registrationNotes: This Calgary Dress tartan is based on the original Calgary tartan that was registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 2002 and subsequently added to the Scottish Tartans Register as a legacy tartan (STR ref. 477). This tartan has been designed to commemorate the Canadian highland dancing championships held in Calgary in 2018, and to honour the highland dancers wearing dress tartans. The colours are significant to Calgary: red to represent Calgary; white and grey for the snow-capped Rocky mountains; black for the local oil industry; blue for the rivers; yellow for the prairie fields.

name: Royal Welsh
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050723.
registrationNotes: The Royal Welsh Tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to Royal Welsh. Significant colours associated with Royal Welsh are: navy blue, red and green representing the colours of their stable belt; white represents their impressive hackle; black represents the Flash worn by Royal Welsh and also represents continual respect for all fallen Royal Welsh comrades.

name: Royal Logistic Corps
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050727.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Royal Logistic Corps. The Royal Logistic Corps was formed on 5 April 1993 by the union of five units: Royal Corps of Transport, Royal Army Ordnance Corps, Royal Pioneer Corps, Army Catering Corps and Postal and Courier Service previously part of the Royal Engineers. This Tartan encompasses the significant colours associated with the Royal Logistic Corps being red, blue and yellow/gold. Black is for the continual respect for all fallen Royal Logistic Corps comrades.

name: Royal Corps of Signals
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 December 2018, registration number: 6050724.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Royal Corps of Signals. The Royal Corps of Signals was formed in 1920 and by the end of World War 2 members of the Royal Corps of Signals had served in every theatre of war. This tartan encompasses the significant colours associated with the Royal Corps of Signals being: light blue, blue and green. White represents the ‘silvery white’ of the Roman God 'Mercury', as featured on the Royal Corps of Signals insignia and cap badge. Along with their motto; “Certa Cito”, meaning ‘Swift and Sure’.

name: Château Frontenac
designer: Vaugeois, Marise and Patrick King Woollen Company
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written approval from both Patrick King Woollen Company and Lambert & Co. Château Frontenac.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the 125th anniversary of the Château Frontenac, a national historic site of Canada. Ideally located inside the old fortified walls of Quebec City. Perched atop a tall cape overlooking the St. Lawrence river. The blues represent the ever changing colours of the St. Lawrence river with the gold representing the dynasty of the hotel. Château Frontenac is a cultural monument associated with Quebec’s rich history and a historical jewel.

name: Rogers, Jill (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please seek the designer's permission to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Jill Rogers and her family. The lowlander family of Jill’s husband are of Scottish heritage but do not have a tartan. Jill’s mother-in-law had ancestors with both Davidson and Logan surnames and these names both have official family clan tartans. Jill created this tartan using the Logan and Davidson tartan designs as a base.

name: Wrigglesworth Pastoral (Canada)
restrictions: Yes. Wearing and use restricted to all descendants of George and Alice (Gray) Wrigglesworth of Cochrane Ontario Canada and descendants' families and family relations to designer. All descendants of Albert John and Eileen (Mulholland) Banfield of Windsor Ontario Canada and descendants' families and family relations to designer. Prepared for weaving by Al's Tartan Shoppe Thunder Bay Ontario Canada Other weaver(s) by permission of designer.
registrationNotes: The inclusion of the word Pastoral has personal significance for the applicant’s family. Their ancestors immigrated to Canada and were in the field of Pastoral work; taking care of another's land and such for their landlord's interests. For this family, the word Pastoral also represents those who were/are members of the clergy. The colours selected have personal significance for this family. This tartan design is based on Wrigglesworth Family, Canada (Personal) by same designer (STR reference 12088).

name: Lüthold, Jasmine (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Prepared for weaving by Bute Fabrics.
registrationNotes: Jasmine Lüthold designed this tartan to create a feeling of belonging to her family. The colours chosen refer to the designer's origin: the basic colour yellow, the three black stripes and the one orange stripe represent this family; green and brown represent the colours of their family house in Alpnach, Switzerland; blue stands for the rivers next to their family house; red represents the family roots in Switzerland, referring to the red Swiss flag. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the Lüthold surname and their sympathisers.

name: Englund, Paul (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Any weaving must be approved by Paul Englund, the copyright holder and owner of this tartan.
registrationNotes: Designed for Paul Englund, for family pride. This is a tartan that may be worn by others with the Englund surname.

name: Kelly-Cero (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. The designer is also the copyright holder of this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan depicts the ancestral background of Francis Kelly and his wife, Merilyn Cero. The tartan design features a dragon woven into alternating light blue squares.

name: Isle of South Uist
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale or woven unless with the specific authorisation of the copyright holder. Design No:6034144 lntemational Design Classification: Version: 11-2017 Class: 05
registrationNotes: This tartan is supported by the community landlord, Stòras Uibhist and is primarily based on the South Uist flag. The tartan is intended to promote the unique identity of South Uist.

name: Pride of Kinnaird
restrictions: Yes. The Pride of Kinnaird tartan is for the exclusive use of Kinnaird Primary Pupils and Kinnaird Voices. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills. Other persons or organisations wishing to wear/use/weave this tartan should seek permission from Kinnaird Primary School.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the 10th year for Kinnaird Primary School (KPS), a non-denominational school in Kinnaird Village, Larbert, Stirlingshire as a lasting legacy for current, past & future pupils. KPS was established in August 2007 to serve the existing ‘Inches’ housing development and planned building. The new school was formally opened on Friday 16th May 2008. A fashion show held in September 2007 showcased the suggested colour options. Pupils and parents cast their votes and the winning colours were: purple, jade green, black, blue and white. Pupils took inspiration from the Pride of Scotland tartan, but incorporated the winning colours in the new KPS tartan; now named ‘Pride of Kinnaird’. Mrs Shirley Anne Smillie of Border Embroideries collaborated with Ms Laura McLintock, (Depute Headteacher, KPS from 2007 to 2014) to create a unique design. Mrs Pamela Adamson (Headteacher, KPS from 2007 to 2016) gave support. On 9th January 2008, the pupils were piped into their new school by Miss Sarah MacNeil, wearing the new school uniform. All pupils now proudly wear this tartan to show they are part of the family of KPS.

name: Missouri Baptist University
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is not to be woven or reproduced in any way without written permission from Missouri Baptist University. The design right for the Missouri Baptist Uninversity Tartan is held by Missouri Baptist University under U.S. Copyright Act-17 U.S.C.. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: To commemorate the inauguration of Missouri Baptist University's (MBU) seventh president, Dr. Keith Ross, the University released this tartan in the autumn of 2018. The pattern, selected by a group of MBU faculty and staff, is a visual representation of MBU's timeless values and the optimism of what is yet to come. Each colour woven into the tartan pattern represents one of the University's core values; namely truth, trust, loyalty, wisdom and integrity of character and their Christian faith; grey represents social change, which is achieved through alumni whose lives are distinguished by service and leadership.

name: ConGrad
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the family and friends of Connor Welsh.
registrationNotes: The ConGrad tartan has been designed by Lorraine Welsh to commemorate the graduation of her son Connor Welsh from the University of Dundee. It celebrates achieving a Bachelor of Design in Animation. The tartan name Congrad is a word play on Connor’s Graduation. The colours all have personal significance for Connor’s time during his course: orange in 22 threads represents Connor’s age; green celebrates the 4 years of study shown by the colour of the graduation hood worn for Bachelor of Design in Animation; grey represents the 3 years spent living in Dundee; green for memories of numerous days playing frisbee on the Magdalen Green; dark grey symbolising dedication towards friends playing the science fiction tabletop game ‘Shadowrun’ at dungeons and dragons evenings; yellow represents walks in the Dundee sunshine. The total sett repeat equals 96 threads to match Connor's year of birth in 1996.

name: Bailey, Chad (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Designed for Chad Bailey. Permission required to wear/use/weave this tartan. Please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd/Chad Bailey regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Chad Bailey, this design has been based on the Gordon Dress tartan sett owing to recent discovery of their family’s lineage from the Clan Gordon. The colouration has been selected by Chad and his spouse to ensure great personal significance: maroon and yellow symbolise the knowledge and prosperity they have taken from their time at Arizona State University where both Chad and his wife graduated; red, white and blue represent their home country of United States of America and, the green and black tie back into the original Gordon Dress design. This design has been created to signify a unique reflection of the Chad Bailey family’s journey from their Scottish roots to the present day. May be worn by others with the Bailey surname.

name: Carrie, Ian (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the family of Ian Carrie using some design elements from the Allison tartan in honour of Ian Carrie's family connection.

name: Baxters 150th Anniversary
restrictions: Yes. Designed exclusively by Kinloch Anderson for Baxters Food Group limited. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Permission required, please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd regarding use.
registrationNotes: Baxters Food Group Limited was founded in Fochabers, Moray in 1868 by George Baxter. This tartan has been commissioned by the present CEO Audrey Baxter, to commemorate their 150th Anniversary. The design is based on the Gordon Dress tartan sett owing to the Baxters family links with the Clan Gordon. Baxters wished to capture their heritage and surroundings of Speyside and the Highlands, and to include all aspects contributing to Baxters success. The colourations have been selected to reflect all these elements. Red and gold (represented by yellow) are Baxters corporate brand colours. Browns and greens represent their farmers and supply, blue of the River Spey and purple for the heather in their surroundings. This celebratory tartan will be used for all activities during their anniversary year, strengthening their family legacy and brand identity.

name: Borderlands
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with express written permission from International Tartans or ReTweed (a registered charity based in Eyemouth).
registrationNotes: The colours of this tartan are emblematic of the beautiful, wild countryside that links the Kingdoms of Scotland and England.

name: Bahanda, Sundeep (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Designed exclusively by Kinloch Anderson for Sundeep and Anshu Bahanda. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Permission required, please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd regarding use.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been commissioned by Anshu Bahanda as a 50th Birthday gift to her husband Sundeep, from herself and their two daughters Anunya and Amaara. The design is based on the City of London sett which has been the base of the Bahanda family for over 25 years and is also the place of birth of their two daughters. The grey base of the design keeps in line with the City of London tartan as this has remained a very important location and base for their family, and is also Mr Bahanda’s favourite colour. The green and red overlay has been taken from the City of Glasgow tartan to represent the birth city of Mr Bahanda and also the place of his education. Red is also Anshu Bahanda’s favourite colour. Whilst the saffron (represented by yellow) and green overlays are representative of the Indian flag and play homage to the Bahanda family roots, heritage and culture.

name: Saueressig, Derek (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan consists of green, grey, yellow, blue and black. These colours have personal significance for this family: green and first yellow indicates their family history with farming, and hunting; grey represents their family's knowledge and experience in engineering; black for their history and knowledge in the automotive industry. The blue and second yellow line are for their careers in the nuclear industry in the generation of electricity. Others with the Saueressig surname are welcome to wear this tartan.

name: Cameron, Mark (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designers. Prepared for weaving by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by two Camerons to celebrate family.

name: Last Drop Distillers, The

name: Deaf community (Scotland)
restrictions: Yes. Pease contact Deaf Link: [email protected] to use this tartan. This tartan is to be used without any misrepresention and/or any misuse or defamation of the design.
registrationNotes: The Deaf community (Scotland) tartan was designed by the Tayside Deaf community in widespread consultation with the Scottish grassroots Deaf community, the Scottish Council on Deafness and members of the Cross Party Group on Deafness. This tartan celebrates the wider Scottish Deaf community and Deaf Culture. Deaf community members were prominent in lobbying the Scottish Parliament in 2015 to have the British Sign Language Bill passed. The colours represent the Scottish identity with varying blues and whites for the Scottish flag. The sett is bold and direct to represent Deaf Culture. The Scottish Deaf community and beyond wish to celebrate their empowerment and a coming of age by having its own tartan. The tartan will provide a unique symbol of identity, instil greater self-confidence and make a statement to the hearing world – we are proud of both our heritage and growing emancipation. The Deaf community (Scotland) tartan will be an iconic moment in the history of the Deaf community at home and worldwide. This tartan represents significant empowerment by the Scottish Deaf community who have been isolated and marginalised for generations.

name: Deaf community
restrictions: Yes. Pease contact Deaf Link: [email protected] to use this tartan. This tartan is to be used without any misrepresention and/or any misuse or defamation of the design.
registrationNotes: The Deaf community tartan was designed by the Tayside Deaf community in consultation with the wider Scottish grassroots Deaf community, the Scottish Council on Deafness and members of the Cross Party Group on Deafness. It represents the Deaf community, language and culture within Scotland and across the world - with the use of strong bold colours and a strong geometric sett. The purple and violet represents creativity, pride, and independence. Pink represents friendship and approachability. Blue represents trust, loyalty, confidence and intelligence. Grey represents maturity and responsibility. The Deaf community in Scotland and beyond wish to celebrate this fact by having its own tartan for their community, culture and language. They are hoping it can be enjoyed across the UK and with all Deaf sign language users worldwide too. The tartan will provide a unique symbol of identity, instil greater self-confidence and make a statement to the hearing world – we are proud of our heritage. The Deaf community tartan will be an iconic moment in the history of the Deaf community at home and worldwide. This tartan represents significant empowerment by the Scottish Deaf community who have been isolated and marginalised for generations. It will form the basis of a social enterprise where Deaf people will produce and market tartan products to the worldwide Deaf community and supporters, and hearing users of the language.

The sett reflects the spirit of Catholic faith by using the liturgical colours of white, red, green and purple, with blue for the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of all and the waters of Baptism. Yellow (gold) represents the Papal colour and treasures of the Catholic faith. The block of green enclosing yellow and purple and bordered by blue represents the agricultural district of Werris creek and the spiritual formation through suffering and love, of the past 100 years. As life's journey continues into the new era, guided by the Holy Spirit of Peace, we seek to be strengthened and nourished by the real living presence of Jesus in the Holy Eucharist and His Redemptive Blood, represented by the White centre Red Cross, this red white red cross (three) also represents the Holy Trinity One God. The White block is bordered by Blue reminding us of the Maternal Love and intercession of Our Heavenly Mother, hence, honouring Her as Mary Mother of God.

The Live Your Life Day charity raises the awareness of blood cancer. The colours yellow, blue for aqua and orange reflect colours taken from the Live Your Life Day charity logo. The colour white in this tartan signifies the light of Franca’s life that still shines on.

Colours: The grey background represents the minerals and rocks on airless bodies. The bold white line represents ice or salt deposits on some bodies, for example, icy comets or ice in the permanently shadowed craters of the Moon. The black line represents organic materials on comets, in lunar polar craters and other bodies. The green line represents life eventually established on these bodies in the form of human exploration and settlement. The silver line represents the future technological transformation of some of these bodies by human settlement and industry. Anyone with an interest in this tartan may wear it.

name: Exploration of Titan
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Geoffrey (Tailor) Ltd.
registrationNotes: Designed on behalf of Charles Cockell, Professor of Astrobiology, Edinburgh University to celebrate science, exploration and outreach activities associated with Saturn's moon Titan. Colours: The brown background represents the brown haze that enshrouds the moon and is a product of its methane and hydrocarbon cycle. The dark brown bands represent the formation of complex hydrocarbons on the moon and their presence on the surface. They may also represent the dark methane lakes of the moon. The white line represents water ice and its role in geological cycles on the moon. The blue line represents the subsurface ocean or the formation of transient liquid water in impact events on the moon and the astrobiological significance of chemical reactions in such environments. The green line threaded through the dark hydrocarbon band reflects the interest in Titan as a place where prebiotic compounds may have formed, the precursors to life and the use of Titan to understand organic chemistry relevant to early life on Earth. It may also represent the interaction of life with Titan in the form of robotic and human exploration. Anyone with an interest in this tartan may wear it.

name: Scotland's War (1914-1919)
restrictions: Yes. Anyone can wear this tartan but the use in preparing goods must be approved by the Trustees of Scotland's War (1914-1919) Charity. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The 2,000+ pages on the Scotland’s War (1914-1919) Charity’s website at www.scotlandswar.co.uk reflect the significant sacrifices made by the Scottish people on the Home and Fighting Fronts, and the Scottish Diaspora, in the Great War. This is the Scotland’s War (1914-1919) Charity’s commemorative tartan. The dominant red colour represents the sacrifices that were made in the War. It is not generally understood that the War was not technically and legally over until the signing of the Treaty of Versailles in June 1919. Until then, there was an armistice which is a formal agreement of warring parties to stop fighting. The Scotland’s War (1914-1919) Project will continue until the centenary of the Treaty of Versailles in June 1919, which ended the War. Scotland’s War (1914-1919) was formally accepted for registration as a charity by the Scottish Charity Regulator on 17 November 2016 and the website hosts the contributions from 21 local authority partners in Scotland, and from individual contributors at home and abroad in the Scottish Diaspora. This followed the decision by the University of Edinburgh not to fund the original Heritage Lottery Funded project. Our work and legacy projects of the Charity is approached in a sensitive, respectful and ethical manner, and ensures that the Scotland’s War (1914-1919) commemorative initiatives are relevant to all ethnic, religious and secular parts of Scottish society.

registrationNotes: The word 'Kwok', regardless of how it is pronounced or written, has 10 strokes. It was the name of an ancient kingdom and also surname of its ruler, long before the arrival of 'Qin' the first dynasty of Imperial China. The meaning of 'Kwok' is castle or outer city wall that defends the city and hence it gives a feeling of solidity with a sense of strength in safeguarding its people. In this design, the colours and threads have been chosen to suggest aspects of the history of the Kwok family.

name: Scottos
designer: Haag, C J, Wellner, C & Schlager, C
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Benedictine Abbey ''Our Lady of the Scots''. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan represents the Benedictine Abbey “Our Lady of the Scots”, located in Vienna, Austria, which became known as the Scottish Abbey. The tartan’s name refers to the founding charter by Henry II, known as ‘Jasomirgott’ , who made it explicit that only monks from “Scotia major” were to be admitted: solos “elegimus scottos”. The Scottos tartan owes its pattern to the history and the architecture of the Scots Church: green, the ground colour, symbolises the Irish origins of the monks who founded the monastery; blue, red, and yellow stripes provide a contrast to the green; blue is the colour of the sky as well as of the coat of Mary: Our Lady of the Scots; red is associated with love and fire; yellow represents the light of the sun. In its proportions, the pattern follows the western façade of the Scots Church. The green corresponds to the naves, the red stripes mark the main nave, the broad blue stripes mirror the pillars on the façade, and the yellow stripes flank the church portal.

name: Digital Gold
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2018. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Designs Nos. 6104305, 6104304, 6104303.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created in recognition of the 21st century cryptocurrency revolution - specifically paying tribute to the first decentralised digital currency - bitcoin. Referred to as pure ‘Digital Gold’ the invention of Bitcoin and Blockchain Technology is said to be world-changing through the emergence of blockchain enabled Digital Assets (the future of currency worldwide), and the foundation layer of Web 3.0. Launched mysteriously in 2009 by an anonymous entity using the name Satoshi Nakamoto, Bitcoin was released into the public domain on Sourceforge the web-based service for open source developers. Designed to reflect the colours of pure gold, the geometry and thread-count within the tartan reference both the limited number of 21 million bitcoins, as well as the timestamp of the genesis date (the creation of bitcoin, and mining of the first primordial block) on 3rd January 2009. It is predicted in time, due to mainstream adoption and the ongoing emergence of cryptocurrencies and digital assets, bitcoin will mature into a gold-like store of value - Digital Gold.

registrationNotes: Designed by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor Ltd. This tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the British Airborne Forces. From its original formation in 1940 by Sir Winston Churchill during WWII, to present day Airborne Soldiers of the 16 Air Assault Brigade. The colours burgundy and light blue (known historically as ‘claret and Cambridge blue’) represent the iconic British Airborne Forces ‘Pegasus Flash’. The Pegasus Flash features ‘the slayer of enemies’ Bellerophon astride his winged steed Pegasus, originally introduced by General ‘Boy’ Browning in 1941/1942. The Pegasus, was an inclusive symbol, worn by parachute and glider formations in WWII. It was reintroduced in November 2015, Pegasus continues to represent all of the British Airborne Forces. Every man and woman in 16 Air Assault Brigade is an Airborne soldier, regardless of their cap-badge, whether they are delivered by parachute, air-landing or ground manoeuvre. From the age of mythology, with a reputation forged from the sacrifices of modern airborne warriors from 1940 onwards, it is recognised internationally as the defining symbol of British Airborne Forces. White signifies the parachute chords. Black is for continual respect for all fallen British Airborne Forces comrades.

registrationNotes: Designed by Margi Lawson of Tartan Manor Ltd. Approved and supported by the SSAFA, in celebration of all the great work they do. The colours are made up of the colours of the SSAFA logo, being dark blue, red, light blue and black. Black also represents respect for all fallen comrades and white symbolises hope for the future for all who need help. The SSAFA formerly known as ‘Soldiers, Sailors, Airmen and Families Association’, is a UK charity that provides lifelong support to serving men and women and veterans from the British Armed Forces and their families or dependents. The SSAFA is the UK's oldest national tri-service military charity. The mission of The SSAFA is to relieve need, suffering and distress amongst the Armed Forces, veterans and their families in order to support their independence and dignity.

name: Jekyll Island
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Betty Smith, a resident weaver on Jekyll Island, which is a 9 by 2 mile barrier island off the Georgia Coast in the Atlantic Ocean. The light yellow for the bright sun. Light green for the canopy from the 100-300 year old live oak trees shading the land. The black represents the trunks of the trees. name: Lost Villages of the Saint Lawrence
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to weave this tartan must seek the designer's permission.
registrationNotes: A tartan to represent the settlements along the Saint Lawrence river, known as the "Lost Villages". The elements of the tartan represent aspects of life in the six villages and three hamlets that were moved before the flooding to the newly created Seaway Towns of Ingleside and Long Sault. In 1958 the construction of the Moses Saunders Dam at Cornwall was completed, the coffer dams were dismantled and the inundation of the former villages began. The blue represents the Saint Lawrence river; the green stripes represent the forests and fields along the Saint Lawrence; the white represents the foaming rapids of the Long Sault; the charcoal represents the rocks and boulders over and around which the Saint Lawrence boiled in the rapids; the green stripes at their intersection form nine squares which represent the nine settlements which were inundated.

name: Schotte Clique 1947 Basel
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of active members of the Schotte Clique 1947 Basel association.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the ‘Schotte Clique 1947 Basel’, one of the oldest traditional carnival marching bands, which was founded in 1947 in the town of Basel in Switzerland. In 1947 a large department store in Basel had a Scottish week and sold clothing, goods and food of Scotland. The then newly found marching band used this as a theme for the carnival and everyone dressed in a Scottish manner and some played self-constructed bagpipes, hence the name Schotte Clique. In 1973 real bagpipe playing was introduced into the marching band. The pioneering members on bagpipes and snare and bass drums were so enthusiastic and successful that it triggered the formation of the ‘Pipes and Drums of Basel’ in 1978 and later pipes and drums bands all over Switzerland. The colours used are derived from: dark grey and white for Basel; white and red for the Swiss flag; blue, white, red and yellow as a tribute to Scotland, for both the Scottish flag and the Lion Rampant of Scotland.

registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the signature style, renowned mage and steadfast spirit of Sir Winston Churchill, who will always be remembered for leading Great Britain victorious through World War II. Churchill was an imposing figure who dominated with his wit, intelligence and dogged determination. Churchill battled for years with depression which he called ‘The Black Dog’. He understood the ‘power of image’ and what attire did for a man’s ‘inner confidence’. This tartan encompasses colours associated with Churchill’s famous defiant British Bulldog image: blue and white for his ‘Dickie Bow’; dark grey for his Homburg hat; light brown for his cigar; black for ‘The Black Dog’.

name: Bergslagen Flag
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of members of the Swedish association "Bergslagsflaggan" and other persons entitled to do so with permission from the association. Prepared for weaving by Andrew Elliot Ltd., Forest Mill, Selkirk, TD7 5EA.
registrationNotes: The Bergslagen flag tartan is named after the mining area in central Sweden. The colours of the tartan are taken from the unofficial flag for the area: black for iron ore; green for forests; orange for fire; blue for water and yellow for farming. Key numbers make up the design of the tartan signifying historical events and dates; 1434 the year of Engelbrecht's rebellion against the king Erik of Pomerania; 1444 the first time the word "bergslag" was used; 1907 the year the blast furnace in Löa was laid down and 2006 the year the flag of the Bergslag became a registered Swedish trademark.

These colours are found in the stained glass windows of the sanctuary, constructed in 1867, therefore yellow was included in the design to represent the gold from the windows. The three white stripes represent the Trinity. The design is intended for use by the choir members, having been inspired by visit to Glasgow Cathedral, Scotland.

name: Intrepid
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: 2O2O marks the 80th Anniversary of the creation of the Special Operations executive (SOE). The legendary SOE was created on July 22,1940. The Canadian connection to the SOE was derived both in terms of the Canadian personnel recruited to serve and the contribution of a training establishment in the form of Camp X. The site of Camp X, situated on the shores of Lake Ontario, is designated as lntrepid Park and named after a key figure in the establishment of the SOE, Canadian Sir William Stephenson (code name "Intrepid"). This tartan has been named after Sir William Stephenson and is aimed at honouring the legacy of the SOE and those who serve. Colours: tan pays homage to Canadian Special Operations Forces; green is a tribute to Canadian lntelligence; black signifies the history of covert operations; red signifies Canada and the sacrifice of the SOE and blue pays tribute to the sky and sea which supports SOE operations.

name: Blooming Poppy
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Tartans 4 Africa, South Africa.
registrationNotes: This Tartan has been designed to celebrate the flower Papaver Rhoeas (Poppy).Colours: red is for the petals of the red poppy and green is for the grass the poppy grows in.

name: Jacovides, Michael (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn by those authorised by the copyright holder Michael Jacovides or his appointed agents. Cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder Michael Jacovides or his appointed agents.
registrationNotes: Partially based on the Bruce tartan from the 1842 Vestiarium Scoticum — the Bruce family were long associated with the Airth estate, the family home of paediatric surgeon Mihalis (Michael) Jacovides. The green, orange and white of the Cyprus flag pays homage to Mihalis's homeland and the blue and white signify the Saltire for the Jacovides Family's new home in Scotland. The three blue lines on orange are for the three boys in the family - Alex, Lucas and Ethan, blue is also the boys’ favourite colour. Mihalis’ wife Cat’s favourite of purple, takes centre place on the red and her profession is represented by the green and white of the Royal College of Occupational Therapists.

name: Falklands, The
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holders The Falkland Islands Government or its appointed agents. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder The Falkland Islands Government or its appointed agents.
registrationNotes: This design is based on an old Stewart tartan in recognition of Scotland's Royal House of Stewart's long association with historic Falkland Palace, the ancient home of Scottish kings and the source of Viscount Falkland's title, whose name was first connected with the Islands in 1690. The focal point is the colours of the Union Jack centred in a vast ocean of blue, framed by the brilliant colours of the islands' most outstanding wildlife, the King Penguin. White also represents the Falklands' southern neighbour - the great Antarctic continent - and blue and red are for the early settlers, blue for the Scottish Saltire and red for the Welsh dragon. The red and black also serve as permanent memorials to the lives lost on all sides during territorial conflicts in the Southern Atlantic. This 21st century adaptation is a celebration of the Islands' unique history and heritage and its proud and inviolable status as a British overseas territory.

name: Moncrieff, Veronica (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Veronica Moncrieff, whose married name is Veronica Taylor. Mrs Taylor’s great-great-grandfather was a Moncrieff from Leith and her tartan in her maiden name is partially based on the Moncrieff family tartan. The red lines on black are for her two sons and the light blue ones are for her grandsons. The darker blue background to those three lines comprises 42 threads - the year of Mrs Taylor's birth.

name: Edinburgh Dog & Cat Home
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used by those authorised by the Edinburgh Dog & Cat Home. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or woven without the express permission of the copyright holder the Edinburgh Dog & Cat Home.
registrationNotes: John Kirk MRCVS was the manager of the Edinburgh Dog & Cat Home for the first 20 years of its existence and, fittingly, this design is based on ‘his’ tartan - the Maxwell. The Home was established in 1884, here remembered with 18 and 84 threads respectively in the two dark green squares. The bright green is the Home's characteristic colour and the grey band represents the Edinburgh and Lothian streets from where so many of the Home's dogs and cats have been saved. Finally, the red symbolises the warmth, comfort and safety that have surrounded the Home's animal guests since its foundation.

registrationNotes: Designed to honour the thousands of volunteers from all over the world, united in the long-term mission of The Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity in the field of health protection. Colour: red symbolises the heart in the Foundation's logo; grey represents the hard work and involvement of volunteers; yellow represents the joy of helping. White and red were included colours of the flag of Poland and white and blue were chosen to represent the involvement and support of the people of Scotland.

name: Elf

registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the elves or “hidden people” in the folklore of Iceland. Iceland’s landscape, filled with volcanoes, hot springs and avalanches and rocked by earthquakes, fuelled the imagination of ancient storytellers. Indeed, many Icelanders to this day, believe in elusive, mischievous and magical elves.

name: Upper Hunter
restrictions: Yes. The tartan must not be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any form without the express permission of the copyright holder or designer, the Aberdeen Highland Games Inc.
registrationNotes: This tartan is based on Campbell of Breadalbane (SRT #517) as the Upper Hunter region has had a connection with the M Campbell & Co stores based in the Upper Hunter Valley, a region of New South Wales, Australia, dating back to the late 1800s. Colours: green is for the lands where lucerne supports the dairy, beef and equine industries; blue is for the waters of the Hunter and Goulbourn river valleys; white is for the milk and cream that flowed throughout the valley to the butter, milk and cheese factories; black represents the black coal seams; purple represents the grapes of the viticultural industry; yellow is for the golden cereal and canola crops as well as the golden wool clips produced; red is for the Light Horseman of the Upper Hunter region and their horses who served in World War I.

registrationNotes: The legislative body of Nova Scotia, the Nova Scotia House of Assembly, is a centuries old institution which has met since October 2, 1758. restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 31 May 2020, registration number: 6091028.
registrationNotes: The Duke of Lancaster’s Regiment Tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to the Duke of Lancaster’s Regiment. Formed on 1st July 2006, by the amalgamation of the King's Own Royal Border Regiment, the King's Regiment and the Queen's Lancashire Regiment. With a strong history and proud tradition dating back to 1680 with the formation of the 4th, or King’s Own Regiment of Foot, raised by King Charles II. This tartan features the Duke of Lancaster’s Regimental Colours: royal blue, orange, deep green and maroon. Black is for continual respect for all fallen Duke of Lancaster’s comrades. The Duke of Lancaster's Regiment is the Infantry Regiment of the North West of England. They have two regular battalions and one reserve battalion. Fierce, strong and courageous, they are known as ‘The Lions of England’.

name: Royal Yorkshire Regiment
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. registrationNotes: The Royal Yorkshire Regiment tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Royal Yorkshire Regiment. The Royal Yorkshire Regiment is the product of a merger of three great Yorkshire Regiments; The Prince of Wales’s Own, The Green Howards and The Duke of Wellington’s, all with an incredible history of achievement. Collectively, the Yorkshire Regiment can trace its history back to 1685. The Royal Yorkshire Regiment was formed on 6th June 2006 and granted Royal status on 7th April 2023, they are known as Yorkshire’s Warriors. This tartan has been created with the following significant colours connected to the Royal Yorkshire Regiment, featured in their Tactical Recognition Flash: green, red, black and the white of their White Yorkshire Rose. Black is also for continual respect for all fallen Yorkshire Regiment comrades.

registrationNotes: The tartan for the Swedish hickory golf player and club maker Ingvar Ritzén is based on the Fife District tartan whose roots go back to the time of Old Tom Morris, the legendary St. Andrews’ golfer and the father of modern greenkeeping. In this design, the greens and fairways are represented by the dark green and dark blue represents the Ritzén’s holiday base on the Firth of Clyde. registrationNotes: The Royal Military Academy Sandhurst Tartan celebrates all past, present and future officer cadets, personnel, and achievements attached to the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. The Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (RMAS), commonly known simply as ‘Sandhurst’, is the British Army Officer initial training centre, formed in 1947. And the traditions on which the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst is founded go back over two centuries. During training, all officer cadets learn to live by the academy’s motto: ‘Serve to Lead’ as featured on the Sandhurst Flag. The colours featured in this tartan are colours from the Sandhurst Flag; Red, Yellow and Light Blue. And Black is for continual respect for all fallen who have passed through Sandhurst. The Royal Military Academy Sandhurst is the home of the British Army Officer and many form overseas countries. Newly trained Officers leave knowing they have excelled at one of the world's most revered military training academies.

name: Maligne Lake
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Patrick King Woollen Company. Written permission must be sought from Patrick King Woollen Company to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: On June 20, 1907, Mary Schaffer, her best friend and two guides set off on an expedition they had planned for months. Their 1907 explorations shaped the future of Jasper and their 1908 expedition brought Maligne Lake and Spirit Island to the attention of the World. Accounts of what Mary Schaffer and other early explorers saw has woven a legend of Canadian wilderness that to this day compels people to seek it out. Stories boast Maligne Lake has some of the most spectacular scenery found anywhere. The colours chosen in this tartan reflect that scenery.

registrationNotes: The Spirit of the Titanic Halifax tartan is a tribute to those who perished during the tragic event. The threadcount is based on the date of the sinking of the Titanic 15/04/1912. Colours: black represents the hull of the Titanic; blue represents the North Atlantic Ocean; white and red represents the White Star Line and the Canadian Maple Leaf for the rescue and recovery efforts; yellow representing gold, consisting of 8 threads, is dedicated to the brave band members that continued to play in an effort to calm and comfort the passengers as the ship was sinking.

registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the NASA Apollo 11 spaceflight and the first moon landing by the Apollo Lunar Module ‘Eagle’ on the 20th July 1969. It also celebrates the first humans to walk on the moon, Commander Neil Armstrong and Module Pilot Edwin ‘Buzz’ Aldrin on the 21st July 1969. ‘Columbia’ Command Module Pilot Michael Collins flew in lunar orbit for over 21 hours until the return of his fellow astronauts when they then safely returned to Earth on the 24th July 1969. 50 years on and NASA still reaches for the stars with an ever increasing inclusion and diversity of astronauts, command and support staff.

name: James Watt Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with permission from Inverclyde Council.
registrationNotes: James Watt (19 January 1736 – 25 August 1819) was a Scottish inventor, mechanical engineer and chemist, who was born in Greenock. He improved on Thomas Newcomen’s 1712 Newcomen steam engine with his Watt steam engine in 1781, which was fundamental to the changes brought by the Industrial Revolution in both his native Great Britain and the rest of the world. He developed the concept of horsepower, and the SI unit of power, the watt, was named after him. The James Watt tartan was designed as part of a year of commemorative events in 2019 held by Inverclyde Council to mark the bicentenary of his death in August 1819. Colours: dark grey represents industrial works and tools; light grey represents steam; orange represents the signage and colours within the James Watt Institution and blue has been included to represent Inverclyde Council.

registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the Bay of Fundy, located on the eastern coast of Canada. Blue represents the dark waters of the bay; yellow represents gold, taken from New Brunswick's provincial flag; dark blue represents Nova Scotia's flag; white represents the waves; red represents the many lighthouses that dot the coast of the Bay and the green is representative of the men and women who earn a living fishing from the waters of the Bay of Fundy.

name: Culross
restrictions: Yes. Restricted tartan to be sold exclusively through Lindsey Marchant at the Greengate Gallery Culross. Please contact Lindsey regarding use: [email protected] Prepared for weaving by Claire Hunter, Taffled Threads.
registrationNotes: The tartan’s design and colours have been inspired by the historic and picturesque royal burgh of Culross, in West Fife. This ancient village, steeped in heritage and folklore, was founded by St Serf in the 6th century and has long been a place of pilgrimage, with the ruins of the Cistercian Abbey. In the 17th century, it became famous as a bustling trading port under the direction of Sir George Bruce, and much of its unique architecture and cobbled streets stem from this era. The blues and greens of the tartan reflect its stunning estuary location on the Firth of Forth, while the orange representing gold, red, brown and black shades were chosen to echo the various distinctive architectural features of the village, including the famous ochre Culross Palace. The Culross tartan brings together these inspirational elements to reflect the village’s unique Scottish heritage.

name: Red Lichtie Spitfire (EP121)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2018. The Montrose Air Station Heritage Centre has been granted full use of the Red Lichtie Spitfire (EP121) tartan indefinitely for its commercial use, in order to raise funds to support the museum for generations to come. All further weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6085115. Red Lichtie ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3004768.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created to pay tribute to the Spitfire, the flagship aircraft of the RAF, and specifically Red Lichtie Spitfire EP121. During WWII the people of Arbroath started a ‘Spitfire Fund’ to raise £5,000 and purchase a Spitfire to help with the war effort. They succeeded in this and a MkVb Spitfire was built at Castle Bromwich Aircraft Factory. On 24th May 1942 Spitfire EP121 was delivered to the RAF at Burtonwood and it was named the ‘Red Lichtie’ after the people of Arbroath who purchased it. The tartan’s creation date and registration date commemorate the 100th anniversary year of the RAF, 1st April 2018 to 1st April 2019, and in so doing also recognises the iconic fighter plane and its key role in winning the Battle of Britain. Colours and geometry: the tartan’s asymmetric design of green and grey represents the spitfire’s camouflage; the red, white, blue and yellow stripes form a representation of the historic RAF roundel and the tail liveries on the aircraft. The single red stripe in the tartan becomes a mark of respect for the ‘Red Lichtie’, which ended its service on the 26th June 1943 suffering from an engine cut on approach causing it to stall and crash. The pilot survived.

The ancient DeForest connection with France is shown by the French flag - the Tricolour - whose colours are also in the Brim-DeForest coat of arms (with gold) and the Stars and Stripes of the Brim-DeForest’s home country. registrationNotes: The Age of Sail was an era where tall ships ruled the waterways, where timber was king and the oceans the highways of the world. This tartan embodies the essence of this era. name: Forth Bridges, The
restrictions: Yes. This design has been exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson Ltd for Transport Scotland/The Forth Bridges, restricted availability. registrationNotes: Commissioned in recognition of, and to celebrate, The Forth Bridges, Scotland, being the only location worldwide to have a transport bridge constructed in each of the 3 past centuries. The widest red bands count 18 representing the completion of the Forth Rail Bridge in 1890. The design features the 3 colours of each of The Forth Bridges, also featured in the brand logo representing this iconic location and visitor destination.

The IAOMS Foundation provides educational and training opportunities for OMF surgeons worldwide. The association represents more than 140countries.

registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for the Vince Bel Mori brand. It was designed to represent friendship and family for the business.

registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Frédéric Hardy, Elisabeth de Romanet and their family. The design was chosen to represent the structure of the family: three green lines for their three sons, two red lines for their two girls and a white line to represent them both as parents. The colours in the design are of significance to the family and their history.

name: Ever Forward, Ever Onward
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be reproduced in any form without written permission and licence from Tarleton State University. The design right for this tartan is held by Tarleton State University under the U.S. Copyright Act-U.S.C. 17. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: Tarleton State University was founded in 1899 and recently celebrated its centennial as a founding member of the Texas A&M University System. This tartan was designed to celebrate their history, traditions and spirit. The tartan's traditional pattern, named "Ever Forward, Ever Onward" to honor the Tarleton fight song, is a nod to the school's rich history and vibrant future as it moves closer to becoming the premier student-focused university in Texas and beyond. The six white crossing lines on the purple field represent the university's core values: tradition, integrity, civility, excellence, leadership and service.

name: Ville de Sainte-Julie
registrationNotes: La Ville de Sainte-Julie is located on the South Shore of Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Founded in 1851, the Parish of Sainte Julie retained its agricultural character until the mid-1960’s, and became a city in 1971. Since then, it has grown substantially, both in terms of population and urban development. Colours: green represents the abundance of local vegetation, trees, and parks; purple represents the blue iris, the floral emblem of the city; grey reflects the city’s urban growth and strong foundations; yellow represents fertile agricultural lands, joy of living, and generosity and white embodies all local families, native or new, as well as future generations. The tartan is a mirror of the social fabric and distinctive character of this community.

name: Soutar, P (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Paul Soutar and his immediate family. Permission to weave must be sought from Paul Soutar. This design must only be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed to mark the silver anniversary celebration of Paul and Karen Soutar using colours of personal significance.

name: Feng, Mingli, & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Mingli Feng and his family.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Mingli Feng and his family using colours of personal significance.

name: Clairbaux, Laurent (Personal)
