registrationNotes: A personal tartan using colours of significance for the family and their history.

name: Batusan, Jose Sakhan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer and owner.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Jose Sakhan Batusan.

name: Mylne, Alfred (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed in memory of Alfred Mylne and his uncle, also Alfred. They both designed beautiful wooden yachts which still sail worldwide and the colours were chosen to represent the sea, timber, tan and white sails. A touch of green has been added as a hull colour they both admired.

name: Tokyogakkan High School
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with approval from DC Dalgliesh Ltd. DC Dalgliesh Ltd
registrationNotes: The Tokyogakkan High school was established in 1979 at Chiba prefecture and this tartan designed to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the school. The colours have been inspired by the school‘s crest “Citrus Tachibana”, white from the flower and orange from the fruit. Citrus Tachibana has been known and loved in Japan as a plant of the icon of long life and prosperity.

name: Mortimer, Rachael and Natalie (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed as a wedding present from Natalie to Rachael celebrating their Scottish heritage and to share with their family and future generations. The colours, yellow and purple, are their favourites and reflects the colour scheme of their wedding.

name: Wilkinson, Emma & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the designer and her family. Others wishing to use this tartan should seek the designer's permission. Prepared for weaving by Scottish mills. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The design takes inspiration from the MacDonald of the Isles tartan which is traditionally associated with the name Wilkinson and celebrates the family’s military history. Colours: black and white are from the Shepard tartan; dark green represents military uniforms; purple represents the achievements and royalty - relating to the medals won in both the first and second world wars by Emma’s great grandparents and grandparents.

name: Takaoka YEG - Ichinomiya YEG
registrationNotes: Takaoka Young Enterprise Group formed a friendship alliance with Ichinomiya Young Enterprise Group in 2008, and celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2018. The tartan was created to commemorate the event.

name: Texas Woman's University
restrictions: Yes. May not be woven without written permission and licence from Texas Woman's University. Texas Woman's University reserves all rights related to this tartan, including, but not limited to apparel, merchandising and digital rights. The design right for this tartan is held by Texas Woman's University under the U.S. Copyright Act - U.S.C. 17. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: Texas Woman's University (TWU), located in Denton, Texas, is the largest public institution primarily for women in the United States. The university was founded in 1901 and enrolls more than 15,000 male and female students in a variety of programs. Students in Fashion Design were asked to design a tartan for TWU. Five finalists were selected in Spring 2018, and students, alumni, employees and friends of TWU voted. This winning design incorporates the university colours maroon and white. Texas Woman's University's first graduate, Beulah Kincaid, was the inspiration for the pattern.

name: Brady, Caitlin – Grayheck, Jim Wedding (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed for the marriage celebration Caitlin Brady and Jim Grayheck. The colours represent the families coming together and includes colours featured at the wedding.

name: City of Geneva (Ohio)
registrationNotes: This design is based around the city of Geneva, Ohio's deep roots in the grape industry. The colours were selected to represent grapes and wine produced by the region and its impact on Geneva’s economy and culture. The blue represents Lake Erie and the red represents both the pride Geneva residents have in their school sports teams and the bravery of the first responders and civil servants.

name: Bordeaux Pipe Band
designer: Johnston, William & de la Landelle, Yann
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Bordeaux Pipe Band. Others should seek the band's permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the links between Bordeaux and Scotland. The Bordeaux Pipe Band performs to promote the Celtic culture and Scottish music that unites Bordeaux with Scotland. It will be worn by band members at international meetings, performances and commemorations. The band previously played for the French Rugby Federation at the Stade de France in Paris for the Six Nations on February 23, 2019. Colours: the blues represent the coast and sea skirting our territory: red represents grapes and vines and yellow represents the gold from the coat of arms of Bordeaux.

name: Rawden, Jack and Katy (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This design has been exclusively designed for Jack and Katy Rawden by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Restricted availability. Please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the wedding of Jack and Katy in the Scottish Borders, and to continue their Scottish family identity for future generations. It is based on the Spirit of Yorkshire sett due to the historical connection of the surname Rawden to the West Ridings of Yorkshire. The colours were chosen to reflect Jack and Katy’s love of the water, the mountain regions of Scotland, and their family connections to the Navy.

name: AS KNOW AS
restrictions: Yes. Use is restricted to AS KNOW AS certified products.
registrationNotes: AS KNOW AS is an apparel company founded in 1989. This tartan has been designed to celebrate the 30th anniversary of AS KNOW AS and will be used on various products for its new collection.

name: General Maczek Academy of Polish Language
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of General Maczek Academy of Polish Language.
registrationNotes: Designed to commemorate General Stanislaw Maczek, Commander of 1st Polish Armoured Division and Commander of the Polish Forces in the UK, who is the patron of the school. He was a significant leader in the 20th century, who took part in both world wars and afterwards settled in Edinburgh, where he died at the age of 102. The colours were chosen to represent General Mazek’s army career with orange for the emblem of the 1st Armored Division and green for the soldiers’ uniforms. Red from the Polish flag and blue from the Scottish flag sit together in the design to represent the school’s special relationship between Poland and Scotland, as well as, the two homelands for General Maczek.

name: Twechar Village
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The Scottish village of Twechar, located in East Dunbartonshire, has a strong history in coal mining and service in the armed forces. The colours have been selected to remind current and former residents of their home and proud history. The people of Twechar generally live their entire life in the village, and those who do leave are known to call Twechar their home and return to the village when they can.

name: Lister, J (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed for and on behalf of Mr John Lister, as a tribute to his love of Scotland and in recognition of his accomplishments whilst living there.

name: An Talla
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with the approval of a director of Jacobite Cruises.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the new Jacobite Cruises development at Dochgarroch on the banks of Loch Ness, Scotland, in the heart of the Dochfour Estate, which has been owned by the Baillie family for over 500 years. This design was inspired by the Baillie (William Wilson) tartan sett. The house and livery colours of Jacobite Cruises are represented in the An Talla tartan; Purple for the ships' hulls; Brown for the traditional funnels and Yellow echoes the ships' livery. Blue represents the huge expanse of water and Brown represents the shingle shoreline of the loch. An Talla is Gaelic for hall or meeting place, the function of the new development at Dochgarroch.

name: Bishopton Rugby
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Bishopton Rugby Club members. May only be woven with permission from Bishopton Rugby Club. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Bishopton Rugby Club.

name: Sharkey, John & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Sharkey family.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created for John Sharkey and his family, and to commemorate the first of many family weddings. The Sharkey family have ancestry which can be traced back to the Murray and Maclean clans and also Ireland. It has been designed to represent the heritage with base colours of black, green, blue and purple representing heather. The colours were chosen to represent the family’s connection with Scotland and various connections to education, sports and business over the years.

name: Spirit Of Le Mans Racing (Reverse)

registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the annual sports car races in Le Mans, France, and in particular those races that took place during the 1960s. This tartan design is linked to the Spirit of Le Mans (STR ref #12079) and Spirit of Le Mans Racing (STR ref #12202) tartans.

registrationNotes: The Vegan tartan has been designed to celebrate vegan living. Using earthy colours the symmetry and equal representation indicates the importance of balance in life.

The society’s objective is to maintain and foster interest in Scottish national life and to promote charitable and benevolent objects that further understanding of Scottish culture.

To commemorate the 1986 wedding of Ranjit Gill and his Welsh wife Nona, the royal blue bands have 86 threads. The five faint lines on that blue represent a musical score and are for their children’s love of music and a reminder of the Five Ks of the Khalsa Sikhs.

registrationNotes: Designed for Georgia Southern University which was founded in 1906 with the commitment to build a college that would prepare students to succeed and would celebrate their heritage. Since then, the school has changed and grown, but one thing has remained the same - Georgia Southern has always been and always will be a school rich in history and rooted in tradition. The design - which incorporates the University’s colours of blue, white and gold - was chosen by students, faculty and alumni who will proudly carry on the new tradition of donning the tartan.

registrationNotes: Designed to portray the colours and beauty of Autumn in the Highlands as part of a seasonally based set of tartans. The set of tartans have been designed to consolidate the company’s Scottish roots while serving as a visible expression reflecting the heritage of its owners and their passion for Scotland. The colours represent a walk into the Highlands on a typical Autumn day but maintain the consistent connection to the main theme within the company’s Rablogan tartan: purple for the heather and thistle; green for the forests and woodlands and red to characterize the essence of the Highlands flowing in the veins of those wearing it.

restrictions: Yes. It is available for use by all Fergusons, Australian Scots and all admirers of Ferguson the Astronomer. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any commercial form without the express permission oif the copyright holder James Ferguson, his agents,heirs or successors.
registrationNotes: Based on and inspired by the plaid reported to be in the Kingussie Museum in Scotland and said to have been made for James Ferguson, the self-taught Scottish Astronomer (1710-1776). The colours have been changed to reflect Australia and to incorporate those of the Eureka Flag.

name: Haymes, David and Hockema, Rachel (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the relationship & marriage David Haymes and Rachel Hockema. It uses colours of significance to family and friends in honour of their support to the couple.

name: Epilepsy

registrationNotes: Inspired by epileptic sufferer Bonnie Pool of Glasgow, the designer's granddaughter. The design incorporates two shades of purple, the colour broadly adopted by Epilepsy organisations and charities, and blue and white to represent the Scottish saltire and the tartan place of origin.

name: Carrington Dean
restrictions: Yes. Please seek permission from Siobhan Mackenzie Limited and Carrington Dean to wear/use/weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for Scottish company Carrington Dean to play homage to their roots.

name: Mule
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for the company Mule Resophonic Guitars based in Michigan. The design was inspired by the owner Matt Eich’s childhood and growing up in Alma, Michigan where the city motto was "Highland, U.S.A" and it held a large Highland festival every memorial day weekend.

name: Cormican, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Sean Cormican.
registrationNotes: Designed in 2019 for the Cormican family coming from the Tipperary and Galway area of Ireland. Incorporates rich greens to indicate the Emerald Isle, red from the family colours, as well as blue, white and yellow drawn from the county flags of both Tipperary and Galway.

name: Nessie
restrictions: Yes. Copyright Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Produced by House of Edgar for the exclusive use of The Promotional Warehouse Ltd. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: Created for Loch Ness monster lovers all over the world. Colours: dark blue for Loch Ness; green for the hills and glens surrounding Loch Ness; white for the clouds reflecting on the loch; blue for the skies of a sunny highland day and the dark colour of Nessie's skin.

name: Bourda, Julien (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Bourda family unless permission is granted by the family. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Julien Bourda using colours to represent the land and the sea of Brittany and colours of personal significance to the family.

name: Pillsbury, James (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for James Pillsbury designed as gift from son Colin Pillsbury. The colours selected are the colours of James’ alma mater, University of Oregon.

name: AttackIQ
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of AttackIQ. May only be woven with approval from the CEO of AttackIQ.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for AttackIQ, an enterprise security company. The colours are connected to their corporate mission: black represents the growing cyberspace which security defenders operate in; red represents the ‘Red team’, employees who attempt to hack into a network using common hacker techniques, with the intent to understand how effective the security program is; blue represents the ‘Blue Team’, who are the traditional security team, responsible for deploying, managing, and auditing the security program to meet the security goals of the organization; purple represents a new organizational construct where the Red and Blue teams work collaboratively together, using their knowledge of how hackers operate to drive and shape the security program delivery and white represents the “white hat” hacker ethos – always focus on discovery of security weakness for purpose of better security.

name: Nursing Now - Edinburgh Nursing Studies
designer: Marshall, Elaine, Chandler, Kate & Duffy, Georgia
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the permission of Nursing Now or the Registrant of the tartan.
registrationNotes: The design was inspired by the national uniform for nurses in Scotland. These colours are worn by every nurse, healthcare assistant and student nurse in Scotland. This tartan is intended to be used as a symbol of identity, kinship and solidarity for nurses.

name: Queanbeyan
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills & Ingles Buchan.
registrationNotes: Designed for the City of Queanbeyan, Australia. The colours are taken from the city’s coat of arms and the flag of Queanbeyan. A combination of all the colours within the tartan embraces the multicultural community and the traditional owners.

name: McDonald-Darkes, I and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the family’s history. The family is descended from the McDonalds of Ross-shire and other families including Urquhart, McCombie, Matheson, and Mclean from the Black Isle and nearby surrounding area in Ross-shire in the Scottish Highlands.

name: US Naval Academy

registrationNotes: This is a tartan for the United States Naval Academy and will be used for a variety of their sports teams and clubs. The colours were inspired by the US Naval Academy song: Now colleges from sea to sea, May sing of colours true, But who has better right than we, To hoist a symbol hue: For sailors brave in battle fair, Since fighting days of old, Have proved the sailor’s right to wear, The Navy Blue & Gold.

name: Woodland, David and Garrett & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the marriage of David Smallwood and Garrett Wentland using colours from the Duncan tartan from David's mother's heritage and the Armenian flag colours from Garrett's mother's heritage.

name: Highland Celebration

registrationNotes: Inspired by the clan tartans, this tartan celebrates the Highlands and the colours found there.

name: Ordinariate, The

designer: Brown, Jonathan Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Written authority to weave this tartan must be sought from from Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: On the 55th Birthday of Prince Edward, Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II bestowed upon him the title of The Earl of Forfar, a title which dates back to 1661. To mark his inaugural visit to the town the Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd were commissioned to create a Tartan to celebrate The Earl’s first official visit. The weave is based on the existing ‘Forfar’ tartan, created by the Strathmore Woollen Company in 2004 – the colours of that weave being based on the Forfar Coat of Arms. It was felt important that the new Tartan should share some of the characteristics of the existing design with the geometry undergoing only minor refinements.

name: Rifles Regiment
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 31 May 2020, registration number: 6091027.
registrationNotes: The Rifles Regiment Tartan celebrates all past, present and future personnel and achievements attached to The Rifles Regiment. The Rifles Regiment formed in 2007 when four of the most famous Regiments in the British Army merged together into a modern and exciting large regiment optimised for 21st Century warfare. The amalgamation of The Royal Green Jackets, The Devonshire and Dorset Light Infantry, the Light Infantry, and the Royal Gloucestershire, Berkshire and Wiltshire Light Infantry was formed in the crucible of operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. The Rifles Regiment holds an incredible 913 battle honours and a world record 117 Victoria Crosses (VC). The Rifles motto is: "Celer et Audax" meaning "Swift and Bold". This tartan has been created with the following significant colours connected to The Rifles Regiment, featured in their Tactical Recognition Flash: Green, Red and Black. White represents the bugle, featured in their crest. Black is also for continual respect for all fallen Rifles comrades.

registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for The Security Goons as a representation of their long and storied history of being enforcers and protectors. As the numbers have grown it was decided that a single tartan was needed to unite all members across the world. The pattern was designed with input from multiple members, with colors representing the different aspects of the group and to represent how the group view themselves as a family. Red and Black are the primary colors. Red representing the blood shed by past and future members, black to represent the darkness we were born from, blue and grey to represent the mighty blows the Security Goon will take to protect the weak and innocent.

name: Street Performers
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any other commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders – Nick Broad ([email protected]) and Kate Mior ([email protected]) – or their authorised agents, heirs or successors.
registrationNotes: This tartan is dedicated to the street performers, and anyone who performs in public spaces for voluntary donations, around the world. The idea was conceived by street performer Kate Mior in conjunction with the Busking Project. The international community themselves agreed on which colours would best represent their culture; black and red are the primary colours, symbolising traditional colours of street theatre costuming; the red also nods to the performer's creative passion and fearlessness; gold represents good fortune and heavy hats in donations; and grey and white were chosen to represent the pavement on which performers do their shows. The grey threads number 24, symbolising how, at any given time of day, a street performer is entertaining an audience somewhere in the world. The adjacent black blocks are comprised of 100 threads, one for each performance perceived busking wisdom suggests are needed to be proficient.

name: Hamish Henderson Commemorative
registrationNotes: The Hamish Matters Committee commissioned this tartan to commemorate Hamish Henderson (1919 – 2002) celebrating the centenary of his birth and his connections with Blairgowrie. Hamish Henderson was a Scottish poet, songwriter, communist, soldier and intellectual. The Hamish Matters Festival, held every year in Blairgowrie, remembers this important man through various folk concerts and activities throughout November. Hamish was an avid collector of stories and poems, from local folklore to the sound of the Travellers in Blairgowrie and East Perthshire. The colours: graphite greys, silvers and black represent the penmanship and recordings of this remarkable man; browns and golden hues represent Hamish's favourite tipple; the greens are a nod to the Henderson tartans and the raspberry red is to represent the berry fields when Hamish recorded the famous Belle Stewart and the song "The Berry Fields o Blair".

The blue and green have been selected to represent Mark’s family ties to both the Army and Navy. Purple has been added to highlight his family’s long-standing connection with the Highlands of Scotland. The two red lines represent Mark’s two children and the gold count of 4 refers to Mark’s position as Captain of a yacht.

name: Iowa State University

registrationNotes: The tartan design is the winning student entry for the competition sponsored by the Department of Apparel, Events and Hospitality Management at Iowa State University (ISU) which was founded in 1858. The contest challenged students from the department to design a tartan representative of Iowa State University brand in a creative and marketable manner using the University’s official colours, Cardinal red and gold. Students, faculty, staff and alumni participated in an online voting system to choose the winning design. The tartan represents a sense of belonging and reminds people of their roots at Iowa State University.

name: Royal Navy (Official)
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 31 May 2020, registration number: 6091024.
registrationNotes: The Royal Navy (Official) Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Royal Navy since its formation. The history of the United Kingdom is the history of the Royal Navy. As an island nation the sea has always been a vital factor, it is the means of people arriving from overseas, a barrier to invaders and a highway for trade. The Royal Navy has transformed from wood to steel in successfully protecting our nation’s interests with pride. The dark navy blue of this tartan represents the Royal Navy Uniform; gold reflects the embroidery of the Royal Navy Head-dress; white as is featured in many elements of the Royal Navy Uniform; light Blue depicting the colourings of the famous striped style of the Middy Top and black is for continual respect for all fallen Royal Navy comrades.

registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to commemorate Scottish band Frightened Rabbit's album "The Midnight Organ Fight". The album was released in 2008 and its 10 year anniversary was celebrated in 2018. Since the album's release it has gained a high level of critical and public acclaim. In 2018 the band's singer, Scott Hutchison took his own life and this tartan celebrates his music and talent.

registrationNotes: Designed for the new school, Bertha Park High School, Perth. The design is a variation of Bertha Park High School Junior (SRT #12605), and is also based on the word Bertha with the number of threads representing each letter's position in the alphabet.

name: Highton
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the use of the Camberwell School (Melbourne, Australia) community, past and present. Prepared for weaving by D C Dalgliesh Tartan Mill Anyone who wishes to reproduce this tartan must seek Michael Koswig's written approval and accept any commercial conditions therein. registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Michael Koswig and named after the original music school building at Camberwell Grammar School, Melbourne Australia, where he and his sons completed their schooling. Having taken up the bagpipes as an adult, Michael has played at the school's ANZAC Day service as well as some church services and thought it would be fitting to design an appropriate tartan to wear using the school's colours.

name: Adam Smith's Panmure House
restrictions: Yes. Copyright Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Produced by House of Edgar and intended for the exclusive use of Edinburgh Business School. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Requests to use this tartan must go through: Edinburgh Business School Heriot Watt University Panmure House
registrationNotes: Between 1778 and 1790, Adam Smith lived and worked at Panmure House. During this time, he revised the final editions of his two master works The Theory of Moral Sentiments and The Wealth of Nations. He also regularly hosted the finest minds of the Scottish Enlightenment, who met here to debate and define the most pressing issues of the day. In honour of Smith’s work and his time at Panmure House, we have created the Adam Smith’s Panmure House Tartan. Colours: blue features on the Kirkcaldy coat of arms and the Heriot-Watt crest; green is from the idea of restoration and revival of the House, and runs through the tulipwood panelling of Panmure itself; grey is from the Scottish Gaelic 'glas' as Margaret Smith’s maiden name was Douglas; red and gold represent the Kirkcaldy coat of arms, and are both featured within the Smith and Douglas tartans.

name: Purdue University
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from Purdue University Trademark and Licensing. The design right for the Purdue University Tartan is held by Purdue University under the U.S. Copyright Act 17 U.S.C. Formal Registration is pending
registrationNotes: Founded in 1869, as a land grant university in the state of Indiana, Purdue University has become a world renowned university with emphasis on science, technology, and engineering. Past students include Nobel laureates in Chemistry (1979, 2010) and Physics (1952) and one-third of NASA's space flight missions have had a Purdue graduate on board. The tartan colours include: Purdue's school colours of gold and black; dark grey lines representing the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) sports offered at Purdue; black representing Purdue's astronauts including Neil Armstrong and Eugene Ceman; gold representing the campus fraternities and white representing the year 1912 when the University’s official song "Hail Purdue" was written by James Morrison and was set to music by Edward Wotawa.

name: Breckenridge, Patti and Wood, Sharna & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by Mrs Patti Breckenridge (Woodson) and her daughter, Dr Sharna Wood for their immediate family and relations after being inspired by a visit to Scotland. The colours in this design are symbolic and meaningful to the family.

name: Criterion, The
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Criterion, a traditional Scottish pub in St Andrews. The colours were inspired by the interior and exterior of the pub. It was designed to be used in the establishment and to create merchandise to promote the pub, St Andrews and Scotland. The pub seats have been upholstered with the tartan and the owners have made kilts, waist coats, bow ties & ties.

registrationNotes: This Tartan was designed, based from the Maclean Clan Hunting tartan, to celebrate the creation of a new family. Nathan and his wife were married in May 2019 after having been together for 7 years and having had two children. Colours: purple was the theme of their wedding and blue is based on the water around Devon and Cornwall where they had family home.

name: White House Historical Association
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland
restrictions: Yes. This is a copyright design assigned to the White House Historical Association, P.O. Box 27624 Washington, D.C. 20038
registrationNotes: The White House Historical Association tartan was created to promote the history of the Scottish stone masons who were instrumental in the building of the White House. Each color represents a key aspect of the White House: blue symbolises the Bellange furniture of the Blue Room, decorated in 1817 during the James Monroe presidency; green represents the Green Room, decorated in 1818 by James Monroe; red symbolises the Red Room, which was furnished with bold red silks during the James Polk administration in 1845; Grey represents the Scottish stone works, including the famous "Double Scottish Rose" that adorns the White House and white represents the White House as a whole.

registrationNotes: This Tartan is designed for the descendants of Cumberland Dugan I, who emigrated from Coleraine, Ireland to North America, settling in Baltimore in 1767. Colours: yellow and blue represent the family colours and the family’s historical ties to the US Navy; light and dark blue represent the ocean which brought Cumberland to the New World and upon which he established a successful shipping company; green represents Ireland and the black and red lines to honour those who were lost before their time.

The colours were inspired by her time both in Singapore and Australia and represent the greens and blues of the oceans and the warm glow of sunshine. Having returned to Scotland she wished to include this experience as part of her family legacy, in the form of a tartan.

name: Order of Vitéz
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn or used by those authorised by the Captain General of the Order of Vitéz , HIRH Archduke Joseph Karl, Archduke of Austria, Royal Prince of Hungary, his heirs and successors as Head of the Hungarian Palatine line of the House of Habsburg-Lothringen, or those to whom he may delegate such authority: who will primarily require to be duly admitted & sworn members of the Order of Vitéz.
registrationNotes: This tartan was presented to Captain General of the Order of Vitéz, Archduke Joseph Karl, Royal Prince of Hungary, Hereditary Palatine of Hungary by Sheriff George Way of Plean, OStJ, Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts etc., in recognition of the humanitarian activities of the Order of Vitéz (Vitézi Rend), and in commemoration of the forthcoming 100th Anniversary of the Order which was founded 20 August 1920 in the Kingdom of Hungary as an noble analog to a hereditary knighthood. The Order of Vitéz now is a dynastic order of knighthood belonging to the Hungarian Palatine line of the House of Habsburg-Lothringen and the Order’s first member, Archduke Joseph August of Austria, Royal Prince of Hungary, Palatine of Hungary (1872-1962), was the great-grandfather of the present Captain General. The design incorporates the colours of the insignia of the Order and includes the red, white and green of Hungary’s national flag. The black band to the left of the flag has 19 threads, the block to the right has 20 - commemorating 1920, the foundation of the Order of Vitéz. The large blue blocks have 100 threads to mark the 2020 centenary of the Order.

name: Red Red Rose
restrictions: Yes. May be worn by customers of Lochcarron of Scotland. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed in celebration of Chinese New Year and Burns Night both on the 25th of January 2020. Chinese New Year is the most important and widely celebrated festival in the Chinese calendar, whilst Robert Burns Night commemorates Scotland’s renowned poet. Festivities take place across the globe to mark both these occasions. The Burns Check, named after Scotland’s National Bard, is woven in a new red colourway - a symbolic colour representing joy and happiness in Chinese culture. The Red Red Rose tartan brings both together to celebrate the historical moment when these two events coincide, the next occasion being the year 2096.

name: Red Thistle Dress
registrationNotes: The dress version of the Red Thistle tartan was designed to commemorate the 500th performance of The Red Thistle Dancers in 2019. The Red Thistle Dancers, founded in 1973, are a Scottish Country & Highland Dance and Music Performance group based in the San Francisco Bay Area. This tartan is based on the California State tartan, birthplace of The Red Thistle Dancers. Colours: parchment for the Scroll of Honour awarded to the Directors of The Red Thistle Dancers by the Royal Scottish Country Dance Society; deep and bright reds and crimsons for the various California red thistle native species (Cirsium occidentale and Cirsium arizonicum); orange & white for the thistledown of the flower as it transitions to its mature stage and grey for the level of achievement represented by all members of The Red Thistle Dancers and Musicians past and present.

name: King’s Foundation, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of The King’s Foundation. Any commercial use will be at the sole discretion of The King's Foundation. May only be woven with written permission from The King's Foundation or The Scottish Tartans Authority as its nominated agent. Design registered with the UK Intellectual Property Office 19th July 2019. IPO Design Registration No. 6066268.
registrationNotes: In celebration of the 70th birthday of His Majesty The King (then HRH The Prince Charles, Duke of Rothesay) on 14th November 2018, The Scottish Tartans Authority designed The Prince’s Foundation tartan for the exclusive use of the Charity created in 2018 and incorporating The Great Steward of Scotland’s Dumfries House Trust. David Stewart, High Steward of Scotland, was the first Duke of Rothesay (1398 - 1402) and this tartan is based on the Old Stewart sett, first recorded in the 1819 Key Pattern Book of William Wilson & Son of Bannockburn. Following the Accession of His Majesty King Charles III, the tartan was renamed in line with the Charity: The King’s Foundation.

name: The Sassenach
designer: Campbell, Clare Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Great Glen Company LLC. All enquiries with regards to the design must be discussed with a Director of the Great Glen Company. This tartan can only be woven in Scotland as commissioned by the Great Glen Company LLC.
registrationNotes: The Sassenach design has been inspired by the story of the Great Glen Company and founder Sam Heughan. Sassenach is a historic Scottish term meaning English person or Lowland Scot. Sam, a Scottish actor, has become synonymous with the phrase where both on screen and off screen Sam uses Sassenach as a term of endearment. Sam, who would refer to himself as a Sassenach, was born in Dumfries, part of lowland Scotland in 1980. The threadcount of the tartan reflects dates and time of meaning to the company whilst adopting a subtle black and grey colour palette. The four shades within the tartan have been inspired by Scotland’s dark landscape, from rigid natural rock formations to the heavy skies rolling in the glens.

name: The Sassenach - First Love
designer: Campbell, Clare Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Great Glen Company LLC. All enquiries with regards to the design must be discussed with a Director of the Great Glen Company LLC. This tartan must only be woven in Scotland as commissioned by the Great Glen Company LLC.
registrationNotes: The Sassenach - First Love design forms part of the Sassenach collection, as created by the Great Glen Company and founder Sam Heughan. The base pattern for the tartan design can be read about in more detail at tartan register entry “12675 – The Sassenach”. The single variation for the first love design is the deep red strike through, representing 14 threads, the date of creation.

registrationNotes: The London Scottish Volunteer Enterprises Ltd are responsible for the running operations within the iconic London Scottish House building. To celebrate the founding Scottish roots and continued engagement with Scottish cultural and community values in the centre of London a tartan has been created to commemorate their purpose and provide a symbolic Scottish fabric to promote this.

registrationNotes: London Scottish House is the custodian charity for the iconic building of the same name. As part of the charities ambitious London Scottish House Appeal launched in 2019 to refurbish the whole property, a tartan has been created to specifically compliment its rich historical and cultural connections. Home to the Hodden Grey Tartan the charity wished to create a design that was symbolic of the current and future community who will gather for centuries to come in its new format.

registrationNotes: Members and Trustees of the London Scottish Regiment decided that creating an undress tartan specific to the unit would be implemented to further distinguish members during non-ceremonial duties. It was also designed to allow the friends of the regiment to share an aspect of its identity in social events.

name: Alba Gu Bràth
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2019. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design Nos. 6068418, 6072020, 6072021.
registrationNotes: The tartan (which is the Scottish Gaelic translation of “Scotland Forever”) celebrates a multi-cultural and prosperous Scotland, looking forward into the future with a sense of openness and optimism. The vibrant design represents the wide range of nationalities and communities to be found throughout Scotland. When worn or printed on the bias blue and white in the tartan creates a visual representation of the Scottish National Flag - the St. Andrew’s Cross - a unifying banner for the wide diversity of peoples of the whole of Scotland.

registrationNotes: This West Point Association of Graduates tartan, known as the ‘Old Grad Plaid’, is representative of a long history of illustrious military leadership and service to the United States of America and celebrates their 150th Anniversary. For the past 150 years the Association of Graduates has served West Point and ‘The Long Gray Line’. A Cadet who makes it through the arduous forty-seven-month experience and graduates is known as an Old Grad. The Academy colours of black, grey and gold stem from American Military History. These colours represent the components of gunpowder: charcoal, saltpetre and sulphur, and are also used in the uniforms of the school mascots and cadets.

The colours of the tartan correlate with the those of the blacksmith's anvil, the wine grape, the forge fire, refined metals, and of the vine leaf.

name: Army Air Corps
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 31 May 2020, registration number: 6091022.
registrationNotes: The Army Air Corps Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Army Air Corps since its formation. The Army Air Corps (AAC) is the combat aviation arm of the British Army. Recognisable by their distinctive ‘Sky Blue’ berets. The Army Air Corps was formed in 1957 on the foundations of the Glider Pilot Regiment and the Air Observation Post Squadrons of the Royal Artillery and Royal Air Force. Since then, they have watched over the UK and taken part in combat operations across the world. The Army Air Corps Tartan features the principal colours of the Army Air Corps. Being a Dark Blue and a Sky Blue which are historically known as Oxford and Cambridge Blue. The Red symbolises ‘Infantry’. As during WWII the troops were trained to jump out of aircraft to fight and also as Glider Pilots who then fought as infantry soldiers after landing. Black is for continual respect for all fallen Army Air Corps comrades.

restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 31 May 2020, registration number: 6091029.
registrationNotes: The Royal Military Police Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to The Royal Military Police (RMP). Antecedents of the RMP is one the most ancient appointments in the service of the British Crown, with its origins lost in antiquity. In Norman times known as Provost Marshal and later Military Mounted Police (MMP), Military Foot Police (MFP) and the Corps of Military Police (CMP). In 1946, in recognition of its outstanding record in WW1 and WW2, King George VI granted the 'Royal prefix' to the Corps henceforth known as Royal Military Police (RMP). Since WW2, the RMP has been active in every operational theatre to date. The RMP are easily distinguished by their scarlet red-topped service dress cap or beret that they wear, which has gained them the name of the ‘Red Caps’. This tartan incorporates the colours of the Royal Military Police; Blue and Red.

restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designers for permission to weave and to use this design. Dr. Drew Smith, 235 North Centre Road, Suite 301, London, Ontario, Canada N5X 4E7 Email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: Designed to commemorate the heroic British Antarctic explorer, Sir Ernest Shackleton. He will be remembered forever for his perseverance, bravery and dedication to the successful rescue of every man of his crew in August 1916 after their ship, the "Endurance" was lost to pack ice many months before. Colours: brown represents the oak, Norwegian fir and greenheart chosen by master Norwegian shipbuilders to construct the Endurance; green represents the rolling hills of County Kildare, Ireland, Shackleton's birthplace; grey represents the seals used as food and oil for the sailors' lamps and stoves and the rocky cliffs of South Georgia and Elephant Islands; red represents the courage and strength of Shackleton's leadership; white represents the Antarctic pack ice that trapped the Endurance; blue represents blue Antarctic summer sky, the pack ice reflected by the sun and the relentless Southern Ocean. Taken together, the red, white and blue represent the Union Jack flag.

registrationNotes: The Welsh Guards Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Welsh Guards since its formation. The Welsh Guards were formed in 1915 by order of King George V and are Wales’s Senior Infantry Regiment. The Welsh Guards serve the UK as fighting soldiers and also take immense pride in their ceremonial role as the guardians of the royal palaces. They have distinguished themselves both on and off the battlefield, and have taken part in almost every British Army campaign since World War I. The Welsh Guards Tartan features the principal colours of the Welsh Guards being; dark blue and crimson, recognisable in areas such as their Tactical Recognition Flash and Stable Belt. White and green denotes the plume worn on the right side of the bearskin, whilst carrying out duties as one of the five foot guards regiments of the Household Division. Black is for continual respect for all fallen Welsh Guards comrades.

name: Declaration of Arbroath 7th Centennial Anniversary
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2020. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6085120. The Declaration 1320 ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3138756.
registrationNotes: The tartan commemorates the 700th anniversary of the Declaration of Arbroath - 6th April 2020 - a letter in Latin submitted to Pope John XXII in 1320. Written on behalf of the earls, barons and nobles, and community of the whole Kingdom of Scotland. The letter asks the Pope to recognise Scotland's independence and acknowledge Robert the Bruce as the country's lawful king. The 7 colour tartan visibly portrays the artefact itself; light tan with the narrow black stripes represents the document and the literary work; green and red represents the seals and signatories; the white pivot represents the recipient of the letter Pope John XXII; the scarlet pivot represents the Scots of old who died fighting for freedom; the broad black stripe becomes a memorial of remembrance for those who fell on the Scottish battlefields. The thread counts in the two opposing pivots are created from the two relevant dates: 6th April 1320 and 6th April 2020 - thus the numeracy in the tartan spans seven centuries. 32 threads in the dark red pays tribute to Robert the Bruce who was crowned king at the age of 32; 100 threads span the complete width of the light tan field, representing the famous excerpt from the Declaration of Arbroath “for, as long as a hundred of us remain alive…”

name: Corps of Royal Engineers
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 29 June 2020, registration number: 6093625.
registrationNotes: The Corps of Royal Engineers Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Corps of Royal Engineers, since its formation in 1716. After expansion and many expeditions around the world, the Corps of Royal Engineers was formally established in 1856. The design features dark blue and crimson of the Corps of Royal Engineers Stable Belt and silvery grey denotes the crest buckle on their stable belt. Black is for continual respect for all fallen Corps of Royal Engineers comrades. Royal Engineer soldiers are called ‘Sappers’. Sappers originates from the French word Sappe and became connected with military engineering during the 17th century. Trenches and tunnels, called ‘Saps’, were engineered to cause the walls of forts under siege to collapse, and their diggers became known as ‘Sappers’. Today Sappers are multi-skilled soldiers, combat engineers and tradesmen, providing essential support to all areas of defence in peacetime and on operations.

Colours: grey represents the rocky alpine mountains; green represents the many alms and mountain forests; light grey represents the snow covered mountain tops and the mist surrounding them and blue represents the icy mountain lakes and streams. The red/white/red stripe represents the markings along the alpine foot paths, which connect the peaks and the lakes with each other, for without those many a hiker would get hopelessly lost.

restrictions: Yes. Only to be worn by the copyright holders and those authorised by them. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders or their descendants.
registrationNotes: In the early 20th century the Okhai family emigrated from India to Malawi from where, in 1966, 26 year-old Ibrahim Okhai emigrated to Dundee. There, his determination and business acumen soon enabled him to bring his parents and siblings to join him. After years of hard work and business advancement, he acquired the failing James Keiller factory which he built into a world-renowned brand that was given a Queen’s Award for Export. After selling the company, the family ventured into many other business areas in Dundee and founded the Aydya Group. This Okhai family tartan is based on the Dundee design and with its orange ‘strands’,’ highlights the family’s marmalade beginnings. The white on blue is for the Saltire flag and the family’s passion for their adopted country. Orange is also the house colour of the Aydya Group and the black squares comprise 66 threads to commemorate the family’s ‘first foot’ in Scotland.

name: Here's tae us!
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder Brian Wilton MBE, his heirs, successors or agents. IPO registered No. 6094787
registrationNotes: The "Here’s tae us!" tartan celebrates Scotland, bringing two ancient banners together in the design. The Royal Banner of Scotland or Lion Rampant, is one of the country’s most recognisable symbols and dates from 1222. The National Flag of Scotland - the Saltire – is, according to legend, even older. It originated in 832AD in a battle fought in today’s East Lothian when an army of Picts and Scots became cornered by a superior force of Angles and Saxons. Prayers for deliverance, led by their leader King Angus, were answered by an inspirational diagonal cross of white cloud in a clear blue sky — the cross of St. Andrew. The Picts and Scots won the day; St. Andrew subsequently became Scotland’s patron saint and that cloud became the national flag — the Saltire. When printed or worn on the bias, the white cross of 30 threads — for St. Andrew’s Day on 30th November – becomes the Saltire.

name: Scotch Whisky 1494
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2020. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK IPO Registered Design No. 6014261. Scotch Whisky Tartan ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3158697. 1494 ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3204936. The Angels’ Share Scotch Whisky Tartan ® is UK IPO Registered Trademark No. 3158692.
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate Scotch Whisky Scotland's world famous national drink, fondly referred to as ‘the Water of Life’. It is intended to represent the origin story of Scotch (the first written record of whisky production in the Exchequer Rolls of Scotland 1st June 1494), and the Tironensian Grey Monks of Lindores Abbey who distilled the spirit for the first time in history. The design is also intended to reflect the amber hues and tones of Scotch whisky, as it sparkles in the glass. This is the third interpretation of the designer’s creation of the Scotch Whisky tartan; the sett and colours were adapted from the original Scotch Whisky tartan reference #11686, which itself was inspired by the Angels’ Share tartan reference #11497. Refer to these two preceding tartans for the expanded rationale within the weave.

The Oshidori bird is known for cuddling close to its partner and, therefore, is often considered to be a symbol of affectionate couples in Japan.

The white accent is for the amazing local snowdrop display in Spring. The red accent is a further nod to the Stewart Clan. This tartan was commissioned by the Poppleton family, whose family home is in Drumin, and to celebrate the marriage of their daughter Ellen and her fiancé Oliver.

restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2020. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. registrationNotes: The tartan was designed to depict the Phoenix, a mythical bird of fire and flame which rises from the ashes becoming a universal symbol of renewal, rebirth, immortality and resurrection. name: Blesma
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed for Blesma and their clients. Please contact the designer regarding permission to use.
registrationNotes: The Blesma tartan honours the Association’s Scottish heritage. In 1921 the first Branch of the Limbless Ex-Service Men’s Association was formed in Glasgow. Groups soon formed throughout Scotland before branching across the United Kingdom. In 1932 the Branches united to form the British Limbless Ex-Serviceman’s Association. Blesma The Limbless Veterans is dedicated to assisting serving and ex-Service men and women who have suffered life-changing limb loss or the use of a limb, an eye or loss of hearing in the honourable service of our country. The tartan is made up of the Blesma colours, representing the three branches of the Services, and the design incorporates ‘lines’ commemorating the Association’s founding in 1932 and Golden Jubilee in 1982. The Blesma tartan also honours the dedicated work of Peter J Shields MBE QGM, who retired in 2020 after 15 years of dedicated service as a Blesma Support Officer.

name: Allied Rapid Reaction Corps
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147389.
registrationNotes: The Allied Rapid Reaction Corps Tartan celebrates all achievements attached to the Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), since its formation 2 October 1992. The ARRC's history began in 1815 when its antecedent – ‘the 1st Corps’ - had its weight thrown against Napoleon's forces by the Duke of Wellington at the Battle of Waterloo. Throughout its history the Corps has played a key role in international events; WWI, WWII, throughout the Cold War, Bosnia, Kosovo. Other operations have included the formation of the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) in Afghanistan in 2006 and as ISAF Joint Command in 2011. The Allied Rapid Reaction Corps Tartan features historical colours associated with the Corps; Blue, Green and Light Grey. Black is for continual respect for all fallen Allied Rapid Reaction Corps comrades. The ARRC’s motto is ‘Audentis fortuna iuvat’ meaning ‘Fortune favours the Brave’.

The colours in this tartan reflect the long association that the Air Cadet League of Canada has enjoyed with the Royal Canadian Air Force, in particular, and with Canadian aviation, in general. Their motto is "Ionnsaich, Frithealadh, Adhartachadh", which means “To learn, to serve, to advance”.

name: Posukuma

registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the continuous service provided by and in honour of the national institute that is Japan Post. The colours are intended to represent: the red post box; the Japan Post bear emblem ‘Posukuma’: the green of his forest home and the friendly service provided by all the individuals that make up Japan Post. Posukuma means post bear, Postu is post and Kuma is bear in Japanese respectively.

name: Posukuma and Friends Colourful
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Japan Post, co Ltd Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Taking inspiration from the colourful character of the Japan Post Kuma (bear) and his friends which represent the service delivered to customers young and old by Japan Post. The colour combination is intended to be both calm and cheerful, friendly and fresh and to represent the happiness and joy of the giving and receiving of mail and parcels through Japan Post.

name: Nishijin
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Nishijin, the weaving district in Kyoto, Japan. The design references the year 1467, the start of the Onin war. Nishijin was where the western army had been camped during the war. This is the origin of the name Nishijin, which means ‘west position’. After the conflict, the weavers returned to Kyoto to resume their craft. The colours are intentended to represent the area of Nishijin: yellow represents the gold brocade of Nishijin and the ginko trees found in Horikawa street; light blue represents rivers of Kyoto; green represents the nature found in Kyoto; purple represents Miyabi (elegance in Japanese).

name: Kishut
registrationNotes: Kishut means ‘adornment’ in Hebrew. The colours are intended to represent aspects of the Jewish faith: blue represents Judaism; white represents the purity of Torah; yellow (gold) represents the Star of David, the menorah, and the adornments of the Tabernacle and black represents commemoration of the Shoah. The tartan is intended to be for those of the Jewish faith and those in support of Judaism.

name: Neeson, William & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Neeson family who emigrated to Canada when the patriarch of the family, William Neeson, married Maureen MacQuarrie. The family’s roots can be traced back to the Davidson's from Ross & Cromarty so this tartan was derived from the Davidson of Tulloch tartan with the addition of MacQuarrie tartan colours. The red and white section is intended to represent the Canadian flag.

name: St Edmund's of Enders Island
registrationNotes: A tartan for St Edmund's Retreat on Enders Island in Mystic, Connecticut, USA. It was inspired by the establishment of their Pipe and Drum Corps as part of their Institute of Sacred Art. The colours are intended to represent elements of St Edmund’s and the Catholic faith: the blues represents the Coat of Arms of St Edmund, the sea surrounding Enders Island and the ‘Blue of Our Lady’; red represents the Sacred Heart of Jesus and The Immaculate Heart of Mary as well as the Cross of the Society of St Edmund; yellow in intended to represent the Glory of God.

name: Blackthorne, A (Personal)
