registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the Blackthorne wedding and the beginning of their family. The surname was chosen by the couple as their married name to represent their love for nature, trees, the sea and Scotland. The colours of the tartan represent heather, transitioning seasons with spring and autumn leaves, the sea and sunset.

name: Talisker, Alexander & Johnson, Sarah - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Alexander Talisker and his family. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: Created for the wedding of Alex Talisker and Sarah Johnson to join two families over continents. The colours were inspired by both the Scottish Saltire and the American Stars and Stripes, joined together as their family is now.

name: St Rose High School Pipe Band
restrictions: Yes. Copyright owned by St Rose High School, Belmar, New Jersey, USA.
registrationNotes: A tartan for St. Rose High School, located in Belmar New Jersey, USA. It was designed by the Music Educator and Bagpipe Instructor at the school, Jennifer Weingarten.

name: Dodds, R Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone with the name Dodds and derivatives. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Dodds, R (Personal) (SRT #13048) tartan. It is intended to be used for informal wear.

name: Pennington, Jonathan Lemar and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Jonathan Lemar Pennington and his family. The colours selected for the design are intended to represent what is important to the family: blue represents truth and loyalty; grey (silver) represents peace and sincerity; yellow (gold) represents generosity and elevation of the mind and black represents the service the family has performed as generational firefighters.

name: Colegate, A & Barber-Colegate, C (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Carian Barber to Adam Colegate and uses colours of significance to both of them.

name: Heil, Rüdiger Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended For the exclusive use of Rüdiger Heil, his immediate family and descendants and all other branches of the family whose ancestral home is the village of Künzell in Hesse, Germany. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven, or copied in any way, without the written permission of the owner of the intellectual property rights (IPR). Prepared for weaving by Andrew Elliot Ltd, Selkirk, Scotland.
registrationNotes: A dress tartan for Rüdiger Heil, his family and descendants. The colours used for this pattern derive from the unique coastal landscape of the Isle of Mingulay: green for the moss; blue for the sea and red for the lonesome guardian of the island, the red rock, known as Ulbhag Ruadh in Gaelic.

name: Educational and Training Services
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147390.
registrationNotes: The Educational and Training Services (ETS) Tartan celebrates all personnel & achievements attached to the ETS since its formation. The history of the ETS dates back to the Corps of Army Schoolmasters, 1845. After WWI a Royal Warrant was issued & it became the Army Educational Corps. The Army Educational Corps served throughout WWII, receiving a Royal title in 1946, becoming the Royal Army Educational Corps, until the formation of the AGC (ETS), 1992. This tartan features the principal colours of the ETS; dark blue & light blue. Red & Yellow are intended to represent the flame of the Promethean Torch of the ETS Crest. Black has been included in continual respect for all fallen ETS comrades.

name: UK Brave
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147391.
registrationNotes: The UK Brave Tartan was designed to celebrate individuals in the UK who have an innate sense of bravery. It may be as part of their chosen career or volunteer actions, they perform tasks and duties that come with an element of danger or extreme difficulty. They are brave and compassionate, they come from all walks of life and are often unsung heroes. The UK Brave Tartan includes the colours of the flag of the United Kingdom, and black for continual respect for all our fallen brave individuals.

name: Dennis’ 70th Birthday – 2021
restrictions: Yes. Any use associated with this tartan out with the weaving of fabric for commercial purposes must only be carried out with prior approval via Beano Studios Ltd (part of DC Thomson & Co Ltd). There are no restrictions as to who can wear this tartan Beano Studios Ltd (part of DC Thomson & Co Ltd) will approve all and any weavers to weave this tartan. Please contact them directly with any enquiries.
registrationNotes: This birthday celebration tartan was created to mark the 70th birthday of one of Scotland's iconic comic characters, Dennis The Menace. Dennis first appeared on the edition cover of Beano on the 17th March 1951 and this tartan has been inspired by the dates and colours connected to this occasion. The colours represent the colours of Dennis's jumper, black and red.

name: Pipes & Drums of the Blue & Gold
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Pipes & Drums of the Blue & Gold, members of the New Jersey State Police or those authorised by them or by the designer. This tartan may only be woven with the written consent of the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Robert K Jones of Rablogan of Scotland in collaboration with the New Jersey State Police pipe band known as the Pipes & Drums of the Blue & Gold. The colours are intended to represent the official colours of their home state of New Jersey and the traditional colours incorporated within their uniforms. The red stripe was included to honour those members of the troop who have passed away 'in service' or after.

name: Lyle, D & S and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Daniel and Shannon Lyle, their heirs and descendants and any other person authorised by any of the above. May only be woven by a mill approved by the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Daniel and Shannon Lyle and is intended to reflect their life together, the family they created and raised and their connection with their Scottish roots including their connection to the Lyle family, Duchal Castle and the Maxton family. The tartan has been designed to represent various elements of their Scottish ancestry through the choice of colours: brown for their family roots in Scotland; light green for the meadows where the family first flourished; dark red, gold and black to represent their Clans; blue for the waters that nourished the meadows and purple for the heather of Scotland.

name: Slaven, W & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the family and those with the Slaven surname.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for W Slaven & his family to celebrate their Scottish heritage and their family name. The 4 equal width colours in the tartan represent the 4 children of the family. It is intended to be passed to future generations.

name: Green, F R & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by descendants of the late Frederick Robert Green and their direct family line.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to honour Frederick Robert Green and the family’s British and military heritage. Frederick Robert Green served in the military at a young age, and in later life he joined as a bandsmen for the Sutherland Pipes and Drums. The colours are of personal significance: green, in particular, was included to honour the family’s ancestors; red was also included to commemorate 'The Thin Red Line' where the Scottish artist Robert Gibb’s celebrated painting depicts the 93rd Highlanders halting a Russian cavalry charge at the Battle of Balaclava during the Crimean War in 1854. The tartan is intended to be used by future generations of the family to connect them to their heritage.

name: Andrever, J C (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by Jasmine C Andrever for her family. The colours chosen are intended to represent what is important to the family including: the flag of Cornwall; dark yellow to represent copper, after the family's Cypriot heritage; the deep sea and nature.

name: Veitch, H & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those who bear or whose ancestors bore the names Veitch, Veatch, Veech, Veach. There are no restrictions on who can weave the tartan.
registrationNotes: The colours chosen for this tartan are intended to represent the history of the Veitch surname which was first recorded in Berwickshire when Randolph Veitch witnessed a charter by Henry de Graham c.1200; red and grey represent the Aberdeenshire granite of Darwyk House, first built by the Veitch family; green represents the Dawyck arboretum and botanical gardens; blue represents the River Tweed and the Scrape burn which runs through the gardens; yellow and white represent the yellow Winter Aconites and white Snowdrops which carpet the banks of the Scarpe burn in springtime.

name: Tough, Stanley William (Personal)
designer: Tough, Fergus & MacDonald, Ewan Houston Kiltmakers
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with consent from Fergus Tough.
registrationNotes: Designed for Stanley William Tough by his son Fergus. It is based on the colours of the Gordon tartan which Stanley wore. The tartan was designed to be worn at Fergus' wedding to Rebecca and by their son Alfie, and to signify the start of the Tough family in Australia. The colours represent Scottish landscape as well as meaningful connections between Fergus and Stanley.

name: Musselburgh RFC Centenary
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability, please contact Musselburgh RFC regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Musselburgh RFC.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate Musselburgh Rugby Football Club's Centenary in 2021. The design incorporates the club’s colours; navy and white of their traditional 'Butcher's Apron' playing strip and red of their socks.

name: Rablogan KGJ
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by direct descendants of Keith Gordon Jones or those authorised in writing by the designer or descendants. May only be woven with written authorisation from the designer or descendants. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Robert K Jones of Rablogan of Scotland as a memorial to his father Keith Gordon Jones, whose ancestry was connected with both the Keith and Gordon families. He served in the 2/30th Battalion AIF in Singapore spending 3 and a half years as a prisoner of war and medic in Changi. One of his best memories from that time was of a piper from a Black Watch regiment who played daily. The colours for this tartan incorporate those of the Keith and Gordon tartans with the addition of his unit colours - purple & gold.

name: McGillan, Ursula (Personal)
designer: Mayo, Erina and Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the marching team that Erina Mayo is a coach and member of and others who have permission from Erina Mayo or her family. May only be woven in consultation with and with the permission of Erina Mayo.
registrationNotes: Designed by Erina Mayo in honour of her mother, Ursula Mayo, née McGillan. The colours depict a link to the seaside Eastern Bay of Plenty area of New Zealand, where both Ursula and Erina grew up, with the blues representing the ocean and yellow the sun.

name: Warrior, The
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147392.
registrationNotes: The Warrior tartan is intended to celebrate the image and spirit of a warrior. The Warrior tartan encompasses shades of grey representing the metal armour, helmet and swords worn and used by some warriors throughout history. Black signifies the dark days of battle they had to endure and white symbolises the hope for their future.

name: Judique Spirit
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/reproduced with permission from The Judique Tartan Group
registrationNotes: The Judique Spirit Tartan was created in 2020 by the Judique Tartan Group to celebrate the strength, faith, culture, and community spirit of the seaside village of Judique, Nova Scotia, Canada. The colours and design are intended to represent the heartbeat of the community: blues for the ocean and sky; green for the forest and fields; dark yellow for the red-orange-yellow sunsets; white for the first settlers' Winter arrival and red for the faith and strength of the people. The community participated in the selection of tartan colours and the process was a labour of love.

name: Longniddry Golf Club
restrictions: Yes. Designed exclusively by Kinloch Anderson for Longniddry Golf Club. Permission required. Please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for Longniddry Golf Club in their centenary year. The Club was established in 1921. The design takes inspiration from the Wemyss tartan to celebrate the Club’s connection to the Earl of Wemyss and the Wemyss Estate. The shades used reference the colours of the golf course’s coastal landscape and the Saltire, which is also part of East Lothian’s heritage. The threadcount includes a block of 106 threads which represent the overall dimensions of the course at 106 acres.

name: Green Finance
restrictions: Yes. Designed exclusively by Kinloch Anderson for Chartered Banker Institute. Permission required. Please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd regarding use. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for the Chartered Banker Institute (formerly the Chartered Institute of Bankers in Scotland) to mark the importance of Green Finance and to highlight Scotland and the UK’s contribution to this issue at the COP26 Climate Summit in Glasgow in November 2021. The design takes inspiration from elements of the Chartered Institute of Bankers in Scotland tartan and the Hay tartan. Sir Roger Gifford is the Chair of the Green Finance Institute and Gifford is a sept of the Hay Clan. Shades of green are used to represent Green Finance and the environment, blue and white for Scotland and gold for banking and finance.

name: Koala, The
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be woven/reproduced in any form without the express permission of the designers and copyright holders.
registrationNotes: The Koala tartan was designed to celebrate the beauty of the Australian native marsupial, a much loved Australian national icon. The tartan colours are intended to represent the Koala: dark and light grey for the majority of their coat colour with white speckles or patches on the rump and chest area and inside ears; black for their nose; pink for the skin colour around the nose and mouth, only seen on close inspection; dark brown for their eye colour and green for the eucalyptus leaves which is their main diet and dwelling tree.

name: Green, J & Agostini, I and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the immediate members and descendants of the Agostini and Green families. Prepared for weaving by Houston Kiltmakers or another kilt maker chosen by the head of the family on the occasion that Houston Kiltmakers no longer exists.
registrationNotes: The colours chosen for this tartan are intended to represent colours of significance to the family and the mythical bird the Phoenix: red represents the Dragon of Wales and the colour of an enflamed Phoenix; purple represents the importance of learning; yellow and orange represent gold to symbolise the surrounding fire of the phoenix and also as a reminder that through hard work, great rewards are earned.

name: Redside Sports
restrictions: Yes. Use is restricted to Redside Sports, LLC.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Lane United Football Club and to also to commemorate the lumbermen of the area who built a stadium for the community.

name: Edmonton Scottish Society
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Edmonton Scottish Society members, their families and any others who have received written permission from the Board of the Edmonton Scottish Society. The tartan may only be woven with written permission from the Board of the Edmonton Scottish Society. The tartan can not be sold or used for manufacturing of goods without written permission from the Edmonton Scottish Society.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Edmonton Scottish Society of Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, a Scottish Canadians club supporting Scottish cultural and heritage since 1949. The tartan design intends to honour Scotland and Alberta. Colours: the colours of the Lion Rampant and St. Andrew’s cross are featured in the tartan over check; grey is intended to represent Burns’ “cup of friendship”; purple represents heather, thistle flowers and the Alberta Wild Rose. The under check colours represent the summer and winter night sky of Scotland & Canada’s shared northern latitudes.

name: Edmonton Scottish Society Dress
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Edmonton Scottish Society members, their families and any others who have received written permission from the Board of the Edmonton Scottish Society. The tartan may only be woven with written permission from the Board of the Edmonton Scottish Society. The tartan cannot be sold or used for manufacturing of goods without written permission from the Board of the Edmonton Scottish Society.
registrationNotes: A dress version of the Edmonton Scottish Society tartan using white to represent the area’s winter snow.

name: Webster, Maxim (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions for this tartan, however the designer would appreciate a donation in Maxim's honour to the Thin Green Line Foundation for each garment produced.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in memory of Maxim Webster (1993-2020). Maxim was very passionate about Scottish culture, history and tradition including wearing kilts. The colours are intended to represent Maxim and his passions: dark red and grey represent the cotton shirt and tweed kilt frequently worn by Maxim; blue and green represent his love for nature; the thin green pivot represents the Thin Green Line Foundation, a conservation foundation of which Maxim strongly supported and the brown pivot represents Maxim's beloved dog Odin, an Irish wolfhound who sadly passed away shortly after Maxim.

name: Kilted Coaches, The
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with The Kilted Coaches.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Kilted Coaches, an online health and fitness brand with an international following.

name: Hulderman, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Registered by House of Tartan Ltd, on behalf of Steven D Hulderman.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Hulderman family. It was designed to celebrate their long and diverse ancestral connection to Scotland. The colours chosen are intended to represent their Scottish and family ancestry; purple represents the thistle; blue represents vigilance, truth, and loyalty and the Scottish Flag. The design and the blending of the colours is intended to represent the diversity of their ancestry.

name: Caley, J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for John Caley.

name: OSCA Scotch College Melbourne
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Registered by House of Tartan on behalf of The Old Scotch Collegians' Association, OSCA House, 1 Morrison Street, Hawthorn, Victoria, Australia, 3122.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for the Old Scotch Collegians' Association to recognise the School's Scottish Heritage and features the School's colours of cardinal, gold and blue. The final design was chosen by John Jeffreys and members of the Old Scotch Collegians' Association.

name: Great Scottish Events
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any other commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder Terry Crossley, Great Scottish Events.
registrationNotes: Based on the 1970 Edinburgh District tartan and incorporating the Great Scottish Events colours of blue and white. All the blue squares comprise 68 threads to mark the 1968 foundation of Great Scottish Events.

name: Scottish Summit
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Mark Christie, Scottish Summit. Registered by House of Tartan Ltd, on behalf of Mark Christie, Scottish Summit.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Scottish Summit gathering in Glasgow 2022. The Scottish Summit began as a way to showcase Microsoft Dynamics 365 in Scotland.

name: Redside Sports Dress
restrictions: Yes. Use is restricted to Redside Sports, LLC.
registrationNotes: A dress version of the Redside Sports tartan (SRT #13082), incorporating the colours of the Cascadia bioregion.

name: Nesbit-Bell, P (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com for approval to weave/use.
registrationNotes: The Nesbit-Bell tartan has been created to celebrate the Nesbit-Bell family, their connections to both the Bell & Nisbet families and a family wedding.

name: Migraine
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to be used by those wishing to raise Migraine awareness. The principal colour purple is the widely accepted colour used to promote Migraine awareness. The grey-green colour, similar to a thread colour called "maelstrom", was included to represent the metaphorical "storm" felt in the head during a migraine attack.

name: Spirit of the Columbia Icefields
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the Columbia Icefields located in the Canadian Rockies. Over 100 ancient glaciers span the majestic Icefields Parkway between Lake Louise and Jasper. The Athabasca Glacier that spills from the Columbia Icefield is the most accessible glacier in North America and one of the world's most visited. The tartan’s individual threads and colours, woven and layered together, is intended to represent the creation of the glaciers, which form over tens of thousands of years from individual snowflakes layered together.

name: Waldron, Cameron and Ashlee & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by Cameron and Ashlee Waldron and immediate family. May only be woven with the designer's permission. Prepared for weaving by Andrew Elliot Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Cameron and Ashlee Waldron's 10th Anniversary using colours of personal significance.

name: Chu, T and B & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from the Chu family to wear/use this tartan.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by Teresa Chu with Boris Chu to celebrate Boris’s years in Edinburgh and the family’s appreciation for Scotland.

name: Coindeau, Olivier & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Coindeau family. owner is Olivier Coindeau
registrationNotes: A tartan for Olivier Coindeau and his family using colours of personal significance.

name: Judique Spirit Fall/Winter
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/reproduced with permission from The Judique Tartan Group.
registrationNotes: A fall/winter version of the Judique Spirit Tartan (SRT #13077) created in 2020 by the Judique Tartan Group to celebrate the strength, faith, culture, and community spirit of the seaside village of Judique, Nova Scotia, Canada.

name: Widows Sons France
restrictions: Yes. Restricted to Chrystel Amyot and Widows Sons France members.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the members of the masonic riders association biker group - Widows Sons France. The colours were chosen to match their logo and the patch worn on the riders’ backs.

name: Kobe Shoin
designer: FHD students of Kobe Shoin Women's University
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with permission from Shoin Joshi Gakuin Educational Corporation or Kobe Shoin Women's University. May only be woven by request of above educational corporation or university.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by the students taking the course of "Seminar in Collaboration for a Local Community" in 2020 at Kobe Shoin Women's University, a part of Shoin Joshi Gakuin Educational Corporation, for the purpose of celebrating the 130th anniversary of their corporation in 2022. The colours are intended to represent the history of Shoin Joshi Gakuin Educational Corporation founded in 1892 in Kobe, Japan: blue and white are from the school uniforms; red is for the embroidery of S.M.S (Shoin Mission School) featured on the uniform; light red and green represent the school building of the university against the backdrop of the Rokko Mountains since 1982 and green represents the three pine trees, the origin of the name of "Shoin", which used to stand as a symbol in the schoolyard of the original school.

name: Berkhamsted Strathspey and Reel Club
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is produced by The House of Edgar for and is intended for the sole use of members of the Berkhamsted Strathspey and Reel Club. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Berkhamsted Strathspey and Reel club and to celebrate their platinum anniversary. The colours chosen are intended to represent the club’s history: light blue represents the connection of the club’s founders who were both at Cambridge; blue is for the canal and river which pass through Berkhamsted; black represents the railway line; red represents the brand colour of the club’s logo.

name: Ronald McDonald House Charities UK
restrictions: Yes. Designed exclusively by Kinloch Anderson for Ronald McDonald House Charity. Permission required. Please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd regarding use. Permission required. Only to be woven by supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to celebrate the opening of Ronald McDonald House Edinburgh inside the Royal Hospital for Children and Young People in 2021. The design takes inspiration from the City of Edinburgh tartan and uses the branded colours of Ronald McDonald House Charities UK.

name: Patrick King's Little Lamb
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the written permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: The Little Lamb tartan is for Patrick King Woollen Company's signature baby tartan products.

name: COP26 - A New Dawn
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven, printed or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder – the Scottish Government or its appointed agents.
registrationNotes: This vibrant design represents the new dawn rising from the United Nations 2021 climate change summit in Glasgow, Scotland. The conference branding is rooted in the MacGregor tartan – associated with the Scottish town of Callander and the remarkable scientist of that name whose monumental discovery in 1938 linked the concentration of atmospheric carbon dioxide to human activities, primarily through burning fossil fuels. The COP26 colours of blue, green and white, surround the new dawn and represent the hopes of up to 30,000 delegates, that the conference will herald new initiatives, new targets and new achievements to tackle the global climate emergency. In keeping with Scotland’s determination to continue reducing emissions to net zero, the tartan, in woven form, uses a combination of new wool and – for the first time – recycled wool from Prato in Tuscany, the traditional and historic recycling centre of Italy – Scotland’s COP26 partner.

name: Sunny Sea
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Tartania LLC, Japan.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan based on the province of Okayama, which generally has more sunny days than the rest of Japan. In addition, in the south of the province there is a clear sea full of islands. The colours are intended to represent a sunny day in Okayama: blue for the colour of the sky; dark blue for the colour of the deep ocean; yellow for the sun and white for the sun’s rays reflecting on the water.

name: Hannona, Rafie & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by the family. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Rafie Hannona by MacGregor and MacDuff. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar; a subdivision of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for the Hannona family and their descendants. This tartan is a celebration of both Scottish and Iraqi / Assyrian culture. The deep green and blue are intended to represent the renowned landscapes found within Scotland, and the red and lighter blue highlights are a nod to the Assyrian Flag.

name: Palmer, Ralph and David (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used or worn by future generations of Ralph and David's respective families.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ralph and David recognising their Scottish heritage. It is intended to be used by future generations of their respective families.

name: Erdeslau
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the owner regarding use. Copyright rests with the owner of the tartan.
registrationNotes: Erdeslau is the ancient name for Ardsley, the designer’s birthplace. The name is associated with coal mining and agriculture and later - railways. The colours are intended to represent the area and colours of significance to the designer: black represents coal from the area and the designer’s father who was a coal miner; purple and green represent the changing colours of the Yorkshire moors; blue represents the sea and sky and light purple was included as it was the favourite colour of the designer’s mother.

name: General Staff
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147393.
registrationNotes: The General Staff Tartan celebrates all past and present personnel & achievements attached to the General Staff. This tartan features the colours associated with the General Staff No. 1 Dress; dark blue represents the tunics and hats of the General Staff; red & yellow representing gold signifying the uniform accoutrements and of the General Staff Crest. Black is included for continual respect for all fallen General Staff comrades.

name: Santa's Toy Shop CCS
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Clan Claus Members. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar (Macnaughton Holdings Limited).
registrationNotes: A tartan for members of the ‘Clan Claus Society’ (CCS). The Society registered their first tartan over 10 years ago - Claus of the North Pole (SRT #5816) - and they felt it was the right time to design a new one.

name: Pfountz, Aaron & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with authorisation from Aaron Pfountz: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Pfountz family using colours of personal significance.

name: Lawson, Nicola & Dawson, Mark - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Nicola Lawson & Mark Dawson. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created to celebrate the marriage of Nicola Lawson and Mark Dawson. The colours and threadcount of the tartan are inspired by their Scottish heritage, the lochs and heather clad hills of the Scottish Highlands and their home at Polmaily, Drumnadrochit. The single gold overcheck which unites the design is in memory of Mark’s beloved sister, Sally.

name: Anekagotra
restrictions: Yes. Please contact Slanj Kilts regarding use.
registrationNotes: Anekagotra (Sanskrit - “belonging to two families”) is inspired by the colours of the Scottish Saltire and the Indian Tiranga, and designed for those who would like to celebrate or associate with the longstanding links between Scotland and India. The tartan is intended to be for Indian Scottish people and the Indian diaspora globally.

name: Klarna
restrictions: Yes. This design cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any commercial form without the express permission of Klarna, the copyright holders or their appointed agents.
registrationNotes: Klarna Bank AB, is a Swedish fintech company that provides online financial services such as payments for online storefronts, direct payments and post purchase payments. Their core service is designed to eliminate financial risk for buyers and sellers by managing store claims and customer payments. The colours in this design are those used by Klarna in their imaginative advertising campaigns.

name: Horne, Philip (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder, Phil Horne:[email protected], or his agents.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Philip Horne and his extended family.

name: Giglio, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Giglio family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Marco Alessandro Giglio to Anna Patricia Halford. As Marco is a graduate of St. Andrews University, the Earl of St. Andrews tartan was used as inspiration. registrationNotes: A tartan for the Special Observers Association. The designer served with a specialist organisation within the Royal Artillery called, 4/73 (Sphinx) Special Observation Post Battery. Their motto is ‘Lateo’ which means ‘We lie hidden’. The colours are intended to have specific meaning; black represents the Battery stable belt; grey represents the term used by the reconnaissance and surveillance unit "...to remain grey" which is a reference to remaining unseen; green represents the specialist qualification badge which is a green Observation Post triangle and red has been included in remembrance of Special Observers who never returned from operations.

name: Scottish Arts Club
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with approval of the Scottish Arts Club.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Scottish Arts Club. The tartan is based on the Geddes tartan sett, in honour of one of the club’s most influential members, Sir Patrick Geddes, who joined the Scottish Arts Club in 1894. He was among the first lay members to be permitted and he played a vital role in their history. Geddes was an eminent ecologist and biologist who travelled widely and was responsible for promoting the Arts in Edinburgh. Geddes became good friends with Colourists, John Duncan Fergusson and Samuel Peploe, whose works are inextricably linked to the history of the Club. The tartan incorporates colours reflecting the influence of Geddes and Scottish Colourists, particularly Peploe: Turquoise, blue and green represent the great outdoors representing the many overseas travels of Sir Patrick; light red, brown and purple reflect the landscapes of Scotland and in particular Peploe’s paintings of one of his favourite subjects, the island of Iona.

registrationNotes: The Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) tartan has been created to celebrate 100 years since the Australian Air Corps became the Royal Australian Air Force, with HRH King George V approving the use of the word "Royal" in the name in June 1921, and to honour the service of all the men and woman who have served in the RAAF for the last 100 years and to those who continue to serve. The colours are intended to represent those associated with the RAAF: light blue represents the RAAF Ensign; dark blue represents the Australian National Flag and the blue roundel in which is located the red kangaroo, “in motion”, facing forward to the front of the aircraft; white represents the seven pointed Commonwealth Star, the five white stars of the Southern Cross constellation and the central background of the roundel; red represents the British Union Jack and the securing & placement of the red kangaroo.

registrationNotes: Angels' Share Glass Ltd was founded in 2012 by father and daughter, Tom Young MBE and Karen Somerville. This tartan is for their company, representing the glass craftsmanship of their product collections and their inherent links to whisky and, its pairing partner, water. The colours are associated with the Angels' Share Glass brand. The threadcount represents the story of Angels' Share Glass; 82 and 14 threads in teal blue marking the 82 years of Tom's life and the age he began glassblowing. The Angels' Share is a Scottish phrase associated with the evaporation process of whisky cask storage, and in 82 years anything from 56%-81% of whisky could have evaporated from a cask. These numbers are also incorporated in the design, with rich gold and black representing the whisky mystically being captured by the 'Angel'. The white overchecks notes the partnership of Tom and Karen since 2012, which is also marked with 12 bright gold threads across the main brand colour of teal blue.

name: Perth Grammar School

The school colours of black, gold and silver complement the red, blue and green bands, the house colours for Almond, Earn and Lomond respectively. All these historical and contemporary elements combine in this tartan to create an educational and achievement ‘clan identity’ for one of Perthshire’s oldest schools. restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders, their guardians, heirs & successors or appointed agents.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Skye Museum of Island Life. One of Scotland’s most romantic and famous heroines, Flora MacDonald was only 24 when she first met Prince Charles Edward, Bonnie Prince Charlie, on the island of South Uist. On the run after the ill-fated Battle of Culloden, the Prince persuaded her to help in his escape and in June 1746 they set sail from Benbecula on the perilous 37 mile (60km) sea journey to the Isle of Skye. This tartan’s name is taken from the famous 19th century ‘lullaby’ — the Skye Boat Song; “Speed bonny boat like a bird on a wing, Onward the sailors cry. Carry the lad that’s born to be King, Over the sea to Skye.” Based on an old MacDonald tartan, the blue and white are for the sea and the breaking waves on the shores of Skye. Green is from the Jacobite ribbon, and red is for the government Redcoats and the courage and fortitude of that 24 year old Highland heroine.

name: Highland Heroine
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders, their guardians, heirs & successors or appointed agents.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Skye Museum of Island Life. One of Scotland’s most romantic and famous heroines, Flora MacDonald was only 24 when she first met Prince Charles Edward, Bonnie Prince Charlie, on the island of South Uist. On the run after the ill-fated Battle of Culloden, the Prince persuaded her to help in his escape and in June 1746 they set sail from Benbecula on the perilous 37 mile (60km) sea journey to the Isle of Skye. After an eventful life which included imprisonment in the Tower of London, short emigrations to North Carolina and Nova Scotia, she returned to her Scottish home and died on Skye in 1790. She was buried at Kilmuir wrapped in a sheet in which Bonnie Prince Charlie had slept. Based on the 1842 tartan for MacDonald of the Isles the blue and white are for the sea and the breaking waves on the shores of Skye. Green is from the Jacobite ribbon, grey is for Skye’s romantic name of The Misty Isle and red is for the courage and fortitude of that 24 year old Highland heroine.

name: Moss Cottage - Taigh a' bhèiceir
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Kenneth and Grace Mackenzie, their direct family, and any other future owners, & their direct family, of Moss Cottage while in ownership. 1b Eorodale Isle of Lewis, Scotland HS2 0XJ May only be woven with permission from the owners of Moss Cottage.
registrationNotes: Moss Cottage - taigh a’bheiceir (the baker’s house) - was built in the 1840s & 1850s in Ness on the Isle of Lewis, and is reputed to be the 2nd oldest building there. It has served as a home, a bake house, a shop-keep, and now it has been restored is able to serve more generations as a home once again. The stone house was a shell of its former self when purchased in 2016 by Kenneth and Grace Mackenzie and their love & devotion to the property brought it back to life as a modern home. The tartan is intended to represent the beauty of the locale and the cottage; the white house and black roof stands out against the moss green of the surrounding countryside, the green and blue of the surrounding sea, and the red is intended to represent the blood and passion of those involved in the restoration of Moss Cottage.

registrationNotes: This design has been developed by the Town of Annapolis Royal to recognize its historical communities and its setting. The Annapolis Royal Heritage tartan incorporates 7 colours which are intended to represent multiple flags in various combinations: red, white and blue for the French and British flags; red and white for the Mi'kmaq flag; green, yellow, and red for the African Nova Scotian flag; red, white, blue, and yellow for the Acadian flag; blue and white for the Saltire. The colours are also intended to represent the landscape: green for the forests of Nova Scotia; blue for the waters and sky; grey for the fog and rocky coast. The Tartan is intended to celebrate not only the land, which has been known for millennia as a place of beauty and abundance, but also the groups which comprise the community.

The Presbyterian Church in Camden was established before the American Revolutionary War. The church building was designed by American architect Robert Mills. The threadcount is based on the anniversary years; 1822–2022. Liturgical colours of green, white, purple, red and gold are combined with the white and blue of South Carolina.

It was designed as an expression of their Scottish ancestral connection with MacNeil of Barra while including elements of their individual upbringings and their lives together in the mountains of Virginia. name: Felix EOD Mascot
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 7 July 2021, registration number: 6147395.
registrationNotes: The Felix EOD Mascot Tartan celebrates the ‘lucky cat’ Felix EOD Mascot and the work carried out by Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel. Cats have always been associated with luck, possibly due to their innate ‘righting reflex’ of always landing on their feet. Felix (Latin for ‘happy’ or ‘lucky’) was the name given to the EOD Felix cat mascot in the 1970’s by accident when a young signaller asked the Officer Commanding (OC) of his bomb disposal unit, which radio call-sign he wished to use. The OC, having lost two operators that morning, decided on ‘Phoenix’, to reflect the squadron rising up from the ashes. This was misheard by the signaller as ‘Felix’ and was never changed – hence the phrase ‘Fetch Felix’ whenever a suspect device is found. This tartan features the colours of the Felix EOD Mascot; the green of his helmet and beige, white and red are from his face. Black has been included for continual respect for all fallen EOD comrades.

name: Star-Spangled Banner (Flag of 1814)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2014. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. UK Registered Designs: #6104320 (Colour), #6147549 (Pattern). USPTO Patent Pending: #29/800,256. Star-Spangled Banner ® is a registered trademark: #UK00003667073.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed to pay tribute to the Star-Spangled Banner - the historic US flag carried during the War of 1812, and the same ‘Great Garrison Flag’ that flew over Fort McHenry during the harbour Battle of Baltimore, Sept 13th 1814. British warships pounded the American fort for 25 hours sending a bombardment of shells and rockets. After the battle in the early dawn of Sept 14th, seeing the flag still flying, Francis Scott Key was stirred to write the poem “Defence of Fort M'Henry”. The poem not only inspired the name of the flag but also became the lyrics of the national anthem of the US. The sett is created to visually represent the Stars and Stripes (the red, white & blue of the flag), and the explosive drama of the battle. The thread count of the design incorporates the past and present: 15 blue threads & 15 red threads represent the 15 stars & 15 stripes of the Star-Spangled Banner; 13 threads in the broad red and white stripes, and 50 threads in the dark blue field represent the present-day US Flag.

name: Fortnum & Mason
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Fortnum & Mason. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from both Fortnum & Mason and Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with Fortnum & Mason.
registrationNotes: Designed for Fortnum & Mason, this tartan combines details from a remarkable history with Fortnum & Mason’s distinctive wit and style. The design begins at the beginning: depicting the founders, William Fortnum and Hugh Mason, in the double Eau de Nil checks at the centre. As sellers of recycled candles from part-used candles discarded by the royal household, the design picks out the candle wax in the yellow. Beehives & beeswax continue to be important to Fortnums, and the company apiaries are acknowledged in the pale yellow placed across the soft green ground; 6 threads for the metropolitan hives, and 4 threads for the hives on the roof of the flagship Piccadilly building. Beginning in 1707, Fortnum & Mason now has 4 satellite stores, which are signified in the horizontal and vertical checks. The red echoes the carpeting of the Piccadilly store and the richness of the delicacies on offer. The outer red check of 12 threads, represents the twelve British monarchs who have been served by Fortnum & Mason, including Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.

name: Eternal 'Ericht', The
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer for permission regarding the tartan sett.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by the pupils of Blairgowrie High School to tell the story of the River Ericht (Abhainn Eireachd) and its importance to the communities of Blairgowrie, Rattray and nearby villages. The river used to be diverted for water wheels which powered local weaving mills. As the industry declined many mills were lost. A few, such as Bramblebank and Keathbank Mill, have been converted with the history & features being preserved. The bridge over the river, built in 1777, provides a vital transport link. After being washed out in 1847 it was rebuilt and has expanded throughout centuries, most recently being widened in 1954 to accommodate modern vehicles & support local industries. The bridge provides a focal point for celebrations in the community and a valuable connection between Blairgowrie and Rattray and is crossed by pupils every day. This tartan captures the natural colours of the river landscape and is intended to preserve the memories and history of the River Ericht.

The colours within the tartan represent military uniforms worn by the Continental Army during the American Revolution, and are also the official colours of the Society.

name: Blue Northern

registrationNotes: Northern Blue is intended as a universal tartan for anyone who has, or feels, a connection to the northern lands around the North Atlantic Ocean, North and Baltic Seas. The colours in the tartan were inspired by those present in the flags of these lands; red, white, yellow and blue. Blue, most commonly present in the flags, is intended to represent the water connecting these lands. It is part of a collection of four tartans; Blue Northern, Red Northern and their respective Dress versions.

registrationNotes: John Smedley Limited was formed in 1784, making it one of the world's oldest textile manufacturing factories. The company, and legacy of John Smedley, was with 8th generation family member Ian Maclean at the time this tartan was created. Due to the rich history of the company, from pioneering the 'Long John' to driving forward sustainable fabrics and textile technology for the future, Ian felt the time was right to add the first official tartan to the company’s story. The design was inspired by the Maclean of Duart tartan, c. early 19th century, to honour Ian’s connection with Clan MacLean and combined with the navy blue of the John Smedley Limited brand. The tartan is intended to acknowledge the strong cultural and textiles connection the company has with Scotland.

The colours and threadcount of this design recognises both birth years, with 65 in a pink for Alan's birth year of 1965, and violet for Miriam's 1941. Yellow is a favourite colour of Alan's and tumeric is symbolic of Miriam's connection with the land and soil of the Austrailian Outback. The blue and green over check combination represents 45 for a number of reasons including Alan and Miriam's passion for Scotland.

registrationNotes: This tartan represents the Atlantic Association of Community Business Development Corporations (CBDCs). Starting from a federal-provincial government funding pilot programme that began in 1975, 41 Community Business Development Corporations (CBDCs) now assist in the creation and expansion of small businesses in rural Atlantic Canada through the provision of financial and advisory assistance to entrepreneurs. CBDCs are not-for-profit community based organizations governed by independent volunteer Boards of Directors from the local business community, people who firmly believe in improving the economic viability of their communities.

The tartan is intended to symbolize the feeling of pride associated with being a part of the Augusta University community.
