registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for Daniele Scarpi de Claricini and is intended for use by all Scarpi de Claricini family members and those who bear the surname. The thread count rotates around the number of letters in the name, Daniele's date of birth, and Blantyre in Scotland. The tartan is based on the Daniele’s Coat of Arms, registered in the Public Register of Arms in Scotland, which includes colours and charges inspired by ancestral Italian Arms. The gold and dark red, Saint Mark’s banner colours, are also intended to allude to the ancient Scarpi connection with the Republic of Venice.

name: Schiller, Moira & Anthony (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Moira & Anthony Schiller & Family. Permission to weave must be sought from both the Schillers and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Moira and Anthony when they visited Scotland at the time of their engagement, with various numerical inspirations informed by significant dates. The tartan has been created in two mirrored colourways (this and their hunting version), for each of them, and has been created exclusively for their use and for future generations.

name: Schiller, Moira & Anthony Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Moira & Anthony Schiller & Family. Permission to weave must be sought from both the Schillers and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Moira and Anthony when they visited Scotland at the time of their engagement, with various numerical inspirations informed by significant dates. The tartan has been created in two mirrored colourways (this and their original version), for each of them, and has been created exclusively for their use and for future generations.

name: Kane, Arran (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by family and friends only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to be a family tartan and was created in memory of Arran’s late father. Arran’s name holds special meaning to the family as the names Kane and Arran together mean ‘Majestic Little Warrior’ (Arran from Hebrew meaning ‘exalted’ or ‘mountain of strength’ and Kane from the Irish & Gaeic word ‘Cath’ meaning ‘battle’). The colours used in the tartan were taken from a family keepsake so the keepsake will live on in the tartan design.

name: CWIN
registrationNotes: This tartan was created through a collaborative project with designer Christopher McEvoy, Central and West Integration Network (CWIN) and the Glasgow School of Art. The project explored textiles and fabric skills over 3 months and concluded with the creation of a banner and a co-designed tartan. This tartan uses the colour palettes that participants created during the project, which were inspired by their home countries. The design was registered to commemorate the project and to be used as the official tartan for CWIN.

name: Steps to Hope
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Lochcarron of Scotland and its customers. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Dedicated to the work carried out by Steps to Hope, the Edinburgh based charity dedicated to caring for the homeless and those suffering from addiction. This tartan was created to help support them and their clients in turning lives around and restoring hope.

name: Spirit of Le Mans (72)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from Andy Clegg, the designer and copyright holder of the tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the annual sports car races in Le Mans, France, and in particular the races that took place in the 1970s.

name: Fibonacci8
restrictions: Yes. May be woven with permission from the registrant.
registrationNotes: Fibonacci8 was inspired by the mathematical “Fibonacci sequence”. It is based on the earlier Fibonacci7 tartan (SRT #11454) and uses the first 8 numbers of the sequence: 1,1,2,3,5,8,13,21 in an asymmetrical sett.

name: Drey Balken Lodge Münster
designer: MacKenzie, D; Tomada, R & Kersten-Brückner, M C
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Lodge Members or those with permission from the Lodge only. May only be woven with permission from the Lodge.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Masonic Lodge “Zu den Drey Balken” based in Münster, Germany. The colours chosen have special significance to the Lodge and its members: dark blue is intended to represent the Lodge’s devotion and solidarity with the Grand Lodge of the United Grand Lodges of Germany; blue is intended to represent Freemasonry, loyalty and friendship; brown is intended to represent the sandstone from Münster, also known as the ‘marble of Münsterland’.

name: Explorers Club, The
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn or used with approval from The Explorers Club based in New York.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Explorers Club using the colours from the famous Explorers Club flag. The flag has been carried on various expeditions, including Apollo 11 where Neil Armstrong became the first man to set foot on the moon. The design of the tartan was based loosely on a Ferguson sett in honour of Seamas, an explorer and mapmaker and a well-respected long-time member of the club.

name: Spirit of Tarka
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave must be granted by Jo Davies, the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan inspired by the designer’s favourite walking trail - the Tarka Trail, near Devon. The colours are intended to represent the landscape: blue represents the sea; green represents the moor; yellow represents sand; light red and white represent flowers and purple represents heather. It also includes a reference to the colours on the Devon flag; green, black and white.

name: Scarpi de Claricini, Daniele Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any other commercial form without the express permission of the owner, Daniele Scarpi de Claricini - or his authorised agents, heirs or successors. Design registered with the UK IPO, design registration no. 6168472.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Scarpi de Claricini, Daniele (Personal) tartan (SRT #13,308). The design is intended to capture the colours of the woodlands and fields around Blantyre.

name: Teague-McHugh, D J (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for D J Teague-McHugh and family. The design uses colours of significance to the family: green is intended to represent the lush grass of Cornamucklagh, County Tyrone, Ireland; brown the soil; yellow represents the crops and the farming tradition that runs through the family ancestry; purple represents the heather and blue symbolises where the Rivers Tweed and Teviot meet near the family home - Oakfield Farm, Kelso, Scotland.

name: Araminta Campbell - Beech Dappled Skies
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Araminta Campbell Ltd Permission to weave must be sought from Araminta Campbell
registrationNotes: Drawing inspiration from her childhood and the landscape surrounding her family home in Aberdeenshire, this tartan was designed by Araminta Campbell and is intended to depict the blue skies seen through the dappled leaves of the beech tree woodlands in spring. The Araminta Campbell tartan and its colours were inspired by nature. Using a natural plant dyeing process, Araminta meticulously colour matched each of the yarn colours to reflect the colours found in the landscape.

name: Chartton, A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for family use only. May only be woven with permission. Enquiries should be sent to [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Chartton family. It was designed by members of the Chartton family using colours of personal significance.

name: Knapton, Steven & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by family and friends only.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Steven Knapton and his family. It was registered by Natasha Knapton as a gift to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary. They were married on November 9th, 2001. The tartan was designed by their son, Gavin David Knapton, using family colours and it is intended to be used at family celebrations.

name: Lee, Braxton & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the Lee family, Pleasant Garden NC and those authorised for use by said family.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for the Lee family for personal use. It was created in 2021 when the family resided in Pleasant Garden, North Carolina, and uses colours of significance: blue is intended to represent the sky; yellow represents the company the designer worked for at the time; green represents sustainability and the environment; black is intended to represent the fact the family are ‘night owls’ and red is for their fighting spirit.

name: Scarpi de Claricini, Daniele & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced in any other commercial form without the express permission of the owner, Daniele Scarpi de Claricini - or his authorised agents, heirs or successors. Design registered with the UK IPO, design registration no. 6168473.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to be a mourning tartan. The design was based on Daniele Scarpi de Claricini’s personal tartan, STR #13308.

name: Turner, Hayley (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May be used by others with the Turner surname.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Hayley Turner using colours inspired by her first visit to Scotland in autumn: blue represents the Firth of Forth; yellow, orange, and green for the colours seen on the trees and vines and the white and black represent the colours of buildings and the overcast sky.

name: Cerbin, Michael (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Michael Cerbin using colours of personal significance.

name: Unison Lothian Health Branch
registrationNotes: A tartan for Unison Lothian Health Branch to celebrate their Scottish heritage. The colours in this tartan are based on Unison’s colours, which are based on the colours associated with the suffragette movement due to Unison’s high proportion of women members. The tartan was designed in memory of Tam Waterson, branch chair, following his sudden death. The tartan is intended to be a reminder of his enormous contribution to the trade union movement and how he was an inspiration to all their members.

name: Heil, Erich Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Erich Heil and his immediate family. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven, or copied in any way, without the written permission of the owner of the intellectual property rights (IPR). Prepared for weaving by Andrew Elliot Ltd, Selkirk, Scotland.
registrationNotes: A hunting tartan for Erich Heil and his immediate family.

name: Blair Estate
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding use of this tartan must be directed to Charles Hendry of Blair Estate or through Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Blair Estate in Dalry, Scotland, which was purchased by the Hendry family in 2012. This tartan combines elements from both MacNaughton tartan, worn by the Hendry family, and the Blair tartan to create a single design for the Blair estate.

name: Riffard, A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is produced by House of Edgar for the exclusive use of the Riffard family. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Alexandre Riffard and his family to celebrate the ties between their Scottish Heritage and European Culture. The colours were chosen because as Alexandre Riffard's favourites and are the corporate colours of the shirt-maker brand he founded.

name: Ware, Leslie & Amy (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Leslie & Amy Ware and family. Permission to weave must be sought from both Leslie & Amy Ware and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This design has been created exclusively for the use of Leslie & Amy Ware. The design was inspired by their love of Scotland. The colours were chosen to represent their love of vivid colours and the bright blue is intended to represent the Texas Bluebonnet. The design is centred on sets of four checks to represent the couple's four children.

name: Dyball, Stephen (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Registered on behalf of Stephen Dyball by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Stephen Dyball. Stephen wanted to create a tartan due to the historical links the family name has with Scotland. The white in the design is intended to represent Stephen’s wedding and the red represents his partner’s surname – MacDonald.

name: McCluskey, David John and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave must be sought from the designer or his heirs and successors.
registrationNotes: A tartan for David John McCluskey and his family. It was inspired by his wife Lyn, and their two children who were born in Aberdeen, Scotland. The design is intended to represent the family history, the places they have lived, and their ancestors who travelled and lived on many continents. The colours were chosen by the family members and have specific meanings for them: blue, chosen by their son David & his family, represents the vast and mighty Atlantic Ocean as well as the warm Pacific Ocean coastlines; purple, favoured by their daughter Laura & family and David’s late mother Elizabeth, is intended to evoke images of heather covered hills and Scottish thistles; red is for the colour of the maple leaf of Canada and black signifies the coal hauled and sold by David’s father and grandfather many years ago.

name: FitzJoly, Henry, Stobo (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Henry FitzJoly, his family and supporters. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: A sett reserved for ceremonial use by Henry FitzJoly, his family and supporters. This design incorporates colours from his personal arms and those of his father, William Jolly.

name: Order of the Griffin, Chestnut Hill College
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be reproduced without the express written consent of Chestnut Hill College President's office.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Chestnut Hill College in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The colours in this tartan were chosen to reflect current and past college colours.

name: Valaris
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by those with consent from Valaris. Weaving restricted by Valaris. Prepared for weaving by Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: Designed for Valaris, this tartan incorporates the official colours of their company branding.

name: Albany
restrictions: Yes. The use of this tartan is restricted by Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & ScotlandShop USA Inc. This tartan can only be woven or reproduced with prior written consent from Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & ScotlandShop USA Inc.
registrationNotes: The Albany tartan was designed to represent the Scottish community within Albany County, New York, United States. The colours were inspired by the Albany County Seal, The Town of Colonie Seal & The City of Albany Flag. The sett was inspired by the Royal Stewart tartans. The design includes an additional white stripe intended to represent the Scottish Saltire when crossing the blue ground. It was designed by ScotlandShop to celebrate the links between Scotland and Albany and the opening of their store there.

name: Boulamy, Jean-Baptiste & Aguilar, Mariana (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the family, their children and descendants. Permission to use this tartan must be granted by the owner or their heirs. Permission to weave this tartan must be granted by the owners or their heirs.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent the couple’s passion for Scotland, its culture and landscapes. The design is intended to represent the marriage of Jean-Baptiste & Mariana using colours from the flags of Scotland, France & Mexico.

name: Segura, Luis Horacio (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Luis Horacio Segura and family members. Others wishing to wear, use or weave this tartan should seek written authorisation from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created for personal use of Luis Horacio Segura. The colours are based on the natural colours of Eastern Patagonia's landscape, the designer's homeland and place of residence.

name: Brougher, J & M (2021) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Jackson & Madeline Brougher. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created celebrate the marriage of Jackson & Madeline Brougher. The design takes inspiration from the Fraser tartan as Jackson’s family on his mother’s side are all Frasers. The threadcount includes numbers that reference the couple’s wedding date. The colour palette was inspired by the flags of significant countries & states, reflecting the family’s international heritage. The grey overcheck represents the couple’s pet greyhound.

name: Brown, Douglas Ian Cameron (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those authorised by the copyright holder Douglas Brown. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder(s).
registrationNotes: Closely based on the 1842 Cameron tartan, the blue, representing Rangers Football Club, is surrounded by 50 marled dark grey threads to mark, not only his 50th birthday but also to represent the Harris Tweed from Douglas's strong North Uist roots. The black bands have 22 threads - the house number of Douglas & Mairi's new home and the red comes from both the Cameron and the MacDonald of Sleat tartans to commemorate Douglas's Mother & Grandmother respectively. The blue band has four threads, one for each of the Brown family - Douglas, his parents Iain & Mairi and his sister Shona.

name: Ferreira Fialho dos Anjos, Miguel Nuno (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Miguel Anjos and his immediate family. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Miguel Anjos and his family based on Miguel’s personal history. Colours: the red, green and yellow, representing gold, are based on the colours of the flag of Portugal, Miguel’s native land; red and white represent Canada, where Miguel grew up; blue and white represent Scotland, where he is a Professor at the University of Edinburgh and the addition of purple, an imperial colour, is a nod to his fascination with history.

name: Clydeview Academy
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Clydeview Academy.
registrationNotes: The school is located on an enviable site overlooking the River Clyde, Scotland. The school celebrated 10 years of leading education in this beautiful landscape, and wanted to communicate their rich natural and cultural heritage through their new school tartan. The colour palette is intended to evoke visions of shimmering silver seas and heather laden hills. The accents of dark purple and gold link with the school’s colours.

name: Gatlin, Charles M and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the family of Charles M Gatlin and Frances Walker Gatlin, and all their descendants. The colours red, white and blue were chosen as those colours are featured in the flag of Texas, the state where Charles and Frances raised their family. Green and white are intended to represent the University of North Texas, of which several family members are alumni.

name: Plaid for Dad
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone. May only be woven with written permission from the owners of the tartan - The Canadian Cancer Society, 55 St Clair Ave W, suite 500, Toronto, Ontario, M4V 2Y7, Canada
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Canadian Cancer Society "Plaid for Dad" campaign, to raise funds and awareness of prostate cancer and to support research.

name: Hillsden, Kenneth J Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Ken Hillsden and his family. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from Ken Hillsden and family. Prepared for weaving by Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: A hunting tartan created for Ken Hillsden and his family, combining their Scottish and English heritage. The design and colours are intended to symbolise their passion for field sports, and the pursuits of sailing, fishing and hill walking in the beautiful landscape of Scotland: muted green is intended to represent the hills and forests of the Glens; purple represents the heather clad grouse moors; yellow represents the fields of wheat and barley in the beautiful county of Angus and red is intended to represent Ken’s love of Scotland and the red rose, symbolising the eternal love for Ken’s late wife and his children’s mother, Irene.

name: Viking Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland; House of Edgar; Strathmore Woollen Company; Marton Mills. May only be sold through USA Kilts and St Kilda Store.
registrationNotes: Colours: green represents the earth; blue represents the sea; grey represents the fjords of Norway and the white lines are intended to represent the realms of Norse mythology.

name: AgbioInvestor
restrictions: Yes. All tartan enquiries must be directed to AgbioInvestor or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed using a combination of corporate company colours. It is intended to aid promotion of AgbioInvestor and their proud Scottish heritage to their global client base.

name: Our Hero Scot
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone, however it but may not be used for commercial purposes unless under a valid licensing agreement. May only be woven with written authorisation from the owners, Our Hero Scot Productions, 1344 Hillcrest Drive #30, Thousand Oaks, CA, 91362, USA
registrationNotes: A tartan for Our Hero Scot Productions, California, named after the company mascot. The colours chosen are intended to represent the wild Scottish landscape with a touch of heather.

name: Bickerstaff, C & S (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and purchased by the Bickerstaff family unless advised otherwise with written confirmation from a member of the family. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Conor Bickerstaff by MacGregor and MacDuff. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for the Bickerstaff family and their descendants. The green and blue threads are intended to represent the beautiful coastal landscapes and seaside from their hometown of Troon on the west coast of Scotland. With the red and brown threads referencing family bloodline and connections to Dundee.

name: Silver Darlings
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate 15 years of business for Soy Kilts Ltd. The Silver Darlings tartan was produced with local history in mind - Silver Darlings being the local name for herring which have been fished for in the North East & in fact the full east coast of Scotland for decades. The colours chosen are intended to represent the following: blues and dark grey represent the sea; grey and silvery white to represent the ‘silver darlings’ themselves and the thin red line to represent the sails of the drifter boats traditionally used to fish for the herring.

name: Gaspésie
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Gaspésie area, Quebec, Canada. It was based on an idea from M. Benoît Poulin, a bagpiper from the Gaspésie area, who thought the region should have its own official tartan. The design was inspired by the proposed regional flag created by the historian Marc-Antoine De Roy in 2001.

name: Trinder, Svend and Patricia & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the family of Svend and Patricia Trinder. The design is intended to represent the family’s Scottish heritage and Danish heritage joining together.

name: Sharma, Shyam & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Sharma Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the Sharma family’s academic connections to Scotland and is inspired by elements of the City of Edinburgh and Aberdeen tartans. The colour palette used reflects the family’s Indian heritage.

name: Sumner, M & Green, L (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Matthew Sumner & Louisa Sumner (née Green). Colours: the blue and red are intended to represent the household division where Matthew served with the Grenadier Guards; green is for Louisa’s family name and yellow represents the Welsh daffodil.

name: Buchanan Inauguration
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Buchanan family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the new Buchanan Clan Chief's Inauguration in October 2022 as a colourful option to wear at the event and to use for different items related to the event. The colours used in this tartan are a twist on the colours found in the Buchanan tartan. This was designed to be an option for those who want to wear the Buchanan tartan but uses a different palate; forest green is now a deep turquoise; yellow is a coral shade and red is a bright pink.

name: Suginamigakuin
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Takimoto Co Ltd. Used for the DC Dalgliesh brand in Japan.
registrationNotes: A tartan for school uniform produced by Takimoto Co Ltd for Suginamigakuin High School, of Tokyo, Japan.

name: Buckley, R & E (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed using colours of significance for the couple. They have spent a lot of time in Scotland for travel and working with youth groups.

name: Lahey, E & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for personal and family use only. May only be woven with permission from Eric Lahey. Cannot be used for commercial purposes without written consent.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Lahey family and future generations. It includes colours intended to represent the geographical areas where the family are from: blue is for lakes and rivers; greens for cedars and forests; light blue for winters and red is intended to represent future bloodlines.

name: Kerrigan, William George & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Kerrigan family. It is intended to celebrate the family’s heritage and be worn by all family members.

name: Chan, Marco & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Marco Chan and his family. It was inspired by the family’s love of the bagpipes, which Marco plays, and their love of Scottish Culture.

name: Girouard, J L (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed as a gift for Jean-Louis Girouard to celebrate the wedding of his daughter Julie Girouard and Benedict McAndrew on 11th June 2022.

name: Lindsay-McGee, C & V - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designers.
registrationNotes: A tartan to celebrate the wedding of Victoria Lindsay and Calum McGee.

name: Yen, Alexander (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Alexander Yen's immediate family or anyone else with written permission. May only be woven with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Alexander Yen.

name: Kelvinside Academical Club
restrictions: Yes. All tartan enquiries must be made to Kelvinside Academy or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: In the early 1900s Kelvinside Academy Former Pupils held a meeting to decide the club colours and they all agreed on green, purple and black which were used to create a striking tie. In 1998 Kelvinside Academy created its own tartan (STA ref #7936) in the school colours of blue and silver and the Kelvinside Academical Club have now created a Former Pupil Tartan to compliment this. This tartan will also celebrate 150 years of the School in 2028.

name: Tully, Andrew Michael & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Andrew Michael Tully and his family. The colours are based on those traditionally associated with the name Tully and ancient family arms. The ‘weathered’ green is intended to pay homage to their ancestor Gilla-Michael Mac Taichligh (MacTully), who fought in the Battle of Moy Slecht in 1256. The number three is featured throughout the design as this is a significant number for the family.

name: Tabili, M & L and Bianchi, C & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Marco Tabili, his mother, sister, family and successors.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed for Marco Tabili, his sister Livia Tabili and their mother Cinzia Bianchi. The design incorporates the family colours.

name: Mojeiko, Vladimir & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the Mojeiko family and their descendants. Other use requires permission from the Mojeiko family. Prepared for weaving by Red Label Kilts Inc.
registrationNotes: The Mojeiko family tartan was created to celebrate the family emigrating to Canada and to represent new beginnings. Colours: red and white represent the family’s European (Belarus) and Canadian roots, and represents China where the family spent thirty years building their family; blue represents the journey across the seas and green represents the beautiful forests of Cape Breton Island. The two black lines are intended to represent the two families of eagles who nest on the edge of their new property. The thread count references thirty years in China and the thirtieth anniversary in 2021 of the couple’s marriage.

name: Heather's Christmas Wish
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Heather's family and those with permission from the family. Prepared for weaving by Red Label Kilts Inc.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to commemorate and celebrate the life of Heather MacNeil Adams, beloved wife, mother, sister, daughter and friend. Heather had a wish; a tartan of her own with bright and vibrant colours to symbolise hearth and home and to celebrate Christmas, her favourite time of year. In honour of her Christmas wish Heather’s friends and family designed this tartan in her memory. The colours are intended to represent what was important to Heather: Red is for love; green was her favourite colour; blue represents her husband and sons; pink is for her daughters and purple represents pancreatic cancer. Yellow represents the rose planted by Heather which blooms every year, even in the snow.

name: Ruane, M (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Ruane Family. The design is intended to represent their family motto of ‘I grow through the cross’ and uses the family colours; green and yellow. The blue in the design is intended to represent the oceans that separate the family members but the yellow cross represents their connection, despite the distance.

name: Doerr, Michael & Riley and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Prickly Thistle for the Doerr family and their use. All weaving of the tartan must be commissioned with permission from the Doerr family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the marriage and future family legacy of Michael & Riley Doerr. Married on the 18th September 2021, they honeymooned in the Scottish Highlands and together during that time created a family tartan that reflected their love for family identity unified and symbolised by a tartan cloth. The colour inspiration for this design reflects their fondness of the Scottish skies and waterways, the strong and soft blue tones of deep lochs that also connects them to their first memories in Naples. The light overchecks of deep claret and grey represent Michael and Riley. Forming the basis of the threadcount to this design are dates of significance to them; their wedding date and the date they first met.

name: Doerr, Michael & Riley and Family Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Prickly Thistle for the Doerr family and their use. All weaving of the tartan must be commissioned with permission from the Doerr family
registrationNotes: A dress version of the Doerr, Michael & Riley and Family (Personal) tartan (SRT #13372). It was created for all members of their family to use and wear at celebratory events. A range of silvery grey hues, intended to symbolise celebration for the family, were selected for this design which uses the original threadcount from their Personal tartan.

name: Educational Institute of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by those authorised by the Educational Institute of Scotland. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the Educational Institute of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Educational Institute of Scotland tartan is inspired by the Balmoral tartan, which was designed around 1851 and later attributed to Prince Albert, the same year that Queen Victoria granted a Royal Charter to the organisation which was founded in Edinburgh in 1847. Woven into the design are 175 threads of purple yarn – one for each year of the Institute’s professional life – making it the oldest teaching union in the world. Black is essentially for the traditional dominies’ mode of dress and, together with the purple, mirrors the Institute’s graduation gowns. Blue and green are additional house colours of the EIS and the red represents the rampant lion of Scotland in the Institute’s coat of arms, the banner of which proclaims ‘Learning promotes natural talent.’

name: LaFemina, Peter & Lori and Family (Personal)
designer: Urquhart, Blair, House of Tartan, Scotland
registrationNotes: A tartan for the LaFemina family from Chicago. The colours were chosen to represent the different family members: dark blue for the family's patriarch, Peter; green for the matriarch, Lori; the three brown lines are for the 3 children, Niki, PJ, and Joey and the yellow line represents the newest addition to the family, Julia, who was a baby when the tartan was designed.

name: Vogelsang, Peter (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Dellman family. It is intended to be used by future generations and to be a symbol of unity for the family.

registrationNotes: A universal tartan to celebrate ancestral connections all over the world.

name: MacMahoon - Larp Group Germany
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be offered, woven or manufactured in commercial form without the express permission of Werner Schlothauer, his family or Torsten Arends.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the German Larp (Live Action Role Playing) group who portray a Scottish Fantasy Clan – MacMahoon. The group was founded in 2004 by Werner Schlothauer. Members all share a passion for Scotland, its people, history and traditions and always wanted to have a tartan of their own. The colours are intended to represent freedom, Scotland’s landscapes and the experiences shared by the group’s members.

name: Grewar, M and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the registrant, their immediate and extended family and any Gruer/Grewar with permission from the registrant. The tartan may only be woven by or with permission from the registrant, his heirs, successors or representative.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Michael Grewar and his family. It was created to celebrate the family history which dates back to the 11th century when the Gruers were first recorded in Braemar.

name: Lacrosse Scotland
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding use or weaving must be directed to Lacrosse Scotland or Slanj Kilts. Manufacture is restricted to those licensed by Lacrosse Scotland, and the tartan cannot be reproduced, printed, woven or copied without the permission of the Board of Lacrosse Scotland.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Lacrosse Scotland, the National Governing Body of the Sport in Scotland. It was designed to be the official tartan of the organisation, members, and representative teams. Colours: blue aligns with the national colour of Scotland worn during international competition; purple represents the origin of the sport as the Creator's Game and is intended to give thanks to the Haudenosaunee for their gift of lacrosse; green celebrates the history of the women's game of lacrosse in Scotland, who wore the MacLeod tartan; orange marks the historic first ever men's game with Syracuse University, prompted as a testimonial following the Lockerbie air disaster. Tartan design – Laura Reid. Lacrosse Scotland community consultation – Tobias Cleaver-Ross. Tartan project coordinator – Stefan Wyroslawski. Lacrosse Scotland Chair – Mason Robbins.

name: Biltmore Forest Country Club
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Biltmore Forest Country Club or Seamus Golf. Biltmore Forest Country Club has exclusive rights for use of the material on merchandise or other uses as they deem fit. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. All persons not affiliated with Biltmore Forest Country Club's Board of Governors, General Manager, Head Golf Professional, or Seamus Golf, must seek written permission from Biltmore Forest Country Club prior to use of the design.
registrationNotes: Biltmore Forest Country Club was established in 1922 by the Vanderbilt family in Biltmore Forest, North Carolina. This tartan was created to commemorate the club’s centennial birthday on July 4th, 2022. The design is intended to bring the different aspects of its history into one piece. In 1921, the club hired Scottish Donald Ross to be the architect of the golf course, which has always been the centrepiece of the club, and this tartan is intended to honour him. The design takes aspects of the Ross tartan and ties it in with the club colours of royal blue and white. The other colours within the tartan are used throughout the club. Biltmore Forest County Club collaborated with Seamus Golf to create this tartan.

name: Docherty, William Thomas and Mary Bridget (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Docherty Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate William Docherty’s 70th birthday and his mother’s 90th birthday. The design takes inspiration from the MacLellan and MacGregor tartans.

name: London North Eastern Railway (LNER)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by employees, or former employees, of LNER. May only be woven by those delegated by LNER.
registrationNotes: The London North Eastern Railway (LNER) tartan features colours that represent the places and communities along the LNER route, from the Scottish Highlands to London. The predominant colour is blue, for Scotland, with other colours including red for England, white for the white rose of Yorkshire (LNER’s historic headquarters), purple for the heather of Scotland, green to represent the rolling hills and beautiful scenery of our destinations, and silver-grey tramlines to convey the steel tracks of the railway that connect the people and communities along the whole LNER route. The tartan recognises the ‘LNER clan’ within the railway family, and is intended to be worn by employees, or former employees of LNER. It was unveiled at Edinburgh Waverley station on 31 July 2019, to commemorate the launch of LNER’s Class 800 train ‘Azuma’ on its Anglo-Scot services, which commenced the following morning on the iconic Flying Scotsman service that departed Edinburgh Waverley at 5.40am on 1 August 2019.

name: Broome County, New York
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holder George Barlow or his appointed agents and officials from the Broome County administration. Cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder George Barlow.
registrationNotes: Based on the Old Stewart tartan, the focal point of three green bands on blue is for the sprigs of broom in the county seal - which in turn were taken from the original Broome coat of arms. Also from the County Seal is the yellow which, together with brown and green represents the rich farming land and afforestation that attracted so many early settlers. The colours of opal blue and white represent the Iroquois confederacy. The red and white stripes are taken from the American flag, while the centre white line represents a letter from George Washington regarding military matters which is kept in the vault of the Broome County Historical Society. The actual date of the founding of Broome County, 28th March 1806, is woven into the thread counts of the green, blue and yellow focal point.

name: Dalrymple, M, of Oxenfoord (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan celebrates the Blairgowrie marriage of Jacob Gunst and Brookes May. In the spirit of kinship, the couple collaborated with Ashleigh Slater, Tartan Caledonia, on a design for their union. Colours: green is intended to represent life, prosperity, nature and peace; gold represents the earth and good fortune; the grey hues represent wisdom and timelessness, and blue represents the sea and sky. This Tartan will serve as a symbol of love, hope and prosperity for the newlyweds and their family now and forever.

name: By Moonlight
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to commemorate those engaged in clandestine operations during World War II. The light and dark colours are intended to represent the stillness of night, a calm before activity and the moon's illumination on land, sea and air during the hours of darkness. The pattern is broken with a touch of red and purple to reflect sacrifice and loss.

registrationNotes: This design was created to celebrate the multiple Scottish lineages in the Ottinger family. The sett was inspired by the Colquhoun and Erskine black and white designs to honour the family's past.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the joining of two families, each from separate backgrounds and starting anew. The colours represent the couple’s favourite colours and their wedding colours.

name: Rozier-Peltier, Morgan and Jean-Philippe & Family (Personal)

Only Morgan Rozier and Jean-Philippe Peltier, and their descendants can commission any weaving of this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the marriage of Morgan Rozier and Jean-Philippe Peltier. The design includes colours that are special to the couple; blue, Morgan’s favourite colour, is intended to represent music and Morgan’s profession as a harpist and black, for Jean-Philippe, is intended to represent mystery, the unknown, and their cats.

name: Smith, Shaila and Seán (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Written permission to use or weave this tartan should be sought from the designer, Sean Smith.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the lineage of siblings, Shaila and Seán Smith. The colours were chosen to represent the nations, modern and ancient, and faiths that shaped the family's migrations. The sett was designed to create a dark area leading to an intensely bright, single stripe. This design is intended to represent how the siblings' line is ending with them, but the family legacy will carry on through other branches of the family tree.

name: Quinnell, Scott & Nicola and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended for use by the Quinnell family from Wales. The colours were inspired by their family home in Monmouthshire: the two grey shades are intended to represent the local rocks and slate; green is for the surrounding lands and white represents the area's regular snowfalls - bringing to mind times of being snowed in together as a family.

name: Royal Agricultural Winter Fair Centennial
restrictions: Yes. The Royal Agricultural Winter Fair must be consulted before this tartan is woven and must provide approval as to which mill should undertake its weaving.
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the 100th Anniversary of The Royal Agricultural Winter Fair which is dedicated to showcasing excellence in Canadian agriculture, local food, and equine sport. Since its inception in November 1922, The Royal Agricultural Winter Fair has become the world’s largest combined indoor agricultural and international equestrian event. The central focus of this 7-colour design is 100 threads of royal blue representing ‘A Century of Champions’. The 22 threads of dark blue represent The Fair’s centennial span (1922 – 2022). Light grey, representing platinum, pays tribute to The Fair’s longstanding connection to the Royal Family and the centennial coinciding with Her Majesty’s Platinum Jubilee. The red ribbon is for The Fair’s commitment to “Best in Class”, balanced by yellow ornaments, representing gold, to signify the excitement for the next 100 years to come.

name: Suggs, B (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with permission from the designer and copyright holder.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Bradley Suggs. The design was inspired by a visit to Urquhart Castle on 2 July 2018.

name: Teaghlach Taghta
registrationNotes: Teaghlach Taghta means chosen family. It was designed for the online group ‘Chosen Family’, an LGBTQ group of friends who have found each other, their ‘chosen family’, in the absence of their actual families throughout the COVID-19 pandemic or as a result of other life challenges. The colours are intended to represent the countries of their members; Scotland, Australia & Brazil. The tartan was presented as a gift to their friend and member Jordan Wilson on his birthday.

name: Dark Sky Alpacas
registrationNotes: A tartan for Dark Sky Alpacas, an alpaca farm in Cornwall producing luxury products from their alpacas’ fleeces. The tartan was designed to celebrate the owners' Celtic roots and the naturally produced fibre.

name: Grzincic, N & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Nathan Grzincic and Chelsea Wintringham. The design uses colours of significance for the couple: red symbolizes the joining of two families; the greens represent the couple, teal for Chelsea and dark green for Nathan, and light blue represents the Air Force, the institute that brought them together.

name: MacRitchie, Iain (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Iain MacRitchie. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan has been created for Iain MacRitchie. The design takes inspiration from a tartan collected in the Hebrides and the Perthshire district tartan where the MacRitchie name has family roots and historical connections. The colour palette has been created and inspired by the beauty of a Western Isles’ seascape, blended with the richness of Scottish landscapes.

name: MacRitchie, Iain Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Iain MacRitchie. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Iain MacRitchie tartan (SRT #13427).

name: Lauren Currie Twilight Foundation
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those with permission from the Lauren Currie Twilight Foundation. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: The Lauren Currie Twilight Foundation was established in 2010 following the death of Lauren at the age of 15. Lauren died from a rare autoimmune condition called vasculitis. Vasculitis means inflammation of the blood vessels, causing swelling of the blood vessels and arteries, blocking the flow of blood to major organs and tissues. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent permanent damage or death.

name: Malcolm de Cunningham Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use this tartan must be sought from Nicholas Chance Burns Mitchell Cunningham or from Logan Jackson Cunningham (son of/and copyright holder of the Tartan). Registered by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland on behalf of Nicholas Chance Burns Mitchell Cunningham, P.O. Box 162, Kingston, Missouri, 64650 Email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan to commemorate Malcolm de Cunningham (c.1040-1096). The colours are intended to represent the bloodlines that branch out from Malcolm de Cunningham, Thane of Cunningham. Malcolm de Cunningham was awarded the Thanedom of Cunningham (Cunninghame) in Northern Ayrshire for his protection of and service to the Crown, namely King Malcolm III. The children and grandchildren of Malcolm went on to establish the Cunningham Clans of Northern Ayrshire.

name: Graham, Robert Lee & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Mr Robert Lee Graham, his siblings, direct descendants and/or others with his written permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Mr Robert Lee Graham, Pasadena, Texas, and his family. The design was inspired by the Graham and Montrose tartans and includes elements intended to represent the coat of arms for William de Graham. The dark red colour, that has been included, is intended to represent the long history of red hair in his family.

name: Fen and Field
registrationNotes: The Fen and Field tartan is intended to be a general outdoors/hunting multi-use design. Using traditional colours and classic muted tones, inspired by the landscape and surroundings it is intended to be worn in, the pallet reflects the grasses, lichen, stones, earth, and water/sky reflection found in and around fens and fields.

name: Wainwright, C and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Chris Wainwright and his family to celebrate their family heritage.

Mounier is the French equivalent of Miller and Miller is a sept of Clan MacFarlane. The threadcount contains numbers of significance to the family. The colours used include the Tricou and Mounier families’ colours.

name: Unique Heritage Media

registrationNotes: This corporate tartan has been created for Unique Heritage Media. The threadcount uses numbers of significance to the Company. The palette uses the Company’s publishing house and main brand colours, and grey to represent the printed word and publishing world.

name: Gordon-Beresford, Roland (Personal)

registrationNotes: A tartan for Roland Gordon-Beresford using colours of personal significance. The sett was inspired by the tartan worn by the Gordon Highlanders, as his mother was a Gordon, and also by the family colours.

name: Langman, Tom and Harry (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Registered on behalf of Harry Langman [[email protected]] by House of Tartan Ltd, Scotland. Phaethon Harry Langman 4 Wright Close St Helens Merseyside United Kingdom WA10 2UR
registrationNotes: A tartan for Tom and Harry Langman. The design was inspired by their Scottish roots and their wedding, which took place on 31st October 2020. The colours reflect the autumnal colours they had for their hand-fasting ceremony and their peacock feather buttonholes. The threadcount includes references to their wedding date.

name: Show Me (Missouri)
registrationNotes: The Show Me tartan was created for the use of Missourians and those celebrating the State of Missouri, United States. The name of the tartan – Show Me - is a nickname for the State of Missouri. The colours were chosen from existing state symbols: the Eastern Bluebird, Grizzly Bear, Missouri Mule, the Crescent Moon, and the State’s mountains, forests, and waterways. Representative Grier proposed the original legislation that this design by Kenneth W. Slayor, originally woven by Jeffery Reynolds, and approved through the Scottish St. Andrew Society of Greater St. Louis, did pass into law making the 'Show Me' tartan a symbol of the state on the 11th of July, 2019.

name: Alba Party
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of the Alba Party. The Alba Party has exclusive rights for use of the material on merchandise or other uses as they deem fit. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland and anyone approved by the Alba Party.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Alba Party. Colours: white and blue are intended to represent the Saltire; black is for strength and bravery and light brown, representing gold, is intended to symbolise the sovereignty of Scottish people.

name: Highland Saga
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by clients, employees, musicians and family members as authorised by the copyright holder. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills.
registrationNotes: Highland Saga is a stage show based in Germany. The story revolves around a musical journey through time that takes the audience to the Scottish Highlands. The production includes bagpipes, drums, singers and musicians intended to give an insight into the Scottish musical traditions.

name: Milne Graden
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Milne Graden Estate.
registrationNotes: This tartan design was inspired by the Milne Graden estate’s history and its approach to today's rural living. Two hundred years ago Milne Graden House was built by Naval Admiral David Milne. The dark colours found in the tartan represent the treacherous seas the Admiral faced during his lifetime in the navy, the natural sandstone the colour of the locally quarried stone used to build the holiday cottages. Flashes of silver grey represent the Spring salmon on their journey up the river Tweed, the golden threads reminiscent of Autumn sunlight through the Milne Graden trees.

name: Ebert-Moran, Yasmin & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Yasmin Ebert-Moran and Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
