The design combines elements of the Connacht and Dundee district tartans with colours that represent the families’ strong association with Leeds, Durham, Oxford, and Hong Kong. The threadcount uses numbers and colours of significance to the family.

name: Cosgrove, Richard and Catherine (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Richard and Catherine Cosgrove and family. Permission to weave must be sought from both Richard and Catherine Cosgrove and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This design was created for the marriage of Catherine Hicks and Richard Cosgrove. Rick and Catherine, and her five brothers, are intended to be represented in the various elements within the design. The colours were inspired by a painting hanging in the hallway of their wedding venue, Skibo Castle.

name: Solveig in Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Solveig Kerdranvat and family. Permission to weave must be sought from both Solveig Kerdranvat and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Created for Solveig in Scotland, this design was inspired by Solveig Kerdranvat’s passion for Scotland and desire to create a tartan to fit her brand aesthetic. The colours are intended to represent Scotland’s rich landscape and her Highland pony ‘MacNab’.

name: Yamato International
registrationNotes: The Yamato International tartan was designed to commemorate the 60th anniversary of their brand ‘CROCODILE’ which launched in 1963. The tartan uses the colours associated with the brand: white represents wool, the raw material of the fabric used; dark blue represents the tradition and style of the brand; dark yellow represents sophistication and dignity and green represents their crocodile icon.

name: Spirit of Le Mans (GT)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave this tartan must be sought from Andy Clegg, the designer and copyright holder of the tartan. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar; a subdivision of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the annual sports car races in Le Mans, France, and in particular those races that took place during the 1960s.

name: Kilcamb Lodge
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Kilcamb Lodge. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This corporate tartan has been designed for Kilcamb Lodge in Strontian. The Hotel’s location inspired the design. The Lochaber district tartan was used as a starting point. Colours: grey represents the granite stonework of the Hotel and the area’s historical lead and Strontium mines; blue is for the sea and with white is intended to represent the Saltire; purple is for the flora of Scotland’s West Coast and the shades of brown celebrate the landscape of the nearby Ariundle Nature Reserve and the local wildlife which includes sea otters, eagles and pine martens.

name: Warm Your Heart
restrictions: Yes. Written permission from Patrick King Woollen Company is required to reproduce this tartan in any form. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Patrick King Woollen Company’s ‘Warm Your Heart’ campaign. The goal of the campaign is to distribute one million blankets globally to help the homeless. The colours are intended to represent: red for love and strength; black is for dignity; green is for kindness and white is for hope.

name: Monarchist League of Canada, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of members of The Monarchist League of Canada. Weaving mill to be chosen by The Monarchist League of Canada.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as an entry into a competition held by the Monarchist League of Canada in February 2021, enabled by the benefaction of Dr Oscar Vicente to mark the League’s Golden Anniversary. Over forty-nine entries were received, then narrowed down to four and subsequently members chose this design by way of online voting. Taking inspiration from the Royal Stewart tartan, the central white line pays tribute to Her Majesty’s Platinum Jubilee; red and gold represent the colours of the League’s heraldic flag and badge; purple symbolizes royalty and blue recalls the blue found on the Royal Standard flag and also represents Canada’s numerous lakes and surrounding oceans.

name: Campeaux, W and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by William Campeaux-Peterson for his wedding and to represent the two sides of the family. It is intended to be worn by worn by all members of both sides of the family.

name: International Beard Alliance Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer: [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan for the International Beard Alliance Scotland Club. The club has members all over the world. The tartan was created to help the club’s purpose which is to raise money for various charities.

name: Festival Intercéltico de Avilés
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the Festival Intercéltico de Avilés. Copyright belongs to the Festival Intercéltico de Avilés.
registrationNotes: The design of this tartan was donated by the Scottish Tartans Authority and presented as a gift from Scotland to the Festival Intercéltico de Avilés y Comarca for its long-standing commitment to promoting Celtic culture in Spain. The yellow cross on light blue represents the flag of the Principality of Asturias, the Festival's annual venue and the red, green and black are from the Principality's Coat of Arms. Finally, the white line on blue is for Scotland's flag - the Saltire. Combined they celebrate the vibrancy of the Celtic spirit throughout Europe.

name: Gray Stephens, Douglas (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for the family of Douglas Gray Stephens. The tartan started life as a marital tartan and is now worn by the family.

name: Cecil D Pickersgill Commemorative
registrationNotes: A tartan to commemorate the designer's father, Captain Cecil D. Pickersgill of the Royal Engineers, who died working as a POW on the Burma Railway in 1943. While held at Changi Prison Camp he built a lychgate for the cemetery, basing the design on the one at Holy Trinity Church, Startforth, Barnard Castle. The red and blue of the tartan represent the colours of the Royal Engineers, and the black bars and grey threads represent the beams and barbed wire used in the lychgate's construction. The lychgate now stands at the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire.

name: Gueltas, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn, with permission from the owner, by those with the surname Gueltas, Gweltaz, spelling variations and those living in places devoted to Saint Gweltaz. Permission to weave this tartan must be obtained from the owner.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Steven’s wedding and the family surname, Gueltas, which is associated with the Breton Saint Gweltaz, originating from Strathclyde. The colours used are based on the family colours and the colours found on the Strathclyde Blue district tartan.

name: Dunnet, J, Canisbay (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by all those with the surname Dunnet in all its forms. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder John Dunnet, his agents or heirs & successor.
registrationNotes: This family tartan for John Dunnet is based on the 1819 Green MacKay from Wilsons of Bannockburn (STA #703). The first significant feature is the brown lines on green which represent the traditional lines of peat that - when a boy - John dug with his grandfather. Where those lines cross and form a mesh, they're for his grandfather's fishing creels that John helped to pull up from the seabed. Those lines of brown number four and they celebrate John being a fourth generation Freemason in the footsteps of his father, grandfather and great grandfather. Finally, his lifetime in the fire service is remembered with the red from the Highlands & Islands Fire Brigade badge and the dedication of that service is woven into the design with 24 threads of black and 7 threads of grey.

name: Broken Arrow, City of
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Cody Wagnon and Steve Campbell, and submitted by Scotfest Inc on behalf of the municipality. Scotfest is a large established Scottish cultural festival of over 40 years and is hosted in the City of Broken Arrow. The design uses the colours of Broken Arrow and their public school.

name: Mounier, Emmanuel Remi Beranger & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Emmanuel Mounier and his family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created for Emmanuel Mounier and his family. The design takes inspiration from elements of the MacFarlane tartan. Mounier is the French equivalent of Miller and Miller is a sept of Clan MacFarlane. The threadcount contains numbers of significance to the family.

name: Panton, F and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Florence Panton, her family and descendants. The colour blue is intended to represent an area in Scotland where the family lived in the 19th century and the colour yellow is included in an historic Coat of Arms associated with the family. The numbers in thread count are significant numbers in the family’s history.

name: Lutton, Wayne & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the Lutton family and those related by marriage. Those who can show lineage linking them to the designer’s family will be permitted to weave this tartan. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Wayne Lutton and his family. The design was inspired by the Black Watch and the family’s military background. The tartan is intended to be worn as a family tartan and used at family events, including Wayne’s wedding.

name: Under Ukrainian Skies
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission from the designers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed with the intention of it representing hope and inspiration for the designers’ home country of Ukraine. Colours: blue is intended to represent the people of Ukraine; black is for the rich fertile soil of the Ukrainian farm lands; yellow representing gold is for the fields of wheat and the deep blue for the sky.

name: Sanctity
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for those who try to live their lives as saintly as possible. The colours: red is intended to represent duty, and the duty to help one another; white represents the purity that sanctity brings; blue is intended to represent justice and yellow is intended to represent religion.

name: National Manufacturing Institute Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Enquiries regarding use/weaving should be directed to www.nmis.scot
registrationNotes: A tartan for NMIS using their brand colours.

name: Child Human Rights Defenders
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries and interest in the tartan regarding wear/use/weaving must be directed to Children and Young People’s Commissioner Scotland or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by young people working with the Children and Young People’s Commissioner Scotland. It was designed to recognise and celebrate the crucial work that child human rights defenders do in standing up and challenging power. The grey background and black lines represent the challenges of standing up for human rights and reference a Maori proverb ‘He pokeke Uenuku?i tu ai’ which means ‘Against the dark cloud the rainbow stands out brightly’, this symbolises the bravery of human rights defenders. The colours chosen and what they intend to represent are: yellow for happiness, positive change and optimism; purple for youth, energy and Scotland’s thistle; green for growth, climate and nature; red for passion and the strength to stop injustices. Across the pattern to represent the support structures to their work is blue for Scotland, the Council of Europe, and the United Nations – the human rights framework.

name: Holliday, Marc & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Marc Holliday and his family. The design was inspired by the colours of an historic Halliday coat of arms featured in Burke’s Peerage General Armoury.

name: Ukraine Forever
restrictions: Yes. The use of this tartan is restricted by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd. This tartan can only be woven or reproduced with prior written consent from Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Great Scot (Scotland) to show solidarity with the people of Ukraine in respect of the conflict which began in their country during February 2022. It was created as part of their fundraising efforts to support the Ukraine Humanitarian Appeal and the related Disasters Emergency Committee charities. The colours were chosen to reflect the Ukrainian flag's blue and gold, and the blue and white of Scotland's Saltire.

name: Doten, J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. No commercial use without written authorisation from the designer.
registrationNotes: This Tartan was designed for Jeffrey Royce Doten, his progeny and his family. The design is based on the Doten (2013) tartan (SRT #10941) and incorporates new elements intended to represent Jeffrey Royce Doten.

name: Doten, J Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. No commercial use without written authorisation from the designer.
registrationNotes: A Hunting tartan for Jeffrey Royce Doten and his family.

name: Doten, J Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. No commercial use without written authorisation from the designer.
registrationNotes: A Dress tartan for Jeffrey Royce Doten and his family.

name: Cuming, W, Australia (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Will Cuming. Intended to be worn by all of the name. Not to be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright-holder, his heirs and successors and/or his appointed agent(s).
registrationNotes: A tartan for Will Cuming. Based on the 1850 Clan Cumming tartan (STA #1157) and using iconic Australian colours of ochre and eucalyptus with a light blue for the expansive skies of the Australian Cumings’ home.

name: Spirit of Glasgow
designer: Slanj Kilts & The House of Edgar
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding use/weaving must go through Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan design intended to encapsulate the vibrant nature of Glasgow and its people, with thread colours inspired by the hues of Glasgow’s night skyline.

name: Spirit of Palestine
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is owned by Mazhar Khan, with all proceeds going to charity. Permissions are limited and the owners must be contacted for rights and usage – [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan has been created to highlight the Palestinian struggle, with all proceeds going to charity. The design incorporates key symbols from the Palestinian flag and the Kufiya scarf. The colours used from the flag include; white meaning peace and love; green symbolising the green plains of the land of Palestine; red symbolises martyrdom and black to represent mourning for injustice and persecution. Additionally, the colours blue and purple are intended to represent security and compassion and gold has been added to symbolise the Dome of the Rock and Jerusalem. Key dates are also incorporated into the design include 1948, the year of the Nakba (Catastrophe), and the 1967 war. Elements taken from the Kufiya scarf include the white cross threads for fishing nets and the green threads for olive leaves representing strength. Finally, the thick black lines are intended to represent the trade routes going through Palestine, and the rich history of merchants, travel and cultural exchange.

name: Edinburgh International Conference Centre 2022, The
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for The Edinburgh International Conference Centre. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This corporate tartan has been designed for The Edinburgh International Conference Centre. This contemporary new colourway uses the Company’s brand colours and is based on the sett of the original Edinburgh International Conference Centre tartan.

name: Scottish American Diaspora
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2022. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. The tartan is created from the amalgamation of UK IPO Registered Designs - Numbers: 4036938 and 6104315 [also registered as US PTO Patent No. D878,059].
registrationNotes: Created for the Scottish Diaspora, the tartan is intended for all Americans of Scottish extraction and their descendants who share a centuries old history and heritage. Large-scale emigration from Scotland to North America began in the 1700s after the Battle of Culloden where the Clan structures were fragmented. The Scots made their transatlantic journey in search of a better life and settled in the thirteen colonies, mainly around South Carolina and Virginia. It was created by merging sett elements from two registered tartans; ‘Declaration of Scottish Independence, Arbroath 1320’ (SRT #11182) and Old Glory (1824) (SRT #11557). The Scottish American Diaspora tartan combines the Red, White & Blue of the United States Stars & Stripes with the Scottish Saltire, the banner of Scotland. Refer to these two designs for the full combined rationale within the weave. Tartan design inspired by Prickly Thistle, Scottish Highlands, 2022.

name: Spessartfolk
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven or used with the expressed written consent of Johannes Heßler. Copyright rests with the designer: Johannes Heßler Contact: [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan for the artist ‘Spessartfolk’. The colours were inspired by the Spessart region, a low mountain range in south-western Germany, with both shades of green intending to represent the dense deciduous forest populating the region. The original name of the region is ‘Spechtshaardt’, which translates to ‘Woodpecker’s forest’. Spessart is home to seven native species of woodpecker and all are represented in the colours of the tartan. The number seven is also reflected in the arrangement of the stripes. The yellow stripe is a reference to the regional specialties of cider and beer.

name: Bards, Ovates and Druids
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the express permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for anyone who calls themself a Druid. The design incorporates colours intended to represent the three grades - Bard, Ovate & Druid - and five elements; earth, air, fire, water and spirit. The three yellow overchecks are intended to represent the three golden strands of Awen.

name: Robin, Paul (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the family only.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Paul Robin and his family.

name: Prieuré St-Pierre de Noron
restrictions: Yes. Use is restricted to the owner of the Prieuré St-Pierre de Noron.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Prieuré St-Pierre de Noron (Priory of St-Pierre de Noron). The design is based on the ancient Coat of Arms of the abbey.

name: Mayvans, J & D (Personal)
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the joining of the May and Evans families. The colours are intended to represent the Scottish, Irish, and American flags.

name: Commonwealth Games Scotland - Team Scotland 2022
restrictions: Yes. All permissions are exclusively at the discretion of Commonwealth Games Scotland.
registrationNotes: Corporate Commonwealth Games Scotland have commissioned this tartan to be designed for Team Scotland for The Commonwealth Games 2022 held in Birmingham. The colour palette draws inspiration from the Team Scotland branding with the addition of yellow to pay tribute to Birmingham 2022's visual aesthetic.

name: Aonaich
restrictions: Yes. Free for public usage. Please contact the designer for artwork and designs.
registrationNotes: The Aonaich tartan, Scottish Gaelic meaning Unite, uses colours reflecting Scotland’s backdrop from the Lowlands to the Highlands. The design is intended to represent the rich diversity of the culture; the arts, the Gaelic language and the range of cultures and creeds. The unity through the colours symbolises the unity of these elements throughout Scotland.

name: Trujillo, A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for family use/wear only or with consent from family members. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, part of the Macnaughton Group Ltd.
registrationNotes: Created for the Trujillo family on the occasion of Antonio Trujillo’s graduation, celebrating their Colombian and Scottish family heritage. The colours combine those found in both coffee plantations and highland glens, within a sett that is based on the beat of a salsa dance and contains details that refer to the Colombian flag.

name: Lively, C & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by anyone with the surname Lively and can be reproduced for personal use. Any sort of commercial production may only be carried out with express permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lively family. The colours, thread and weave are intended to reflect the family’s Irish and Scottish heritage.

name: Holliday, Marc & Family Dress (Personal)
registrationNotes: A dress tartan for Marc Holliday and his family. The design is intended to honour his 3rd Great Grandfather William Holliday and his wife Diannah Hudson Holliday. The colours are intended to represent the family farm: the reds represent the strawberries grown on the farm; green represents the strawberry leaves; the blues represent the waters of lake Ontario and white represents the heavy snowfall that buried the strawberry fields during winter. The purple shade created from the blending of blue and red is intended to represent the coming of night when runaway slaves came out from the caves located on the bluffs of Lake Ontario where William Holliday would hide them before helping them to be ferried across Lake Ontario to Canada.

name: Purdy, L, Cape Breton (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by Leah Purdy for a Purdy Family reunion in August 2022. The design is intended to reflect Cape Breton Island, Nova Scotia, where the family have been for more than 200 years. The design also includes a tribute to Leah’s late grandmother Violet Purdy. Leah wrote a poem to go with the tartan: “Green trees of bonny Breton isle, wind-swept sentinels of old Blue mist rivers, lakes, and streams, and a defiant sun of Gold Grey fog shrouded rocky shores, and silver sea, and squall, and Violet, my island’s heart, makes family of us all.”

name: Fabbro, Jordan & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Jordan Fabbro and direct family members. This tartan may only be woven in Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a family tartan to be worn by Jordan Fabbro and his family.

name: Saviers, Carl & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Saviers family. May only be woven/used with permission from Carl Saviers, his direct family and/or descendants.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Carl Saviers and his family inspired by their connection to Scotland which became apparent when researching their family tree. The family managed to trace their ancestors back to both the lowlands of Scotland and the Orkney Islands.

name: Jones, Philip, Killernie (Personal)
designer: Trivett, Alan, House of Tartan Ltd., Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by all those within the family of Philip Jones, Killernie. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of Philip Jones, his heirs and successors.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Philip Jones and his family based on the Jones tartan #2476 with added gold stripes. The gold represents the golden hair which each member of this branch of the Jones family has.

name: Norman, David (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for family use only. Permission from the designer is required to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A tartan for David Norman inspired by his life spent at sea and family ties to Scotland.

name: Supporters of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. © 2022 House of Tartan Ltd, Crieff, Scotland
registrationNotes: This tartan was created as a tribute to the bravest fans in the world of sport, Supporters of Scotland. Game after game, week after week, year after year, they show up, they and the pipes which give a voice to the Flower of Scotland. They're always there, whether met by absolutely glorious victory or crushing disappointment.

name: Maura
registrationNotes: The Maura Tartan was designed by Isle of Cumbrae Distillers as part of a gin label for their Maura Handcrafted Scottish Gin. An ancient Celtic name meaning ‘Star of the Sea’, Maura is intended to celebrate Scotland’s women, who helped shape its history, legends, and stories of the sea. It is also to commemorate St. Maura, a devotee of St. Columba, who settled on Great Cumbrae in the 7th Century, devoting her life to the religious instruction of young girls to help bring Christianity to the West of Scotland.

name: Emma Basic
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of The Basic Ingredients Ltd. Permission must be sought from both The Basic Ingredients Ltd and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed especially for the Emma Basic brand within The Basic Ingredients Ltd. The colours are intended to represent the story of the Emma Basic brand: orange and red represent the salmon fan, showcasing the exceptional quality of Scottish Salmon; white reflects the clean, simple, signature of the brand; the blue hues reflect the water of Scotland alongside the vivid blue of the Saltire in Scotland and with a diverse and rich landscape, the greens represent colours of the Scottish countryside.

name: Roy, R (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the express permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Randy Roy and his family. The design was inspired by the Maclaren and Robertson tartans.

name: John Hancock
restrictions: Yes. Permission to wear/use this tartan must be sought from John Hancock. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the John Hancock Company based in Boston, Massachusetts. The design uses colours to represent the brand: blue represents the stability synonymous with John Hancock; the green symbolizes life, renewal & energy and cranberry is the state colour of Massachusetts, the home state of John Hancock. These colours are also intended to represent the tranquil lochs, spectacular glens and infamous heather clad mountains of Scotland.

name: Xbox
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used with permission from Microsoft Xbox. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created in 2022 to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the launch of the original Xbox in Scotland and the UK. It formed part of Xbox’s worldwide #Xbox20 celebration, acknowledging the role of the Scots and those of Scottish descent in the creation and success of the videogame console. It’s intended to celebrate the past, present and future of Xbox. The predominant black and green colouring recognise Xbox’s original brand colours, while the white and vivid green accents represent Xbox’s journey from the original console, to Xbox 360, to Xbox One, to the Xbox Series S & Xbox Series X, and onwards to the future of Xbox Game Pass and Xbox Cloud Gaming. The tight sett represents the closeness Xbox enjoys with its vibrant community. A small number of commemorative Xbox controllers were created and wrapped with the Xbox Tartan, woven at Lochcarron of Scotland, and made available for Xbox fans to win.

name: Zekulin, A (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Anthony F Zekulin to celebrate his love of Scotland and all things Scottish.

name: Asturcon
restrictions: Yes. This tartan design is intended for personal use, by horse enthusiasts, the Asturianos and their descendants. This tartan design may only be woven into cloth to be used as a personal article of clothing. It may not be sold commercially, may not be reproduced into graphics or to be published for sale. May not be permitted to be woven by anyone that would profit financially or for monetary gain.
registrationNotes: The design is intended to represent the Asturcon horse, a symbol of strength and fortitude. The ancient horse breed is native to the autonomous principality of Asturias, a Celtic Iberian Nation on the Northwest of Spain. Colours: light blue and yellow are intended to represent the victory cross and the flag of Asturias; red and yellow represents the Spanish national flag; dark blue lines signify the lakes, streams and the Cantabrian sea; black signifies the dark winter coat and mane on the pony; green represents the forest, prairies, meadows where it graces and white is for the fog and snow on the highlands of the Picos de Europa mountains where it roams free.

name: Schiffmann, D C (2022) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of D Schiffmann and his immediate family. May only be woven with written permission from the designer or his family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for D C Schiffmann, his wife and their family using colours of personal significance.

name: Morel, Norma (Personal)
designer: Morel, Norma and Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven in the UK or Switzerland.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Norma Morel to celebrate her Celtic ancestry.

name: Stuart, Roy and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was registered in memory of Roy Stuart, whose family came from Strathdon, and is intended to be used by all of his relatives and family descendants, and Roy's former law students. The threadcount was taken from a piece of tartan handed down to him by his great-grandfather.

name: Tabar, Matthew & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: Carah Smith Tabar designed this tartan for Matthew Tabar for their wedding. It is based on the Smith tartan.

name: MacBride, W M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the designer, his immediate family and descendants. May only be woven with permission from the designer or his descendants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for William MacBride, his family and descendants. The design uses colours of personal significance intended to represent the family, their shared history and their values.

name: Poncelet, Sebastien (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be restricted to those with permission from the designer. May only be woven with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan uses colours of personal significance: blue, Sebastien’s favourite colour, represents the blue in the flags of France and Scotland; yellow represents stars and grey is from the Coats of Arms of the cities of Soissons and Paris. The design incorporates a mathematical pattern, known as a fractal, where the percentages of green and blue in the tartan are intended to reflect the percentages of land and water on earth.

name: Kajul
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the designers Kathy and Julian Eardley, and is intended to represent both of them and their Dalmatian dog.

name: GHK (Glasgow High Kelvinside)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries should be directed to GHK or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: The GHK tartan was designed to mirror the colours of the iconic playing jerseys that have been worn since Kelvinside Academy and the High School of Glasgow former pupils amalgamated in 1982. The tartan is intended to be worn by all the players and their legendary supporters. Black and grey were included so it could also be worn for black tie occasions.

name: Continue
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Brad Wilson, bagpiper and advocate for mental health suicide awareness, and was the winning design for the Sport Kilt 2022 Tartan Design contest. The tartan is dedicated to those who fight the invisible battle every day. Teal and purple are often colours used to represent suicide awareness and feature prominently in this design along with a white stripe intended to represent hope.

name: Hellenic Alliance of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission from the Hellenic Alliance of Scotland and D C Dalgliesh, Dunsdale Mill, Selkirk TD7 5EB. The tartan was registered on 8 September 2021 with the Intellectual Property Office as Design Number 6159999 in the name of the Hellenic Alliance of Scotland, 32/7 East Fountainbridge, Edinburgh EH3 9BH.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Hellenic Alliance of Scotland. It was created to support one of its key aims: to advance public interest in Hellenic culture and heritage and support the development of local Hellenic communities. The design is intended to represent the integration of the Hellenes from Greece and Cyprus with their local communities in Scotland and the shared love of their respective heritages. The colours are intended to reflect key elements of the history and culture of all three countries: blue symbolises the sea and sky, truth and justice; white is for freedom and the foam of the sea; yellow and green symbolise the copper of Cyprus and the desire for peace and red is intended to be a reminder of the blood that has been shed by all three nations throughout their histories.

name: Athwal, Kuljit and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Any enquiries regarding the use of this tartan should be directed to Kuljit Athwal at [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to represent the Athwal family and their journey from Punjab to Scotland. The colours pay homage to the agricultural heartland of India, the Punjab. Colours: the greens are intended to represent lush crop fields of Punjab as well as the beautiful landscapes of Scotland; yellow (gold) represents the beautiful sunsets and also serves as tribute to the Athwal family's Sikh heritage.

name: Halbert, D & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone bearing the Halbert surname or any of its spelling derivatives. There are no restrictions on the weaving of this tartan. The Registrant would ask that before a request for weaving is submitted, that he be notified of such request.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Donald Halbert and his family using colours of personal significance to celebrate the family’s heritage.

name: Lochcarron of Scotland Platinum Jubilee
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by customers of Lochcarron of Scotland. Only to be woven by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The fourth commemorative tartan in the Holyrood series from Lochcarron of Scotland, this was designed in recognition of the Platinum Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. The original sett of the Holyrood, as designed in 1977 by Mr Alistair Buchan, has been recoloured to include purple and platinum in celebration of the reign of Queen Elizabeth II through several Jubilee years.

name: Beal, Richard & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those of the same name or spelling variations thereof. Please contact Denise Beal [email protected] for information on weaving this tartan.
registrationNotes: The Beal family tartan was inspired by the colours of the lichen and rocks on Richard's favourite island off Mossyard near Kirkcudbright. It is intended to evoke happy memories of the family’s favourite corner of South West Scotland.

name: Lowe, John & Ethel and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the family and their descendants. May only be woven with permission from the family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Lowe family in honour of their grandparents John and Ethel Lowe. John married Ethel (Best) on May 18th, 1918. They farmed near Carleton Place Ontario, at Scotch Corners raising a family of 5 daughters and 4 sons. Their descendants bonded to record this history in a unique manner and designed this tartan to represent that shared bond and history. Colours: dark green represents the family’s Irish heritage; red represents Canada; white is in memory of John and Ethel's life together; blue honours their sons and the light green, white and yellow section is intended to symbolise a white Irish rose and the trillium of Ontario flowers for their daughters. The family was gifted with musical talent which continues through the generations and this is symbolised by light grey lines for instrument strings.

name: Out & Proud (LGBTQIA+)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2022. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. The ‘Out & Proud (LGBTQIA+)’ tartan – ref. 13525 – is a variant rightfully derived from UK IPO Registered Design No. #6085117.
registrationNotes: Inspired by the LGBTQIA+ community [lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, queer (questioning), intersex & asexual (aromantic or agender), the + representing other sexual identities]. The tartan contemplates the 1979 Pride Flag by late American artist & activist Gilbert Baker, & its 6 rainbow colours which are intended to depict: Red for life; Orange, healing; Yellow, sunlight; Green, nature; Blue, serenity; & Violet, spirit. It also remembers the New York City Stonewall riots – June 1969 – a significant catalyst for the gay rights movement & progressive activism in the US & around the world. Thus 69 light grey threads represents both that year of change as well as the designer’s year of birth, recognising his own personal journey. 48 dark grey threads represents the age the designer embraced his own self-acceptance. The transition from dark grey – to light grey – considers the process of coming out, as well as reflecting a calm spirit, one which may be found in the serenity of acceptance.

The colours are intended to represent the lanscapes that are important to the couple: green represents the green Scottish hills; blue and grey represent Scottish waters and the sky; soft purple was chosen to reflect the native flowers of three landscapes: the heather of Scotland, the lavender fields of Provence (where Paloma was born) and the blossoms of the Jacaranda tree in Nairobi, Kenya.

name: Carnegie Corporation of New York
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions on who can wear this tartan, however should any party wish to use this design in any way they must seek approval from the Carnegie Corporation of New York. This tartan can only be woven with instruction and authority from the Carnegie Corporation of New York.
registrationNotes: The Carnegie Corporation of New York tartan was created to represent the Scottish ancestry of its founder, Andrew Carnegie. Carnegie established the corporation in 1911 to promote the advancement of knowledge and understanding. It is one of the oldest Amercian grant making foundations. The design incorporates the colours of the corporation and the design charts key aspects of its existence. The pivot of 35 magenta threads surrounded by 18 black notes year of Andrew Carnegie's birth 1835. 8 navy threads are symbolic of the 8 organisations he endowed prior to his death - 5 in the US and 3 in the UK. 10 magenta threads note his final donation to the corporation, $10m from his estate. 8 blue threads represent the number of years he was the Corporation’s first president, 1911-1919. 19 red and 19 black threads represent the year of his death. 84 navy blue threads represent the 84 years of his life. Finally, the pivot of 2 magenta threads represent his passions, knowledge and understanding.

name: Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions on who can wear this tartan, however should any party wish to use this design in any way they must seek approval from the Carnegie Corporation of New York. This tartan can only be woven with instruction and authority from the Carnegie Corporation of New York.
registrationNotes: The Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy was formed in 2001 and is bestowed every second year by the Carnegie family of institutions. It was created at the centennial observance of Andrew Carnegie's career as a philanthropist. Incorporating official colours of the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy, the design includes: blue threads at the pivot of the design, which is symbolic of Andrew's first earnings in the USA at the age of 13, $1.20 per week as a bobbin boy in a cotton mill, and the 5 days he worked for his first wage, to later give away all of his wealth to help others. These blue threads are then surrounded by 18 yellow threads and then 35 gold threads to represent his year of birth 1835. Repeated 10 ten times in the sett is 20 navy threads and 2 blue threads, acknowledging at the time of this tartans creation 10 years of medals have been awarded and as a reminder the tartan was created in 2022.

name: Wester Ross Salmon
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Wester Ross Salmon. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven by a supplier commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This company tartan has been created for Wester Ross Salmon. The design takes inspiration from elements of the founding family’s tartan and the colour palette used draws inspiration from the lands and waters of the company's birth, and the practicalities of life and farming at sea.

name: Nebraska
registrationNotes: Representatives from five different Nebraska organisations honouring Celtic culture and heritage came together to design this tartan for all Nebraskans, regardless of lineage, that captures the Spirit of Nebraska in both the land and her people: Scottish Society of Nebraska; Omaha Irish Cultural Center; Ancient Order of Hibernians; Metro Area Kilted Throwers and KZUM's Thunder on the Plains. The colours are intended to represent the State of Nebraska: blues, greens, and yellows represent the rivers, lakes, prairies, and farmland; black gives a nod to the railroads, bringing transportation and employment to the many immigrants during the Homestead Act, including those of Irish and Scottish background; scarlet represents the blood shed of those gone before us and the state’s motto, which is represented in the white stripe, “Equality before the Law.” The tartan was recognised as part of Governor Proclamation in April 2022.

name: Sheena Christie Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. The tartan may be used commercially with permission from the designer, with donations being made to a UK Heart Charity, otherwise with no restrictions for non-commercial purposes. Please contact Steve regarding license to use: [email protected]. UK IPO Registered Design No. #6212389 - Designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - © 2022.
registrationNotes: The tartan commemorates the life of the designer’s dear mother, celebrated Scottish artist Sheena Christie (12.4.45 – 23.5.22), inspired by her love for spring-time daffodils & her favourite colours, purple & lilac. It intends to depict the daffodil with shades between the purple & yellow representing the withering flower, a poignant reminder of the fleeting nature of life. Registered on the date of internment it celebrates her life, but also is a reminder to cherish time spent together. The purple also alludes to her faith and the special significance in the meaning of her name: Sheena, ‘God is Gracious’; & Christie, ‘follower of Christ’. Yellow on purple is a nod to the painting Sheena was most proud of – her portrait of the late Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother – which is displayed in Arbroath Infirmary, where she spent her last days with her family. The thread-count includes: the age she gave birth, 24, & her son’s birth year, 1969; also the age the designer lost his mother, at 52.

The reds intend to characterise the essence of the Highlands flowing in the veins of those appreciative of this imagery. The tartan is the central element to a range of products by the same name.

Aoife's Sensory Bus all started from the life experiences of a beautiful, feisty little girl called Aoife Kidd who sadly died from a brain tumour in December 2019 aged 6. She is the charity's inspiration and behind everything the charity has achieved so far. The blue is intended to represent the Scottish west coast and seaside that Aoife loved so much, with the pink and yellow threads referencing her favourite colours and her bright, free spirit. Aoife's charity was created to remember Aoife and also to create a service for children and young people with additional support and complex needs across Ayrshire.

name: South Georgia
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn/used by those authorised by the copyright holders, The Government of South George & the South Sandwich Islands (GSGSSI). May only be woven with permission from the Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands.
registrationNotes: This design is based on the Roxburgh Red tartan to mark the historic link between South Georgia and the famous British explorer Captain James Cook. Cook landed on the island in 1775 and his father was a farm labourer in Roxburghshire. Colours: blue is intended to represent the vastness of the South Atlantic Ocean; red represents the fisheries patrol vessel; green is intended to represent the biologically diverse coastal strip of the island; yellow is for the millions of penguins that make it their home; purple is for the abundant burnet plant which colours the coastal fringe; white represents the ice and the glaciers that dominate the interior and shape South Georgia's landforms and grey represents the seven former whaling sites, not just for the whales of yesteryear but also the vast number of birds and seals that breed on the islands and the fish that live in what are now a Marine Protected Areas.

name: Rablogan A Monarch's Winter

registrationNotes: The Rablogan A Monarch’s Winter tartan was designed for the company as part of its fashion range so to portray, through colour and density in a traditional Scottish cultural manner, the visual image of the Highland Red Stag in the winter landscape of the Highland Glen. Colours: the variations of blue are intended to depict a wintery sky and reflective shadows in the landscape; white for the natural snow cover; the thin brown lines are intended to depict the scant vegetation during winter; the heavier browns portraying the Monarch himself and the reds intend to characterise the essence of the Highlands flowing in the veins of those appreciative of this imagery. The design incorporates the temperature changes from 1850 to 2022 to create a tartan version of the infographic. The warp and the weft consist of 173 threads, each marking a year of global temperature change.

name: Zeta Psi Fraternity, Inc.
designer: Martin, C A L; McNeillie, G; Boisvert,T; Gillan, B
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of members of the Zeta Psi Fraternity and their families. Weaving mill to be chosen by the Zeta Psi Fraternity.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Carol Martin in collaboration with George G McNeillie, Tyler P Boisvert and Barth H Gillan to mark the 175th anniversary of Zeta Psi Fraternity, one of the world’s oldest collegiate fraternities. Founded in 1847 at New York University, Zeta Psi Fraternity strives to be the premier international men’s fraternal organization and is dedicated to encouraging academic excellence while forging lifelong bonds of brotherhood. Zeta Psi is an international fraternity and has active undergraduate chapters at the finest universities and colleges in the United States, Canada, Great Bitain, Ireland, France, and Greece. name: Rivière-du-Loup 1673

The tartan is intended to honour the major role of the Fraser family in the historical development of the village which became the town of Fraserville and is today Rivière-du-Loup. Under Charles Aubert de la Chesnaye (1632-1702) during the period of Nouvelle-France, the seigniory was exploited for the commerce of fur and fisheries and later for its forest products. At the time, the territory was inhabited by the First Nations, the newly arrived French pioneers and later some British. Colours: orange is intended to represent the First Nations; blue is for the French pioneers and the red represents the arrival of the English, Scottish and Irish people after the British Conquest of 1760. The light blue is intended to represent the modern city of present day.

name: Ayr Rugby Football Club
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries must be directed to Sarah J Sharkey at Ayr Rugby Club.
registrationNotes: Ayr Rugby Football Club was founded on Wednesday 22nd September 1897 in the King's Arms Hotel, Ayr. The original Club colours were black and cerise. The Club played at many local sportsgrounds for the next 65 years before an Extraordinary General Meeting took place in 1962 where the purchase of the Club's home ground, Millbrae, was agreed. In 1984, the committee met to formally agree the exact shade of Ayr RFC cerise as over the years, the shade had become far paler. A tassel of yarn was produced and formalised as the official shade and this tassel is still held at the Club. In 2019, the addition of a part time professional team at Millbrae, the Ayrshire Bulls added grey to the iconic pink and black colours. The Club celebrated it's 125 year anniversary in season 2022/23 and to mark this achievement, the Club commissioned this tartan to be worn by their players and supporters.

The colours are intended to represent their history: the black in the design is for beats of music to represent A&M Records; orange is intended to represent passion, adventure and creativity; the off white is for light, wisdom and optimism as well as their joy and happiness. The green and brown in the design are inspired by the racecourse and fields their racehorses enjoy.

name: Audley, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the ArtFarm Group.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the opening of The Audley Public House, Mayfair, London, in 2022. It was commissioned by ARTFARM, owned by Iwan & Manuela Wirth. The original building was constructed and first registered as a pub in 1730, during the Jacobite era. The design style was informed by tartans from the Jacobite era and the colours obtained through natural dyes. Using this as inspiration, the designer created a palette of natural dyes which are the basis for the colours in this tartan, including cochineal, logwood, indigo and onion. Cochineal, made from the dried body of a beetle, was used to create the shades of red, the inspiration for the ground colour of this tartan. At the time, it was the most expensive dye to obtain and was therefore used as a sign of wealth. The design was created to be used for the Jacobite room in The Audley.

registrationNotes: A hunting version of The Audley tartan (SRT13779). The colours used in this version are intended to reflect the rich Scottish landscape. The design style was informed by tartans from the Jacobite era and the colours obtained through naturally occurring dyes. Using this as inspiration, the designer created a palette of natural dyes which are the basis for the colours in this tartan, including cochineal, logwood, indigo and onion. registrationNotes: A tartan for the Pentreath family, whose name dates back to at least 1398 from Corwall. The name means ‘head of the (sandy) beach’ in Cornish and the majority of male family members have been mariners, this connection with the sea persists to the present day. The design was inspired by the family history: the two shades of blue are intended to represent the deep sea and the sea over a sandy beach; yellow is for the beach and white is for the waves. The combination of all the colours are intended to represent the family’s connection with Cornwall, St Piran’s flag, its historical kings and the national bird of Cornwall, the Chough, that inhabits the cliffs and is said to be the spirit of King Arthur.

name: SALT3 Submarine
restrictions: Yes. Permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought from the designer, Michael Sanders. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The SALT3 Submarine tartan was created for the SALT3 project which explores pollution around submarine bases in United Kingdom coastal waters. The design takes inspiration from submarines that must remain unseen but make their presence felt to present an effective deterrent. Colours: the dark ground is intended to represent naval bases at night and the acoustic tiles on Vanguard nuclear submarines; rust red references the decommissioned submarines stored at Devonport and Rosyth and neutron activation of iron in their nuclear reactors; Blue, green and grey are intended to represent the pollutants Cobalt-60, Tritium and Carbon-14 created in reactions between Uranium reactor fuel, its cladding and water; white denotes salt made from local seawater; Red is intended to represent the patrols escorting submarines in and out of port and grey is a nod to pinstripe suits in Westminster where nuclear decisions are made. The sett reflects the isotopes Uranium-235, Hydrogen-3 and Carbon-14.

name: Royal Odonto-Chirurgical Society of Scotland, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by members and honorary members of the Royal Odonto-Chirurgical Society of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The Odonto-Chirurgical Society of Scotland, founded in 1867, is the oldest dental society in the world, still actively functioning under its original title (the use of the title “Royal” was granted in November 1966) and upholding the original objectives. Its root are traceable to January 1865, when John Smith invited a few surgeons to meet in the Edinburgh Dental Dispensary, with the purpose of founding a society of persons practising ethical dentistry. The founding of the Odonto-Chirurgical Society proved a great stimulus to the ethical and scientific progress of the profession in Scotland. The Society has strong links with the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh, the University of Edinburgh and the City of Edinburgh. The colours are intended to reflect those links: grey from the College and City, azure blue from the University and College, red from the City and to represent blood, pink to represent gingival tissue and ivory colour for teeth and bone.

name: Hail Holy Queen (Salve Regina University)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be worn or reproduced (woven, printed, or any other means of display) with the express written consent from either the designer, John Dale Ritchie or Salve Regina University. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: Salve Regina University in historic Newport, Rhode Island, derives its name from the Latin hymn "Salve Regina"; meaning Hail Queen or Hail Holy Queen. In 1831, Catherine McAuley founded the Religious Sisters of Mercy (RSM) in Ireland. They formed Salve Regina in 1934 after The State of Rhode Island granted them a charter. Salve Regina welcomed its first class in 1947, becoming coeducational in 1973, and achieving university status in 1991. Colours: 3 gold threads for University’s mission to work toward a world that is harmonious, just, and merciful; 47 light blue threads represent 1947; dark green is intended to represent the University’s 80 acre oceanfront campus, a level II Arboretum; 21 black threads for Salve's 21 historic structures; 8 light green threads for the original 8 RSM faculty; 90 navy threads for the 90th Anniversary of Salve receiving its Charter and 8 white threads for Salve's 8 presidents.

registrationNotes: A tartan for the University of Lynchburg, Virginia, United States. It was created to honour the University’s 11th president, Dr. Alison Morrison-Shetlar. The colours are intended to represent the university and its history: red and its location at the heart of the tartan, is intended to represent the students, faculty, and staff; Green is from Clan Morrison’s tartan; grey is intended to be symbolic of the University’s eight pillars and C.L. Snidow, former board of trustees chair and chapel namesake; dark blue represents the dedication of founders Josephus and Sarah Hopwood to the principles of faith and reason on which they began Virginia Christian College (now University of Lynchburg) in 1903; black is intended to represent commitment to civic, professional, and spiritual leadership, which students take into the world and blue is intended to represent the University’s location at the foot of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

registrationNotes: The Perseverance Tartan was adopted by the Lord Strathcona's Horse (Royal Canadians) Regimental Society for the 125th anniversary of Lord Strathcona's Horse (Royal Canadians). The Regiment was raised by a Scot, Donald Smith, Lord Strathcona and Mount Royal. 'The Perseverance' uses the definite article to highlight the regimental motto’s instantiation as Society device. The design and registration were a gift to the Regimental Society by the designer. Colours: red is intended to represent Canada and and is a Regimental Colour; green is a Regimental Colour; yellow, representing gold, is for WWI Cavalry Brigade patch, and 'The Last Spike'; black is for the RCAC Beret and Fallen Comrades and Cavalry Blue for WW I Cavalry Brigade Patch and Alberta Sky. The black stripes are intended to represent the parallel tracks left by armoured vehicles and the cross of blue and gold is intended to evoke cavalry overalls.

The family unit itself is featured in the black bands on navy blue with threadcounts marking Ajay’s arrival in the UK from Ghana (2014), his marriage (2016) and the birth of the couple’s daughter (2018).

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed especially for The Balmoral Hotel, Edinburgh. Taking inspiration from the rich heritage of the hotel, the design is intended to reflect The Balmoral Hotel’s unique story. The 120 blue threads depict the 120th year of the hotel. The famous clock overlooking Waverley railway station that runs three minutes early to prevent people missing their trains, is represented by the three pale green checks. The central blocks of 25 green threads within the design symbolise the 25th anniversary of Rocco Forte Hotels. With family at the heart of The Balmoral Hotel, the two sandy grey checks represent Sir Rocco Forte, Chairman, and his sister Olga Polizzi, Director of Design. The soft pink threads represent Sir Rocco’s three children. The cherry blossoms that line Princes Street in spring are depicted in the pink and white, the pale blue reflects the city on a sunny spring day and the grey represents the sandstone which most buildings in Edinburgh are made from, including The Balmoral Hotel.

name: Monoceros
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2020. All weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. Design registration pending
registrationNotes: The tartan was created to represent Monoceros, a faint star constellation lying to the east of Orion in the northern sky on the celestial equator, 700 light years from Earth. Derived from Latin – the name meaning ‘the Unicorn’ – the star formation was first recorded in 1612 by Dutch astronomer and clergyman Pertrus Plancius. The tartan is intended to visibly portray the pure white and grey shades of the Unicorn; the yellow pivot, a single gold stripe, represents the horn; the white pivot, and cluster of fine grey stripes, represents the Monoceros star chart. The Unicorn (a fabled creature being described since antiquity) appears in many cultures throughout the ages – importantly being linked to Scottish mythology for centuries. A symbol of masculinity and power, purity and innocence – the Unicorn was first used on the Scottish royal coat of arms by William I in the 12th century.

restrictions: Yes. This design and all products created with this design are for the exclusive use of Delta Airlines Inc. This tartan can only be woven with permission from Delta Airlines Inc. Prepared for weaving by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd.
registrationNotes: To celebrate the launch of Delta Air Line Inc’s new Scottish flight route from Atlanta to Edinburgh in May 2023, Edinburgh Airport gifted the creation of a bespoke and unique corporate tartan. The inspiration for the tartan colours has been taken from the Delta iconic branding, visible on every tail fin in their fleet. The thread count records the connections that Delta have made possible with Scotland, by embedding the 3 flight numbers associated with their New York, Boston and now Atlanta charters. In addition to this, a series of white, red and blue overchecks collectively are intended to represent the long history of the airline. Founded in 1925 the company started life as a crop dusting service business, and in 1929 they carried their very first passengers. Both of these dates have been coded into the design.

The tartan has been specifically crafted using the brown and grey hues from Nala’s coat and markings along with the famous mint of her harness.

name: Ayr 200
restrictions: Yes. this tartan is intended for individuals and groups affiliated with the community of Ayr, Ontario, Canada. However, if others wish to do so they can send their requests to Highland Emporium at [email protected] or through the Ayr (Dumfries) Pipe Band, Canada [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to commemorate the 200th anniversary of the town of Ayr, Ontario, Canada, in 2024. In 1824 the village, later named Ayr, comprised of a group of settlements; Mudge's Mills in the centre, Jedburgh to the east and Nithvale to the west. As the settlements expanded over time they eventually combined into one town. The tartan design includes elements intended to represent the area including: rivers that drove the mills; green farmlands; fall colours; the railway that allowed the mills and industry to prosper and the more modern gas pipeline and highway that run close to the community. The tartan will be worn for the celebrations in the town by the Ayr Pipe Band Canada, formed in 2018 they were the first recorded pipe band in the community.

name: Canadian Para Rescue Honor
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by graduates of Canadian Forces Para Rescue. May only be woven/reproduced with authority from Para Rescue Association of Canada.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to honour and remember those who have served in the Canadian Armed Forces Para Rescue, which been in operation since 1944. The Canadian Para Rescue is made up of specialist operators who originate from all of Canada’s military environments Army, Navy & Airforce and all ranks and career fields. They are responsible to respond to all civilian air and marine emergencies and disasters throughout Canada’s many austere environments and associated weather/climate conditions. This tartan is intended to celebrate the occupation’s distinctness, rich history, strong traditions and the many risks associated and to honour the injured and those that paid the ultimate sacrifice, in the service of others.

Colours: green and blue are intended to represent the family’s Scottish ancestry as well as the agriculture, mountains and sky of the region; grey, brown and red are representative of elements of special significance to the property including signage, soil, sunrises and sunsets; white is for the family home while the black and yellow are intended to further define the Scottish ancestral connection.

This tartan is intended to highlight the importance of slow, sustainable, circular and regenerative approaches to textile and clothing production, whilst celebrating creativity in Scottish Fashion. The colours are intended to symbolise key elements of their work and also reflect the Southern Uplands landscape: pink for the wild flowers and hillside heather, representing fashion and creativity; green for forest, coastal and upland landscapes; black for the shadows of hills and forests and to representing community and yellow for the perfumed coastal gorse and a brighter future.

registrationNotes: The Ranger Regiment tartan celebrates all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the Ranger Regiment, since its formation on 1 December 2021. It is only the third regiment to be formed since World War Two. The Ranger Regiment is optimised to operate below the threshold of war alongside, and through, specialised partners to deliver operational-level insights and effects. Colours: grey is intended to represent the Ranger Regiment beret and stable belt; brown symbolises the Peregrine Falcon of the cap badge; white, red and black are the colours from the Brigade Flash featuring the Fairbairn-Sykes fighting knives and black is also intended to represents continual respect for all fallen Ranger Regiment comrades.

The tartan is based on the Royal Stewart in recognition of Bonnie Prince Charlie’s stay in the town enroute to Culloden. The design is intended to represent the four cardinal points to link the petals of the cloverleaf and the roads leading from the Crieff Hub. This graphic shows the warp only and not the weft variation.

name: Royal Artillery
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 January 2024, registration number: 6341118.
registrationNotes: The Royal Artillery tartan celebrates all past and present personnel, and achievements attached to the Royal Artillery since its formation on 26th May 1716. In 1716 King George I issued a Royal Warrant to set up two permanent field artillery companies of 100 men each. The Royal Artillery motto is ‘Ubique’, meaning ‘Everywhere’. Also known as ‘the Gunners’, the Royal Artillery are everywhere across the battlefield, providing the British Army with its eyes, ears and firepower. The Royal Artillery tartan features historical colours associated with them: dark blue is intended to represent their beret; red, blue and yellow signifies the colours of their stable belt and black is for continual respect for all fallen Royal Artillery comrades.

name: Royal Horse Artillery
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 January 2024, registration number: 6341119.
registrationNotes: The Royal Horse Artillery tartan is intended to celebrate all past and present personnel, and achievements attached to the Royal Horse Artillery since its formation in 1793. The Royal Regiment of Artillery created a mounted branch to provide mobile fire support to fast-moving cavalry units. Initially formed of two troops, this new unit was known as the Royal Horse Artillery (RHA). The Royal Horse Artillery tartan features historical colours associated with them: dark blue is intended to represent their beret; blue and yellow signifies the colours of their stable belt and black is for continual respect for all fallen Royal Horse Artillery comrades. Their motto is 'Honi Soit Qui Mal Y Pense' meaning ‘Shame on him who thinks evil of it’.

registrationNotes: The Changing Climate tartan is intended to represent the implications of the changing climate in recent years - rising temperatures, more extreme storms and precipitation and fiercer forest fires - in the use of colours and arrangement of the pattern. Colours: yellow is intended to represent the burning sun, forest fires and rising temperatures; the five blue and four brown stripes are intended to represent swirling streams of water, gale-force winds and storms; green, brown and black is for trees and crops, types of soil and ’temperaments’ which, on the one hand, ravaged by drought, fires and precipitation, change colour, but on the other hand, thanks to the power of nature, are also able to recover.

registrationNotes: The design for this tartan was based on the Australian Heavy Horse tartan (SRT #10136) with changes intended to represent the Clydesdale Horse breed and history. Its popularity as a work horse has spread worldwide and their distinctive colour of dark bay to chestnut with white markings on the face, body and legs represented in the tartan. Colours: brown and green are intended to represent agriculture; black represents the breed’s role during war time pulling guns and heavy wagons; dark grey is for the area of the Clyde and light grey is for the road ways used for haulage. This tartan was designed for those who love and support this breed and to continue the Scottish tradition of wearing tartan attire and kilts when exhibiting Clydesdales.

registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate mankind's return to the moon, from the first lunar landing by Apollo 11 which took place on 20 July 1969 until the crew of Apollo 17 set the last foot on the moon on 19 December 1972 to the newest project to return. The design was inspired by the lunar surface and the designer used the colours of lunar rock samples to select the colours for the tartan. The sett incorporates elements to represent Neil Armstrong, who is said to have taken a piece of Armstrong tartan to the moon.

name: Selkies and Kelpies: Lure of the Water
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer regarding use.
registrationNotes: As far back as before stories were written down, the Kelpies and Selkies have served as a cautionary tale. The need to explain the unexplainable fed into the incredible tales of creatures and the world of the fae. This tartan design is broken into two portions; blues to represent the water and neutral tones for the earth. Black is intended to represent the malevolent Kelpie, which inhabits the water and is said to appear as a horse on land to lure man to his death. In contrast, the grey and brown are intended to represent the playful and curious Selkie, which takes human form on land and that of a seal in the water where it will save the lives of those in peril.

name: De Laurentis Fullerton, Erica (Personal)

registrationNotes: Erica’s sixth great grandfather landed in South Carolina in 1742 and the tartan colours are from the flags of the many states through which he travelled. His Scottish descendants lived mostly in the southwest of Scotland and Arran with which the name of Fullerton is closely associated. The structure of the design is based on an 1850 tartan and the date of 1742 has been commemorated in the red and black threadcounts.

Colours: dark blue is the main Lodge colour; light blue is for the blue blanket, the banner carried by the Incorporations of Edinburgh; yellow, representing gold, and white is for their incorporation in the Lodge’s regalia and black is for Blackfriars Street.

name: King Charles III
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the private use of His Majesty King Charles III. May only be woven with written permission from The Scottish Tartans Authority under instruction from the Royal Household. Design registered with the UK Intellectual Property Office 30th July 2024. IPO Design Registration No. 6381804.
registrationNotes: In the year of the Coronation of His Majesty King Charles III, The Scottish Tartans Authority, with HM The King's approval, designed this tartan in recognition of His Majesty's strong support in preserving the culture and traditions of Highland Dress and Scottish Tartans. The design is based on the Balmoral tartan sett which dates from c.1850. The cloth, first woven in 100% Scottish wool by Lochcarron of Scotland in Selkirk, includes a central stripe motif (one broad and two narrow), a feature of Royal tartans previously worn by His Majesty including the Duke of Rothesay, Duke of Rothesay Hunting & Lord of the Isles Hunting tartans. The colours and shades have been matched to the natural dyes of 18th century specimens in the collection of The Scottish Tartans Authority and so admired by His Majesty.

name: Dartmoor
restrictions: Yes. This tartan cannot be woven/used/reproduced without permission from the copyright holder. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan inspired by the colours of Dartmoor, for those who love the landscape of this unique wilderness.

name: MacLosgainn (Son of a Frog)

registrationNotes: The MacLosgainn tartan (Scottish Gaelic meaning Son of a Frog) was designed by Tartan Caledonia at the request of a community of friends and families of French Armed Forces members posted in the United Kingdom. The colours blue, white and red were inspired by the tricolour flag of France, intended to represent their connection to France, and green is for their connection with Armed Forces.

name: Mels-Colloredo, R & R and Family (Personal)

name: Snakatak (Crieff)

name: Islay Collection, The - Uisge Beatha
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive of the The Islay Collection Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Uisge Beatha tartan was inspired by the whisky-making traditions of Islay and the colours of the Islay landscape. Uisge Beatha is the Scottish Gaelic term for whisky, translating as ‘water of life’. The yellow is intended to reflect the colour of barley, the main ingredient in Islay Single Malt. The white lines are based on the colour of Islay’s traditional whitewashed buildings, the distilleries and lighthouses, which line the coast. Green reflects Islay's close links, both historically and geographically, with Ireland - it is said that the Irish people taught local crofters on Islay how to set up illicit stills during whisky prohibition. The grey/green colour was inspired by moss on the aged stone of Islay’s ancient monuments. Blue is for the sky and pink for the Sea Thrift, which grows on the coastline. The sett number reflects the distance of the Island, running 25 miles from north to south, 15 miles from east to west, and 40 kilometres north of the Northern Irish coast.

name: Islay Collection, The - Eilean Mòr
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive of the The Islay Collection Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Eilean Mòr tartan was inspired by the ancient history of the Isle of Islay. Eilean Mòr, Gaelic for Great Isle, is one of the islands that lies in Loch Finlaggan, which formed the administrative centre of the Lordship of the Isles during the 13th to 15th centuries. The colours in the tartan are intended to reflect the beautiful landscape of Finlaggan; blue for the Loch and green to represent the close relationship with Ireland, parts of which were ruled by the Lords of the Isles; grey was inspired by the remains of the stone buildings on Eilean Mòr, such as the chapel and castle, and yellow, pink and white are intended to reflect Finlaggan as it is now, with wild flowers growing among the ruins and sheep grazing on the island. The sett number reflects the distance of Islay, running 25 miles from north to south, 15 miles from east to west, and 40 kilometres north of the Northern Irish coast.

restrictions: Yes. The tartan was designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2023. Weaving is managed only by the designer. For enquiries about acquiring the tartan or any other questions, please contact Steve at the email provided below. UK IPO Design Registration Number: 6316309 Trademark Pending
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by Yin and Yang, a Chinese philosophical concept that represents balance and harmony. Black and White are intended to symbolise the duality of nature and the complementary forces of Yin and Yang, with black representing Yin and white representing Yang. The threadcount includes numbers of significance: 1 is intended to represent unity, completeness, and the beginning of all things; 2 is for duality, the interdependence of Yin-Yang, and balance; and 8 is for prosperity, success and good luck. Ten threads in the sett (repeated four times) is intended to signify completion and perfection, echoing the harmony of the Five Elements in Chinese philosophy (wood, fire, earth, metal, and water) and the cyclical nature of the 10 Heavenly Stems. These Elements symbolise the interplay of opposites, mirroring the balance of Yin and Yang, and emphasising equilibrium in daily life, all of this aligned with the natural order of the universe.

registrationNotes: The U.S. Immigration & Customs Enforcement Tartan was created in 2017 through the collective work of Homeland Security Investigations Special Agents in Newark, NJ, USA; the House of Edgar, Scotland; and New Jersey-based kilt maker Missy O’Kane. The colours and weave were chosen to reflect both the band and agency’s origins and purpose. Red, white, and blue are intended to represent the Flag of the United States, with the blue doubling as a reference to the agents’ status as law enforcement officers, and yellow, representing gold, for the traditional colour of U.S. federal law enforcement officers’ badges. The design incorporates elements intended to remember the events of September 11 2001. The events of September 11 and the lives lost led to the creation of the Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE). The tartan will be used by members of ICE and worn in memory of those lost and the efforts of all who responded to the terrorist attacks.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Fraserburgh Football Club. They were formed in 1910 and have always played at Bellslea Park. Prior to 1910 they played as a select side made up of the best players from the local amateur league, which was run by the Fraserburgh Football Association. In 1909 there was a campaign in the town to form a team to play as Fraserburgh Football Club. This was supported by two famous 'Brochers'; Henry Low, who played for Sunderland AFC, and his brother Wilfred Low, who played for Newcastle United FC. The select side wore a strip donated by Newcastle United, through Wilfred's connections, and when the club was officially formed in 1910 the colours remained as Black & White stripes, which is reflected in the tartan design.
