name: AI (Artificial Intelligence)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan was created by ChatGPT, mentored by The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2023. Weaving is managed by Steven Patrick Sim. UK IPO Registered Design No.6316306
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate the dawn of Artificial Intelligence, the tartan was systematically designed by an AI language model based on advanced machine learning algorithms. The colours: navy blue, bright gold, two shades of grey, red & green, are intended to represent mankind's vast knowledge, enlightenment, impartiality, journey of learning, creativity & innovation, and the environmental impact of AI's evolution. Significant numbers in the threadcount (42, 256 & 56) nod to ‘Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy’, the maximum values in a computing byte & neural network, and 1956, the year of the foundational Dartmouth Workshop. It is intended to honour one of the ‘founding fathers’ John McCarthy, who coined ‘Artificial Intelligence’ in a collaborative 1955 proposal for the project and whose legacy is remembered on October 24th. Overall, the tartan is intended to capture the essence of AI development, its impact on the world while also warning about its potential risks & unintended consequences.

name: Memories of D-Day
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from Robert Paterson.
registrationNotes: D-Day June 6, 1944, was the largest amphibious invasion in military history, bringing together the Air, Sea & Land forces during WWII. The operation, codenamed OVERLORD, delivered 5 naval assault divisions to the beaches at Normandy in France, facing Hitler’s Atlantic Wall. By days end, some 156,000 Allied soldiers landed on the beaches. The Battle of Normandy lasted 85 days, it was the beginning of the end of WWII. This tartan is intended to reflect that historic event. The threadcount within the tartan represents the date of D-Day 06-06-1944. 5 within the weave represents the beaches where soldiers made the ultimate sacrifice so that other may enjoy the freedoms held today. Red, white & blue in this design mirrors the colours of the flags nations fought under during that historic event. The black lines in the tartan are intended to represent dignity & honour of the brave men & women that laid down their lives during WWII. It was also utilized to openly show sadness, grief & mourning.

name: Europa Clipper

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the development, launch, operations and science of the Europa Clipper project, to study the icy moon of Jupiter, and to honour the many hundreds of people around the world who are part of the project team. Europa Clipper’s main science goal is to determine whether there are places below the icy surface which could support life. The Europa Clipper mission is designed to understand the nature of Europa’s ice shell and the ocean beneath it, along with its composition and geology. Colours are based on imagery from Jupiter and its moon Europa. They are intended to represent the ice and dust on the surface of Europa, the various colours of the planet Jupiter, and the depths of interplanetary space.

restrictions: Yes. The tartan was designed by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2023. Weaving is managed only by the designer. For enquiries about acquiring the tartan or any other questions, please contact Steve at the email provided below. UK IPO Registered Design pending
registrationNotes: Created to celebrate light, this tartan is intended to honour Sir Isaac Newton and his groundbreaking 1704 work, 'Opticks.' The tartan's asymmetrical pattern featuring 17, 4, 12, 6, 6, 12, 4, 17 threads, reveals a geometric prismatic element when viewed at a 45-degree rotation – a tribute to Newton's prism and his pioneering experiments with light. Thread counts of ’84’ (Newton's age at passing) and ‘1704’ (the publication year of 'Opticks') weave historical reverence into the design, also acknowledging his enduring legacy. 7 monochromatic pinstripes in the sett represent the spectrum of light waves contained within white light, alluding to Newton's discoveries and setting the stage for a future series of 7 coloured tartan variants. The name of the registered design, ‘Prismatic Light’ in French, ascribes to the ancient Franco-Scottish Alliance. The tartan was registered on the winter solstice 2023.

registrationNotes: Fleeing WWII Europe the soon to be McStroul family line fled to Scotland where the family name was changed from Alta Zin(t) stroul to McStroul. name: Crieff & Strathearn Museum
restrictions: Yes. This is a promotional tartan and is intended to be worn by all purchasers. This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders, the Crieff & Strathearn Museum. Copyright rests with the Crieff & Strathearn Museum.
registrationNotes: The Crieff & Stathearn Museum tartan blends notable historical elements of the town and its surroundings. Based on the Royal Stewart tartan (reputed to have been worn on social occasions by Bonnie Prince Charlie), it commemorates the Prince’s connection with Crieff – on his way to fateful Culloden, his horse was shod by a local King Street blacksmith and his war council was held uphill from the old Drummond Arms in James Square. The town also knew Rob Roy MacGregor, his escapades and dealings at the famous annual cattle market, the Crieff Tryst, and the design includes red and black of the Old MacGregor/Rob Roy tartan. The colours of the design also echo those of the Drovers’ Tryst tartan, the browns and greens of the moors, forests and grazings that comprised the ancient drove routes to the Crieff markets. Finally, the central blue on green is intended to represent Strathearn, the broad valley of the river Earn where the ‘frontier town’ of Crieff was originally established on the Knock of Crieff.

registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by John Payfair to honour of those in the Playfair family past and present. The earliest recorded Playfairs made their home in the 15th century in the Carse of Gowrie on the north bank of the river Tay in Perthshire. From there, they expanded north over the Sidlaw Hills to the parish of Bendochy in the Vale of Strathmore and the south across the Tay to Abernethy. The history of the family has been published in at least 9 different volumes over the last 150 years. In recent years, digital media has facilitated research proving the connection to the Perthshire family to a wide diaspora of Playfairs across the globe. This tartan is intended to capture the family’s connection and to give them a tartan of their own.

The colours are themed around the wedding colour scheme: red for their August birthstone and green reflects the ivy, intended to represent marriage. The sett incorporates their 20+ years together and the wedding date.

name: Scottish Refugee Council
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries must be made to the Scottish Refugee Council or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Scottish Refugee Council. The chosen colours are intended to symbolise the vibrancy and diversity of Scotland's communities as refugees settle and build their lives here.

name: Kinniburgh, A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All permission must be sought from the Kinniburgh family or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Adam Kinniburgh and his family. This tartan was created for use at Adam’s wedding and for the family to have their own tartan for use in the future. The tartan colours were chosen by the family, including Adam’s brothers, and are intended to be a representation of the Kinniburgh name but also their love for Scotland.

name: McCaskie, B & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ben McCaskie and his family. The colours were inspired by the family’s favourite places and interests: blue is intended to represent the sea and sky; green is for motorsport and yellow is for Daffodils and the family’s connection to Wales.

name: Near Earth Object Surveyor
registrationNotes: Joseph Masiero and Craig McMurtry designed this tartan to commemorate the NASA mission Near Earth Object Surveyor. The thread count relates to aspects of the mission: 70 blue for 70m radius objects; 25 black for 25cm radius telescope; 12 red 8 black 40 dark red for the NC1 and NC2 filter bandpasses; 12 black for 12 year mission; 4 blue 4 light blue for the NC1 and NC2 detectors and 2 yellow and 6 black for the first mission proposal submitted in 2006.

name: Wilhelm, Marco & Weiss, Silke - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by anyone with the surname Wilhelm and their family. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Marco Wilhelm by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of Marco Wilhelm and Silke Weiss. The colours are intended to represent their German background, the rough mountains of the alps, green pastures, sparkling rivers and their deep love for Scotland.

name: Ashcroft, David & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from David Ashcroft. Please contact: [email protected] Copyright rests with David Ashcroft.
registrationNotes: A tartan for David Ashcroft and his family. The colours were inspired by the family’s history: grey is intended to represent David’s Grandfather’s time served in the RAF; purple and slate grey are intended to represent heather covered mountain slopes; dark green is a nod to the family’s heritage; green and orange is for the family’s ancestry in Ireland and lime green was included as it is David’s favourite colour.

name: Hall, Graeme (Personal)
designer: Hall, Graeme & Tessa and MacDonald, Ewan
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Graeme Hall and his family. May only be woven/reproduced with permission. Copyright rests with Graeme Hall.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Graeme Hall and his family. It was designed to be worn at his wedding to Tessa in August 2024 and by the family in the future. Colours: green is intended to represent Styria in Austria, the region Tessa is from; light blue is for Graeme; dark purple is for the flowers in their garden in London; and purple is intended to represent heather which reminds them of Scotland, where Graeme is from, and their time in Cornwall.

name: Missouri Military Academy
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by Cadets, Alumni, Parents of Cadets, Faculty and Staff of Missouri Military Academy and Friends of the Academy.
registrationNotes: One of the oldest private Military Academy boarding schools in the United States, Missouri Military Academy has had a long tradition of graduating leaders and innovators in all walks of life. Their school colours of Maroon and Gold are worn with pride by Alumni from all over the world. The maroon is intended to symbolise strength and determination, while the gold symbolises success and love. This tartan includes accents of white and black which are intended to symbolise purity and mourning those lost.

name: Basler, R G & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and used by family and friends. Others should contact the tartan owner. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland or other weavers in Scotland with permission from the owner or his authorised agents, heirs or successors only. The threadcount may be obtained with permission from the tartan owner or his authorised agents, heirs or successors on direct request only.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Rolf G Basler and his family. It was inspired by the views and colours of Scotland’s sea and coast, the owner’s native country and colours of personal significance.

name: Cruse, C & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Chad Cruse and his family to celebrate their marriage and to pass to future generations.

name: Artists Rifles
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only by members and former members of the Artists Rifles, and any honorary members as deemed by the Artists Rifles Association Council. May only be woven by those approved by the Artists Rifles Association and the designer. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The Artists Rifles Regiment dates back to 1859. During the Second World War, it was used as an officer training unit. The regiment was disbanded in 1945, but in 1947 it was re-established to resurrect the Special Air Service Regiment. Created by the Artists Rifles Association, this tartan is intended to reflect the colours of the Artists Rifles; grey is for the main colour associated with the Artists Rifles, along with some black and white. The Special Air Service colours of Oxford and Cambridge blue were also included in the design.

name: MacCuspic, Eldon Peter & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the MacCuspic family and extended family, with bloodlines to North American MacCuspics and remaining family in Scotland. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Eldon Peter MacCuspic. It is intended to be used by any North American descendants of the MacCuspic Family and celebrates the 200 year anniversary of when the family emigrated from Berneray, Outer Herbrides in 1825. The colours are intended to represent the MacCuspic family and their journey: blue for the Atlantic Ocean; dark blue for night skies; gold for the stars in the night sky, which were a guiding influence when crossing the Atlantic Ocean; red to represent their love and connection and white to represent their religion and spirituality.

name: Pink Castle
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and distributed by the National Trust for Scotland only. May only be woven with permission from the National Trust for Scotland. Threadcount will only be released with permission from the National Trust for Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the completion of a major conservation project at Craigievar Castle, near Alford in Aberdeenshire. The castle is well known and much loved around the globe for its distinct pink exterior. The project involved high level repairs to the roof and harling on the building as well as refreshing the lime wash that gives Craigievar Castle its distinctive pink colour. Craigievar Castle has been under the care of the National Trust for Scotland since the 1960s. Colours: the reds were chosen directly to match the pink hues of the castle’s exterior; the blues are intended to represent the slate spires and the sky over the castle; yellow, representing gold, was inspired by the castle’s weather vane; and brown and green were inspired by the detailing on the castle and the trees surrounding it.

name: Ploysongsang, Edward and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Edward Ploysongsang and his immediate family. Others may wear with express written permission from Edward Ploysongsang or his heirs. May only be woven with written permission from Edward Ploysongsang, his heirs or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: The tartan incorporates the colours in the armorial bearings of Edward Ploysongsang recorded at the College of Arms in London, plus the addition of green, which is the favourite colour of his wife. The design’s colours also reflect the flags for the US, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Myanmar, The Philippines, Indonesia, China, Vietnam, Bangladesh and India, all countries for which he and his family have ancestral connections.

name: Scottish Pantry Network, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use and distribution by The Scottish Pantry Network. May only be woven/reproduced with permission from The Scottish Pantry Network.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Scottish Pantry Network to celebrate the organisation's connection to Scotland and its communities, and to honour their Scottish roots.

name: Hudnall, B & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Hudnall family lineage.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the Hudnall family’s history and to be passed to future generations. The design uses colours of personal significance.

name: Young Women's Movement, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used only by YWCA Scotland. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate 100 years of the Young Women’s Movement, previously known as YWCA Scotland, and incorporates across the sett the numbers 19 and 24 to commemorate its founding in 1924. The colours of this tartan are intended to represent the core values of the charity to be brave and take radical steps to make gender equality a reality in Scotland. The design is woven in bright colours intended to represent their commitment to promote joy, with contrasting colours to represent the rich diversity of young women and girls in the movement. Yellow links the logos of World YWCA and European YWCA, and the brand colours of the Young Women’s Movement.

name: Raj, Mark & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by anyone with the surname Raj or Thomson. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Mark Raj and Sarah Thomson by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to represent the of the joining Raj family together with the Thomson family and their lives together in Scotland. Purple is intended to represent the thistle and the blues to represent the tradition of public service within the Raj family.

name: Cires, M & Milian, M, Doddiscombe (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by family members and their descendants. Copyright rests with Marian Cires & Maria-Madalina Milian.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Marian Cires & Maria-Madalina Milian, Doddiscombe, Devon, using colours of personal significance.

name: Appalachian Saint Andrew's Pipes and Drums
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Appalachian Saint Andrew's Pipes and Drums Inc., a registered non-profit corporation in the State of Georgia, USA. The Band, created in 2004, celebrated their 20th anniversary in 2024. The Band is based in the Southern Appalachian Mountains of North Georgia. The tartan colours were inspired by the Appalachian mountains; greens for the foliage of the trees and plants; grey for the geologic make-up of the mountains; orange for the clay soil; black for the coal, oil, and rich earth of the mountains; and blue, red and yellow for the wildflowers found throughout the mountains.

name: CMA
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used solely by CMA as an organisation, CMA staff and for use at CMA events. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for CMA to be used at events and in marketing. It was created to celebrate the international conference hosted by CMA in May 2025 in Scotland.

name: Howard, J and Basu, N & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by James Howard, Nina Basu and the family & descendants only. May only be woven with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the union of James Howard and Nina Basu, their family heritage and shared bond. The colours were inspired by the flag of Maryland, United States.

name: Ng, Hin Yeung (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Hin Yeung Ng. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted, only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Hin Yeung Ng. The threadcount includes numbers that reference his birth year, and the five stars and petals of the Singapore and Hong Kong flags. Shades of blue and green are intended to represent the sky, sea, and lush greenery of Singapore and Hong Kong. Red and white accents reflect the colours of both flags. Finally, grey is intended to represent his favourite animal, the koala.

name: Durand, Christophe (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/use/reproduce this tartan must be sought from Christophe Durand and Siobhan Mackenzie.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the personal use of Christophe Durand, to be woven and made into his own kilt.

name: Kopp, Olaf Markus Albert (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Olaf Kopp's friends, family and those with permission. May not be woven/used/reproduced without permission from the designer. Design registered with the European Union IPO on 5th June 2024, No 015062663-0001.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Olaf Markus Albert Kopp. The design includes colours of personal significance based on his uniform and troop colours from his time in the German army and his Baden-Wuerttemberg State Police uniform.

name: Pontelli, E & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Enrico Pontelli and his family to celebrate the Pontelli name. Colours: blue is intended to represent Italy; yellow is for the eagle contained in the flag of Friuli; green and brown are intended to represent the green expanses of Scotland and the glades of the Highlands.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Daniel P Relihan and his family. The colours are intended to represent the crest associated the Relihan family name, which originated in Ireland and is derived from the Gaelic sept O'Roileachain.

name: Stevens, Dann Brady & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be use by Dann Brady Stevens, his family and friends. Dann Brady Stevens should be consulted before weaving.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Stevens family to celebrate their Scottish ancestry. The sett was inspired by the various tartans worn by the family members at Christmas over the years, where it is a family tradition to wear tartan to Christmas dinner. The colours are intended to represent the various places that link the family together to create a tartan for all family members to wear.

name: Lime Rock Park
restrictions: Yes. Use of this tartan is restricted by Browne White Ltd T/ A ScotlandShop.com & Lime Rock Park. This tartan can only be woven or reproduced digitally or in print with prior written consent from both Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & Lime Rock Park Tartan.
registrationNotes: Designed for Lime Rock Park, America's second-longest continuously operating road racing circuit. Open for racing since 1957, Lime Rock Park has played a key role in the rich history of American motorsports. Its setting is a village in Connecticut’s Litchfield County, renowned for its historical, cultural and recreational resources. The sett was inspired by the family tartan worn by legendary Scottish racing driver, Jim Clark as well as the chevron icon included with Lime Rock Park’s branding. The colours were taken from the Lime Rock Park brand colour palette.

name: Baglow, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval required to weave/use/reproduce this tartan from Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com, James Baglow & Louise Martin.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of James Baglow & Louise Martin. The colours are intended to represent: the Baglow family’s heritage, hailing from Lancashire, Yorkshire and Devon; James's future with Louise in their home in Scotland and their love of the outdoors.

name: Mayland Community College
registrationNotes: A tartan for Mayland Community College, North Carolina, United States. Colours: dark blue and dark red are from the traditional colours of Mayland Community College; light blue is intended to pay homage to the majestic Blue Ridge Mountains; green was inspired by the local flora and yellow is intended to represent warmth and sunshine. The design combines elements that are intended to represent the story and history of the College and its connection to the local community.

name: Eckford Johnson, D J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is restricted for the exclusive use of David Johnson and his family. To be commissioned by David Johnson. To be woven by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: A tartan for David Eckford Johnson who, after spending nearly 40 years in the textile trade specialising in woollens and tartans, wanted to commission a new tartan for his family which celebrated the family name Johnson and his mother’s maiden name Eckford. The colours chosen are of personal significance and the sett includes elements that are intended to be a nod to historical tartans linked to the family.

name: Kermack, S (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by those with permission from Steven Kermack. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Steven Kermack to celebrate three generations of the Kermack family. The sett is includes numbers that are intended to represent the years of birth for the father, son and grandson.

name: Blackstone Association, The
restrictions: Yes. The use of this tartan is restricted by the Blackstone Association. Permission to wear or reproduce this tartan requires permission from the Blackstone Association. Weaving and production is prepared by Red Label Kilts Inc.
registrationNotes: The Blackstone Association is an assembly of past and present military veterans from Canada's Elite Warrior Community. Blackstone operates to support those members. Colours: light brown/tan is intended to represent the Unit ‘cutting its teeth’ in the Afghanistan Theatre of Operations, transforming into a true Special Operations Forces Unit, and the Tan Beret; black is for the Unit’s Counter Terrorism/Hostage Rescue roots and is a predominant colour within the Unit's history (Black Team, Blackstone); green represents the traditional and historical Special Operations Forces roots of the Unit - Reconnaissance, Direct Action, Patrolling, etc; grey is for the compartmentalized elements of the Unit and the future of Special Operations Forces warfare at the Unit and red is for the Canadian Maple Leaf in the Canadian Flag.

name: CANDU (Cancer Lived Experience)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the exclusive use for the charity CANDU (Dundee) please contact them regarding tartan permissions.
registrationNotes: The charity CANDU created this tartan at a conference at the V&A Dundee based on the lives of cancer survivors and those who have had cancer and experienced its effects. The colours are intended to represent hope, optimism, happiness, courage, and inspiration. Each line in the design is intended to represent an experience of those who are living or have lived with cancer.

name: Worshipful Company of Carmen
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan design to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 21 May 2024, registration number: 6367416.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Worshipful Company of Carmen, one of the Livery Companies of the City of London, to celebrate the members and history of the Carmen. Carriers have plied for hire for nearly two thousand years. The Carmen existed when the City was born, moving goods, materials, wine, wood and fuel within and beyond the City. Traditionally, the Carmen fellowship dates from the 13th century when, in 1272, the city passed a by-law controlling carriers. Today the Company of Carmen remains associated with transport and logistics, keeping alive the traditions of fellowship, benevolence, civic pride, and commercial integrity. This design features the following colours from the Worshipful Company of Carmen’s coat of arms; white, pale yellow, green, red and grey and brown is intended to represent the original wooden hand carts.

name: Collington, J, A, R & F (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Collington family unless otherwise requested. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of the Collington family by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A personal family tartan for the Collington family, and their descendants, using colours of personal significance.

name: Loubet del Bayle, J-C & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Eric & Jean-Christophe Loubet del Bayle and their families. Intended to be worn by family members, associated families and their descendants. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted, only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the brothers Eric and Jean-Christophe Loubet del Bayle and their respective families. The design is based on an historical Coat of Arms within the family: the triple gold overchecks on the red refer to the three bells of the Coat of Arms, and the red overcheck on gold refers to the red wolf. The additional colours are intended to represent aspects of the Pyrenees: green for the forest; grey for the rocks and brown for the bears (typical of the valleys where the family are from).

name: Loubet del Bayle, J-C & Family Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Eric & Jean-Christophe Loubet del Bayle and their families. Intended to be worn by family members, associated families and their descendants. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted, only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Loubet del Bayle family tartan (SRT# 14265). This design was inspired by the wild and beautiful mountains of the Pyrenees, the so called ‘Pyrenean Highlands’; green is intended to represent the forests;, grey/silver is for the rocks and brown for the wildlife of the Pyrenees, in particular the bears that inhabit the valleys where the family come from (Haut Couserans).

name: Charlottetown
designer: Paterson, R; Watters, W & McGladdery, G
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from Robert Paterson of Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Charlottetown, the capital city of the province of Prince Edward Island, Canada. The City was named after Queen Charlotte Sophia of England, wife of King George III. The City’s flag includes Queen Charlotte's brilliant burgundy crown along with the five squares that represent the greenery of Charlottetown: Queen Square, where the Father's of Confederation met; Rochford Square; Connaught Square; Hillsborough Square and Kings Square. The City was created under the City of Charlottetown Act on April 17th 1855, and this date is featured in the threadcount of the tartan. Colours: burgundy is intended to represent Queen Charlotte along with green and white for the City’s flag; blue is intended to represent the Sea and fishing industry.

name: Brooks, Ivan & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by Ivan Brooks in August 2023, during a trip to Edinburgh. Ivan, from Kent in England, has been playing the bagpipes in the City of Rochester Pipe Band since 1978. At the time of registration, he was the Pipe Sergeant and his dad Brian, was the Drum Major. The tartan was created to be used by the Brooks family and future generations. The design was inspired by the Irvine tartan and includes colours of personal significance.

name: Dhillon, Rana Harkirat Singh & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the family and those with permission. May only be woven with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the Dhillon family’s Sikh and Punjabi heritage. The colours chosen are intended to reflect the essence of the Punjab region in India: blue for the 5 rivers of the state; yellow, represent gold, as Punjab is known as India’s Golden state; green for the vast vegetation and greenery of the state; white to signify the peaceful nature of the Sikh faith and black is intended to acknowledge the sacrifices during the birth of the Sikh faith.

name: George Washington's Mount Vernon
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven or replicated with written permission from Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: A tartan for George Washington's Mount Vernon. Days after the Continental Army’s surprise victory at Trenton, New Jersey, General George Washington decided to execute another daring manoeuvre to confront the British at Princeton on January 3, 1777. The resulting victory boosted American morale and inspired many recruits to join the Continental Army the following spring. The colours of this unique tartan were inspired by Charles Willson Peale’s painting portraying General Washington after the Battle of Princeton. The design blends the hues of Washington’s distinctive uniform. In this tartan, each thread is intended to be a brushstroke, inspired by Peale’s brush and the indomitable spirit of Washington’s triumph.

name: Xanterra Parks & Resorts Inc - Glacier National Park Lodges
designer: Paterson, Robert Xanterra Parks & Resorts Inc
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven or replicated with written permission from Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: The colours in this tartan were inspired by the alpine scenery and lakes seen within the Glacier National Park. Glacier National Park was established May 11, 1910, and became America’s 10th National Park. The photo that inspired the creation of this tartan was of Mount Grinnell, named after George Bird Grinnell, an influential leader that pushed for the creation of the National Park in the late 1800s. The threadcount incorporates the date the Park was established. Colours: light and dark grey are intended to represent the Glacier-carved mountains of which there are 26 glaciers within the park, all shrinking in size; white is for the snow-covered mountains, the Glacier has 175 mountains, the highest being Mt. Cleveland at 10,448 ft; turquoise is for the appearance of the rivers and lakes due to the finely ground sediment called Glacier flour. The park has a total of 762 lakes, of which only 131 of them are named, and there are 563 streams or rivers within the park.

name: Xanterra Parks & Resorts Inc - Yellowstone National Park Lodges
designer: Paterson, Robert & Xanterra Parks & Resorts Inc.
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven or replicated with written permission from Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: The colours in this tartan were inspired by a photograph of Old Faithful Inn, with Old Faithful Geyser in the foreground in Yellowstone National Park. Yellowstone was established on March 1, 1872, which is represented within the thread count. Colours: white is intended to represent the eruptions of Old Faithful Geyser, approximately every 90 minutes, Old Faithful shoots 3,700 to 8,400 US gallons of water nearly 185 feet into the air for 1.5 to 5 minutes; green is for the 2.2 million acres, filled with alpine meadows, grassy plains, and lush forests, the Park is one the largest intact thriving ecosystems in the world; blue represents the streams, flowing rivers, and deep lakes, including the largest freshwater lake above 7000 feet in North America; yellow is for the vibrant rhyolite rock that formed the volcanic caldera walls seen throughout the park; brown represents Yellowstone’s renowned historic lodges, including Old Faithful Inn, one of the largest log structures in the world.

name: Boys Town
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be woven or replicated without written permission by Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: Born in Ireland, Father Edward J. Flanagan arrived in the United States in 1904. An ordained priest, he became a social reformer and true visionary for changing how America cared for its children and families by passionately speaking out and taking action on social issues that others refused to address. Believing that all children deserved to be valued and provided with the basic necessities, he founded Boys Town in 1917. Over the past 100 years, Boys Town has witnessed countless historic moments that tell the tale of one man's vision and how it changed the way America cares for its children. Colours: blue and white are the official colours of Boys Town; blue and gold are found in Boys Town’s corporate logo; green is intended to represent the rich Irish heritage of Father Flanagan and how his visionary thinking and original mission continue to guide Boys Town today and yellow, representing gold, is intended to symbolise the bright futures of the youth in care.

name: Bondurri, Massimiliano & Popesco, Emmanuelle (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the union of Massimilano Bondurri and Emmanuelle Popesco in 2013. The design and colours are intended to represent their emotions and milestones experienced together, challenges surmounted, joys shared and their bond that strengthens each year.

name: Vincere Ad Astra
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced by written permission from the designer. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: ‘Vincere Ad Astra’ translates to ‘conquering the stars’. The is intended to celebrate the pursuit of discovery and knowledge in outer space. Colours: yellow, representing gold, is intended to symbolise the promise and possibilities in outer space and the wealth of knowledge and ground-breaking discoveries awaiting us; white is intended to represent diplomacy, and the need for collaboration; purple pays homage to the Scottish designer's heritage and Scotland’s Space ambitions; green is intended to represent our Earth and how space exploration must be sustainable and responsible; blue is intended to signify the Kármán line, the ethereal boundary where earth's atmosphere surrenders to the vast expanse of outer space and the stars above and black is intended to represent a gaze into the abyss of the unknown, beckoning the viewer to explore uncharted territories and unravel the mysteries of the universe.

name: Bagad Les Sonneurs du Lion
restrictions: Yes. This tartan will be woven exclusively for the members of the Bagad Les Sonneurs du Lion from 90300 – Valdoie (France) and Chrystel Amyot & Robert Amyot.
registrationNotes: The Bagad Les Sonneurs du Lion is a French Pipe Band situated in Valdoie, Belfort, France, which is home to ‘The Lion of Belfort’, a monumental lion sculpture. The tartan design uses the Band’s colours.

name: Millisor, E J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Eric John Millisor or designees in writing. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Eric John Millisor, an American of Scottish and German descent, and his family. The tartan is intended to pay homage to his family heritage which dates back to the occupational last name for millers and iron workers (Mühleisen) who farmed, forged, and fought in every major American war since the Revolutionary war.

name: Hesketh, D (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: Designed to commemorate the marriage of David Hesketh to Melissa Cheney. Colours: yellow is intended to represent the brightness of spirit of both David and Melissa; red, green, black and white threads represent the colours of the Welsh flag which is David's country of birth and the tartan as a whole is intended to represents Melissa's Scottish nationality.

name: Disability Advocate
restrictions: Yes. The use of this tartan is unrestricted. Permission to have woven/reproduced is required from the designer.
registrationNotes: The designer, who is of Scots-Irish heritage and autistic, created this tartan in colours which, for them have special meaning: blue is intended to represent 'true blue' friendships gained by people with disabilities; black is intended to represent awareness of strife that people with disabilities may have fought through, such as bullying, discrimination and personal/interpersonal struggles; purple is for awareness and prevention of violence; grey represents the assemblance of black and white, in turn representing people, with and without disabilities, working together as one; and finally orange is intended to represent bright futures, in which people with disabilities feel included and accepted. This application was supported by the Wyoming Institute for Disabilities (WIND).

name: Elkmont Game Day Collection
restrictions: Yes. This tartan can only be woven or replicated with written permission by the designer or Patrick King Woollen Company.
registrationNotes: The Elkmont Game Day Collection tartan was created for the Elkmont Trading Company, Clemson, South Carolina. The tartan is intended to celebrate the beauty of Elkmont, where the Blue Ridge Mountains overlook a highland dale carved by the Little River and Jake's Creek. Settlers came to the valley in the 1840's seeking gold, but instead discovered a lush forest teeming with wildlife, canopied beneath hemlock giants and rhododendron thickets, rambling streams and a location visited each June by the synchronous fireflies spectacular light show.

name: War and Service Animal (AWAMO)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by the Australian War Animal Memorial Organisation (AWAMO) to commemorate War and Service Animals. Colours: purple is recognised as a colour for war and service animals; blue is intended to represent the animals that have served in the Navy; light blue is intended to represent the animals that have served in the Air Force; green is for the animals that have served in the Army and red is in recognition of the blood of the animals that have served.

name: Bremner, Gordon (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone with the Bremner surname, or their descendants.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Gordon Bremner and his family tartan, designed by his son Stewart. It was loosely inspired by the Farquharson tartan, as the Bremners are a sept of that clan. The people who became the Bremners came to Scotland from the Flemish region of Brabant, settling in Caithness. The colours of the tartan are based on the heraldic colours of both those regions.

name: Trading Bay Grouse and Trout Club
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Trading Bay Grouse and Trout Club. Prior approval to weave/reproduce is required by Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & The Trading Bay Grouse and Trout Club
registrationNotes: The Trading Bay Grouse and Trout Club was founded by Lake of Bays cottager Matthew Gaasenbeek and friends in 2009 to bring together like-minded friends who have a shared passion for their lake, cottage lifestyle and protection of nature and the environment on Lake of Bays, Muskoka region, Ontario, Canada. The colours in the tartan are intended to represent the following: grey and pink are for Muskoka granite; green is for the moss found on the Muskoka rock and the trees in the area; light blue is for the sky; dark blue is for the lake and white is for the colour of the sand on the local beach.

name: Fürth Rotary
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Fürth Rotary Club only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Fürth Rotary Club, Germany.

name: Scottish International Eco-schools Planet Earth
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Scottish and International Eco-schools and other environmental organisations with permission. Prepared for weaving in Scotland. Registered with IPO, design registration number: 6353680
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Eco-schools Programme, which operates in 81 countries focussing on climate action, protecting biodiversity and reducing environmental pollution. The tartan was designed for Eco-school children to wear to show their support for the environment and to be used in ongoing projects.

name: Social Hub, The
restrictions: Yes. Permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought by TSH Glasgow OpCo Limited, Trading as The Social Hub.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed to celebrate The Social Hub opening their first UK hotel in Glasgow. Using the brand's colours the tartan is intended to represent their inclusive global community of creatives. The threadcount includes counts of 20 and 24 for the opening of the site in 2024.

name: Edinburgh 900
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson, strictly for City of Edinburgh Council use only. Restricted availability, permission for use required. Please contact Kinloch Anderson.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for City of Edinburgh Council and the Edinburgh 900 celebrations taking place in the city in 2024, which mark 900 years since Edinburgh became a royal burgh. This colourway is based on the sett of the original City of Edinburgh tartan and the palette references one of the 10 celebratory themes, the 21st century - Edinburgh as a city of diversity.

name: Brewshido Standard
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use Brewshido owners and staff only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Brewshido, a small family run craft beer brewery located in Japan focussing primarily on Scottish style beers. The colours in the tartan are intended to represent particular elements in the brewery’s history: dark blue is intended to represent the founder’s association with Scotland; light blue is for the Niyodo river which borders this village the brewery is located; red is from the flag of the village and yellow is intended to represent barley and beer.

name: Mitchell, Andrew (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Andrew Mitchell using colours of personal significance.

name: Remarkable Aircraft Markings
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the aircraft of the Allied air forces during D-Day as part of Operation Overlord. Friendly aircraft were painted with white and black stripes on the fuselage and wings, the colours have been incorporated into this design. Other colours are green, grey and brown intended to represent the aircraft’s upper sides; blue for the sea and grey for the ships of the naval forces which transported the land forces to the 5 brown beaches of Normandy where so many fell, indicated by the black threads. The threadcount includes numbers of significance intended to represent; air force personnel; the date June 6, 1944 and the 5 beaches.

name: Habikino J Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and sold within Habikino City. Business owners in Habikino City can use the design and trade the products outside the city.
registrationNotes: The colours in this design were inspired by Habikino City's history, nature, and specialty products. Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan, is a city which is home to natural and historical attractions, including the Mozu-Furuichi Tumulus Cluster, which is registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site, and the Takenouchi-kaido Road, which is registered as a Japanese Heritage Site. In addition, various specialty products such as vegetables and fruits are grown on this land. This tartan is intended to represent the city’s Japanese heritage: light green is for the ancient tombs and agricultural products (green peas, shine muscat, etc); yellow is for the fruit of the tachibana tree and brown is for the Takenouchi-kaido Road and excavated items (haniwa).

name: Habikino W Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and sold within Habikino City. Business owners in Habikino City can use the design and trade the products outside the city.
registrationNotes: The colours in this design were inspired by Habikino City's history, nature, and local specialities. Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan, is home with nature and historical sites, including the Mozu-Furuichi Tumulus Cluster, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the Japanese World Heritage site, Takenouchi-kaido Road. In addition, various specialty products such as vegetables and fruits are grown on this land. This tartan is intended to represent the city’s World Heritage connection: dark blue is for wine; purple is for grapes; yellow is for the fruit of the Tachibana tree; light brown is for an item (haniwa) excavated from Takenouchi-kaido Road and green represents ancient tombs and agricultural products (green peas, shine muscat, etc.).

name: Honouring Service - TKH Kilts
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is not restricted to just US Veterans. Please contact Tavis Tindal of TKH Kilts for permission to weave - [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan is for TKH Kilts and is intended to honour all those US personnel who have served. The colours include elements with personal significance for the designer along with elements intended to acknowledge all branches of the US Military, with colours that can be found in each of their Service or Combat Uniforms. The red stripe is intended to acknowledge the sacrifice of those members who gave all.

name: Tombow 150th Anniversary, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of clients of Tombow Co. Ltd. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the 150th anniversary of Towbow, the Japanese school wear company. The colours of the tartan are intended to reflect both the corporate colours of the company and colours signifying, pride, respect, trust, faith, diversity, appreciation and environmental protection.

name: Shand, Jamie & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use/wear by any individual with an association to the Shand name e.g. Immediate family & their kin. This may also be worn by any other individual expressly authorised by Jamie or Gavin Shand. It is not to be used for any commercial purpose without clear authority to do so and details of the terms under which this is governed being approved in writing. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from designer Jamie Shand. Copyright rests with the designers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Gavin Shand and his son Jamie Shand to honour their family's Scottish ties. The family originates from Northern Scotland so this tartan is intended to be a link to their Scottish heritage; to each other and to future generations. Jamie is a bagpiper and will proudly wear this tartan whilst performing.

name: Albyn School
restrictions: Yes. The wearing, and use, of this tartan is restricted to current pupils of Albyn School and other individuals associated with the School by virtue of being former pupils, staff, former staff etc. This tartan may only be woven by the School's authorised uniform supplier. Anyone else wishing to weave this tartan should contact Albyn School to seek permission. Copyright rests with Albyn School.
registrationNotes: As part of a uniform review carried out in 2022, Albyn School, Aberdeen, decided to hold a competition to design a tartan specific to Albyn School that is intended to represent its history and heritage and that would be worn as part of the approved school uniform. The competition was won by a pupil at the School. The design was introduced as school uniform during the 2024-25 session.

name: Thunderbird
registrationNotes: This tartan was created as part of the RCAF (Royal Canadian Air Force) centenary celebrations. The colours are based on the heraldic crest of 426 Squadron, the dress uniform of the RCAF and includes Pacific Sunset gold, as a nod to the West Coast home of the mythical Thunderbird, the Squadron icon.

name: Simpson, B and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use of the extended Simpson family, spouses, and their descendants. Contact the designer or his estate for permission to weave the tartan.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Bruce Simpson, his extended Simpson family and their descendants. The colours in the tartan are intended to represent the colours from the national flags of the countries of origin of the different branches of the family.

name: Scots-Knight, Eric and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Eric Scots-Knight and his immediate family. May only be woven with written permission from Eric Scots-Knight, his heirs or a nominated agent
registrationNotes: A tartan for Eric Scots-Knight and his family using colours of personal significance.

name: Chartered Institute of Arbitrators
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Members of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators only. The tartan was designed by Brandon Malone and the IPR is gifted by him to the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators. Permission from the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators is required to weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the The Chartered Institute of Arbitrators by Brandon Malone, the Chairman of the Scottish Branch of the Institute. The colours used, are those found in the Institute's Coat of Arms.

name: Pride of Neurodiversity (Chlo Jack on Her Mac)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: The neurodiversity tartan is intended to represent the principles of neurodiversity inclusiveness, and the visibility and value of neurodivergent individuals. The palette of vibrant colours were deliberately chosen to symbolise the spectrum of emotions intrinsic to the neurodivergent experience of the designer, author of the Chlo Jack on Her Mac blog site. This tartan is intended to be used by the designer to promote acceptance, understanding, and empowerment for neurodivergent individuals, as well as advocating for a future where neuro-inclusion is a paramount societal objective.

name: McFraticelli, Roberto and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Roberto McFraticelli and his family incorporating several elements intended to represent their European heritage. Colours: dark blue is intended to symbolise the sea and the Navy; red, white and green are intended to represent the Italian flag, and symbolise combining their Italian and Scottish cultures; brown is intended to represent the habit of the friars, Fraticelli meaning ‘the little friars’, and light blue is intended to represent a clear sky and Italy.

name: Golf & Social Health
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is restricted and permission to weave must be sought from The House of Edgar. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Golf and Social Health group, a group of lifelong friends who despite being older (at the time this tartan was registered) still felt young at heart. Colours: black and red are intended to represent the school the majority of group members attended; gold denotes the winner of the semi-annual golf tournament and light blue is a nod to the many overseas trips made by the group over the years.

name: JetBlue, Minted
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of JetBlue Airways Corporation. May only be woven with the written permission from JetBlue Airways Corporation or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: The JetBlue, Minted tartan was gifted by Edinburgh International Airport to JetBlue to celebrate their inaugural 2024 route to the Scottish capital’s airport. Designed in collaboration with Ciara Cordasco, JetBlue Product Design Manager, this design features the two iconic blue tones of the JetBlue brand. Their signature mint green colour, often found throughout their aircrafts, is featured as a bold overcheck in the design. The threadcount was developed using numbers and dates of significance to the story of JetBlue, including; their founding year 1998; their IATA identified number 6 and the number 17, which is intended to representing the numbers associated with their first flight to Scotland, 22 May 2024.

name: JetBlue, Born of Queens
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of JetBlue Airways Corporation. May only be woven with the written permission from JetBlue Airways Corporation or a nominated agent. May only be woven with written permission from JetBlue Airways Corporation or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: A tartan for JetBlue, who are based in Queens, New York, based on the same threadcount rationale as the JetBlue, Minted design. The mint colour was swapped with orange, a new colour for JetBlue, which is intended to represent their new route to Scotland in 2024.

name: Interpol 92
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those authorised by the copyright holder only. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders or their agents. To follow.
registrationNotes: INTERPOL was officially created in 1923 at the second meeting of the International Criminal Police Congress in Vienna. The 92nd Interpol General Assembly held in Glasgow, Scotland in 2024 is celebrated with the Interpol 92 Tartan especially designed for the occasion. Scotland's Black Watch Regiment upon whose tartan the INTERPOL 92 is loosely based, was formed in 1739 to 'Watch upon the braes", to guard the hills, keep the peace and prevent the widespread theft of cattle.' A very worthy forerunner of today's international police body. The distinctive red, white, and blue logo marque of the 2024 Congress, is the focal point, balanced by the wide navy-blue band comprising 92 threads - one for each annual INTERPOL International General Assembly. On either side of that navy, woven in INTERPOL blue, and separated by narrow reds, are threads of 7, 9, 19 and 23 (7th September 1923), the precise date of the 1923 Congress and the foundation of INTERPOL.

name: Iwuagwu, Chukwuemeka (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding weaving/reproduction/use must be directed to Stephen Hutchings or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created as a gift for the Reverend Canon Chuks Iwuagwu. The design was inspired by the Clergy tartan. Chukwuemeka was born in the area of Nigeria that sought independence in the 1970's, so the design incorporates colours intended to represent the Biafran flag, which is significant in Igbo (his tribe) culture. He went to university and trained as a priest in Glasgow.

name: Balmoral Hunting
restrictions: Yes. The tartan can only be exclusively purchased from Balmoral Castle Shop. Permission to weave must be sought from Balmoral Estate Office and Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with Balmoral Estate Office.
registrationNotes: The Balmoral Hunting tartan was commissioned by Balmoral Castle & Estate by kind permission of HM The King. The design was based on the Hunting Stewart tartan. The colours were inspired by the landscape of the Cairngorms. The colour palette is based on natural dyes including; comfrey, indigo, logwood, cochineal and walnuts. A total of 172 threads creates the four main green checks within the tartan, a nod to the number of years Balmoral has been the Highland home of the Royal Family. The year King Charles III acceded to the throne, 2022, is represented within the two navy blocks between the green, these blocks are created from 22 threads. Six fine black checks have been created in the crossing of the tartan to mark the 6 monarchs since the reign of Queen Victoria when Balmoral became a Royal home. The four grey checks represent the four prominent turrets on the Castle Tower.

name: McToy, K & B, Ythan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval is required to weave/use/reproduce this tartan from Kurtis and Benjamin & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: A tartan for Kurtis and Benjamin McToy. The pattern is intended to pay homage to their families - both belong to a set of 5 siblings and this is represented by the 5 stripes at the pivot. The colours were inspired by a combination of heritage, location and personal preference: green, purple and yellow are from the McMillan tartan; light blue is for the Toy family; black and the yellow are a nod to Kurtis’ Cornish heritage and dark blue is intended to represent the Ythan estuary where Kurtis and Benjamin live.

name: Quinn, Christopher & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding use/weaving must go through Christopher Quinn or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Christopher Quinn and his family. The tartan was created to celebrate his marriage in 2024 and includes colours that are intended to represent his birthplace of Ireland, his wife’s family and his time as an adult in Scotland.

name: Dench Williams, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Dench Williams, J & Family. Permission must be sought from Dench Williams, J & Family and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: A tartan for J Dench Williams & Family. The colours of the tartan are intended to represent a love of soft muted colours and the outdoors including; blue skies, a love of trees, particularly Oak, a cherished family holiday to Barbados and the rugged landscape of Scotland. Each of the family members is represented in the green, blue, pink, and yellow checks. Made from 9 threads, each of these checks, is intended to symbolise the bond between husband and wife and their shared birthdays on the 9th of their respective months. The check of 23 threads is intended to represent the date of Shakespeare’s birth and death.

name: Briley, Steven & Briley, Louise -Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Steven & Louise Briley. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted, only be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created for Steven & Louise Briley to celebrate their first wedding anniversary in 2024. The threadcount includes their wedding date and the design uses colours that are of special significance to them.

name: Alberta Dental Association
registrationNotes: This design was chosen by the Board of Directors at their May 2024 meeting from a selection of proposed designs. The yellow and blues are intended to represent the Association’s logo and the three white lines represent dentistry and the acronym ADA.

name: Toronto Crown & Bridge Study Club
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Toronto Crown & Bridge Study Club, Canada. The design consists of pink and two shades of grey consistent with their logo. The 19 lines making up the houndstooth pattern along with the surrounding pink section made up of 54 threads, represent the year the club was founded – 1954. The houndstooth pattern is symbolic of the Club’s affiliation with the art and science of dentistry.

name: Tigh Cladaich
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be a private tartan for the family. May only be woven with permission from Reuben Johnson.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Sainsbury-Johnson family, named after their home ‘Tigh Cladaich’ (which means Costal House), Wellington New Zealand. The Sainsbury-Johnson’s genealogy (whakapapa) ranges from Scotland, the UK and Aotearoa, New Zealand. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent the seas and rivers of the UK and New Zealand; dark green is for the landscapes of Scotland, Cumbria, Westmoreland and New Zealand; red is intended to represent interacting with the land and black is for New Zealand.

name: Cercle de Fermières Saint-Joseph - 85th Anniversary
restrictions: Yes. Intended for wear/use by active members of Cercle de Fermières Saint-Joseph or by others with permission. May only be woven by active members of Cercle de Fermières Saint-Joseph or by others with permission.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created to celebrate the 85th anniversary of the Cercle de Fermières Saint-Joseph. The colours used are those of the coat of arms of the City of Drummondville: gold which is intended to represent faith, strength, wealth; silver which is intended to represent purity; blue for justice, loyalty, and beauty; red for charity, justice, and heroism; green is intended to symbolise youth, hope, optimism, confidence in the future, and entrepreneurship. This tartan was unveiled during an exhibition at the Drummondville Public Library in October 2024.

name: Order of Christian Knights
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Order of Christian Knights. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The tartan was created to represent the Scottish heritage shared by many members of the Order of Christian Knights, an organisation based in the United States of America.

name: Cuillin Scottish Country Dancers
registrationNotes: Designed by Katrin Edelmann, dancer, teacher and head of the dance group ‘Cuillin Scottish Country Dancers’, which re-formed in 2020. Colours: purple and green are intended to reflect a national emblem of Scotland, the thistle; white is intended to represent the sky and dark grey is for peat soil where thistle and heather grow.

name: El-Ahl, Jad & Kelly, Elhana - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval to weave/use/reproduce required by El-Ahl, Jad & Kelly, Elhana, Kelly, Liz & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: Designed to celebrate the marriage of Elhana Kelly and Jad El-Ahl using colours significant to each of them: yellow is for the chosen stone of Elhana’s engagement ring; green is intended to represent Jad and the Lebanese cedar; blue is for the sea; significant to both and ivory is intended to represent new beginnings. The thread count references the date they first met.

name: Association of Hackney Carriage Drivers of the City of Edinburgh (CIC)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Association of Hackney Carriage Drivers if the City of Edinburgh (CIC) only. May only be woven with permission from Association of Hackney Carriage Drivers if the City of Edinburgh (CIC).
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Association of Hackney Carriage Drivers of the City of Edinburgh (CIC) using colours associated with the City of Edinburgh and the Saltire.

name: Polar Nights
restrictions: Yes. There are no inherent restrictions on who can wear or use this tartan for personal use, however for commercial reproduction or use, please contact the designer for licensing details. For any form of commercial exploitation or reproduction, please contact the designer to obtain the appropriate licensing. IPR registration pending.
registrationNotes: The tartan was inspired by the aurora borealis witnessed by the designer on March 16, 2015, at Þingvellir, Iceland. The design is intended to capture the vivid interplay of colours in the sky and ephemeral beauty of the Northern Lights.

name: Sleigh, C W L (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Christopher Sleigh & Family. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Christopher Sleigh and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Created for the Sleigh family, for personal and business use. The colours of the tartan are intended to represent Scotland's land and sea in the green, brown, and blue, whilst the yellow is symbolic of daffodils in the spring, gorse in the summer and the rising and setting of the sun. A flash of purple was included for the heathers and Scottish thistles. The Sleigh’s brand consists of 3 family run branches which are represented by the two sets of three blue checks. 100 green threads are intended to represent the Sleigh family, who have been Royal Warrant holders for 100 years. The central green check of 50 threads is intended to represent 50th anniversary of WL Sleigh in 2024.

name: McLarty, Richard and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the McLarty Family. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from the McLarty Family and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the McLarty Family. The design was inspired by their time on the golf courses of Scotland, particularly the view from their St Andrews home with the design intended to reflect the land, sea and sky. The two main blocks are intended to represent Richard and Liz with their two daughters depicted in the white and purple checks.

name: Barry Martin Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by any individual, with the permission of the surviving spouse and sons of Barry Martin. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Shelley Martin and her sons by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Mcnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kilt Makers
registrationNotes: Barry Martin was a dedicated Firefighter based in Edinburgh. He lost his life 4 days after attending a fire at the former Jenners building on 27th January 2023, where he sustained critical injuries. Barry was married to Shelley in 2010 where he proudly wore the Lionheart tartan. Based upon the colours of this and incorporating the Thin Red Line which symbolises the loss of firefighter life in the line of duty, the Barry Martin Commemorative tartan was created to remember the magic Barry brought to the lives of his family and friends.

name: Bowman, Zachary Clark & Ward, Mary Elizabeth and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by individuals with the surnames Bowman, Clark, Ward, Kelley, and family members in relation to Zachary Clark Bowman and Mary Elizabeth Ward. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Zachary Clark Bowman and Mary Elizabeth Ward by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to mark the wedding of Zachary Clark Bowman and Mary Elizabeth Ward in 2024. The colours utilized in this pattern were chosen from their ancestral clans and woven together to represent the joining of families. The deep red and yellow represent the MacQueen clan tartan from Zachary Clark Bowman’s lineage. The slate gray and pastel green colors were chosen to represent the Kelley clan associated with Mary Elizabeth Ward’s family.

name: Built Environment - Smarter Transformation
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Built Environment – Smarter Transformation. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Built Environment – Smarter Transformation in celebration of the organisation’s 10th anniversary in 2024. The numbers in the threadcount reference the significant years of 2014 and 2024 & the colour palette reflects their brand colours.

name: Benchmark
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by staff and guests invited to the event, permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought by Benchmark Mineral Intelligence LTD. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar; a subdivision of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with Auld Alliance Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Benchmark Mineral Intelligence LTD, known as ‘Benchmark’ to celebrate their 2024 AGM taking place in Scotland. The Colours are based around the company’s brand colours; yellow, orange and black colours are the colours of Benchmark Minerals’ logo; light blue is intended to represent the flow of data about rare and raw minerals that Benchmark Minerals Intelligence LTD provides to their clients.

name: Stephansen, Cathrine (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for personal use within the Stephansen family. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Cathrine Stephasen, intended for use in traditional Norwegian "bunad" (National costume). Reds, greens and black were frequently used in designs in Gudbrandsdalen, Norway.

name: FENDI
designer: Campbell, Clare, Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of FENDI SRL. May only be woven with the written permission from FENDI SRL or a nominated agent. May only be woven with written permission from FENDI SRL or a nominated agent. Copyright rests with FENDI SRL
registrationNotes: FENDI and Prickly Thistle worked closely to create this design, that is intended to tell the story of the Maison and Fendi family. Colours: brown reflects FENDI's Pequin striped design and yellow is a nod to the Maison’s heritage. The number five, representing the five Fendi sisters is included in the design together with the meaningful dates of FENDI’s founding year (1925) and the launch of Baguette (1997) and Peekaboo (2009) bags.

name: Odd, J & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Dr James Odd and his family. The design includes colours which carry a specific meaning for the family: red is intended to symbolise passion and courage; the shades of pink represent compassion, kindness, and grace, qualities embodied by Dr. Odd’s mother and his wife, whose middle name is ‘Rose’; white is intended to represent purity, clarity, and new beginnings and deep maroon is intended to represent tradition, nobility, and steadfastness. The design is intended to represent the family’s commitment to upholding their heritage and values, ensuring that their traditions are passed down through generations.

name: Witchery
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery. Copyright rests with Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery.
registrationNotes: James Thomson first opened the doors of The Witchery on Halloween 1979. This tartan was commissioned to celebrate 5 decades on the Castlehill, Edinburgh. The design was inspired by the Munro tartan in honour of James' grandmother and is intended to reflect The Witchery’s historical setting and the gothic allure of Edinburgh's Old Town. Colours: black is intended to symbolise the period between 1470 and 1722 when witchcraft held sway in Edinburgh; gold (yellow) pays homage to George Heriot, Goldsmith to the King and founder of George Heriot’s School where James was educated; red is a nod to James’ love of Burgundian wines and green was inspired by the 5th Duke of Gordon, Keeper of the Keys to Edinburgh Castle, whose former residence forms part of The Witchery today. 352 threads form the sett of the tartan, mirroring The Witchery's address, 352 Castlehill, The Royal Mile, while the 7 blocks characterise the 7 hills of Edinburgh.

name: Witchery - Dress
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery. Copyright rests with Castlegate Investments (Edinburgh) Ltd T/A The Witchery.
registrationNotes: A dress version of the Witchery tartan commissioned to celebrate 5 decades on the Castlehill, Edinburgh. This red version is intended to reflect the walls within the Witchery, panelled with 17th century oak rescued from a fire at St Giles Cathedral and panelling from a Burgundian Chateau. Colours: wine-red is intended to reflect the Burgundian wines cherished by James and showcased in The Witchery's cellar; the crimson shade nods to the procession of monarchs traversing the Royal Mile on route from the Palace of Holyrood house to Edinburgh Castle; black is intended to evoke the era when witchcraft held sway Edinburgh between 1470 & 1722; the gold (yellow) check mirrors the Witchery’s heraldic painted and gilded ceilings, and green was inspired by the Witchery's passion for the long-term conservation and sustainable future of historic buildings. 352 threads form the sett, mirroring The Witchery's address, 352 Castlehill, The Royal Mile.

name: Boeing

name: Beer, Jane & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: A tartan for Jay Hexter-Carmichael and his family. name: Spirit of Glyndwr

registrationNotes: A Welsh fashion tartan, using colours associated with the Welsh slate and dark lakes of North Wales, intended to celebrate and embody the passion of Welsh soldier, Owain Glyndwr (c.1354 – c.1415). The tradition of wearing the Cilt in Wales (spelt with a ‘C’ as there is no K in the Welsh language) while seen as commercial, has grown in popularity since being introduced by Wales Tartan Centres circa 1998. Designed for Wales Tartan Centres by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys (now closed).

name: Koepke, K & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Kenneth Koepke and his family. Colours: blue and white are intended to represent Kenneth’s mother’s heritage from the Clark family in Scotland; black, yellow and red are based on his father's German heritage.

name: Tuluhungwa, G & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: A tartan for Geoffrey Tuluhungwa and his family to celebrate their affiliation and love for Scotland since they arrived in 1979. The design uses colours intended to represent Tanzania and the family’s close links with Scotland.

name: Aiken, Maxine & Family (Personal)
