registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Maxine Hvass (nee Aiken). The design blends elements intended to represent her Australian upbringing and her Scottish heritage from her father. Colours: green and blue were inspired by the landscapes and seascapes of both countries; orange is intended to represent the red earth of north west Australia; pale cream pays homage to sandy coastlines and black is intended to represent star filled night skies.

name: Emily Joubert
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the In Any Event., (DBA) Emily Joubert. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be sought from In Any Event., (DBA) Emily Joubert and Araminta Campbell LTD. Copyright rests with In Any Event, Inc., (DBA) Emily Joubert.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Emily Joubert, a home and garden lifestyle brand in San Francisco, California. The namesake for the store, Emily Joubert, honours the cherished memory and enduring legacy of founder Judy Sieber's grandmother. The colours were inspired by Judy’s love of the untamed Scottish landscape. Judy’s two sons are intended to be represented by the checks formed of 8 threads to represent them being born 8 years apart. The largest block of green comprises 35 threads, a tribute to Judy and Mike’s 35 years of marriage. Two soft purple checks are for the two Emily Joubert stores and consist of 4 threads to represent the first store opening in 2004, while the yellow celebrates the second store opening in 2023.

name: King-Jackson, A & L (Personal)
designer: Paterson, Robert; Jackson, Andy & King, Laura
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the wedding of Laura King and Andy Jackson, who had both given up on ever meeting someone special until they met each other. This tartan is intended to represent the couple and their shared love of travelling and adventure. It is made even more special by the threadcount of ‘15/09/2024’, the date of their wedding.

name: Duettrasson, I & H and Family (Personal)
designer: Duettra, Hannah; Anderson, Ian & Paterson, Robert
registrationNotes: A tartan to celebrate the wedding of Hannah and Ian Duettrasson and their family. The design combines elements from Ian’s family tartan and Hannah’s favoured Scotland Forever tartan, to represent their wedding in Scotland, and where Hannah and Ian decided to spend their future together.

name: Liberty University Inc.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Liberty University, Inc., Virginia, United States. This tartan is intended to represent family, community, competitiveness and a warrior’s spirit. The founding date of 13/09/1971 (09-13-19-71) is captured within the thread count.

name: Western College

registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Western College, part of Miami University, for their 2024 Homecoming Weekend; ‘Celebrating the Spirit of Western: A Homecoming for Love, Honor and Legacy’. The tartan was created using dates for the founding of Western College on July 14, 1853 and the Homecoming football game on September 28, 2024. The design, weaving together these two dates, is intended to celebrate the legacy of Western College and Miami University.

name: Higgins School of Highland Dance
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be limited to the use of Higgins School of Highland Dance and its owner, dancers, dancers' families and instructors. May only be woven with permission from Kathleen Higgins.
registrationNotes: The Higgins School of Highland Dance Tartans, created for the school’s 15th anniversary, serve as a tribute to the heritage and community that shaped HSHD. The designs were inspired by a mix of tartans that reflect the school's roots, its regional ties, and Kathleen’s family history in Cape Breton and Ontario. Combining elements of local tartans and Nova Scotia symbols, they embody the deep connection between the school, its location, and the province. The blue represents the waters of Dartmouth, while the warm yellow and red echo the Nova Scotia tartan. The colours also draw from the Cape Breton tartan, the Ontario provincial tartan, the Dartmouth City of Lakes tartan, the Heritage of Halifax tartan, and Nova Scotia’s provincial flag. A purple stripe honours HSHD’s original brand colour, evolving with the school’s growth and new branding in blue, white, black, and yellow. The tartans symbolize the school’s enduring spirit, history, and connection to its home.

name: Tartania

name: Coal Mining

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate and celebrate the role of coal miners in producing coal. Colours: black is for coal; white for the light from a miner’s lamp; red is intended to represent the blood of the many men killed and injured in the dangerous conditions in which they worked and blue is intended to represent scars that miners carried on their bodies.

The sett was inspired by the Robertson tartan, honouring Jen's grandmother and great-grandfather.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Lyons Autoracing, Canada, to be used in their branding for both sim racing and car racing. The colours are intended to reflect the Lyons Autoracing logo, yellow for the lion and gold for the king’s crown, along with black and white which is intended to represent the checkered racing flag.

name: Leaviss, I and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Isobel Leaviss or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Isobel Leaviss and her family using colours of personal significance.

name: Gude!

The colours were inspired by those associated with his home city – Darmstadt – including: the city’s Coat of Arms; the flag of Darmstadt; the colours of the local soccer club SV Darmstadt 98; the white lily; the brooks running through the city; ESAs European Space Operation Center, as the Darmstadt is known as the City of Science; the forests that are surround the city and the outskirts of the Odenwald.

name: Bell-Smith, S & R (Personal)

Colours: green is intended to represent the green of Kwazulu-Natal and the Province of Ulster, along with the Smith Family tartan; blue is for the Bell's, loyalty and the waters and skies they have encountered; red is intended to reflect both of their families and where they grew up and white is intended to be a symbol of happiness and longevity.

name: Davis, L W & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: A tartan for Luke William Davis & his Family. The colours are intended to signify: connections to the Channel Islands where Luke, the designer, was raised; an affinity with the countryside and agriculture; and a family anniversary, which is the same date as Luke’s birthday.

name: Nova Scotia SPCA
restrictions: Yes. Individuals who have purchased the tartan products through the Nova Scotia SPCA may wear/use this tartan. Only businesses who have approval from the Nova Scotia SPCA may weave this tartan.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Nova Scotia SPCA, a registered charity in Canada, that helps companion animals in need and proudly follows open-admission and no-kill principles. Every year, around 16,000 pets are helped through animal rescue, progressive programs, and rehoming opportunities. With six animal shelters in Nova Scotia, this design includes colours of significance: red is intended to represent the Mi’kmaq; yellow (gold) is intended to symbolise African Nova Scotians; blue is for welcoming newcomers to Nova Scotian shores; light grey (silver) is intended to represent protection; green is for new beginnings and white represents hope.

name: Bernardino, Laura & Claussen, Laurence - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by immediate family and descendants. Permission can be granted to third parties upon request. Please contact the tartan owners regarding weaving.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Laura Bernadino and Laurence Claussen on 1st August 2024. The couple first met in Aberdeen and return to Scotland with friends and family to visit their favourite places as often as they can. The colours are intended to represent their love for Scotland: green for the mountains during summer; brown of autumn; blue for the lochs and skies; purple for the heather and the yellow of the sun.

name: Flintlock
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail and is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388834.
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to celebrate all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the United States Army’s Exercise Flintlock, since its formation in 2005. With forces from U.S. Special Operations Command Africa partnering with nearly 30 nations and approximately 1,300 personnel. Exercise Flintlock is the largest annual special operations forces exercise that works to strengthen combined partner force collaboration in Africa alongside international and NATO international special operations forces. Colours: olive green and black are intended to represent the Flintlock crest; red is from the Special Operations Command Africa crest; sandy-beige and navy blue represent the land and maritime operational elements of Exercise Flintlock.

name: Greens Retail
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Greens Retail. Permission to wear/use/weave must be sought from Greens Retail.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Greens Retail to commemorate a milestone for the company. The design was used for the opening of their Braemar store and celebrated their achievement. The design is intended to be centred around the 4 company values; people, place, product, and planet. Since the opening of their Braemar store the tartan has been introduced throughout all stores, to proudly display the company’s Scottish heritage and identity in communities.

name: Spirit of Le Mans (Rally)

registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the annual sports car races in Le Mans, France, and in particular those races that took place during the 1960s.

name: Moir, Shawn & Family (Personal)

The white line is intended to commemorate the cleaned bones of the fallen at the Battle of Teba in 1330, brought back by the Progenitor of the Moirs, Sir Kenneth de la More (where he was given the name Moir for these services).

name: R&A World Golf Museum

The varying widths of checks within this design were inspired by the historical stained-glass window in The Royal & Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews which symbolises the Museum’s connection to the origins of the game, bringing the past, present and future of golf to life.

name: Luder, Ian & Luder, Lin and Family (Personal)

This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Ian and Lin Luder by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kilt Makers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to mark the election of Ian Luder as Deacon of the Incorporation of Coopers of Glasgow. The colours are intended to mirror the Armorial Ensigns and Badge granted to Ian by Garter King of Arms in London in 2001, and to reflect the elements thereof which refer to his wife Lin, along with their admiration of Scotland.

name: Lantern of the North
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the 50th year of the Elgin & District Pipe Band in 2024, to be worn by the band and the communities who support the organisation. The name ‘Lantern of the North’ is a nod to the centre piece of the bands badge, Elgin Cathedral, which was situated in the centre of the town and was affectionately known as the Lantern of the North prior to its destruction by fire in 1390. The tartan itself has been designed to reflect the blue waters of the River Spey, the Moray Firth and the barley and whisky for which the locality is famous: the blues, comprising both lighter and deeper hues are intended to capture the varying tones of the River and Firth; dark yellow, representing golden amber, is intended to reflect the local barley fields which, when joined by the waters of the Spey, form the amber nectar Whisky.

name: Morford, A and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This design was created for A & A Morford to be used as a family tartan and by their descendants. It was inspired by the red and gold colours of San Francisco and the natural blues and greens of south-west Scotland to represent both sides of the Morford family.

name: Koehler, Dirk & Jarzemski, Beate - Wedding (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the wedding of Dirk Koehler and Beate Jarzemski in 2024 and their love for Scotland. The design was inspired by an iris photograph of the bride and groom.

restrictions: Yes. Approval required to use/weave/reproduce by the Birgersson Family & ScotlandShop (Formerly House of Tartan).
registrationNotes: A tartan for J & S Birgersson and their family. The design was inspired by their Viking heritage and the numerous family members who have careers as mariners.

name: Le Clan Mac O'ier
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by members of the association. Cannot be woven without the written authorisation of one of the co presidents of the association. This Tartan was registered in France at the INPI (National Institut of the Intellectual Property), ref no 20242310.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the association ‘Le Clan Mac O'ier’, located in France. The organisation is run by a blended family with step-sons, step-daughters, sons-in-law and daughters in law. The organisation’s motto is ‘We don't need to share the same blood to belong to the same clan’.

name: Kilbride, I W S and Family (Personal)
designer: Kilbride, Ian William Sefton and Slanj Kilts
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Ian Kilbride or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ian William Sefton Kilbride, and his family, to celebrate their Celtic roots and also their deep love of Africa, which they have now made their home. The colours are intended to be a reflection of all aspects of the Kilbride’s lives.

name: St Andrew’s Society Melbourne
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by members of the St Andrew’s Society Melbourne. Prior approval to weave/reproduce required by Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & the St Andrew’s Society Melbourne.
registrationNotes: Founded in 2020 by Nick Broadley, The St Andrew’s Society Melbourne brings together a vibrant community of Scottish business leaders. Their mission is to foster enduring and meaningful relationships within the Scottish business community in Melbourne, with a vision that spans generations. The colours used within the tartan are intended to represent the link between Scotland and Australia: blue to represent the Scottish Saltire; black for the Australian Aboriginal Flag; light purple to represent Heather; light green to represent Eucalyptus and finally navy, the colour associated with Melbourne and Victoria.

name: Illing, R & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Rowland Illing and his family to celebrate Rowland’s 50th Birthday and to be used by all members of the family, now and in the future.

name: Scottish Celebrant, The
restrictions: Yes. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Paul Browett, The Scottish Celebrant by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Mcnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Paul Browett, The Scottish Celebrant. Paul was faced with the challenging task of being asked to compose and deliver the funeral eulogy of his terminally ill twin sister Nicola, the catalyst for Paul becoming a celebrant. Paul soon established himself as a successful celebrant and became known as ’The Scottish Celebrant', conducting ceremonies all across Scotland. The inspiration for this tartan and the chosen colours are intended to reflect the far reaches of Scotland which played an important role in The Scottish Celebrants journey: blue for the sea in Harris; the sand of Portobello; purple for the heather filled hills of the Pentlands and shadowy purple peaks of the Highlands; white for the bothys of Glencoe and finally fuchsia pink as a reminder of the loved one that started this journey.

name: Gainbridge
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of Gainbridge. May only be woven with approval from the CEO of Group 1001.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Gainbridge, a financial services company based in the United States. The colours are based of the company’s logo.

name: McMenemy, J R and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by the McMenemy family only. May only be woven/reproduced with permission from the tartan owner.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for J R McMenemy and his family using colours of personal significance that are intended to represent tranquillity, calmness and stability.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Brandon and Lydiah Harrell and their family.

registrationNotes: A tartan for David Geneen and his family to celebrates their roots in Glasgow's Jewish community. The tartan is intended to symbolise the family’s heritage, blending their Scottish and Jewish identities into a visual representation of the family's history and values.

name: Great Uncle Bulgaria
restrictions: Yes. Intended for sole use by Wombles Copyright Holdings Limited. Permission is required from Wombles Copyright Holdings Limited to weave/use/reproduce this tartan. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the character of Great Uncle Bulgaria, the warm and respected Elder of our Wombles. Ancient and wise, he has a sharp eye and a keen wit. He revels in his Scottish heritage and wears his Womble tartan with pride. The Wombles were created by Elisabeth Beresford in 1968, via her first book 'The Wombles'. In 1973 The Wombles were made into the hit stop-motion television series and have since maintained a special place in British culture over the course of the years.

name: McDavid, N & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by immediate family and descendants. Permission can be granted to third parties upon request. Please contact the tartan owners regarding weaving.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Nicholas McDavid and his family. The colours were inspired by the national flags of England, Scotland, Wales and the United States, places all connected with the family’s ancestry.

name: Diaz, Rosemary & Eddy - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Eddy and Rosemary and their immediate family, unless otherwise confirmed with written permission. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kilt makers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the wedding of Rosemary and Eddy Diaz on 18/09/2024. The design includes their favourite colours.

name: Whitehead, E (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those with the surname Whitehead or with Whitehead ancestors. Permission to weave/use/reproduce this tartan must be obtained from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by the designer to commemorate his ancestor Elizabeth Whitehead and to be used by their family to celebrate their Scottish heritage. Elizabeth was born in Kirkcaldy in 1811, the illegitimate daughter of George Whitehead and Elizabeth Chalmers (or Chambers). After secretly marrying a French fisherman in Kirkcaldy, who was already married in France, she left to join him and live in France in 1837. They officially married under the French administration in 1874. Elizabeth died in 1889 in Gravelines, France.

name: Boogaarts, Y and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Boogaarts family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Yari Boogaarts and his family. It was designed while Yari was on holiday on a tour of Scotland. The design uses colours of personal significance.

name: Marubeni Europower
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those connected to Marubeni Corporation and its subsidiaries or those with approval from Marubeni.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Marubeni Europower, a subsidiary of Marubeni Corporation that specialises in delivering innovative and sustainable energy solutions across Europe. Marubeni Europower established its Glasgow Office in 2022. The design includes; Marubeni's corporate colours, blue and white from the flag of Scotland and elements intended represent Marubeni’s links with Scotland and their work with local communities to create a sustainable society.

name: Humlechok
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by initiated members of the rover scout division of Skallerup-Vennebjerg scout group in Vensyssel, Denmark. May only be woven with permission from the designer or from the rover scout division of Skallerup-Vennebjerg scout group in Vensyssel, Denmark.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Humlechok rover division of the Skallerup-Vennebjerg Scout Group. Founded in 1983, the Scout Group leaders formed the rover division for 18+ year olds who were missing out on the activities and community that the younger scouts were enjoying. In Denmark, and across the world, neckerchiefs are used by rover groups to differentiate from each other and this tartan was created by founding member and certified weaver Hanne Käthe Skamriis to be worn by the Humlechok group. Colours: blue is intended to represent the sea near the scout group base; green for their uniforms and for the surrounding nature; red and orange for the campfires and sunsets that make evenings on a jamboree special.

name: Masonic Whisky Syndicate
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Masonic Whisky Syndicate. May only be woven with permission from the tartan owner.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Masonic Whisky Syndicate based in Switzerland. The colours are based on traditional masonic colours and the colour of whisky.

name: Rayson, D, J & C and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was created for siblings Duncan, John and Catherine Rayson and their families. Colours: the 3 red lines are intended to represent the three siblings; green was inspired by the green used in the Nisbet tartan, which ties them to their Scottish ancestry; white and blue based on the colours on the flag of Scotland.

name: Solaja, M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Solaja extended Solaja family. Permission to use/weave/reproduce the tartan should be sought by the Solaja family. The owner agrees that all tartan weaving requirements shall be exclusively arranged by Auld Alliance Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar; a subdivision of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with Auld Alliance Kiltmakers Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Michael Solaja and his family to celebrate Michael's Nigerian roots and Scottish upbringing. It was designed to be used as both clothing and a way to preserve family and national identities, and is intended to reflect a mix of Nigerian and Scottish traditions. Colours: grey is intended to represent Scotland's cloudy weather; green and white are intended to represents the Nigerian flag, in addition green is for hope and fertility and white is for peace and unity; purple is for Michael’s wife Kirsty’s favourite colour.

name: Adam, Erika (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan was designed exclusively for Erika Adam, her immediate family members and those with her permission. Permission to weave/use/reproduce this tartan must be obtained from Erika Adam.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created by Erika's sister for her 40th birthday on 04/09/2024. The thread counts includes numbers to signify her birth year, her age at the time of the design and her age when her son was born. Colours: light green is intended to symbolise Erika; dark green represents her life; the other colours are intended to represent her immediate family with the larger light blue being for her son.

name: Black Reiver

registrationNotes: This company tartan was designed for Black Reiver Consulting for use across their various divisions. The dark colour palette is intended to evoke the spirit of The Black Reiver.

name: Characternyk, The (Black Reiver)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Black Reiver Consulting. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This company tartan was designed for Black Reiver Consulting to promote their connection to their subsidiary company Kotermak Training and Consultancy in Kyiv and their part in the development of Ukraine Geothermal. The Characternyk is part of Ukranian folk legend. The threadcount includes numbers that are intended to reference the date of Ukraine Independence Day and the year that Ukraine became independent. The triple overcheck is intended to represent the Ukrainian trident and the colour palette includes the yellow & blue of the Ukrainian flag.

name: PureMalt
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Pure Malt. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This company tartan was designed to enhance the PureMalt brand and to celebrate the company’s proud Scottish heritage. The design takes inspiration from the Lamont and Tyneside tartans which are similar in sett. These tartans reference the Turner (a sept of Lamont) family’s ownership and the company’s Haddington location. The palette uses PureMalt’s brand colours.

name: Comann Albannach UQ

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Comann Albannach UQ (University of Queensland, Australia), which is a social society for anyone who is connected, identifies or interested in Scottish culture, history and people.

name: Holtry, Anthony & McLeod, Barbara - Wedding (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Elizabeth Holtry & Laura Holtry-Hughes to celebrate their parents’ 60th wedding anniversary. The design and colour palette take inspiration from elements of the McLeod and Marshall tartans which reference the family’s Scottish heritage. The threadcount includes blocks of 60 threads to represent their 60 years of marriage.

name: Bowers, I and A & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: Tartan was designed by brothers Iain David Bowers and Andrew James Bowers from Lochaber, as a personal tartan for family use.

registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for Habro, a commercial property advisory company based in London and Copenhagen, specialising in sourcing, financing and managing investments on behalf of institutions, private individuals, and offshore investors. The tartan combines the Habro corporate colours and the colours of the Danish and UK flags.

name: Pettigrew, J & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Jerad Pettigrew and his family. It is intended to celebrate the family’s ancestry, with one of the earliest records of the name being found in Lanarkshire.

name: Dirou, A, M & T and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. Please contact regarding use.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Armel, Maïeul & Tugdual Dirou and their families. The colours were inspired by the family’s origins; black and white is intended to represent the traditional flag of Brittany, which is the black St George's Cross on a white flag; green refers to the green hills of Brittany and the area around the family home, as well as to the colour of oak which is connected to the family’s name; red family's most distant origins in Wales and blue is intended to represent the Channel crossed by the family's ancestors to settle in Armorica.

name: Brandt
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be used with the permission directly from Brandt. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Brandt Group of Companies, based in Canada. The colours are based on Brandt’s corporate colours: orange is intended to represent energy and vitality; black for power and sophistication and grey for balance and refinement.

name: Frances Irwin Handweavers Guild 50th Anniversary
designer: Augustino, C; Lande, D & McCarthy E
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the 50th Anniversary of the Frances Irwin Handweavers Guild. The tartan design uses the Fibonacci sequence in the threadcount and the colour palette is intended to represent the sunny skies, lakes and fields of the Garden State of New Jersey where the Guild in based.

name: Swagelok Company
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be used with permission of Swagelok. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Swagelok Company, based in the United States. The design is intended to represent the legacy of the company providing innovative fluid system components and solutions to customers around the world for over 75 years. The Swagelok blue, from the company’s logo, is incorporated within the design is intended to represent a connection to the company’s core values.

name: Pride of Hal-con
restrictions: Yes. It is intended for use by the extended Hal-con family, Board members, staff, volunteers, guests and attendees. Permission to weave or produce the tartan for commercial applications is required from the Hal-con board. Address: Hal-Con Sci-Fi, Fantasy, and Gaming Convention, 5675 Spring Garden Rd., Suite B6 Halifax, Nova Scotia, B3J 3R4 Copyright rests with the designer. Tartan was designed using the Clan.com online tartan designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Hal-con, Nova Scotia's largest Science Fiction and Gaming convention. Hal-con has a long history of tartans being worn by staff and volunteers. In 2022, after volunteering for the first time, Tim Poirier designed a tartan for the organisation. Colours: green, purple and grey are Hal-con’s corporate colours and a rainbow stripe has been added to represent the diversity and inclusiveness of the event.

name: Holker, G & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by George Holker, his immediate family, his descendants, and descendants of his immediate family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for George Holker and his family. The sett was inspired by samples from the ‘Holker Album’, compiled by an 18th Century ancestor of the family, Jacobite soldier, John Holker. The colours used, green of fresh larch growth, purple of heather, yellow of broom and the browns of the moors, are intended to reflect the environs around the family home, while the bright sky blue is associated with the Manchester Regiment formed during the Jacobite uprising.

name: International Myeloma Society
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use by the International Myeloma Society. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to mark the 23rd International Myeloma Society Annual Meeting, hosted in Glasgow, Scotland in 2026.

name: Clackmannanshire
restrictions: Yes. Approval required from Clackmannanshire Council. Handwoven restricted to residents and businesses in Clackmananshire such as Taffled Threads Ltd. Mill woven restricted to Scottish Mills. Permission required from Clackmannanshire Council for Promotion of Products, People and Heritage of Clackmannanshire.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Clackmannanshire, Scotland. The colours represent the nature and culture of the Wee County, celebrating the people, history and achievements: red represents the red squirrels in the trees of the hillfoots, the old red sandstone of the Ochil’s and the autumn colours across the landscape; blue for the bluebell woods, the cobalt mines near Alva and the blue tattoos of the Pictish Miathi tribe who made their home in the Ochils; black is for the old coal industry and the Black Devon which springs from the Ochils; white is for the clouds at the base of the Ochils, sheep that dot the countryside and provided the wool for the textile industries, and the snowcapped hills in winter; yellow is for the wheat fields and golden barley used in the ales of the local brewing industry. The green represents the rolling hills and woodlands which together with the black and white of the Erskine and red and yellow of the Bruce families all feature in the heraldic crest of Clackmannanshire.

name: Hogwarts

Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. registrationNotes: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie, is described as the most heavily haunted dwelling in Britain. Each school house has its own ghost; Slytherin House boasts the Bloody Baron, Ravenclaw House has the Grey Lady, Hufflepuff House is haunted by the Fat Friar and Gryffindor House has Nearly Headless Nick. Colours: white is for the school ghosts; red, green, blue and yellow and the Hogwarts House colours; light brown is for the Hogwarts stonework and dark grey is for the Hogwarts spires.

name: Harry Potter
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. registrationNotes: Based on the character Harry Potter, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Colours: black is intended to represent Harry’s round glasses & wizard robe; white is for Hedwig, Harry Potter’s owl; brown is for Harry’s Holly wand; red is intended to represent Harry’s lightning shaped scar and maroon & yellow Harry’s Gryffindor House colours.

name: Hermione Granger
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388818.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Hermione Granger, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Hermione was described as the cleverest witch of her age and is one of Harry Potter's closest friends. The design uses colours associated with a few of her famous spells including the Polyjuice Potion, which turned her into Millicent Bulstrode's cat, and her clever use of the Timer Turner: dark grey, light grey & white are intended to represent Millicent Bulstrode's cat hairs; light green/yellow are for Hermione’s accidental cat’s eyes; yellow and pale beige are intended to represent the gold & sand of Hermione’s Time Turner; brown is for Hermione’s Vine Wood Wand and maroon & yellow are for Hermione’s Gryffindor House colours.

name: Ron Weasley
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388819.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Ron Weasley from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Ron is Harry’s best friend, from a homespun family background of ginger haired wizards & witches. Colours: dark orange is intended to represent the Weasley Family’s famous ginger hair; beige is intended to represent the big ‘R’ on Ron’s home-knit jumper; maroon & yellow are for Ron’s Gryffindor house colours and Ron’s Big R jumper and brown is for Scabbers, Ron’s pet rat.

name: Draco Malfoy
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388820.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Draco Malfoy, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Draco progressed from a school bully to a more dangerous person because of his parent’s allegiance to Voldermort, his nature became darker and darker as he moved over to the dark-side with his parents. Colours: dark green & grey is for Slytherin House; green is intended to represent his sneaky, snakey and sly nature; white is for the Malfoy’s famous white hair and black is intended to represent his actions getting darker as the films progress, influenced by the dark side.

name: Luna Lovegood
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388821.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Luna Lovegood, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Luna was nicknamed ‘Loony’ for her quirky ways, but she was in fact often one of Harry’s most clear-sighted friends. Luna stands out from the crowd with her eccentric brightly coloured image. Her courage, loyalty and kindness earned her place in Harry’s circle of most trusted friends. Colours; white is intended to represent Luna’s striking hair and red, yellow, pink, green, purple & blue are for Luna’s bright rainbow style fashion, including her famous blue and pink glasses, known as 'Spectrespecs' that allowed the wearer to see invisible Wrackspurts.

name: Lord Voldemort
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388822.
registrationNotes: Based on the character of the Dark Wizard/Dark Lord Voldemort, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. This design is intended to be dark and deathly looking, inspired by the French origins of the name Voldemort: ‘vol’ meaning ‘flight’ or ‘theft’; ‘de’ meaning ‘of’ or ‘from’; and ‘mort’ meaning ‘death’. Colours: black, dark grey & charcoal are intended to represent the Dark Lord and his billowing dark robe; green is for when Voldemort was known as Tom Riddle and his Slytherin House colour and white is for Voldemort’s eery pale white face.

name: Rubeus Hagrid
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388823.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Rubeus Hagrid from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Hagrid shares the father-figure role with Dumbledore towards Harry Potter. He is the Hogwart’s game-keeper, living on the edge of the Forbidden Forest which he likes to visit and look after strange creatures. The character loves the outdoors, is warm, nature-loving and practical but wild and messy at the same time and therefore this design is intended to appear more disordered in appearance. Colours: red was inspired by Hagrid’s first name, Rubeus, which means ‘Red’ in Latin; dark brown is intended to represent Hagrid’s famous bushy beard and wild hair; blue & white are for the sky and clouds of the great outdoors that he loves and green & brown are for the Forbidden Forest, full of his creature friends.

name: Albus Dumbledore
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388824.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Albus Dumbledore, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie, a father towards Harry Potter. Dumbledore is Headmaster at Hogwarts and is described as spiritual, wise, calm and one of the world’s greatest Wizards. This design is intended to be slick and elegant to represent his character. Colours: white was inspired by Dumbledore’s first name, Albus, meaning ‘white’ in Latin and also his famous long white hair and beard; light grey is for Dumbledore’s silver half-moon glasses sat on the end of his nose and his silver rings, chains and balls worn in his beard; gold & blue are for Hogwart’s Gold Owl and the blue glass ball lectern and dark grey is intended to represent one of Dumbledore’s favoured elegant grey velvet gowns and matching hat.

name: Professor Snape
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388825.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Professor Snape, from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie, who is a simple but smart individual in appearance. The colours, black, dark blue & white, are intended to represent Snape’s signature look with his sleek black hair and dark un-fussy clothing with a crisp white collar.

name: Professor Umbridge
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388826.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Professor Umbridge from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie, one of the most reviled characters in the Harry Potter series. Her love for rules and regulations, combined with her sadistic tendencies, made her a menacing figure both in the Ministry and at Hogwarts, she was controlling and cruel. The colours are intended to represent Umbridge’s sickly sweet taste in clothing and décor, her ornate and flowery China tea cups and cat plates displayed in her office and the blood from Harry Potter’s hand when writing his lines because of Professor Umbridge’s evil ‘quill spell’.

name: Professor McGonagall
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388827.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Professor McGonagall from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Professor McGonagall is Scottish and wears Green and Purple, being the colour of the Scottish thistle and also the colours Witches and Wizards favour in order to reveal themselves to each other in public. She can turn into a cat which is usually a grey striped variety. She is straight to the point, orderly and smart, which is intended to be represent within the look of this design. Colours: green and purple are intended to represent the Scottish thistle and witch & wizard clothing colours; black and grey are for the stripes of the cat form Professor McGonagall takes and black is for her famous witch hat and her robe.

name: Dobby
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388828.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Dobby from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. Dobby is a house-elf who was utterly devoted to Harry Potter, putting himself at great risk (and in serious physical pain) when he went out of his way to protect the young wizard from what Dobby knew would be significant danger. His loyalty and bravery were rewarded eventually, as he was freed from his cruel wizarding family with a gratefully received dirty sock. Colours: cream is intended to represent the fabric tied in knots that Dobby had to wear when enslaved as a house-elf; grey for Harry Potter’s grey school sock that freed dobby from his servitude to Lucius Malfoy; light green is for Dobby’s piercing light green eyes and pale salmon pink is for Dobby’s fleshy house-elf body.

name: Hedwig
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388829.
registrationNotes: Based on the character Hedwig from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie. A gift for Harry Potter’s eleventh birthday from Hagrid. Hedwig was a snowy owl who came to be one of Harry's closest companions. Not only did Hedwig deliver Harry Potter’s mail but she was a friend to Harry during his loneliest moments. Colours: white is intended to represent the main colour of Hedwig; dark brown is for the flecks on her feathers and yellow & black are for Hedwig’s eyes.

name: Hogwarts Express
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 16 September 2024, registration number: 6388830.
registrationNotes: Based on the Hogwarts Express, the famous locomotive steam train from Warner Bros’ Harry Potter Movie that takes Hogwarts pupil’s to and from Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Colours: red, black and gold are the colours of the Hogwarts Express locomotive steam train and pale grey is intended to represent the billowing smoke rising from the steam locomotive’s chimney.

restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Norman MacSween & Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted, may only be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created for Norman MacSween. The colour palette is intended to reference the scenery and history of the Hebrides.

registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Norman MacSween & Family tartan.

name: Weintraub, L (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for personal use. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be obtained from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created in memory of the designer’s grandmother and uses colours of personal significance.

name: Unity Presbyterian Church Fort Mill, SC
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be used by the Committee of the Unity Presbyterian Church. Design copyright is the property of Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd, Station Works, North St, Forfar, DD8 3BN, Scotland. Email Contact - [email protected]
registrationNotes: Created for The Unity Presbyterian Church, Fort Mill, South Carolina, to celebrate their 235th Anniversary in 2023. Formed in 1788, the roots of those who founded Unity, can be traced to early Pennsylvania settlers, direct descendants of Scots and Scots Irish. Colours: yellow is intended to represent the path of congregants and the Holy Trinity; blue represents the lakes, streams, and Catawba River of Fort Mill; grey represents the ashes from 3 fires that decimated former Unity sanctuaries; dark red is intended to represent the blood of Christ and where the yellow crosses itself is intended to be the cross he died upon.

name: Brandes, Rainer & Brandes, Christian (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Tartan may not be woven/used/reproduced without written permission from Mr Rainer Brandes or Mr Christian Brandes.
registrationNotes: A tartan for father and son, Rainer and Christian Brandes to celebrate Rainer’s retirement and their strong family bond. Colours: yellow was inspired by the harp background of the municipal Coat of Arms of Ilvesheim town, Germany, where Rainer lived; dark blue, green & black are intended to represent the Scottish landscape and weather which they enjoyed on many trips together and blue is of personal significance.

name: Ormond College
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for students, alumni, and staff of Ormond College. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ormond College, a leading Presbyterian tertiary education facility located in Victoria, Australia, which opened its doors in 1881. The university college was established by Scottish educators, Presbyterian ministers, and migrants to Australia. This tartan is intended to celebrate Ormond College’s Scottish heritage and educational ethos.

name: Klaus, Mario Christian (Personal)
designer: House of Edgar & Geoffrey Tailor Kiltmakers
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Mario Christian Klaus. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Mario Christian Klaus, a bagpipe player in a band of the Royal British Legion, using colours of personal significance.

name: USAFA United States Air force Academy
designer: Olde School Blazer Company, The and USAFA
restrictions: Yes. This tartan was created exclusively for United States Airforce Academy Cadets and Graduates. Express permission from the USAFA must be sought to wear or use this tartan. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by The Olde School Blazer Company in collaboration with the United States Air Force Academy's Association of Graduates. The tartan was created for those who will become officers of the United States Air Force and Space Force. The colours in the tartan are based on gold, blue, silver and red, which are colours that can be seen in campus architecture and are assigned to classes on a rotational basis; yellow, representing gold, is for the grassy plains; blue is for the ‘Wild Blue Yonder’; grey, representing silver, is for the stainless steel of aircrafts and red is intended to represent the sun.

name: Kelso, Y and M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be sought from the Kelso Family to use/wear/reproduce this tartan. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A family tartan for Yanick and Megan Kelso to celebrate their heritage and link their Scottish origins with their new Swiss home. Colours: dark green and light green are intended to pay tribute to the landscapes of both Scotland and Switzerland; three golden lines represent the three golden garbs and black is intended to symbolise the raven, both found on a historic family crest; white and red are intended to represent their new home in Switzerland.

name: Evans, Keith F T (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for personal use by the Evans family only. It may not be duplicated in any way. Authorisation is required before use. Special authorisations may be granted upon approval. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Keith F T Evans and is intended to honour and preserve the heritage of Keith's three Scottish families. The colours are a blended mix of those found on historic shields of the Evans, Jack and Shand families.

name: City of Chicago Pipe Band
restrictions: Yes. The wearing of this tartan is intended to be restricted to the City of Chicago Pipe Band and its overtly approved designees. The authority to weave this tartan or produce it in any other manner is restricted in perpetuity to the City of Chicago Pipe Band. Copyright and design right rests with - City of Chicago Pipe Band. Contact details: Andrew Hoinacki - [email protected] and Patrick Lynch - [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to provide a unique appearance, public image, and branding for the City of Chicago Pipe Band. Upon celebrating the organisation’s 20th anniversary in July of 2023, the band founder and President, Pipe Major Patrick Lynch, initiated and managed the design project. Band co-founder and Lead Drummer, Andrew Hoinacki, acted as principal designer. Band Quartermaster and professional artist, Emily MacArthur, consulted on aesthetic factors including colouration and threadcount.

name: Spirit of Edinburgh
restrictions: Yes. All interest must be submitted to Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the City of Edinburgh. Colours; blue was inspired by the Firth of Forth that so much of Edinburgh sits along and desert brown/gold was inspired by the sandstone that features throughout much of the City’s architecture. The design, which includes larger areas of colour mixed with busier areas with overchecks, is intended to represent the split between the old and new towns of Edinburgh.

name: Santa Fe Firefighters Pipes & Drums
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be only used with expressed written permission from the designer, Fred Hawkins, Local 2059 or the City of Santa Fe Fire Department - [email protected] Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The Santa Fe Firefighters Pipes and Drums tartan is intended to represent the unity of the City of Santa Fe, the fire department, and the Firefighters Union Local 2059, its members and the community it serves. The colours are based on the City’s seal and the design incorporates the department’s 144+ years of service to the community since 1880. Colours: red is intended to represent the fire service and the red clay on which the city of Santa Fe is built; black is intended to honour those who have given the ultimate sacrifice; yellow represents firefighters past and present and the diverse community they serve; blue represents compassion, caring and the professionalism of the medical, water and the clear blue skies of Santa Fe and white is intended to represent the honour and dedication of those who served within the ranks.

name: Bell Canada
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Bell Canada Enterprises, Inc. (BCE). Prior approval to weave/use/reproduce required from Bell Canada Enterprises, Inc. & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: Designed for Bell Canada Enterprises, Inc. Canada’s largest communications company. The company is named after their founder & Scottish born inventor of the telephone, Alexander Graham Bell. The tartan combines the brand colours of blue, black, white & grey and incorporates the company’s founding in April 1880 through 4 grey threads, 18 white threads, 80 black threads, and 188 blue threads within the tartan repeat.

name: Tarbat Discovery Centre
designer: Houstons and volunteers at Tarbat Discovery Centre
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be obtained from Tarbat Discovery Centre, Tarbatness Road, Portmahomack, Tain, Highland, IV20 1YA.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Tarbat Discovery Centre, a museum in Portmahomack, Scotland, on the grounds of the ancient church of St. Colman, which displays works of art created in stone by the Picts more than 1,200 years ago. The Centre displays Pict and Early Medieval tools, artefacts and moulds used in the 8th century to create religious masterpieces, such as chalices and reliquaries in gold, silver, enamel and glass. The colours were chosen are intended to represent the Tarbat Discovery Centre: black and white are for the building the museum is housed in - St Colman’s Church; green and blue represent the surrounding land and seascape and the sandstone colour represents the carved 8th-century Pictish stones that were found at the archaeological exhibition that resulted in the foundation of the museum.

name: McCulloch Rail Group
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the McCulloch Rail Group, their employees and permitted business associates. Copyright rests with the designer, Graeme Bone.
registrationNotes: A corporate tartan for the McCulloch Rail Group in Ayrshire, Scotland. The colour palette is based on the original company colours, with the addition of the group’s new company colours following their rebrand in 2023.

name: Rablogan Highland Heather
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with the express written permission of the designer, Rablogan Castle Limited or their heirs and descendants.
registrationNotes: The Rablogan Highland Heather tartan was designed for Rablogan Castle Limited as part of its fashion range so to portray through colour and density in a traditional Scottish cultural manner the visual image and grandeur of the flowering Heather shrub in the Scottish Highlands. The colours chosen are intended to reflect all of the natural colours of the blossom (purples and lavender) seen during the peak of the blooming season while also acknowledging the foliage (greens) and stems (barley). The deep red is intended to recognise those whose efforts, over the centuries, have contributed to the preservation of the Scottish Highlands and culture. This tartan is the central element to a range of products with the same name.

name: Bryson, D (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Dennis Bryson. Prior approval to weave/reproduce/print required by Dennis Bryson & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: Designed for Dennis Bryson taking colour inspiration from an historic crest of the Bryson family.

name: Brinton, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be a worn by any members of the Brinton family. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned on behalf of John ‘Jack’ Brinton as a wedding gift from Katherine Brinton (née Thomas). The colours of the tartan were inspired by John’s time spent living on the Moray Coast and his wife’s green eyes.

name: Capella Edina
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Capella Edina. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the launch of Edinburgh’s first symphony orchestra since 1937 in the city’s 900th anniversary year. Capella Edina’s mission is to make orchestral music more accessible, to bring people together and to share the joy of music with a special focus on contemporary music. The tartan takes inspiration from elements of the City of Edinburgh district tartan and uses shades from Capella Edina’s brand colour palette.

name: Rangers F.C.
restrictions: Yes. Permission must be obtained from Kilts 4 U to use/weave/reproduce this tartan. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Rangers Football Club using the official Club colours.

name: Catr Amins
designer: Epailly, C; Paul. K; Ollitrault, S & Gautier, V
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from the tartan owners.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the social group ‘Catr Amins’ in Saint Brieuc, France, which means ‘Four Friends’ in a popular language that used to be spoken in the area. The group was started by the four designers, who all love tartan and decided to create one for their group.

name: Kia America Inc
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with permission of Kia. Prepared for weaving by Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Kia America, Inc. to celebrate their annual recognition of their top Dealerships and in conjunction with their incentive travel award to London and Scotland. The design was based on Kia America, Inc.’s official brand colours and is intended to reflect their design philosophy ‘Movement that inspires’. This tartan was used as part of the celebration for the winners of the 2023 President’s Club, recognised in 2024.

name: Shalamov, Igor & Inna and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of Shalamov family. May only be woven with permission from the tartan owner.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Igor & Inna Shalamov, and their family, to celebrate their wedding anniversary using colours of personal significance.

name: Gleneagles Hotel Centenary
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of The Gleneagles Hotel. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be sought from The Gleneagles Hotel and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Gleneagles Hotel Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate 100 years of the Gleneagles hotel in 2024. The two broad blocks of cream, each comprising 50 threads, are intended to collectively symbolise 100 years of Gleneagles. The colour palette is intended to reflect a walk through the Perthshire hills and symbolise the natural beauty that surrounds the hotel. A significant part of Gleneagles' history is its role as a military hospital during the Second World War; to honour this past, khaki threads are woven into the tartan. Running through the heart of the tartan are lines that intended to represent the train tracks that historically brought visitors to Gleneagles and still reside in the hotel's basement today.

name: Storey, Alastair & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of immediate family & representatives. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be sought from A Storey, E Storey & H Storey, & Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Alastair Storey and his family to celebrate the couple's 47th year of marriage. The prominent dark blue (navy) check consists of 47 threads, symbolising the years of marriage. The outer green check and the pewter check mark the anniversary date. The couple's children are also represented in the design, with the secondary green check intended to symbolise their son, bordered by two double red checks to represent their four daughters.

name: Orzabal, R & Rath, E (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Roland Orzabal & Emily Rath. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be sought from Roland Orzabal, Emily Rath, and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with the designer, Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Roland Orzabal and Emily Rath as part of the celebration of their marriage. The colours in the design were inspired by their love of Colorado, the east coast, and the British countryside, from the blue mountains and red rocks, to green hills and rolling sea. Aspects of the design were inspired by the Menzies tartan as this was Roland’s mother’s surname, as well as the MacAulay tartan because of Emily's ancestry.

name: Curtis, Joshua & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Curtis family. Prior approval to weave/use/reproduce required from Joshua Curtis & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Joshua Curtis and his family. The colours and pattern selected are intended to represent their faith and their family. It was designed with the intention to pay homage to their heritage and their ancestral families from Scotland.

name: Curtis, Joshua & Family Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Curtis family. Prior approval to weave/use/reproduce required from Joshua Curtis & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the Curtis, Joshua & Family (Personal) tartan.

name: White, David Cameron & Susan - Anniversary Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from David Cameron White & Just Kilts. Prepared for weaving by House of Edgar.
registrationNotes: A hunting version of the White, David Cameron & Susan Anniversary tartan (SRT #13949), designed to celebrate their 40th wedding anniversary in 2024.

name: Yousaf, Humza (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries must be directed to Slanj Kilts or the Yousaf family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Humza Yousaf and his family to commemorate 60 years since Anwari and Muhammad Yousaf arrived in Scotland from Mian Channu, Pakistan. Since then, the family has grown considerably and on to their fourth generation of Yousafs in Scotland. The green in the tartan is intended to represent both the colours of the flag of Pakistan and the Islamic identity of the Yousaf family and blue is intended to pay homage to the Saltire of Scotland.

name: Lahaise, A, D, J & T (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for James Lahaise & family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lahaise family to celebrate their love for Scotland as their family home. The design was inspired by the Black Watch tartan in homage to their ancestor's service in the esteemed regiment. Contrasting highlights woven into the design are intended to be an expression of the Lahaise's other significant familial heritage.

name: Grant, Kieran, Dún Laoghaire (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Kieran Grant. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. May only be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Kieran Grant to celebrate his wedding. The design was inspired by elements of the Grant tartan. The colour palette is intended to reflect the marriage being a union of families from Scotland & Ireland by using tones of blue and green.

name: Rose and Thistle, The
restrictions: Yes. May only woven/used/reproduced with permission from Simon and Clare Cotton and their family. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Rose and Thistle tartan was designed by The House of Edgar to celebrate the 20th Wedding Anniversary of the owners Simon and Clare Cotton in 2024. The colours are intended to represent the red rose and purple thistles at their wedding day and the union of an English bride and Scottish groom. The design is based on the setts of the Campbell and Gordon clan tartans and incorporates two blue lines for their sons, James and Seth, with a multitude of coloured lines representing the many others who have been part of their life together. The numbers two and ten have been used within the design to recognise their wedding date of the 2nd of October.

name: Rablogan Secrets of the Firths
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with the express written permission of the designer, Rablogan Castle Limited or their heirs and descendants.
registrationNotes: The Rablogan Secrets of the Firths Tartan was designed for Rablogan Castle Limited as part of its fashion range. The design is intended to reflect the many secrets held in the depths of the Scottish firths as a result of maritime incidents over the centuries. The colours chosen are intended to depict: the depths through deep blue and black; brown for the ships that lay there; the lives lost in the waters; and the valuable cargoes of silver, gold, whisky and gemstones. This tartan is the central element to a range of products with the same name.

name: Rablogan Along Firth Shores
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven with the express written permission of the designer, Rablogan Castle Limited and their heirs and descendants
registrationNotes: The Rablogan Along Firth Shores tartan was for Rablogan Castle Limited as part of its fashion range. The design is intended to portray the visual image of the subtle beauty and solitary peace to be found at the beaches and along the shores of the Scottish firths. The colours are intended to reflect the natural elements experienced while one is strolling along the shores and taking in the elements: blue for the firth waters; beige for the shoreline sands and the driftwoods; greys for the shadows and green for the seagrasses. This tartan is the central element to a range of products with the same name.

name: Chest Heart & Stroke Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval to weave/use/reproduce this tartan is required from Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com & Chest Heart & Stroke Scotland.
registrationNotes: Designed for Chest Heart & Stroke Scotland, Scotland’s largest health charity working to support people with chest, heart and stroke conditions live life to the full. In 2024 one in five of people in Scotland live with chest, heart, stroke or Long Covid conditions, this is intended to be illustrated within the tartan design as a single pink stripe between four white stripes.

name: Alvarez, P & Arzola, E and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Patrick Alvarez & Esmeralda Arzola. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. May only be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created for P Alvarez & E Arzola in celebration of their 10th wedding anniversary in 2024. The design includes themes that are intended to represent their family, past & present, and colours of significance to their family. The threadcount includes numbers that reference the date of their wedding and the year their daughter was born.

name: Herlem, P & Fant, C and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and purchased by Charlotte Fant and Pierre Herlem, and their family & friends, unless advised otherwise with written confirmation. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Charlotte and Pierre by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of MacNaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff Kilt makers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the marriage of Charlotte Fant and Pierre Herlem. They were inspired to create their own tartan after their proposal on the Island of Islay in June 2024. Colours: the dark blue is intended to represent the water and the light blue is the sky in Islay; red and purple represent the favourite flower of each spouse and the white is for their beloved dog who is with them on every adventure.

name: Torrance-Shahid, M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by the Torrance-Shahid family and their children, and to their descendants and to whom they and their blood lines give permission. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with the Shahid Family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the dual cultural heritage of the family of Michaela Rowatt Shahid (née Torrance) and Mohammed Shahid. The ground colours are intended to reflect their marriage with blue and white from the Saltire and green and white from the Flag of Pakistan. Red is intended to celebrate the red sandstone of their family home in Glasgow where their four children grew up. Dark yellow was added to honour the colour in both of the family tartans of Michaela Rowatt Torrance - Forsyth (maternal) and Burns (paternal).

name: Bailey, Roy and Lacerda Aviles De Bailey, Carolina (Personal)

registrationNotes: The Grand National Curling Club (GNCC) tartan was produced in 2017 in commemoration of 150 years of curling in the United States. The GNCC was founded in 1867 and was the National Governing Body of curling in the United States until 1958. The GNCC is a Recognized Regional Association within the United States Curling Association. The tartan was inspired by the (Old/Red) Gordon tartan. Robert Gordon was elected the first patron of the GNCC from 1867–1884. Originally a Dumfries man, he became an influential figure in New York City as one of the incorporators of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, President of the Down Town Association, President of the St. Andrew’s Society, and a partner of the financial house of Maitland Phelps and Company. Colours: red for the Olympic Curling Trials known as the Roar of the Rocks; white for the bright ice; green for the Grand National organisation; dark blue for excellence in competition and blue is intended to represent life- long curling friendships.

Likewise, the outer green check, created from 10 threads, is a nod to the 10th month of the year, a popular birth month for the Konski family. The colours and threads are, together, intended to capture the essence of the Konski family’s home, their heritage, and the cherished moments that define their journey together.

name: Beaver Falls
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the history of Beaver Falls, located in British Columbia, Canada. Robert Affleck (1780-1838), a weaver, was born in Lanark, Scotland. In 1820 he, his wife, and family emigrated to Canada. This was one of the "Scottish Settlement embarkations in 1820 which enabled Scottish weavers suffering hardship though the collapse of the wool trade after Napoleonic War to begin a new life in Canada. Boyd Affleck (1882-1969) was Robert's grandson. After fighting in WW1, he searched the province for land with a water falls upon which he could build a power plant. He was able to purchase 220 acres which included the falls on Beaver Creek through the Soldier's Settlement Board. Boyd built the power plant at the falls which supplied the house and barn with the only power in the area. Melanie Vance (1955) bought the farm in 1991, and alongside her husband, is keeping up and expanding the farming tradition with large gardens, honeybees, weaving and a large workshop.

The tartan may be used by Rogue for future occasions and events.

registrationNotes: This tartan was specially commissioned to mark Alderman Alastair King DL's becoming the 696th Lord Mayor of London, honouring his Scottish heritage. The Lord Mayor of London holds the prestigious position as the mayor of the City of London, England, and serves as the leader of the City of London Corporation. Within the City, the Lord Mayor is granted precedence over all individuals save for the sovereign, and upholds various traditional powers, rights, and privileges, including the esteemed title and style of The Right Honourable Lord Mayor of London. This office stands as one of the oldest civic appointments in the United Kingdom. The tartan is intended to be featured in the attire of Mansion House staff during State Banquets and official gatherings and will also be used in crafting gifts for presentation by the Lord Mayor and Lady Mayoress.

name: Balmoral Glen Gelder
restrictions: Yes. At the discretion of His Majesty King Charles III, intended for domestic, ceremonial and commercial use by Balmoral Castle & Estate. May only be woven with written permission from Balmoral Castle & Estate or The Scottish Tartans Authority under instruction from the Royal Household. Design registered with the UK Intellectual Property Office 28th March 2025. IPO Design Registration No. 6434058.
registrationNotes: Glen Gelder sits at the heart of the Balmoral Estate, its lower slopes lying close to Balmoral Castle and its upper reaches providing spectacular views to the dark, north facing corries of Lochnagar. Since 1848, successive Royal generations have enjoyed the wild and majestic splendour of Glen Gelder and the surrounding mountains, rivers and forests of Upper Deeside. At the request of His Majesty The King, The Scottish Tartans Authority designed this tartan using the specific shades of the King Charles III tartan. These hues reflect the natural dyes of 18th century specimens so admired by His Majesty. The sett is based on a unique piece of rural Highland tartan discovered in Glen Affric and now in the collection of the Authority. Dating from c1500-1600 AD, this is the oldest surviving specimen of true tartan found in Scotland. The Balmoral Glen Gelder design provides a link to cloth that most likely originated in the reign of James V, Mary Queen of Scots or possibly James VI and I.

name: Cabot Highlands
designer: Campbell, Clare; Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/reproduced with explicit permission granted from Cabot Management Company Limited.
registrationNotes: To celebrate the 400 year anniversary of the building of Castle Stuart, Cabot Management Company Limited, the owners of the Castle Stuart Links created this tartan. The Castle which sits within the greens of the links was finished in 1625. The anniversary also coincides with the opening of the second course in 2025. The colours of the tartan all form part of their corporate colours, which have been inspired by the natural landscape that surrounds the links and Castle. This design includes 400 threads in navy, reflective of the deep coastal views of the Moray Firth that run alongside the links. The design also includes 16 grey threads next to 25 navy threads, for the year the Castle was built, the grey reflecting the castle’s stonework. 20 dark green threads when paired with the 25 navy threads represent the year the second green was completed, 2025. Two overchecks of gorse yellow, 9 threads in each, when combined represent the 18 holes. Finally the pivot has 2 light green threads, one for each of the courses.
