restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by any genealogical descendant of Samuel Drenning of Bedford County, Pennsylvania (1787), and their families.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Andrew Drenning and his family. The design was inspired by Drennan tartan (SRT #975), of which the Drenning surname is a variant. Andrew’s ancestors lived for generations in Bedford County, Pennsylvania. Samuel Drenning, was a landowner in and one of the founders of Bedford County in 1771, serving as an early local official before his death in 1787. Of Scottish descent, Samuel was part of the Scots Irish (Ulster Scots) diaspora from Ulster Province, Ireland, a common heritage among early settlers of Bedford. The colours in the tartan were inspired by the Ulster Province and County Antrim district tartans and are intended to reflect this family connection.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 80th birthday of Roy du Preez. Commissioned by his daughter Catherine, it is intended to pay tribute to his remarkable life. The sett is derived from the Cameron of Erracht tartan, and relates to his military service as a gunner in the Natal Field Artillery. The sett also incorporates deliberately significant threadcounts intended to represent; Roy’s birthday, his three daughters and his seven grandchildren. Colours: blue is intended to reflect Roy’s blue eyes; black is for his career in the global coal business; dark blue is for his cherished Ferrari; red and white overchecks are intended to symbolise his passion for English rugby; light blue refers to his youth by the Indian Ocean and finally, a thin thread of gold is intended to honour his commitment to his wife, Louise, and their enduring bond.

registrationNotes: Holt is a lively market town in North Norfolk, busy with; tourists, shoppers (many independent shops and galleries and few “chain stores”), holiday makers, and visitors admiring the Georgian architecture – stone and flint built (including an early fire station) to replace the medieval timber and thatch town almost totally destroyed by the great fire of 1708. One gallery owner proposed the adoption of this tartan (supported by the Town Council) as an emblem of Holt’s unusual and attractive culture. Colours: red is intended to represent the fire of 1708; brown the surrounding arable agricultural economy; green the pasture, woodlands, new growth; and, a fawn/beige for both the chalky soil and the tawny owls who have been adopted as the emblem of the Town Council.

registrationNotes: The Fan Fryske Grûn, which translates to From Frisian Ground, was created for the province of Frisia in the Netherlands. Colours: blue is intended to represent the waters, the lakes and the sea; green is for the wide green meadows; grey is for the wetlands (Wadden) and the farmlands in the north-east and the narrow black lines are intended to represent the roads and paths cutting through the landscape. These colours were combined with the colours of the Frisian flag including red which represents ‘It Frysk Bloed’, the anthem of the area, and yellow which is a reference to Leeuwarden, the capital of the province of Frisia.

name: Partnership 125
restrictions: Yes. Any commercial use will be at the sole discretion of The King’s Foundation. May only be woven with written permission from The Scottish Tartans Authority as nominated agent for The King’s Foundation. IPR Pending.
registrationNotes: The Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement was signed in 1899, launching official diplomatic relations between the State of Kuwait and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. In celebration of the 125th anniversary the Agreement, The King’s Foundation commissioned this tartan. The design is based on the proportions of some specimens of traditional weaving examined by The Scottish Tartans Authority at Sadu House in Kuwait. Within Bedouin culture, the possession of finely woven articles was traditionally seen as a symbol of tribal identity. The parallel with historic tartan is obvious. Colours and shades have been matched to those used in traditional Al Sadu weaving. The predominant colour, red, symbolises joy and prosperity while brown represents the bands of undyed camel hair often woven into Al Sadu cloth. The black and white interplay in Al Sadu weaving is called Aein (Eye) and this distinctive effect has been incorporated within the pattern.

name: Royal Environmental Health Institute of Scotland, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of The Royal Environmental Health Institute of Scotland only.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Royal Environmental Health Institute of Scotland, often referred to as REHIS, a registered Scottish Charity whose objectives are to promote the advancement of Environmental Health for the benefit of all sectors of the community through education, training and qualifications. REHIS was established following the merger of the Royal Sanitary Association of Scotland which was founded 1875 and the Scottish Institute of Environmental Health. REHIS created this tartan to celebrate 150 years in 2025. The colours within the tartan design are based on their crest and the threadcount is intended to reflect the date of 1875 and 150 years.

name: Bussemakerhuis
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Bussemakerhuis museum located in Borne, Twente in The Netherlands. Historically, Twente specialised in textile and Borne had a focus on linen. The house, where the museum is located, is the oldest (1779) linen house in the country. The museum focuses on linen, trading, the people that lived there and the Spanjaard family, who had a big influence on the region's textile industry. Colours: yellow and green represent the original colours of the house; white is intended to represent linen; red is for the Spanjaard family. This tartan was designed by Saxion University textile and fashion technology students Nicoletta Bardelli, Mai Boon and Nina Schilthuis for a commission of the Bussemakerhuis while being financed by founding Creatieve Broedplaats Enschede.

name: Kokoszka, J (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Józef Kokoszka’s 60th birthday, as well as the occasion of his daughter and son-in-law moving to Scotland. The design is intended to reflect the family’s new Scottish connections and celebrate their Polish heritage. It incorporates colours that hold personal significance to the family and are intended to recognise their passion for geography, nature and the environment: blue for the seas and oceans; dark yellow for stars and sunlight; light brown for earth and 60 dark grey threads to mark the 60 years of Józef's life.

name: Ocean Sciences 2026
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced by those authorised by the copyright holders. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders - AGU, 2000 Florida Avenue N.W, WASHINGTON, DC 20009, USA Design rights owned by AGU, 2000 Florida Avenue N.W., WASHINGTON, DC 20009, USA
registrationNotes: Marking the 2026 Ocean Sciences Meeting to be held in Glasgow, Scotland, this Thomson-based design includes the logo colours of the three partner societies of the Ocean Sciences Meeting – TOS, ASLO, and AGU. Colours: the darkest blue is intended to represent the deep ocean, lightening into the photic zone, ringed by the white surf that links all the oceans of the world; green is for the Earth and red for the Sun and the ecosystem. The Challenger Expedition, considered the first ever global ocean-going expedition, was launched from Portsmouth on 23 December 1872 and this date has been included in this design with a green band of 23 threads, adjacent blue of 12, the small dark blue of 18 and the broader adjacent blue of 72 threads. HMS Challenger’s 69,000 nautical mile voyage laid the foundations of oceanography and today’s ocean sciences community intends to honour the past while also proactively embracing and advocating for a more inclusive science future.

This tartan incorporates the colours of the three framework nations: Poland, Germany, and Denmark. This design also incorporates the palette normally associated with a traditional hunting tartans which is intended to reflect of MNCNEs role as a Regional Response Corps, and acknowledges its role as a land tactical warfighting Corps.

The river was given the name ‘rotten’ due to the iron in the ground giving it a red/brown hue and the tartan incorporates these colours to celebrate this connection.

name: A Thread in Time
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the direct descendants of Trisha L. and J. Christopher Marmo, along with their spouses (for as long as they are married); immediate family (siblings, nieces/nephews, aunts/uncles) or with special permission by Trisha L. Marmo and her heirs. Permission to weave must be sought from Trisha L Marmo & her heirs and Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the book ‘A Thread in Time’, written by Trisha Marmo, which captures the essence of love, Scottish heritage, and the shared threads of family woven across time. It was commissioned by the author and her husband to on the couple’s 30th wedding anniversary in 2024. The dark blue, composed of 30 threads, is intended to symbolise their three decades together since their wedding on April 24th, 1994 and the blue are grey checks, made of 24 threads, are to honour the 24th day. The couple’s five children are intended to be represented in the tartan in the red and white checks. The tartan’s was inspired by Trisha’s recently discovered Scottish heritage, rooted in the Skene and Forbes Clans.

name: Shepherd, H & Sayles, D and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. For the exclusive use of the Shepherd-Sayles Family, restricted to the families and descendants of both parents: Iain & Helen Shepherd and DuWayne & Aminah Sayles. Permission must be sought from Helen & DuWayne Sayles; or their children, Iain Sayles and Leila Rovito; and Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Shepherd-Sayles family and is intended to be a representation of the family's heritage, personal history, and values. The design was based on the Gordon tartan to connect to the family's Scottish ancestry. The colours are dominated by various shades of blue, intended to symbolise Helen's love of water and both families crossing oceans. The two purple checks within the design represent Helen's two children, while the dark charcoal checks, made up of 22 threads, symbolise the shared significance of the 22nd day of their respective birth months. The purple threads are also a nod to Helen's homeland, representing the heather clad hills. Green is intended to represent DuWayne’s African and Indian heritage and is a colour that holds personal significance for the family, honouring the resilience of their ancestors, who were brought to America through the transatlantic slave trade and worked on plantations, and reflecting their journey of conversion to Islam.

name: Mactaggart & Mickel Centenary
designer: Fowler, Claire, Glasgow School of Art.
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries must be addressed to the Mac Mic group.
registrationNotes: The Mactaggart & Mickel Centenary tartan was designed to celebrate of the rich history of Mactaggart & Mickel, known as the Mac Mic Group. As part of their centenary celebrations in 2025, the company collaborated with The Glasgow School of Art (GSA) on the Mac Mic Centenary Tartan Project, providing a unique live project opportunity for BA (Hons) Textile Design students. Students were tasked with creating tartan designs that reflect Mac Mic Group's deep-rooted values and themes such as cultural heritage, legacy, community, and 100 years of placemaking. Claire Fowler was the winning designer. Claire used the brand colour palette as a foundation and added extra colours intended to reflect the company's ethos and values. The digital version of this tartan has the weave printed in a distinctive chevron design.

On 12 February 2013, Detective Jeremiah MacKay was killed in the line of duty. The threadcount includes numbers of significance including: 58 to represent the Sheriff Departments in the State of California; 22 for the SBCSD County and City Stations; 18 for the SBCSD Divisions; 36, Jeremiah’s age (35 years old) when he died and 14/2 for Jeremiah’s SBCSD call sign (14D2).

The threadcount includes numbers that reference significant dates - 1988, the year that wildcats became legally protected and 2020, the start of the Saving Wildcats project. The shades used represent the colours of the Wildcat and the charity’s brand colours of orange and dark green.

name: George Watson's College
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for George Watson’s College in Edinburgh. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: The George Watson's College tartan celebrates the 50th anniversary of the coming together at Colinton Road, Edinburgh of George Watson’s Ladies College and George Watson's College. The design was inspired by elements of the Buchanan tartan as the Watsons were a sept of Clan Buchanan and it also references colours from the Lindsay tartan, which was introduced to the school uniform in the 1990s. The maroon, navy, green, gold and white reference key elements of the school including the uniform, school badge, pipe band colours and magnificent playing fields. The red overcheck is intended to represent the school’s motto ‘Ex Corde Caritas - Love from the Heart’. The threadcount includes the number 41 to represent 1741, the year George Watson’s Hospital opened, 50 to reference the 50th anniversary of the school becoming co-educational in 1974 and 8 to represent the 810 Watsonians who died in World Wars I & II.

The college was officially inaugurated on October 21st with the support of over 70 students, staff, community partners and government officials from more than 20 different countries. This tartan was designed to commemorate this prestigious recognition and mark the College’s 10th anniversary year as a merged college.

name: Carnegie Club at Skibo Castle, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of The Carnegie Club at Skibo Castle / Skibo Ltd. Permission to weave must be sought from The Carnegie Club at Skibo Castle / Skibo Ltd and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Skibo Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned to create a members' tartan for The Carnegie Club at Skibo Castle in celebration of the Club’s 30th anniversary. This design was inspired by the sett of the original Carnegie tartan, honouring the Club’s heritage. The palette is intended to reflect the surroundings of Skibo Castle set in woodlands close to the Dornoch Firth, intertwining the rich green-grey tones of verdant pine forests, the moody reds of winter heather moors, the deep blue of the sea and the soft blue grey of lichen, which thrives in this part of Scotland. The green checks are made up of 95 threads in total, symbolising the founding year of The Carnegie Club, 1995. The two outer checks each have 30 threads, celebrating the Club’s 30th anniversary, for which the tartan was created. This tartan is intended to encapsulate the essence of Skibo’s natural beauty and storied past.

name: Strathcona County
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by those authorised by Strathcona County. Cannot be offered for weaving or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of Strathcona County. Copyright of Strathcona County. Edmonton, Alberta.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Strathcona County, Alberta, Canada. The County is named after the Scottish-born Canadian businessman, one of the country’s foremost early builders and philanthropists, Lord Strathcona. This design was inspired by the Balmoral tartan as the Province was named for Queen Victoria’s daughter, Princess Louise Caroline Alberta. The green background is for Coronet, inspired by the word 'Strath', a Gaelic word referring to a broad valley. The brown and central green bands are woven with 18 & 76 threads respectively and celebrate the signing in 1876 of Treaty 6 between the Canadian Crown and various First Nations. Brown is for Amiskwaciy, the Beaver Hills, gathering place for Indigenous peoples including the Cree, the Blackfoot, the Nakota Sioux, the Métis and many other nations. Gold is for the prairie wheat. The green and blue central bands are from the Strathcona County logo and the red signifies the shared lives of all of who now form the vibrant Strathcona County community.

name: Statue of Liberty
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the express written permission of the designer, Jeffrey Renson.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the Statue of Liberty. Colours: light brown is intended to represent the Statue's original copper colour when presented to the United States; green and light green represent the result of a natural chemical process known as patination which transformed the Statue to its current colour; red, white and blue are for the flags of both the United States and France. The light brown has a thread count of 18 while the large light green area has a thread count of 86 to represent the Statue's dedication in 1886.

name: Witches of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. This design and all products created with it is for the exclusive use of The Witches of Scotland Limited. This tartan can be worn by anyone. This tartan can only be woven with permission granted by any officer of the Witches of Scotland Limited.
registrationNotes: This design was created to memorialise those who suffered as a result of The Witchcraft Act 1563 to 1736 in Scotland. This tartan will be woven to make products to help create a ‘living memorial’. The black & grey colours are intended to represent both the dark times of this period and ashes of those burned. It also incorporates red & pink colours, symbolic of the legal tapes used to bind papers both during that time and now. The threadcount of this design incorporates the years 1563 and 1736, represented as single entries, 1+5+6+3 = 15 and 1+7+3+6 = 17. These are shown in black and grey surrounding a white check of 3 threads, these threads represent the core objectives of the organisation, which are to ensure a pardon, an apology and memorials are achieved. The large black section of 173 threads is intended to represents the 173 years of darkness and red & pink sections are repeated 3 times, for the 3 prime objectives of the Witches of Scotland organisation.

Starting in 2018, the Hammond Historical Museum has sponsored a yearly Scottish Festival. The Town of Hammond, NY tartan has been designed to reflect the people, landscape and history of the area.

name: Town Of Searsport
registrationNotes: The town of Searsport, Maine was originally Founded by many families of Scottish and Irish descent. The seafaring is a tradition in the town, particularly deep sea captains and businesses to support such ventures. This design was inspired by analysis of tartans linked to the 15 founding families with such heritage, who had the most historic impact on the town in the context of maritime traditions. This tartan was designed by Amber and Victor Mazza, town citizens, and is intended to foster community identity and provide a unifying banner for all people who love Searsport to wear or have in their homes and businesses. It was approved by the town governing body and has been registered with their permission, with no restrictions.

name: Faithful Forgive Traitors
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions as to who can wear this tartan, the design has been created for use by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd only. May only be woven with explicit permission granted by Prickly Thistle Scotland Ltd.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Prickly Thistle inspired by the concept of allegiance, a concept and practice synonymous with Scottish past, present and potentially future. The colours chosen are intended to reflect the allegiance message Prickly Thistle wishes to share when this tartan is worn as clothing, how people over time can change direction. Gold tones have been used as a symbol of commitment and enduring values, while the green tones represent harmony and faithfulness in relationships. The sett of this design uses the number 8, 8 times, a number which is considered to be a symbol of fairness, and the symmetrical design is intended to reflect balance. This design also uses the number 80 three times, these 240 threads mark the 1785 anniversary of the first period of Highland Clearances, at 2025. The tartan was inspired by the concept of change, forgiveness and giving back.

name: Blakey-Thorns, Jonathan and Georgia – Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the wedding couple and their family. Copyright rests with Steven Patrick Sim, The Tartan Artisan, 8a Church Street, Arbroath, Angus, Scotland, DD11 1JL, [email protected].
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Jonathan and Georgia Blakey-Thorns on 13 February 2025, their family, and their legacy. Reflecting the family member’s birthstones - ruby, emerald, aquamarine, and pearl – the tartan is intended to honour their milestones and the strength of the couple’s union. The two white stripes are intended to mark the couple’s union, anchoring the family’s shared journey. The threadcount is intended to reflect their wedding date.

name: Weave of Love (Le Tissage de l’Amour)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2025. Weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. IP created and owned by Steven Patrick Sim, The Tartan Artisan.
registrationNotes: The tartan, Weave of Love - also known as Le Tissage de l’Amour - intends to embody passion, devotion, and eternity. Inspired by Celtic knotwork, its structure was designed to symbolise the unbreakable bond of love, interwoven with the spirit of the ancient Triquetra and Celtic Love Knot. The geometry is intended to represent two hearts: one of red and white, to embody passion and commitment; the other deep purple and navy, for quiet devotion and infinite depth. A bridge of purple threads unites them to symbolise two souls meeting, positioned to create balance between the two pivots. Rooted in Scottish heritage, its French name evokes romance, subtly nodding to the historic Auld Alliance. Whether worn to honour new love or as a quiet tribute to love that lasts, it is intended for all who seek a tartan for pure love.

name: Siham Dabbagh Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Restrictions of use for the Siham Dabbagh Commemorative tartan are limited to use by International Tartans and descendants of Siham Dabbagh only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in 2024 in honour of Siham Dabbagh, a pioneer for Palestinian women’s rights and the preservation of Palestine’s history and heritage. Siham moved to Kuwait in 1969, and joined the General Union of Palestinian Women in the 1970s, taking leadership of the Kuwait branch in 1986. Amid the 1991 Gulf War, she returned to Amman, where she led the Palestinian Culture Centre until her passing in 2019. Through her work, she supported hundreds of Palestinians, empowering women and children in Jordan’s Refugees camps through educational support, creative industries and most notably - traditional embroidery. The Siham Dabbah Commemorative tartan was commissioned by Siham’s Granddaughter.

name: Tribute to Belgian Air Force
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn by those given approval by the Belgian Air Force or the designer of the tartan. Prepared for weaving by Marton Mills Co Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a tribute to the Belgian Air Force by Kevin De Backer, bagpiper for the Belgian Air Force. The colours include the colours of the Belgian Flag, along with blue and white are intended to represent the sky and the uniforms of the Airforce.

name: Franklin, R A (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Franklin immediate family. Permission must be sought from Roy Franklin, Rosalyn Franklin, Alasdair Franklin, Katie Franklin and Araminta Campbell LTD. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a Christmas gift from Rosalyn to her husband Roy. It was inspired by the Baird tartan to honour Roy's Scottish heritage. The blues and greens are intended evoke the beauty of Loch Lomond, while magenta checks are to celebrate the family’s love of safaris, inspired by Botswana’s lilac-breasted roller. The red check represents the traditional red collars of the family’s cherished cocker spaniels. Important family dates are incorporated into the design: two green checks, each composed of 4 threads, signify Roy’s and their son Alasdair's birthdays, both falling on the 4th of their respective months; Rosalyn's birthday is honoured with a grey check featuring 18 threads, reflecting the 18th day of her birth month; the 5-section supporting check is bordered by two 8-thread blue checks, creating the 21 that represents daughter-in-law Katie’s birthday.

name: Boundary Layer Studio - Crìochan Ealain
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Boundary Layer Studio. Restricted availability, please contact Boundary Layer Studio or Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Boundary Layer Studio or Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Crìochan Ealain tartan was designed exclusively for Boundary Layer Studio to celebrate the company’s sense of heritage, continuity and tradition which it intends to carry forward into their future. The design was inspired by elements of the Ross Hunting tartan and uses the company’s brand colours.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Highland dance teacher and students of ROIS - Rome Irish and Scottish Dance School, established in 2017 in Rome, Italy, with the aim of promoting Scottish culture, traditions, music and dance in the Eternal City. The woven tartan is intended to be worn during Scottish events in Rome and even abroad, such as Highland dance competitions, ceilidh, tattoos, dance shows. The tartan would be also worn in every institutional event where ROIS Dance School must be represented. The colours of the tartan are the same as those of ROIS Dance School.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Scottish Country Dance teacher and students of ROIS - Rome Irish and Scottish Dance School, established in 2017 in Rome, Italy, with the aim of promoting Scottish culture, traditions, music and dance in the Eternal City. ROIS is a Royal Scottish Country Dance Society affiliated group. The woven tartan is intended be worn during Scottish events in Rome and even abroad, such as ceilidh, dancing weekends and official RSCDS dance camps and events. The tartan would be also worn in every institutional event where ROIS Dance School must be represented. The colours of the tartan are the same as those of ROIS Dance School.

name: Keatch, C & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by members of the Keatch family to celebrate their connection and deep rooted links to Scotland and its culture. The colours were selected by various family members.

name: Parklands Colours of Care
restrictions: Yes. Ownership of this tartan was transferred on 4 March 2025 to Parklands Care Homes, Rosehall, The Square, Grantown-on-Spey PH26 3HG. For information regarding use of this tartan please contact Donald Morrison, Parklands Group. IPO Design Number: 6424665, Grant date: 25 February 2025.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the colours of the uniforms worn by care workers and was designed to form part of the Highland Hospice HeArt trail. A representation of the tartan was painted onto the back of a large heart, edged by roses, painted by 40 of residents of the Eileen Dubh Care Home, located in Fortress, Black Isle, Highlands. The base of the heart was made of hand prints, in the colours of the tartan, with each hand print made by a care home worker who wears one of the colours in the tartan: green for domestic staff; pale blue for carers; dark blue for nursing staff; deep purple for team leaders; pink for activities coordinators. In 2025 this tartan was adopted by Parklands Care Homes to be used in their staff uniforms.

name: Singapore St Andrew's Society
registrationNotes: In 2009, the Singapore St Andrew’s Society commissioned its own tartan to mark its 175th anniversary. The colours chosen for the Society tartan are intended to reflect the Society’s history. In 1835 the first St Andrew’s Day Dinner was held in Singapore and was presided over by William Napier and Dr Montgomery. The following year, William Napier was elected Chairman and this historic design is based on the 1880 version of the Napier tartan. The central motif of five white lines on red is intended to symbolise the Singaporean flag with its five white stars. Flanking that centre piece is green and light blue for the jungle and seas that surround the island. The Society’s identity is forged by the white line on blue to symbolise the St Andrew’s Cross – the flag of Scotland.

name: Robert Gordon University
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from Robert Gordon University. IPR Pending.
registrationNotes: Bearing the name of Aberdeen merchant and philanthropist Robert Gordon (1668-1731), Robert Gordon University (RGU) traces its educational roots to the late 18th century and was awarded university status in 1992. The RGU tartan is inspired by the Gordon tartan which dates to 1793 and was commissioned as a variation of the Government tartan (Black Watch) by the 4th Duke of Gordon who raised The Gordon Highlanders in 1794. The three yellow stripes represent the three golden boars of Clan Gordon, incorporated within the RGU Coat of Arms. The red line and grey guards represent the castle on a red background from the RGU and City of Aberdeen Coat of Arms. Blue and green are the predominant colours of the Gordon tartan and these hues have additional significance; blue represents the North Sea and the River Dee on whose banks the RGU Garthdee Campus is situated; green reflects the open spaces of the campus and the environmentally sustainable practices championed by the University.

name: Rickard, JoAnna & Barois, Rémy – Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of JoAnna Rickard and Rémy Barois. Permission to weave must be sought from JoAnna Rickard, Rémy Barois & Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: For this tartan, JoAnna and Rémy were inspired by the natural beauty of their island home, located on Snuneymuxw territory. Araminta Campbell was commissioned to design the tartan, a gift from JoAnna's mother, for their wedding. The colour palette blends greens of the woodlands with blues of the seas, intended to symbolise the union of land and water. Drawing from the MacMillan tartan, the design honours their family’s Scottish connections while embracing an asymmetric design that is intended to mirror the wild, untamed essence of nature. The soft grey check reflects the unique sandstone formations of their island. Their wedding date is interwoven into the fabric, with 9 threads forming the grey check, 6 threads forming the bolt of yellow, and 25 threads forming a smaller blue block that sits to the left of the yellow, capturing their special day in the pattern.

name: Tauck, Inc
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Tauck, Inc. Permission to weave must be sought from Tauck, Inc. & Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with Tauck, Inc.
registrationNotes: This tartan for Tauck, an American family-owned travel company, was designed to reflect the brand’s identity and heritage. The tartan’s dark green base, matched to Tauck’s signature brand colour, is comprised of 100 threads symbolizing the company’s centennial, marking 100 years since its founding in 1925, while also representing a decade of Tauck’s growth and evolution. The design incorporates a blend of colours inspired by nature: dark green and ivory representing the land, and blues and greys evoking the serenity of water, while the yellow threads reflect on Tauck’s history along the Yellow Roads of Europe.

name: Weber-Macher, J & M (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan to celebrate the wedding of Johannes Weber and Michaela Macher. The colours are of personal significance to the couple.

name: García Barrios, C & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the García Barrios family to unite them and celebrate their bond. Colours: blue and green are intended to represent the sea and mountains loved by the family; the three white lines are for the three children with black surrounding for their home and parents; red is for the family’s home country, Spain and yellow represents their Brazilian connection.

registrationNotes: The Celtic Brooch series, by Katherine Lowry Logan, is a time-travel romance book series. The series follows members of the MacKlenna clan as they travel through time using a Celtic brooch. The tartan was inspired by the stones found in the brooches written about in the series.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Brooke & Ryan Smyth using colours of personal significance intended to represent different aspects of each other and their coming together and to form a new family.

name: Sandbag Veterans, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Veterans, Veterans’ groups/societies & Veteran-based charities.
registrationNotes: The Sandbag Veterans' tartan was designed by Sandbag, The Veterans' Society, Singapore. Sandbag is a multi-national veteran's society established to offer veterans, ex-emergency services and police personnel a place to connect. Colours: purple is intended to represent a blend of navy blue for maritime forces, red for ground forces, and sky blue for the air forces; green represents the terrain; light blue represents the skies; dark blue represents the seas and oceans, that have all been fought upon and under; red is intended to remember those lost and white is intended to represent the elusive and everlasting search for peace.

name: Selkirk (2025)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent the Royal Burgh of Selkirk, and registered by the Selkirk & District Community Council. The colours chosen represent the colours of the Royal Burgh: Scarlet and Royal Blue, as well as other shades of blue, intended to reflect the local hills and mists.

name: Central Michigan University
restrictions: Yes. Written permission for weaving and reproduction must be authorised by Central Michigan University. Prepared for weaving by Red Label Kilts Inc. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: Central Michigan University was founded on May 24, 1892. It was created as a “Normal College” to advance education in the Mount Pleasant, Michigan community. In 1895, Central became a public institution by an act of the Michigan Legislature. It was assigned the responsibility of educating rural school teachers. It became a university in 1959. In response to the need for doctors to practice in rural areas, the medical school opened in 2010. The student body voted to make maroon and gold the official school colors in 1924. The Central “Chippewas” name was introduced in 1941. “Fire Up Chips” was used for the first time during the 1967 Homecoming. Even though so much has changed over the last two centuries, their values do not stray from those inscribed upon their seal in 1892: Sapientia, Virtus, Amicitia — wisdom, virtue and friendship.

name: Cabot Cape Breton
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions with regards to who can wear this tartan, however is can only be used as a design by Cabot Management Company Limited in any forms with their instruction and permission. May only be woven with explicit permission granted from Cabot Management Company Limited.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate its Scottish connections with its sister golf resort Cabot Highlands. Both resorts are nestled between the coast and nearby communities, both called Inverness. This design was inspired by colours intended to reflect the resort’s location and its historical link to the many Highlanders who left Scotland during the 1800's by boat. The 18 sand coloured threads mark the 1800's, a time when over 50,000 people settled in Cape Breton during the Highland Clearances. The 46 dark green threads represent the 46 holes found at the resort, followed by 18 lighter green for the 18 holes in a game of golf. Next is 2 navy, 4 brown and 75 navy threads, marking the 2475 nautical miles between both golf resorts. The final brown and cream section is an arrangement of 2 and 4 threads repeated to signify the 2 large masts and 4 rigs that featured on The Amity, which sailed from Tobermory to Cape Breton.

name: Zimucha, S & Dzinoruma, A, Zimbabwe (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by anyone who loves Zimbabwe and Scotland. Prior Permission to weave or reproduce this tartan is required from Philip Jones & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Stuart Zimucha and Abigail Dzinoruma, inspired by the Jones Killernie tartan (SRT #13490). The design includes the colours of the national flag of Zimbabwe and is intended to celebrate their love of Zimbabwe and Scotland.

name: Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay
restrictions: Yes. This tartan can only be woven at the express direction from representatives of The Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, including their parent company at Marriott International, and ownership group at Strategic Hotels & Resorts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, California, which overlooks the Pacific Ocean and Scottish-inspired golf links. Honouring their heritage, this tartan incorporates colours intended to reflect the coast and picturesque setting: blue of the Pacific Ocean; light green for the golf links and the rich hues of the surrounding redwood trees. The design is intended to represent strength, serenity, and community, including their nightly ritual of a Bagpiper serenade on the rugged bluff of the Pacific Ocean.

name: Mukhtar, Mohammed & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Mukhtar family. It incorporates red, reflecting the traditional tartans of Fife, where the family’s Scottish journey began, alongside green and white from the Pakistani flag, symbolising the nation’s diverse religious communities. The thread-count includes the graduation year of the tartan’s first wearer, marking a proud milestone of achievement and social integration in Scotland.

name: McAdam, John & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may not be woven/used/reproduced without permission from the designer or designated agent
registrationNotes: A tartan for John McAdam and his family. The design incorporates elements from Clan tartans connected to the family.

name: Think Purple (2025)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by prior arrangement with Joan O'Connor and Think Purple Ltd. Weaving by prior arrangement with Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Think Purple’s 20th anniversary along with the 60th birthday of Joan O'Connor, the Founder and Managing Director of Think Purple Ltd. The shades of purple are intended to reflect the cornerstone attributes of wisdom, imagination, and creativity; all integral to Think Purple's approach to professional coaching. The design is also intended to reflect Joan's strong connection to the country of her birth and her heritage - notably, her paternal connection to Keith, her Glasgow childhood and family links to clan Lamont. Both the Keith District and Spirit of Glasgow tartans have influenced the sett, plus the white overcheck references the Lamont tartan.

name: Fair, James Alexander & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by anyone with their surname or a member of their family. Weaving arranged by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of Alec Fair & Paula Kaptelli. The colours are intended to reflect the couple’s heritage, and the union of their new family. The sett was inspired by the University of Edinburgh tartan, where the couple both studied and met. Colours: green is intended to represent Alec’s Irish roots, with a dark shade of green as the base and a lighter shade representing the lush green of the Emerald Isle and the shirts of the Irish Rugby team; red and black reference Paula’s proud Albanian heritage and the Albanian flag; red and white relate to the Welsh flag, referencing Alec’s mother’s Welsh heritage, and the white checks simultaneously signify the white of wedding flowers and the maroon check represents the Church of Ireland Vestments worn by Alec's paternal Grandfather.

name: Allied Forces Foundation
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor. Use of this tartan design to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Ltd. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 13 February 2026, registration number: 6507016.
registrationNotes: The Allied Forces Foundation tartan celebrates the Allied Forces Foundation (AFF), established to unite wounded, ill, and injured service personnel and veterans from the US, UK, and allied nations’ forces in wellness and healing. AFF is predominantly an American and British charity for veterans, caregivers, and families together for community activities. ‘Side by Side’ is their motto because it exemplifies their approach to recovery. Those who have fought together reunite, share experiences, and offer support to one another. This design features the following colours: red, white and blue representing the Union Flag of the UK and the National Flag of the USA from the AFF logo; shades of green and brown are intended to symbolise the all-important camouflage of armed forces uniforms and equipment and black represents continual respect for all fallen comrades.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Wedding of Josh Sault and Millie Worley. It was inspired by a combination of other family tartans to celebrate the joining of families. It is intended to celebrate the couple’s connection with the country where they were engaged and married.

The design was inspired by elements of different district tartans which reference their ports’ locations. The tartan uses the Company’s brand colour palette and the threadcount includes numbers representing significant dates in the Company’s history.

name: BATSU Moon
registrationNotes: A tartan for BATSU!, a comedy improv show which started in New York City in 2011, has regular shows there and in Chicago, and has performed all over the world. Since 2021 they have been a featured act at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. This tartan was designed to represent the performers' love for the traditions and culture of Scotland and the people of Scotland, who have shown them great hospitality.

name: Proudfoot, H & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Hailey Proudfoot, descendants of Leslie and Elizabeth Proudfoot (in current and all future generations), and anyone else expressly authorized by Hailey Proudfoot. The designer must be consulted before it is woven.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Hailey Proudfoot and her family. The colours are intended to represent the Proudfoot family’s journey from their Scottish roots: light blue is for the Scottish flag; green is for the Irish and Welsh flags; dark blue is for the American flag; red for is for the Canadian flag and white, a colour featured in all of those flags, is intended to represent the family’s heritage across all of these countries.

name: Victory - The American Revolution Museum
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven by written permission of the designer Robert Paterson. Cannot be replicated without written permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: The Victory tartan was designed for the American Revolution at Yorktown. The design was inspired by the uniforms of the continental Army, and the Trumbull flag as depicted in the painting "Surrender at Yorktown" by American artist and one-time Washington aide-de-camp, John Turnball.

name: Susan Constant - Jamestown Settlement
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from the designer. Cannot be replicated without written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: Designed for the Jamestown-Yorktown Foundation, this tartan was inspired by the colourful detailing on the hull of the Susan Constant, the largest of the three re-created ships at Jamestown Settlement.

name: Army & Navy Academy
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from the designer. Cannot be replicated without written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Army and Navy Academy, in Carlsbad, California, which has a rich history that dates back to its founding in 1910. The academy was established by Captain Thomas A. Davis, a Spanish-American War veteran. Captain Davis imagined a school that combined military discipline with a strong academic foundation. The Army and Navy Academy continues to uphold its mission of educating and developing young men to become leaders in their communities and beyond. The academy's story is one of resilience, adaptability, and a dedication to shaping the character and future of its students.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Stuart Braidwood and his family. Colours: black is intended to represent the strength and resilience of their family; red and white are for their new Canadian family roots; green and gold are for their South African origins and the family members still there and dark blue is intended to symbolise the oceans between them.

name: Hilliard, Brandon & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by Brandon Hilliard, his immediate family, and their future immediate families/descendants. May not be woven/reproduced without permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Brandon Hilliard and his family using colours of personal significance intended to represent; his wife’s Scottish heritage, colours from their wedding in 2019 and Brandon's time in service to the United States Army during 2007-2012.

name: Johnson, N & D and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for exclusive use of the Johnson family or those they have gifted it to.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the Johnson family to celebrate their 15-year anniversary. The tartan uses colours of personal significance and is intended to be a testament to their enduring bond, to honour their past and their commitment to stand together for life.

name: Tremblay, J Stephan and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Tremblay family. It should not be used for commercial or governmental purposes without the written permission of the designer. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron. Other companies may weave the tartan upon receiving written permission from the Tremblay of Bellegarde. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Stephan J Tremblay and his family to celebrate their family history and Scottish connections. The Tremblay’s originated from the region of Le Perche, southwest of France. The descendants of this family established roots in Quebec, Canada in 1627. Capt (ret.) J. Stephan Tremblay CD joined and served as a commissioned officer in two Highlanders Regiments of His Majesty’s Canadian Army: the 48th Highlanders of Canada (Davidson tartan) and the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders of Canada (Black Watch tartan). Capt Tremblay married Carol Ann Badger, a descendant of the Kerr family from the United States, and the family settled in a traditionally Scottish area of Ontario, the Grey Highlands of Grey County.

name: Thomas Jefferson 1776
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/reproduced with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: Thomas Jefferson is considered the primary author of the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson submitted his ‘rough draft’ on June 28, 1776 and pressured by the news of a fleet of British Troops lay off the coast of New York adopted the Lee resolution of Independence on July 2nd 1776, and adapted the Declaration of Independence explaining its action on July 4, 1776. This document declared the thirteen American Colonies independence from Great Britain. The threadcount includes reference to these significant dates with within the design - 07-04-17-76-13 - intended to recognise the Declaration of Independence.

registrationNotes: The Radical Weavers were Andrew Hardie, James Wilson and John Baird. In 1820 they led an uprising seeking universal suffrage for the people of Scotland. Baird and Hardie were subsequently executed for high treason in Stirling. The work carried out by the Radical Weavers charity is inspired by the 1820 group, and this tartan was designed in recognition of their contribution to Scottish history.

The bright red squares have 20 threads and the dark red have 15, marking the year of their marriage. The two narrow black lines on the green are for their children. The white line on blue represents St. Andrew, the patron saint of several countries including Russia and Scotland and together, all the colours embrace those of the flags of their home countries - Italy, Antigua and Russia.

registrationNotes: The Maggie’s Home tartan was designed especially for Maggie’s. The design weaves together the vibrant colours of the cancer ribbons: rich purples for pancreatic, thyroid, and testicular cancers; soft whites for lung and brain cancers; subtle greys for brain tumour awareness; and lavender for all cancers and survivors. To honour breast cancer awareness, a warm pink is also incorporated. This tartan is intended to reflect Maggie’s Scottish heritage and be a symbol of support for all those affected by cancer, reflecting the power of community, resilience, and love.

name: Spirit of Utah
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by the Utah Pipe Band to celebrate the landscapes, pioneer heritage, and adventurous spirit of Utah, United States. The colours and their corresponding meanings were inspired by the flag of Utah: white for the snowcapped mountains found along the area's tribal nations; red for the red-rock canyons in the south; dark blue for the skies and lakes; and yellow for the bee skep or ‘beehive’, a widely known symbol of Utah. Light blue is intended to represent the state's Scottish ancestry.This tartan was designed by the Utah Pipe Band to celebrate the landscapes, pioneer heritage, and adventurous spirit of Utah, United States. The colours and their corresponding meanings were inspired by the flag of Utah: white for the snowcapped mountains found along the area's tribal nations; red for the red-rock canyons in the south; dark blue for the skies and lakes; and yellow for the bee skep or ‘beehive’, a widely known symbol of Utah. name: Semple, R J K (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to honour the late WWII veteran Robert Semple OAM BEM (Hawthorn), a dedicated member of the Hawthorn Pipe Band. Initially joining as a bagpiper, he later became the Drum Major, a role he proudly held until his passing in 2020. This tartan commemorates his remarkable 74 years of service and unwavering commitment to the band.

name: Surrey Police Service
registrationNotes: The Surrey Police Service (SPS) tartan was created to commemorate SPS attaining Police of Jurisdiction (POJ) status in Surrey, British Columbia, Canada, on November 29 2024, and to foster a sense of pride, tradition and unity within the Service. It is intended to symbolise the Service’s shared values, dedication to public safety and the strong bonds that connect both Constabulary and Civilian Members. Designed to complement the SPS dress uniform, the SPS Pipes & Drums wear the SPS tartan, representing the Service in ceremonial and community engagements.

name: Camanachd Association
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn when authorised by the Camanachd Association. Cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the Camanachd Association. Copyright rests with Camanachd Association.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Camanachd Association, the world governing body for the Scottish sport of shinty. The colours include the gold and black from the Camanachd Association logo, green for the grass pitch, white for the line markings and the goal posts and red to remember the shinty players who gave their lives in the two World Wars. The gold bands of 18 threads and the large green block of 93 threads, commemorate the founding of the Association in 1893. The small white rectangle represents the scaled down goalposts of 10ft by 12ft and the black bands alternate between 10 and 12 threads signifying the number of players in a women’s team and a men’s team. This graphic shows the warp only and not the weft variation.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Nolen Boe and his family to celebrate their heritage from Scotland and Norway. This design was inspired by the textures and colours of the Moray Firth coastline in the Scottish Highlands and the stone surrounding the course; a base of grey, black and charcoal, highlighted with gold sand.

name: Torridon, The

registrationNotes: This design was inspired by the history of the house and land that surround The Torridon, Wester Ross. The first Earl of Lovelace built The Torridon in 1887. The dark green and dark blue are based on the ceilings within the hall and dining room, which are incredibly intricate with the zodiac signs and the night star constellations. The dark red is intended to represent the red brick sandstone of the house and the red berries that grow on the Rowan tree which is seen on the rocks in the mountains above the house. The green also links the sea and mountains that surround The Torridon including the green of the needles from the old Scott pines trees and the seaweed found in the dark blue waters at the foot of the house.

name: Emperor Penguin

registrationNotes: Inspired by the majestic emperor penguin, this design is intended to reflect the contrast of its black and white plumage, accented by the yellow and golden-orange hues that grace its neck. The silvery-grey was inspired by the down of penguin chicks, which blends seamlessly into the icy Antarctic landscape, along with white to evoke the vast snowfields and frozen seas that is their home. A soft, glacial blue represents the ancient ice that shapes their world and the pristine beauty of their frozen habitat.

Colours: purple holds personal significance as the theme colour for Daniel and Samantha’s wedding, as it was at Daniel’s father’s wedding, where Daniel first wore a kilt; green is intended to represent Ireland and honours Daniel’s father Stephen, who wore the green beret of the Royal Marines; black is intended symbolises Ireland’s historical struggles and those faced by the Kilgallon family and white is intended to reflect Yorkshire and new beginnings.

name: Prof. N K Rutter Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/reproduce this tartan must be obtained from Prof. Rutter's next of kin. Email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the life of Emeritus Professor Keith Rutter, an eminent historian and numismatist of Ancient Greece and the Mediterranean. The design attempts to reflect Keith's varied passions and interests, incorporating different aspects of his life that were important to him. Colours: dark blue represents seas and oceans crossed on his many travels, and his love of the colour; black and white lines evoke piano keys and his enjoyment of music; 'Gold', 'Silver' and 'Bronze' lines commemorate his numismatic expertise and graded White lines evoke ancient columns, seen in many classical sites around the Mediterranean. While no design could ever encapsulate the totality of someone who lived such an extraordinary life, the family hoped that this tartan would be a fitting tribute to someone who is fondly remembered and loved as a scholar, friend, husband and father.

name: George Washington’s Mansion
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven or replicated with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the history of George Washington’s Mansion at Mount Vernon which started as a modest house built in 1734 by Augustine Washington. George Washington’s elder half-brother, Lawrence, lived there from 1741 until 1752. George leased the property in 1754 and inherited it in 1761. He raised the roof to make it two and a half stories high in the late 1750s. By 1774, he added the north and south wings, the cupola, and the piazza. The nearly 11,000-square-foot Mansion dwarfed most late 18th-century Virginia homes. The two-story porch facing the Potomac, designed by Washington, became an iconic image. This grand façade, rare then, became widely copied in America.

name: Morris, R & Family (Personal)

name: Fergus Scottish Festival

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Fergus Scottish Festival and Highland Games, Ontario, Canada, which has enjoyed tremendous success since its inception by Alex Robertson in 1946. The Games have had two locations over its history, Victoria Park and more recently, the Centre Wellington Community Sportsplex (Fergus). The Games exemplify all things Scottish with a focus on heavy events, dancing, piping, clans and heritage. The design includes the founding date of the Fergus Scottish Festival & Highland Games, August 17th 1946, within the threadcount.

name: Niagara Falls Gifts
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Niagara Falls Gifts inspired by the impressive sight of Niagara Falls, witnessed by over twelve million people per year. Formed at the end of the last glacial period, water from the Great Lakes carved a path through Niagara to the Atlantic Ocean and led to the formation of three waterfalls at the southern end of the Niagara Gorge. The largest of these waterfalls is Horseshoe Falls, sometimes referred to as ‘the Canadian Falls’, which sits on the international border between Canada and the United States of America. The two smaller waterfalls, respectively known as the American Falls and Bridal Veil Falls, face Canada from across the border. Collectively, the hydroelectric energy generated by the waterfalls provides most of the electricity for Ontario and the State of New York

name: Scheuermann Vineyard and Winery

registrationNotes: A tartan for Scheuermann Vineyard and Winery, Ontario, Canada. Open since 2011 their mission has been to work in harmony with their surroundings, using the highest standards and sustainable practices in the vineyard and in the cellar. This tartan was created to celebrate this family run business.

name: Henwood, Ellen S (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 70th birthday of Ellen S Henwood, her Scottish heritage, love of tartan, and community involvement. Colours: three stripes of blue represent the trefoil of Girl Guides; black is for Ellen’s coal-mining hometown of Springhill; dark blue is intended to represent her childhood growing up in ‘La Belle Province’, Quebec; green for her love of adventures and the outdoors; and purple for the amethyst found on the shores of Nova Scotia. Within the design are the numbers 19, 55 for her birth year and 20, 25 for her 70th birthday.

name: Poet’s Rose (My Love is Like a Red, Red Rose)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2025. Weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. IP created and owned by Steven Patrick Sim, The Tartan Artisan. IPR Pending.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the romantic legacy of Robert Burns and his iconic poem, 'A Red, Red Rose', first published in 1794. Closely echoing the sett geometry of the registered tartan ‘Weave of Love (Le Tissage de l’Amour)’ (SRT #14663), it continues the same Celtic knot-inspired structure, originally shaped by the Triquetra and Celtic love knot to symbolise unity, eternity, and emotional depth. In this design, the sett is altered to evoke a red rose in bloom. The pattern intends to portray a fusion of bright scarlet and faded burnt orange threads representing layered petals, while an arrangement of green and yellow suggests leaves and enduring devotion. Inspired by one of Scotland’s most cherished love poems, this tartan is intended to honour romantic love, cherished remembrance, and a poetic soul.

name: Black Heart (Shadow & Light)
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is designed and owned by Steven Patrick Sim - The Tartan Artisan ® - Copyright © 2025. Weaving, tailoring, and commercial use is managed by the designer. Contact Steve regarding use at: [email protected], or use the email below. IP created and owned by Steven Patrick Sim, The Tartan Artisan. IPR Pending.
registrationNotes: This tartan - Black Heart (Shadow & Light) - being the second in a series of four designs, was developed from the tartan Weave of Love (SRT Ref: 14663), using the original threadcount while changing the palette to represent different emotions. The tartan is intended to honour the role of memory, grief, and resilience, and its colours—black, grey, and violet—are intended to represent sorrow, balance, and reflection. This design, whilst preserving the four-stripe violet motif central to the Weave of Love, also completes one half of a conceptual pairing, balanced by the tartan White Heart (Light & Shadow) - (SRT) Ref: 14760.

The tartan is intended to mark personal milestones and honour cherished memories, and its colours - purple, white, and silvery grey tones - are intended to symbolise grace, light and reflection. This design, whilst preserving the four-stripe purple motif central to the Weave of Love, also completes one half of a conceptual pairing, balanced by the tartan Black Heart (Shadow & Light)—SRT Ref: 14759.

name: Davis, A & J, The Pastures of Craigellachie (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of A & J Davis in Braemar, the family home in the Scottish Highlands, their long service in the Royal Air Force at bases across the North East of Scotland and their love of the mountains.

name: Anne of Green Gables
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven or replicated with written permission from the designer. This tartan is licensed by the Anne of Green Gables Licensing Authority Inc.
registrationNotes: Anne of Green Gables is the first in a series of novels written by Canadian author, Lucy Maud Montgomery. The initial novel of the series, first published in 1908, follows Anne Shirley, a spirited, opinionated red-haired orphan, from her arrival in Avonlea, when she came to be in the care of Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, throughout her life until she became a school teacher. Lucy Maud Montgomery's works explored themes of belonging, community, and family values - themes which continue to be relevant. Green Gables has itself become an iconic historic site, drawing fans from around the world. Honouring the original oil painting ‘Beyond Summer Fields’ by Ben Stahl, the Anne of Green Gables tartan design and palette is intended to reflect the imagery that captures the essence of Anne, in her home at Avonlea, on Prince Edward Island.

name: Anne of Green Gables Farm House
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven or replicated with written permission from the designer. This tartan is licensed by the Anne of Green Gables Licensing Authority Inc.
registrationNotes: The Anne of Green Gables Museum refers to the Green Gables Farm House, a historical site located in in Cavendish, Prince Edward Island, Canada. This farm house and its surroundings inspired Lucy Maud Montgomery when she wrote Anne of Green Gables. It has been preserved and restored to resemble the beloved farm house described in the Anne Green Gables Book Series. The colour scheme of the Green Gables has been reflected in this tartan, designed to commemorate this historic property.

The colour palette was carefully chosen to reflect the values and landscapes associated with the family's Scottish roots: green is intended to represent the natural landscapes of Scotland; brown and red are intended to symbolise resilience, strength, and a sense of purpose; brown and putty are for tradition, humility, and a strong work ethic; light brown is for peace, community, and hope for the future and the red lines are intended to honour the sacrifices made by the family members who served in the military and those who have dedicated themselves to family and community.

name: Commando Heritage No.1
designer: Barnwell, Barry with Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. The Commando Heritage No.1 tartan may be worn by any person having completed the UK or Allied Nations Commando or Special Forces training and/or are members of military units that are descendants of WW2 commando training in Scotland. It may also be worn by close family members of the above authorised military personnel. Additionally, the tartan maybe worn by supporters of the Trust with written permission. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the International Commando Heritage Trust. In 1942, Commando Basic Training Centre was established at Achnacarry, home of Cameron of Lochiel. By 1946, 26,000 British and Allied Nations commandos had been trained at Achnacarry. The sett was based on the tartan worn by the Cameron Highlanders, with yellow and scarlet retained to reflect the Clan Cameron colours. Colours: green reflects the Commando’s coveted green beret as worn by qualified members of the UK Commando Forces; red on navy blue are the traditional colours of combined operations and represent the Army & Royal Navy; light blue represents the Royal Air Force; red is also intended to be reminder of the blood spilled by generations of commandos and black is for respect for those who made the ultimate sacrifice. The yellow, representing old gold, is to recognise the valuable service of such specialist units, reflect the everlasting quality of the training and the indomitable spirit of the Commandos.

name: Broadhurst
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the history of Broadhurst, a 1920 mansion in the Tudor style, located in Pennsylvania, United States. Created by the owners, the Broaddus family, the colours are intended to pay homage to their home and family; green was inspired by the grand living room; red is for the dining hall; blue is for clear blue skies, the seas, and chinoiserie; blue and light grey are intended to evoke imagery of the St Andrew’s Cross.

name: Suttie, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries should be directed to the family or Slanj kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for John Suttie, his wife June (née Pennykid) and their family. The colours are of personal significance and are intended to reflect the family’s combined heritage including: blue for Scotland; green for Ireland; pink their daughter and blue for their son.

name: Dumbarton Scottish Terriers
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval to use/reproduce the tartan is required by Jason Rhodes, Dumbarton Scottish Terriers. Prior approval to weave the tartan required by Jason Rhodes, Dumbarton Scottish Terriers & Browne White Ltd T/A Scotlandshop.com
registrationNotes: Designed for Dumbarton Scottish Terriers, a Melbourne-based Dogs Australia breeder/exhibitor, and member of the STCA and STC UK, dedicated to preserving and protecting the Scottish Terrier. The name ‘Dumbarton’ honours Major General George Douglas, the first Earl of Dumbarton, who famously kept a ‘diehard pack’ of Scottish Terriers in 1675, a legacy that continues to be associated with the breed. The tartan acknowledges the contributions of Captain Gordon Murray who played a significant role in standardising the breed's type in 1879. To reflect the diverse coat colours of the Scottish Terrier breed the design incorporates: light grey to representing the various brindle coat patterns (black, standard, red, and silver); cream for the wheaten coat variation and black for the black coat colour.

name: Vega, Carlos & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: A tartan for Carlos Vega and his family to celebrate their heritage as Anglo Peruvians and the blend of their British and Peruvian roots. Colours: red, white, and blue are intended to reflect the Union Jack and the Peruvian flag; red is for courage and resilience; white is for peace and unity; and blue is for loyalty and trust. The inclusion of grey is intended to honour the family’s ancestors and acknowledge their contributions and sacrifices that shaped the family's journey.

name: Western Star
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan inspired by the sunset sky and stars above where the designer used to live in Arrochar, Scotland. Colours: light blue, dark blue and purple are intended to evoke the colour of the sky as it moves to sunset; yellow is for the night stars and black is intended to represent the oncoming night sky.

registrationNotes: Since 1975 Knowledge Transfer Partnerships (KTP) have been bringing academic intuitions, businesses, and graduates together to solve strategic business challenges. name: Royal College of Psychiatrists in Scotland
restrictions: Yes. No restrictions regarding use, contact [email protected] for more information.
registrationNotes: This tartan is a blend of two designs by Dr Matthew Hastings and Dr Amal Al Sayegh to honour the Royal College of Psychiatrists in Scotland's 30th anniversary. The design combines the College’s blue, which symbolises wisdom and trust, with a silver stripe, intended to be reminiscent of Scotland's Saltire. The tartan incorporates elements from the College arms: golden butterflies on sable, symbolising the goddess Psyche; thin bands of gold and black to represent light and darkness, metaphors for the affective illnesses treated by psychiatrists; a green strip to symbolise mental health awareness, flanked by red bands recalling the Rod of Asclepius, emphasising psychiatry's medical roots. Purple is intended to add a touch of diversity to the design, completing a tapestry of symbolism.

The light blue is a nod to Manchester City Football Club, who the whole family support. The colours of this design were inspired by the autumnal colours seen at the family’s home in Loch Lomond and on their family walks on Wimbledon Common.

name: Rablogan Spirit of the Highlands
restrictions: Yes. There is no restriction on who can wear this tartan. This tartan may only be woven by entities who have the written permission to do so with such permission having been sought and granted by Rablogan Castle Limited, the designer or the heirs of either.
registrationNotes: The Rablogan Spirit of the Highlands was designed for Rablogan Castle Limited as part of its Highlands collection. The design was inspired by Scotland’s many whiskies, know in Gaelic as Uisge Beatha (the water of life). The colours are intended to depict the various stages in the evolution of the amber liquid from barley field to cask maturation, reflecting all of the phases that collectively form the process of the creation of this Scottish spirit: green and light yellow are for the fields of barley; dark grey is for the maltings and cellars; dark yellow, orange and yellow are for the whisky during distilling; brown is for the casks and red is intended to represent the people who make the process of development possible.

name: St. Andrews Society of Charleston
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn by those authorised by the copyright holders, the St. Andrews Society of Charleston. This tartan cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders, The St. Andrews Society of Charleston or their designated agents. Copyright ot St Andrews Society of Charleston. USA
registrationNotes: The St. Andrew's Society of Charleston is the oldest organisation of its kind in the world and its tartan is based on the 1980 Carolina State Tartan with the Society's actual founding date woven into it. In horizontal order the dark purple squares have 30 threads, the red bands have 11, the green 17 and the black 29 - forming the date of 30th November 1729. In further recognition of the Society's antiquity, the triple white lines on green are a design element from a tartan-like graphic from the 3,500 year old engraving found in the tomb of a Bronze Age warrior in Pylos, southwest Greece. The central line has been widened to represent Christ on the Cross of Calvary flanked by the two thieves. The white cross on blue is also intended to represent St. Andrew and the Saltire - Scotland's national flag.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Chopra family as a reflection of their heritage. The colour palette was inspired by a historical Coat of Arms linked to the family. A heartfelt nod to Gopal’s mother Narinder is woven into the tartan through a turquoise blue, inspired by her Firozi shawl. Their wedding date is woven into the secondary checks: the inner dark blue check is for the day of their marriage, while the outer green check represents the month of July. The turquoise check encasing the main blue check symbolises the year 1999. Their sons Raghav Raj and Siddharth Raj are also honoured within the design; a yellow check signifies the decade between their births, while two green checks each represent one of their sons.

registrationNotes: Maria Clementina Sobieska was the granddaughter of the Polish king John III Sobieski, and the mother of Charles Edward Stuart – Bonnie Prince Charlie. This design for the Login family of Poland is thus is based on the Royal Stewart tartan, a pattern that has a long association with British Royalty and one that was particularly popular during the Highland Revival era c.1780 - 1840. The wedding date of Anna and Grzegorz Login on the 2nd June 2007 is woven into this design with light green threads of 2, olive green of 6, dark brown of 20 and the adjacent light brown of 7. The light brown has 13 threads – Anna’s lucky number and completing the tartan are the three red lines for their daughters, Octavia, Maia and Elvira each bordered with purple, their mother’s favourite colour.

restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Inverlochy Castle. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Inverlochy Castle. The design was inspired by Ben Nevis, which dominates the area around the Castle. Colours: white is intended to represent the summit of Ben Nevis; blue represents how ice and snow from the top of Ben Nevis melts into the river Lochy, and also represents the loch that lies in front of the castle; muted greens represent the green needles of the Scots Pine and Sequia trees that grow within the castle’s grounds; purple represents the Scottish Thistle and three red lines represent the rustic red bark of the old giant sequoia trees. These three red lines are also a nod to the Cameron Hunting tartan in recognition and respect for Locheil and the Cameron Clan, as the Castle is situated within their traditional lands. The tartan is intentionally woven in subtle muted colours to mark the importance the site has played over the many years in Scottish history.

name: Carrick, David and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Nancy and David Carrick to celebrate the family's heritage. Rooted in their Scottish traditions, the design draws from the Kennedy Clan tartan, acknowledging the Carrick family's ancestral ties. The tartan's colour palette is of personal significance; black, white and grey form the ground, inspired by Nancy’s signature monochrome wardrobe; blue represents the sea, a defining element of the family's life in Bermuda; soft yellow and off-white are intended to capture the sunlit warmth and golden glow of the Bermudian sun and sand. Special dates are woven into the design, marking the couple's most cherished milestones: the 18th of February for Nancy and David’s first date and 18/8/2012 to celebrate their wedding anniversary.

The tartan’s colours were selected through a community survey led by the Autism Acceptance Team, ensuring authentic representation. A yellow stripe is intended to symbolise ‘Au’, the chemical symbol for gold, which is used within the autism community as shorthand for autism in online and social spaces. The tartan was launched in recognition of National Autism Acceptance Month in April.

registrationNotes: A tartan for the Chicopee St. Patrick's Day Parade. Chicopee is the second-largest city in western Massachusetts USA and is located on the Connecticut River. registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned for the Mill Valley Golf Club, nestled in Marin County in Northern California. The colour palette was inspired by the local landscape and the club’s heritage. Greens and reds are intended to reflect the surrounding redwood forests, with the red also honouring the iconic Golden Gate Bridge and its Scottish counterpart, the Forth Road Bridge. Blue represents the expansive California sky, while sandy tones are intended to evoke the winding trails of Mount Tamalpais and the coastal fog rolling over the Marin Headlands. A vivid streak of hot pink pays tribute to Mill Valley’s countercultural roots in the 1960s and ‘70s. The club’s founding year, 1919, is subtly commemorated with a sandy check formed with 19 threads on each side of the pivot.

registrationNotes: This tartan is part of a collection of fashion tartans intended to celebrate the highlands in Sweden. The climate in northern Sweden is markedly different from southern Sweden. In the south there are lowlands with long and warm summers, while in the north there are highlands with long and cold winters. The Southern Swedish Highlands experiences the best of both. The colours are intended to reflect the landscape and weather experienced during the winter months in the Southern Swedish Highlands including; white snow, grey days, blue skies and frozen lakes.

name: A Man's a Man Ukraine

registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by the Robert Burns World Federation. The tartan was derived from an International Essay Competition created by The Robert Burns World Federation, in which the Ukrainian Children were asked to explain in their own words what they felt Burns’ famous Poem ‘A Man’s A Man for A’ That’ was trying to say. Their answer was global brother and sisterhood. The question was posed: if the poem could be represented in a tartan what would the tartan look like? This design was the outcome and it is intended to be a symbol of belonging, unity and inclusiveness.
