registrationNotes: A tartan for Ferenc Jonas to celebrate his 60th birthday.

name: Ledbetter, S & Zdan, K, Birchfell (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a second colourway tartan for Steven M. Ledbetter and his wife, Kathryn Zdan. Inspired by the ever-changing beauty of the woodlands surrounding their New England home, the tartan is intended to capture the essence of all four seasons and reflect the trees' natural transformation throughout the year. Warm, earthy and grey hues pay tribute to the couple’s beloved whippet companions and their brindle coats. At the tartan's heart, 26 threads in a warm earthy shade honours their wedding anniversary on the 26th of August.

name: Water of Life Society

The colours are those of the University of Edinburgh and are also intended to reflect key aspects of the Society: blue symbolises academic tradition and collegiate identity; bright scarlet evokes the warmth of whisky and the boldness of a dram; and the white lines represent friendship and clarity of purpose.

name: Fickëyjpb, J (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Fickëyjpb family to celebrate their blended family and their bond. The design is intended to be a symbol of their shared identity.

registrationNotes: This tartan was design for Peter De Brabandere and his family. The design is intended to reflect arms connected to the De Brabandere family, incorporating the colours and symbolism into the tartan.

name: Raven, B & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by members of the Raven House/family only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Raven family using colours of personal significance.

name: Gavrielov, Vladislav & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: Commissioned by the Gavrielov family, this tartan was designed incorporating personal family elements. At the heart of the design are five dark blue checks, each representing one of Vladislav’s five children. Developed in collaboration with Vladislav to reflect his colour preferences, the tartan blends varying blue tones, with touches of red, violet, and white. The gradient of colour is intended to represent a thoughtful exploration of harmony and individuality.

name: Davis, Christopher and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Davis family and their visitors of Old Quarry. Permission to weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought from Christopher Davis and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Christopher Davis, this tartan is intended to reflect and celebrate the beauty of the small New England island where four generations of the Davis family gather each summer. ‘Old Quarry’ is characterised by its rugged boulder-strewn coastline, moss-filled spruce forests, wild blue berry meadows and the industrial remnants of a nineteenth century granite quarry. Reflecting the camp's ethos of austere simplicity and natural beauty, the colours of the tartan are intended to reflect the changing greens of the forest, the soft blues of sea and sky, the red of lichen, the subtle pink-grey hues of moss on ancient granite, and even a hint of the rust on old iron toolworks.

name: WC 1990
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the Class of 1990 from Williams College, Massachusetts, United States.

name: Ceilidh (Grove Entertainment)
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions with regards to who can wear this tartan. It can only be used by Grove Entertainment or by others who have written confirmation of permission to do so. registrationNotes: ‘Ceilidh’ is a musical, created by Scott Gilmour and Claire McKenzie. Mirroring the emotion of the show, a whirlwind of lively Scottish dances, this tartan design was inspired by the counts that exist within the songs and dances. From dance crib sheets, to reel like multiples of 4, the design includes a specific threadcount to honour the musical writers and their grandparents that inspired this story. The colours used for this design are intended to reflect the colours associated with Scotland’s national flag, the Saltire, and The Lion Rampant.

name: Turblin, Jean Pierre, Armentières (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with authority from the designer. Copyright rests with Jean Pierre Turblin.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Jean Pierre Turblin inspired by the town of Armentières in Northern France. The design includes elements and colours intended to represent the city’s Coat of Arms and the two Military Crosses received by the City following both World Wars.

name: Collectionneurs Lommois

name: Dickson-Hope, A & M (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent the coming together of two families and the bonds they have forged together. It was inspired by the landscape that brought them together; the greenery and waters that surround the Forth estuary. Hidden within the landscape lies the brown coats of native wildlife, including otters which enjoy the river that draws a line between the couple’s two cities of origin. Present throughout are black and white dashes, intended to represent an energetic border collie exploring the places where the family find themselves most at home. Finally, there are threads of yellow inspired by sunflowers and their adventures.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Lotus Ltd, North America's largest Lotus car club. It is intended to be a tribute to legendary driver Jim Clark and the Club’s vibrant community of members. The design was inspired by the Cameron of Erracht tartan, a tartan Jim Clark was known to wear, with colours inspired by his iconic 1965 Indy 500-winning Lotus 38. Founded in 1973 by two Europa owners, Lotus Ltd has grown into an international community united by the love of driving, engineering, and Lotus legacy. This tartan celebrates the 60th anniversary of Jim Clark's famous win and the spirit of connection between the past and present, the racetrack and the road.

registrationNotes: The tartan designed for the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. The tartan colour palette is based on the Glasgow 2026 brand aesthetic with a grey base added as a nod to Glasgow’s industrial history of shipbuilding - the grey is a variation of steel grey. The large grey section is a 74 thread count - representing the Commonwealth territories involved in the games and the centre dark blue section is 26 threads representing the year 2026.

name: Gemmell, D & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 75th birthday of David Gemmell. Colours: blue is for his favourite colour; black is intended to acknowledge the family's mining history and white is to remember the family home in Whyte Street, Harthill.

name: Scaife Handford, W R (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for William Scaife Handford to celebrate his 50th birthday in 2025. Colours: red is intended to represent the Kentish roots of the Handford name; dark green and blue are for links to the Mitchell and Roffey surnames; purple is for his time spent in Edinburgh and the Scottish hills; yellow is intended to represent celebration and his 50th.

name: Birss, A Dress (Personal)
registrationNotes: A dress tartan for Art Birss. The design is intended to celebrate the life of his great grandfather James Birss, from Shampher near Strachan, who worked the land and died at a young age. As a result of his death Art’s great grandmother, along with most of the family, emigrated to Canada and carried on the tradition of farming.

name: Taymouth Castle
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval is required from The River Tay Castle LLP is required for any use/wear/to weave.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Taymouth Castle to celebrate its journey from past to present and its exciting future. The design is intended to encapsulate the longstanding traditions of the Scottish Highlands, the free spirit of golf, and the story behind Taymouth Castle. It was inspired by Perthshire’s lush, verdant landscape and marries those elements with numerical references in the threadcount. The blue turquoise check contains 94 threads for the year 1994, the year that Mike Meldman founded Discovery Land Company, and the colour is for the waters in the River Tay, River Lyon, and Loch Tay. Grey was chosen to reflect the stone walls of the castle, its subtle green tinge delicately reflecting the time-weathered shade of the stone. Three sets of double tram lines are intended represent Mr. Meldman’s three sons and the bond of family, adding a personal touch to round out the tartan’s unique story.

name: Sexton, Jon T & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those with lineage descended from Sir George Sexton. May not be woven/reproduced without permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Jon Sexton and his family using colours of personal significance inspired by the history of the Sexton surname and their Irish heritage.

name: University of Victoria
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/reproduce this tartan must be obtained in writing from the designer, Robert Paterson.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the University of Victoria, Canada. The design is intended to represent the combination of three elements at the University - dynamic learning, vital impact and an extraordinary academic environment - and how together, these elements nurture an environment of discovery, innovation and creativity. The threadcount includes reference to founding date 07/01/1963.

name: Bucca Dell'Acqua
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/reproduce this tartan must be obtained in writing from the designer, Robert Paterson.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Bucca dell’Acqua, a bookstore located in St Andrews, New Brunswick, Canada. Bucca dell’Acqua translates to ‘mouth of the water’ in the Sicilian dialect that gave owner’s family their name. The design is intended to celebrate their passion for the power of literature, the importance of representation in books, and encouraging a love of reading in people of all ages.

name: Smiling Mountain (Spring)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan intended to represent early spring in the mountains. It was inspired by the traditional Japanese phrase ‘yama warau’, which means 'the mountain smiles'. Smiling Mountain is one a four-part tartan series reflecting the seasonal changes of the mountain throughout the year.

name: Glistening Mountain (Summer)
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan intended to represent the fullness of summer in the mountains, when the landscape is vibrant and full of life. It was inspired by the traditional Japanese phrase ‘yama shitataru’, which means ‘the mountain drips’. Glistening Mountain is one a four-part tartan series reflecting the seasonal changes of the mountain throughout the year.

name: Adorned Mountain (Autumn)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan intended to represent autumn in the mountains, when the leaves of the trees are vibrant red, orange, and gold. It was inspired by the traditional Japanese phrase ‘yama yosou’, which means ‘the mountain is adorned’. Adorned Mountain is one a four-part tartan series reflecting the seasonal changes of the mountain throughout the year.

name: Sleeping Mountain (Winter)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan intended to represent winter in the mountains, when the landscape is blanketed by snow. It was inspired by the traditional Japanese phrase ‘yama nemuru’, which means the mountain sleeps. Sleeping Mountain is one a four-part tartan series reflecting the seasonal changes of the mountain throughout the year.

name: Mouthuy, Stéphane & Chan, Be Mei and Family (Personal)

This tartan cannot be offered for sale, woven or reproduced by any means for any commercial purposes, without the express permission of Mouthuy, Stéphane or Chan, Be Mei or their successors.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Mouthuy-Chan family. The colours are intended to represent the family's origins including the colours featured in the flags of Belgium, Morocco and Taiwan.

registrationNotes: A fashion tartan by designer Mayumi Materiaali, based in Japan. It was inspired by the dish papeton which originated in Avignon, France, and is made of cooked aubergine mixed with egg, Colours: purple and white are for eggplant; light yellow is for egg; green and blue are for herbs.

name: Clan Tackle Ltd - Clan Lady
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Clan Tackle Ltd. Prior Approval to weave/reproduce required by John Drummond, Clan Tackle Ltd & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: Designed for Clan Tackle, who blend timeless traditions with cutting-edge innovation, crafting fly rods that offer presentation and performance in all conditions. This design is part of their ladies range. The colours are intended to represent; the green of the Scottish landscape, the gold-brown of the earth, and the steel blue of deep salmon pools with the addition of pink bringing a fresh, distinctive identity to the range while maintaining a strong connection to the brand’s heritage and environment.

name: P.S. Murphy Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for P.S. Murphy Ltd., located in the United States, and incorporates their corporate colours.

name: Parklane Group, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of The Parklane Group, The Parklane Foundation, and their brands: Parklane Properties, Roomzzz, INC, Homezzz, IconInc, rentinc, Leeds Golf Centre, and UOWN. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required by the Parklane Group & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: This tartan designed to mark the opening of IconInc The Bonnie in Glasgow, and to celebrate The Parklane Group’s arrival in Scotland and established roots in Edinburgh through Roomzzz Aparthotels. The design incorporates vibrant orange intended to represent The Parklane Group, with teal threads for The Parklane Foundation and navy for Roomzzz Aparthotels. Woven through the black ground, the four colours of the IconInc heart logo are included to symbolise a coming together of identity, values and future ambition.

name: Spirit of Brazil, The
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: Largs Primary School was selected to take part in a competition to design a tartan for Brazil, titled The Spirit of Brazil, due to its unique connection to Charles Miller, the Brazilian-Scot widely credited with introducing football to Brazil and its close proximity to Kelburn Castle, renowned for its vibrant Brazilian street art adorning the castle walls and turret. Pupils were invited to submit their tartan designs to a judging panel that included the Brazilian Consul General and fellow Primary 7 pupils. The winning entry incorporated the colours of the Brazilian flag, along with a subtle touch of red in homage to the school’s own colours. The final design has been officially recognised as a national tartan of Brazil, endorsed by the first-ever Brazilian Consulate in Edinburgh as a symbol of the deep and lasting friendship between Brazil and Scotland.

name: Edinburgh Castle
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of employees and customers of Historic Environment Scotland. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Edinburgh Castle. Colours: black is intended to represent ‘Auld Reekie’; grey was inspired by the basalt rock upon which the Castle sits; red is for 3 bloodied battles that took place at the Castle and yellow, representing gold, is for the Crown Jewels and Stone of Destiny.

name: Al Farhan 'Al Rataj Al Dahabi', His Excellency Fahad (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use only by His Excellency Fahad Al Farhan and family.
registrationNotes: His Excellency Fahad Al Farhan ‘Al Rataj Al Dahabi' (The Golden Rataj) has heraldic ancestry from the Middle East and a legacy of farm ownership in Eastern Europe. His Excellency Fahad Al Farhan commissioned a personal tartan to reflect deep-rooted traditions, nobility, and agricultural prosperity. The colours are intended represent family strength, legacy, fortitude, and leadership, with purple tones throughout for royalty and heritage. The design includes singular threads intended to represent the family’s lineage.

name: Casa Loma
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Casa Loma, a museum in Toronto, Canada. The design is intended to represent both Sir Henry Pellatt’s and Casa Loma's dedication to Canadian heritage, while highlighting Sir Henry’s own Scottish ancestry. Colours: black is intended to represent the legacy of Casa Loma, its contribution to Canadian heritage and its preservation; blue is for the family crests of the Pellatt’s (Sir Henry), and the Dodgson’s (Lady Mary); red and white represent Sir Henry’s ties to Britain, as well as Canada and Toronto’s flags; green and yellow represent his service to the Queen’s Own Rifles regiment and orange is intended to acknowledge the traditional territory that Casa Loma is situated upon, and Sir Henry’s own positive relationships with numerous Indigenous Nations.

name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with: Culture and Sport Trading, Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow, G3 8AG
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum. The colours were inspired by some of the iconic paintings associated with Kelvingrove, taking greys, blues, greens, orange, and black from FCB Cadell’s Interior – The Orange Blind and Salvador Dalí’s Christ of St John of the Cross. The grey pivot has 19 threads bordered by one black to mark the 1901 opening of the building. The grey surrounding the orange pivot has 22 threads, one for each of Kelvingrove’s different galleries.

name: Burrell Collection, The
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with: Culture and Sport Trading, The Burrell Collection, 2060 Pollokshaws Road, Pollok Park, Glasgow, G43 1AT
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Sir William and Constance, Lady Burrell’s, gift of their collection to the City of Glasgow in 1944. Colours: pink reflects the colour of the Locharbriggs sandstone of the building; blue is for the sky; green for the surrounding parkland and grey for the glass, steel and concrete. The small grey squares have 19 threads, and the large grey squares have 83 to signify the opening of the Burrell Collection in 1983.

name: Hernandez, Melodie & Gomes Da Torre, Flavien - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by members of their immediate family. Permission from the designer must be sought for any weaving of this tartan. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the union of Flavien Gomes Da Torre and Mélodie Hernandez. Colours: red is intended to symbolise their passion and strength; blue for serenity and love for sea and nature; yellow represents creativity and dark grey is for their home and life together.

name: Mayewski, Paul Andrew and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Paul Mayewski and his family. The design is intended to represent Paul’s heritage and life, born in Edinburgh in 1946 to a Polish army officer who fought with the British Army in World War II and a German woman who studied in Cornwall and served as a children's nurse during the war. Colours: blue is intended to represent Scotland; red is for Paul’s Polish roots and his father’s wartime service; black for his German roots and white is intended to represent peace and post-war unity.

name: Green, K & T and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for personal use by the Green family. May not be woven/reproduced without permission. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Tiree Johnstone and Kieran Green and to be worn by their family. It was used for hand fasting during the ceremony on their wedding day.

name: Soofer, R & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive for the use of Sharona Soofer Veiseh, Kaveh Soofer, Guiv Soofer and Immediate Family & Descendants. Permission to weave/use/ reproduce must be sought from the Immediate Soofer/Veiseh Family and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Soofer family. The design was inspired by the family’s Scottish and Iranian heritage and is intended to be a tribute to the couple’s late father. The soft colours are designed to embody the strength of generations of resilient Scottish women in the family, while the deeper shades serve to symbolise the male figures in their family lineage. The purple within the tartan is intended to pay homage to their father and the enduring love that defines their family. The Soofer family are represented throughout the threadcount; the outer green check is comprised of 11 threads, each thread representing the 11 grandchildren within the family, husband and wife are represented within the smaller secondary white check, while their three children are reflected by the light green checks.

name: Harron, J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Jon Harron & his family. Prior Approval to weave/reproduce required by Jon Harron & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Jonwayne Harron to mark the occasion of his marriage to his fiancée Erin on 11 July 2026 in Duns, Scotland. The design is intended to represent bringing together Erin’s Scottish family and Jon’s Northern Irish family, and reflect the couple’s desire to unite both sides as one big family. The colours are of personal significance: red is for the Red Hand of Ulster, a historic symbol of the Northern Irish province Jonwayne’s family comes from; yellow is for the Saffron kilt worn by the Royal Irish Regiment, in which Jonwayne serves, and green is intended to represent the caubeen, the traditional headdress worn by the Royal Irish.

name: Sauter Group
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Scott Stevenson. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed for the Sauter Group. Reflecting the company's identity, the colours are based on Sauter's official corporate palette.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Mackenzie Construction’s 45th anniversary celebrations and to become part of the company’s branded identity. Designed with Sharon Scotland in association with other long serving employees; Alan McCafferty, Michelle Connor, Ritchie Bennett, Thomas Baird.

registrationNotes: A tartan for Tyler Wilkerson and his family using colours of personal significance intended to represent their family’s history and future.

IPR owner: Stany Perkisas Contact details: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Perkisas family descending from Stany Perkisas. It includes 6 colours intended to depict different family values and references to the heritage of the family.

name: VanFossen, Robert & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Robert VanFossen and his family. Each pivot is intended to represent an individual from the family. The colours are intended to reflect their roots: blue and yellow for California; red and yellow for Texas, with yellow connecting the two, and black and white for memories.

name: Prior, P & E - Wedding (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Paul Prior to celebrate his wedding.

name: Glasgow Space
restrictions: Yes. Primarily intended for members and collaborators of the Space Group, the tartan may also be worn by participants in space-related events organised by the University, and by individuals contributing to Glasgow’s growing space sector. All enquiries should go to The University of Glasgow, Gilles Bailet, email: [email protected]
registrationNotes: The Glasgow Space tartan was created by the Space Group of the University of Glasgow’s James Watt School of Engineering to symbolise the city’s leadership in spacecraft manufacturing and space innovation. The design is intended to reflect the unity between academia, industry, and the broader community engaged in space activities across Greater Glasgow. Colours: black is intended to represent deep space, the vast frontier explored by the spacecraft engineered in Glasgow; green reflects Earth observation, environmental awareness, and the city’s growing commitment to sustainable space technologies; blue symbolises knowledge, research, and engineering excellence at the University of Glasgow; soft pink is for humanity, openness, and inclusiveness, a deliberate contrast to the tones often associated with engineering or space and white is intended to trace the precision, clarity, and openness essential to scientific discovery and signal the inclusive ethos of the Space Group.

name: Dörrer-Straub, A & P (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn and ordered by the Doerrer and Straub family.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed to symbolise the merging of two families into one with a shared love of Scotland, its culture and unique landscape.

name: Shortt, D & Family (Personal)
designer: House of Edgar / Shortt, Denys and Deborah
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Shortt family. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Denys and Deborah Shortt and their family inspired by the highland scenery near Braemar and their frequent trips to Scotland.

name: Raineach am Foghar
registrationNotes: The name of this tartan means Autumn Bracken in Scots Gaelic. The designer was inspired to create this tartan for a friends' wedding where he was the piper and best man.

name: Gemmell, Scott & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a gift for Scott Gemmell, a proud Scot residing in Bermuda. The colours are intended to represent the blue and white from the Saltire, pink Bermuda sand and vibrant turquoise waters.

name: Kobe Tokiwa
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Kobe Tokiwa University and Kobe Tokiwa Girls’ High School, Japan. Colours: green and blue are intended to reflect the natural beauty of Mt. Takatori and the Suma Sea, which surround the school; green also links with the spirit of our school name, ‘Tokiwa’ meaning ‘evergreen’; dark blue is intended to represent the students’ intelligence and white is for the school building.

name: Inglis, Kyle (Personal)
designer: Lochcarron of Scotland & Uddingston Pipe Band
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of Uddingston Pipe Band and those authorised by them and the family of Kyle Inglis.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed in memory of Kyle Inglis, son of Uddingston Pipe Band member John Inglis.

name: Clann Taic
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for Clann Taic, the Care Crew Foundation and the Greencloak Initiative, and is intended to be worn on volunteer uniforms and for visual identity at immersive events.
registrationNotes: This tartan was was designed for the parent organisation Clann Taic, and its charitable programs, including the Care Crew Foundation and Greencloak Initiative. The colours are intended to reflect their core values: blue for trust and duty; white for compassion and peacekeeping; green for growth and care; grey for resilience and a single purple line as a nod to honour and leadership. It is intended to be used on uniforms, banners, and ceremonial garb to foster identity, recognition, and pride among their volunteers and those they support.

name: Boyle, Susan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission required from Susan Boyle or her management team to weave or recreate this tartan. Only official suppliers will be able to reproduce this tartan. Copyright rests with Susan Boyle.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the singer Susan Boyle to mark her comeback in late 2025. Working with Susan, the tartan was created to include shades of pink, which she loves to wear, and green, her other favourite colour.

name: Curington, L and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by relatives, family or those with the permission of Logan Curington.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Logan Curington for his family after researching his ancestry. The colours were inspired by the different regions in which his ancestry was linked, including Ayr.

name: Ania´s Thistle Spirit
restrictions: Yes. This tartan can be used and woven by anyone for personal use. Copyright rests with Ania Belloso Garcia.
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to be a tribute to the spirit of Scotland by the designer. Colours: light purple is intended to represent the thistle; white was inspired by the cross of the Saltire; blue is for Scotland’s rivers and lochs, as well as the blue of the Saltire; green is for magic, resilience, and spirituality, and the Highlands and Lowlands; black is intended to honour the memory of those who died defending Scotland and brown is for humility, rural life, honesty, simplicity, and hard work.

name: NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre
restrictions: Yes. Designed and owned by Margi Lawson, Tartan Manor Limited. Use of this tartan to produce various items, garments, clothing, all manner of products etc, for retail is restricted to Tartan Manor Limited. No other person or company will have that right. Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Limited. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 13 February 2026, registration number: 6507017.
registrationNotes: The NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre tartan was designed to celebrate all past and present personnel and achievements attached to the NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre. The NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre (NIFC) provides the Supreme Allied Commander Europe and Allied Command Operations with timely, relevant, and accurate intelligence in order to support planning and execution of NATO operations; and enable deterrence and defence of the Euro-Atlantic area. The tartan features significant colours associated with the NIFC; dark blue, light blue, dark green and grey are from the NIFC tie as worn by NIFC personnel. Black is intended to represent continual respect for all fallen NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre comrades.

name: Helmn, J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the exclusive use of Jack Helmn, his family, and descendants. Permission is required for any weaving, reproduction, or commercial use. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Jack Helmn by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Jack Helmn and Jemma McBride, and the Helmn family's life in Scotland. It is intended to signify a sense of belonging and rootedness, as the family embrace their Scottish home. Blue, inspired by the Saltire, is intended to reflect the couple’s connection to Scotland, while the orange is for Blackpool, the Helmn family’s town of origin.

name: Tzortzis, Alexander & Keery, Jane and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone with the surname Tzortzis or Keery, family or anyone closely affiliated with the immediate family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to mark the wedding of Jane Keery and Alexander Tzortzis, bringing together their respective Scottish and Greek backgrounds, as well as drawing on influence from the Muir tartan of Jane's maternal grandparents.

name: Scotland History Tours (Fummey)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Scotland History Tours or the Fummey Family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Scotland History Tours. Bruce Fummey is the originator and the face behind Scotland History Tours. Fummey is a very recent name from the village of Asadame in the Volta Region in Ghana, and Bruce is the eldest of the first generation in Scotland. The colours are intended to celebrate Scotland History Tours and the family’s ties to both Scotland and Ghana by combining the flags of each country; blue and white for the Saltire and red, gold, green and black for the flag of Ghana.

name: Harper-Allison, Kristopher (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability. Intended for use by Kristopher Harper-Allison, the immediate members of the Harper and Allison families, or others with permission from Kristopher Harper-Allison or a designated family representative. Please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Kristopher Harper-Allison. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was created for Kristopher Harper-Allison, in celebration of his 50th birthday. The design was inspired by elements of the Allison and Buchanan tartan setts. Harper is a sept of Clan Buchanan. The threadcount includes numbers that reference his birthday & wedding dates. The colours used are of significance to him and his family.

name: Louisiana Tech
restrictions: Yes. There is no restriction as to who can wear the Tech Tartan. Weaving is restricted to Louisiana Tech University and its licensed vendors. Tartan merchandise can only be produced and sold by Louisiana Tech University and its licensed vendors.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Louisiana Tech University. The colours of red and blue, the school’s colours, are based on ‘The Legend of the Bulldog’. According to the legend, when the bulldog that saved students from a fire was buried, two students used their jackets to cover the bulldog, one was blue and the other was red. Louisiana Tech University has six academic units - five colleges (Applied and Natural Sciences, Business, Education and Human Sciences, Engineering and Science, and Liberal Arts) and the Library - which are represented by the red stripes. The twelve white stripes are intended to represent the ‘Tenets of Tech’; confidence, excellence, commitment, knowledge, integrity, respect, leadership, respect, loyalty, enthusiasm, caring, hope, and pride. The central pivot is intended to represent the Quadrangle at the centre of Tech’s campus, the home to the University Administration’s offices and the paths that lead to the academic buildings and student life.

name: Coorong Pelican
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the designer’s favourite bird and location, the Coorong Pelican. The Corona region of South Australia is a protected habitat for pelicans and other bird life living in the coastal waters. The colours are based on the plumage of the pelican along with blue, intended to represent the waters.

name: Brügger, R & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ralph Brügger and his family. Colours: red is intended to symbolise courage and bravery; blue is for loyalty and steadfastness and yellow is for honour and generosity. The design is based on a historical Coat of Arms connected to the family.

name: Petersen, Donald J (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in memory of Donald J Peterson by his son. It includes his favourite colours along with blue, yellow and green which are intended to represent water, the sun and vegetation.

name: Spirit of Independence (Slanj)
designer: Halley, Brian & Howson, Charlotte (House of Edgar)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Brian Halley, Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Slanj Kilts to celebrate the spirit of independence.

designer: Marton Mills Co LTD/Kilt Rental USA
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only by officers and members of the Daughters of Scotia Skye Lodge #267 in Tucson, AZ, USA.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Daughters of Scotia, Tucson Skye Lodge #267, Arizona. Colours: purple is intended to represent the Tucson Mountains; white is for the clouds; blue is for the sky and green is for the green brush found in the Sonoran Desert.

name: Copley, E & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Erik Copley and his family. The tartan was inspired by the family's lineage which Erik traced from Scotland, to England, and finally to the United States.

name: Cabe, Stephen (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Cabe family. Prior Approval to weave/reproduce required by the Cabe family& Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Stephen Cabe to celebrate his family’s history and connection to the Scottish Highlands and Clan MacLeod. Colours: yellow, black and red were inspired by the MacLeod tartan; green is intended to represent the Blue Ridge Mountains, where the family settled and purple is for the thistle of Scotland, and the thistle which grows in the Blue Ridge Mountains.

name: Mckay, Graham (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Graham Mckay. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to mark the wedding of Graham Mckay and Sarah Murphy in the Italian town of Sorrento. The tartan features a neutral colour palette of stone and brown tones, designed to be worn in the summer sun.

name: Potter, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those with the Surname Potter, or evidence of familial ties to Potter. May not be woven/reproduced or used for commercial purposes without prior permission.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Potter family using colours of personal significance.

name: Wong, H T (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn/used by the designer and those with his permission.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for H T Wong using colours of personal significance. The design is intended to represent the designer's cultural heritage and his connection with Scotland.

name: Oberon Black
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Oberon Black. Restricted availability, please contact Oberon Black or Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This company tartan was designed for Robert & Tatiana Coulter of Oberon Black. The design was inspired elements of the Coulter tartan and the threadcount includes the number 20 to reference 2020, the year the company was established. The colour palette was inspired by the landscape surrounding their property where the company is based.

name: Sluysmans, Jacques & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Sluysmans family. Permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought by prof. Jacques Sluysmans, his descendants, or any other person with written permission. Prepared for weaving by Auld Alliance Kiltmakers. Copyright rests with Auld Alliance Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the Coat of Arms granted to Prof. Jacques Sluysmans by the Lord Lyon for his acquisition of a feudal barony in Scotland. The name of the tartan has been chosen as it is intended to be a family heirloom, cherished and worn by future generations of the Sluysmans family. Colours: blue and white are from the Coat of Arms commissioned to Lord Lyon and also the Coat of Arms of the village of Simpelveld, Netherlands, where the family comes from; the orange overcheck in the middle of the blue ground is intended to represent the Knight's Cross of the Order of Orange-Nassau - a royal distinction received by Jacques - and his roots in the Netherlands, for the House of Orange.

name: Dalscone
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the owner before weaving.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Dalscone farm, Dumfries, for items produced and sold through the shop.

name: Stone, Joseph F & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the descendants of Joseph F Stone (1856-1915) and Martha J Lewis Stone (1865-1958).
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the descendants and family of Joseph F Stone (1856-1915) and Martha J Lewis Stone (1865-1958) to celebrate the family’s Scottish heritage.

name: Scottish-Acadian (Écossais-Acadien)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by those with a shared history and family bonds between Scottish and Acadian descendants. Permission to weave/reproduce must be granted by the designer in writing.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the shared heritage of Acadian and Scottish settlers who braved the new world between the 17th and 19th centuries. In places such as Cape Breton, Mainland Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and New Brunswick in Canada there are many families that speak both Gaelic and Acadian French. The colours were inspired by the Acadian Flag.

name: Vincent, George (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be open for use for all Vincent’s from around the world. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Andrew Vincent by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by Andrew and Rebecca Vincent for their wedding day. The tartan was named in honour of Andrew’s Dad and Grandad and is intended to be worn by all of the Vincent family. It is intended to celebrate the heritage of the Vincent family and welcoming Rebecca into the family. The tartan was inspired by colours from the places where they fell in love, live and where they will enjoy their life together.

name: Boyer, N and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by members of the Boyer family originating from Hamburg, PA and their descendants, whether they hold the Boyer name or not. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Nicolas Boyer and his family. Colours: white is intended to represent October; purple is for the thistle, their Scottish ancestors and the date of Nicolas and his wife’s anniversary; black red and yellow are for their German ancestry; green is Nicolas’ favourite colour and is for his Irish ancestors and the black checks add to 98 to celebrate the year Nicolas and his wife started dating.

name: Wheat Harvest On The Palouse
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions on who may wear/use this tartan. For weaving, credit and notice should be given to the designer.
registrationNotes: Inspired by a photo by Robin Atkins of the landscape in Pullman, Washington, Whitman Co, United States, this tartan is intended to be a homage to the generations of men and women who braved the incredibly steep grades of the Palouse region to bring in the harvest. The colours were inspired by the cloud dotted blue skies and groomed combine stubble of the hillside harvest.

name: Vieux Frères
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Vieux Frères biker clan, located in France, to celebrate their values and origins. The design was inspired by the cross of the Breton, the ‘Kroas Du’. The black, orange and grey are based on their logo.

name: Murphy-Griffin, R & J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Becca & James Murphy-Griffin. Please contact Kinloch Anderson Ltd. regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for James Griffin & Becca Murphy in celebration of their wedding. The design and colours were inspired by elements from the various tartans connected to their family.

name: Najafian, R & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with permission from the Najafian family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate and unify the Najafian family’s Scottish and Iranian heritage. Designed in collaboration with Reza Najafian, Omid Najafian & Amir Najafian.

name: Woodworth, Gale & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with approval from Gale Woodworth.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Gale Woodworth and their family. The colours are intended to evoke the feeling of a stormy sea, with 2 red lines to represent the red pennants used to indicate a gale warning to mariners.

name: Aicholtz, David (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for David Aicholtz to celebrate his family's Scottish roots using colours of personal significance for David and other family members.

name: Patterson, Robert & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by prior arrangement with Robert Patterson and/or direct members of family. Weaving by prior arrangement with Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by James Webster to mark the marriage of his son, Robert Patterson, to Dione in 2024. The sett was partly inspired by the MacLaren tartan. Colours: dark green is intended to represent Robert’s Irish heritage on both his maternal and paternal sides; red symbolises the Red Rose of Lancashire, reflecting his birthplace of Liverpool and his marriage in Spain; black refers to his mother’s maiden name, Guinness, and the stout of the same name; purple represents the Scottish thistle, honouring his Scottish father. The three overchecks are duplicated to give six in total, symbolising the six strings of a guitar in recognition of Robert’s passion for music. The design is intended to reflect Robert’s heritage, personal milestones, and enduring love.

name: Stace, Wesley & Abbey, Edinburgh (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability. Designed by Kinloch Anderson for the exclusive use of the Stace family. Please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Abbey & Wesley Stace and their family. The design layout and colour palette are of personal significance.

name: PCMA
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for PCMA. Restricted availability, please contact PCMA or Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for PCMA to celebrate its 70th anniversary in 2026, and reflect the origins of its global expansion in Scotland. The threadcount includes the numbers 70, 20 and 26 to reference this event and the palette reflects PCMA’s brand colours.

name: Thistled Pink
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Thistled Pink. Restricted availability, please contact Thistled Pink or Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This company tartan was designed for Thistled Pink. The design was inspired by elements of the Tara tartan, reflecting the founder’s Celtic heritage. The threadcount includes the numbers 20 and 24 to reference 2024, when the Thistled Pink brand was born. The colour palette uses shades that are of significance to the company founder and to the brand.

name: Cox, Aron, United States (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Cox family. Prior Approval to weave/reproduce required by the Cox family & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Aron Cox and his family. The design is intended to represent the family’s Scottish and American heritage, Aron’s military career and achievements, and the family’s influences and lived experiences.

name: Brown, Alexander James & Shonagh and Family, Strathieburn (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May not be woven/used/reproduced without permission from the registrant. Prepared for weaving by MacNaughton Holdings.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Alexander James and Shonagh Brown and their family. The design includes colours of personal significance intended to represent; their surname, their interests and the main colour of their home, Strathieburn.

name: Limousin's Treasure Tribute
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission from the designer, Francois Bourrillon
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Limousin, a former region of France with Celtic origins, its rural character and rich terrain. Colours: green is intended to represent the forests and chestnut trees; blue is for the many springs and rivers; purple is for the heather on the moors; brown represents the cows, famous for their meat; white represents kaolin, from which porcelain is made and yellow is intended to represent gold in the deposits.

name: Boonn, W & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Boonn family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce the tartan required by the Boonn family & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for William Boonn and his family to celebrate the cultures, places and traditions that shaped the Boonn and Silpasuvan families. Colours: red, white, and blue are intended to acknowledge both Thai and American heritage; orange and purple are for their ties to Baltimore and Maryland.

name: Hellmers, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Hellmers Family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required from the Hellmers Family & Browne Whit Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Hellmers family. It is intended to reflect a significant birthday spent together as a family in the West Highlands of Scotland with colours inspired by the landscapes explored and the wildlife encountered.

name: Martino, W (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Stewart & Martino family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required from the Stewart & Martino family and Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a wedding gift for W Martino from his fiancé R Stewart. The design was inspired by a photo of their favourite day, spent in the Scottish Highlands, using colours intended to reflect the landscape and weather of that day.

name: Ayrshire Railway Preservation Group
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability, please contact Ayrshire Railway Preservation Group regarding use. Intended to be worn by members and volunteers of Ayrshire Railway Preservation Group (Doon Valley Railway). Only to be woven with permission from Ayrshire Railway Preservation Group.
registrationNotes: The Ayrshire Railway Preservation Group, operators of Doon Valley Railway, was established in East Ayrshire in 1974. This tartan was designed to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the group in 2024. The colours are intended to reflect the colours of the group’s locomotives and rolling stock as well as the local countryside.

name: Paulina, A and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by the Paulina family. Cannot be woven/reproduced without permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Awfa Paulina, and the Paulina family, to celebrate the family’s Iraqi and Lebanese origins and making Scotland their new home. The colours were chosen to reflect both the Iraqi and Lebanese national flags. The design is intended to represent a generational story as the first members of the family arrived in Scotland as doctors, seeking learning and wisdom. Scotland became not only a place of study but also a permanent home for the family and this tartan is intended to symbolise a bridge between cultures.

name: Dudelsackbund Basel
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the members of the Dudelsackbund Basel society and its Ensemble 4056.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Dudelsackbund Basel, a society that promotes and fosters piping in Basel, Switzerland. Colours: black is intended to represent the society’s attachment to Basel and its black crozier; green represents the many trees that grow in Basel; purple is intended to celebrate the spirit of Scottish Pipe Music that the society cherishes and the colour of their Ensemble 4056 badge and blue is for faith and trust, and is the main colour of the society’s badge.

name: Graves-Deek, S & I and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Restricted availability. Intended for the personal use of those belonging to the family of S Graves and I Deek.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the union of S Graves and I Deek. The colours were inspired by the national flags of the countries the couple are from as well as the autumnal season when the couple first met and were later married. The sett was inspired by the Farquharson tartan, which S. Graves is connected to. The threadcount includes dates of significance to the couple.

name: Fèis Phàislig
restrictions: Yes. Anyone interested in weaving or wearing should contact Fèis Phàislig - [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to celebrate the 10-year anniversary of Fèis Phàislig, a charity providing opportunities for young people in Renfrewshire to engage with traditional music and Gaelic culture. The colours were drawn from the charity’s brand and together they are intended to reflect the energy of young people and the community spirit of Paisley and Renfrewshire.

name: Hinesley-Ferguson, A & K and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the registrant for permission to weave/use/reproduce this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Hinesley-Ferguson family to celebrate their move from California to Stonehaven, Scotland. The colours were inspired by the family’s favourite colours - purple for Adam, green for Kevin, yellow for their youngest child, and red for their oldest - and the threadcount includes references to their ages at the time of their move. Light green and light purple are intended to honour Kevin’s late parents with the green as a tribute to his father’s military service and lilac for his mother’s favourite colour. Blue is intended to represent the Saltire and has 26 threads to represent 2026, the year the family began their new life in Scotland.

name: Tommy Palmer Commemorative
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to weave/use/reproduce this tartan should seek permission from either the designer or from Tommy's daughters; Cara and Shona. Design registered with UK IPO 26/08/25, registration number 6467825.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the life of Tommy Palmer. Tommy joined the Army in 1970, joining the Royal Engineers, and in 1973 he applied to join the Special Air Service. Tommy didn’t pass selection the first time he applied, however he tried again and became one of their youngest recruits at 22. He spent time in Oman, Northern Ireland and the Falklands. Tommy was one of 32 members of the SAS who entered the Iranian embassy in London on 5th May 1980 to end the siege which saw six men take 26 hostages in a situation that lasted six days. Tommy died in a car crash in February 1983 whilst on duty in Northern Ireland. He was aged just 31.

name: Cascadia (The Kilted Hiker)

registrationNotes: The Kilted Hiker is a personal brand based in the Pacific Northwest that celebrates the Cascadian bioregion through hiking, outdoor exploration, storytelling, and cultural identity. Its mission is to inspire stewardship, adventure, and pride in Cascadia’s natural heritage. The colours were inspired by the Cascadian bioregion of the Pacific Northwest: blue and green for the region’s waters, skies, and forests; black for the volcanic mountains and white for the snow-capped peaks.

name: Sharma, C & Family, Pitlochry (Personal)

The tartan is known to the Sharma family as the BharataAlba tartan.

name: Grand Lodge of New York
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Grand Lodge of New York, United States. The tartan includes the New York State colours of blue and orange. The sett includes references to the Blue Symbolic Lodges and the 3 white lines are intended to represent the 3 Degrees.

name: Kestin
restrictions: Yes. May only be produced with approval from Kestin Hare or Gemma Hare.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed in 2025 to commemorate KESTIN’s 10-year anniversary. The design was inspired by a Gordon tartan kilt, owned by Kestin Hare’s father, and is intended to reflect the brand’s identity and Scottish roots. The colours are signature house shades referencing natural Scottish landscapes: forest green, dark navy, sky blue and soft ecru.

name: RAER, The
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is restricted to the exclusive use of RAER Scotch Whisky Ltd employees unless permission, in writing, is granted by RAER Scotch Whisky Ltd. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for RAER Scotch Whisky. The colours were inspired by RAER’s whisky and heritage: white represents whisky, before it becomes whisky, in its fresh and pure form; light yellow is intended to represent the golden fields of Scottish barley, grown by RAER; dark yellow symbolises the gleaming copper stills where the spirit is crafted; dark blue was inspired by Scotland, including the Saltire flag and the Scottish waters that are essential in whisky making; and red was included as a tribute to RAER’s founder’s ancestry, honouring both Clan Gunn and Clan Hay.

name: Scottish Terrier Club of New England
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Scottish Terrier Club of New England Inc. members. Prior permission to weave / reproduce required from the Scottish Terrier Club of New England Inc. & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: Designed for the Scottish Terrier Club of New England Inc, a regional club in the United States dedicated to the preservation and promotion of the Scottish Terrier breed, to celebrate both the heritage of the breed and the community that cherishes it. The colours are intended to reflect the recognised coat colours of the Scottish Terrier: black, brindle, silver brindle, red brindle, and wheaten. To honour the club’s New England home, an additional red stripe has been included, drawn from the red of the historic New England flag. Red is also intended to represent traditional Scottish tartans, serving as a tribute to the dogs’ country of origin.

name: International Association of Women Police (IAWP)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn by those authorised by the IAWP. Cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the IAWP. Design rights owned by International Association of Women Police (IAWP).
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the International Association of Women Police (IAWP). Black - a colour common to many police forces around the world - along with the colours of the 62nd annual conference of the International Association of Women Police, come together to form the tartan celebrating the event in 2025. The founding date of the IAWP is woven into the design with 19 threads in the small black squares and 15 threads in the purple. The conference year is marked with 25 green threads.

name: Technology One
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Technology One Ltd only. May not be woven/used/reproduced without permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Technology One, an Australian based software company who have worked within the UK since 2005. It was designed to celebrate the members of the Australian leadership team who have Scottish heritage along with their Scottish and Scotland based employees. The colours are based on their corporate colours.

name: Balogh, Ticián Máté (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Ticián Máté Balogh, from Hungary, for personal use. The colours are of personal significance: yellow is intended to represent sunshine and happiness; green is for nature and blue is intended to represent success, victory and water.

name: Valour Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Valour Apparel Pty Ltd, the official sports apparel partner of the 2026 Australian Commonwealth Games Team Prior approval to weave / reproduce required from Valour Apparel Pty Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was design for Valour Sport, an Australian owned company and official sports apparel partner of the 2026 Australian Commonwealth Games Team. The design was inspired by Valour’s heritage and its role in supporting athletes on the international stage. Within the sett: one hundred dark blue threads are intended to symbolise Valour’s identity as an Australian brand; twenty teal threads and twenty-six dark teal threads represent the 2026 Games, while nine stripes in teal, dark teal and yellow signify the year of Valour’s founding, 2009. The colour are based on Valour’s brand identity with tones that reflect the Commonwealth Games, creating a design that is intended to celebrate national pride, athletic achievement and the enduring spirit of competition.

name: McCaskie, Sarah & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Sarah McCaskie for personal use, and for use by immediate family and their direct descendants. The tartan is intended to celebrate the family’s unity and the close ties we have with each other, living in the same oceanside town. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent the deep ocean and depth of connection they have as a family; teal and light blue represents the ocean they live beside and love, and their link with their Scottish ancestors from the Isle of Bute; green is for their love of nature and Scottish and Irish ancestry; the coral colour is for the reef located neat where the family live.

name: Cavadias, Madeleine & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Madeleine Cavadias & Family to celebrate their bond with Canada and Scotland. Colours: red and white are intended to reflect the Canadian flag; light blue is for open skies; green for forests; purple for Scotland’s heather and yellow, representing gold, is intended to signify prosperity. It was designed in 2025 as a gift of friendship and connection.

name: Sisokin, Ben & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Ben Sisokin & Family and is intended to combine Canadian symbolism with the Scottish tradition of tartan. Colours: red and white are intended to represent the Canadian flag; green is for the boreal forests and dark blue is for the northern skies. The tartan was created in 2025 to celebrate the family’s identity and international connections, marking the family’s heritage from both Canada and Scotland.

name: Unconquered

registrationNotes: The Unconquered tartan is intended to celebrate the enduring spirit of resilience, sovereignty, family and cultural pride. The colours were inspired by the Native American Spirit Wheel: red is intended to represent strength and the determined courage; light brown, representing gold, is for prosperity; black honours ancestral traditions and white is intended to symbolise spiritual harmony and the continuous bonds of family.

name: Cherokee Gaquenvdi
registrationNotes: The Cherokee Gaquenvdi (meaning Cherokee wrap) tartan was designed by C.D. Mayfield, an enrolled citizen of the Cherokee Nation, to celebrate his Cherokee heritage. The colours were inspired by the Cherokee Nation’s flag: orange is intended to represent courage and endurance; green is for land and nature; yellow represents prosperity; black is intended to honour those who lost their lives on the Trail of Tears; brown is for earth and tradition and white is for peace.

name: Vaughn, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the family only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Vaughn Family to celebrate their family history and lineages from five Scottish families; Ramsay, Thompson, Hunter, Pierce, and Cowan. The colours were inspired by tartans of those Scottish families and have personal meaning: blue is intended to represent steadfastness; green is for endurance; red is for courage; black and white are intended to represent clarity and balance and yellow is for warmth and kinship.

name: Africa-Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by ASBN, their associates and International Tartans only. Can only be woven with the registrant’s permission.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed in collaboration with Africa Scotland Business Network (ASBN) and International Tartans. ASBN focuses on connecting Africa and Scotland. The network is home to member companies from around the globe far beyond the borders of Scotland and the African Continent. The colours were inspired by Scotland, from the Saltire to the heather that cover rural landscapes, and the colours of Africa Scotland Business Network's brand. Light red, representing pink, is intended to symbolise progressive female leadership and yellow, representing gold, represents the African continent; reflecting its rich cultures, natural resources, prosperity, vibrancy and hopes for the future. These values are shared by the international membership of this network, uniting cultural pride with entrepreneurial ambition.

name: Rod-Blair, N & J (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for José Varona Rodriguez & Nicolas Blero. Both firefighters themselves, the design was inspired by the Firefighters' Memorial tartan, created in memory of firefighters around the world who sacrificed their lives to protect others and more specifically the 343 NYFD firefighters who lost their lives on September 11, 2001. Colours: red is intended to represent fire and fire trucks; green is for the Blackwood family, which both are linked with; grey is intended represent the fraternity of firefighters and to be in memory of who lost their lives on the front line and yellow is for the emergency services, essential links in the rescue chain.

name: Edinburgh Southern Orienteering Club
restrictions: Yes. Permission to produce this tartan must be gained from the ESOC committee, found here: https://www.esoc.org.uk/contacts
registrationNotes: This tartan has been designed to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the Edinburgh Southern Orienteering Club. Founded in July 1965, ESOC has offered a welcoming club experience to everyone, from families and recreational orienteers through to athletes representing their country at international events. The tartan reflects ESOC's club colours and badge: dark green complemented with white, red and black. The sett commemorates ESOC's anniversary in different ways. The large dark green band comprises 60 threads, and there are six lighter green checks of differing widths, which evoke the passing of six decades since the club’s formation. These lines become thicker as they move away from the black and red threads, intended to symbolise the club growing from strength to strength across that period.

name: Spowart, N (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with the permission of Mr Spowart. Prepared for weaving by Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Neil Spowart and his family to celebrate their family and history. Spowart is an unusual name, first recorded in Kirkcaldy in Fife with this spelling in 1614 where a Spowart was a witness at a wedding. Colours; black is intended to represent the coal mining industry in Fife and the central belt of Scotland where many Spowarts worked. Purple is intended to represent the heather that covers the Scottish hills, viewed by Neil during his time spent working as a tourist guide.

name: Schwartz, Sönke (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Mr Sönke Schwartz and his immediate family. The colours of the tartan have a personal meaning: black is for the family name; blue and light blue is intended to represent the North Sea and the spray of the waves; green for the meadows of the Schwartz family´s homeland and ochre-yellow is for Sönke´s beloved dog.

name: Powell, Charles & Amanda and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Charles and Amanda Powell. The colours are intended to represent their graduations and master’s degrees: red is for Amanda who graduated from the University of Denver Graduate School of Social Work and blue is for Charles, who graduated from the University of Edinburgh Law School.

name: Rae-Kennedy, A & G (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the union between the Rae, Kennedy and Moffat families. The design was inspired by the tartans for each of these family names.

name: Wee Gem
registrationNotes: The 'Wee Gem' fashion tartan was commissioned by the Riordan family. The design was inspired by the Mackinnon and Robertson tartans, with yellow representing gold. The colours were inspired by their home in Australia, representing “the bush” and golden flowers of the wattle trees, and their Irish heritage.

name: Thomas, M & T, Isle of Lewis (Personal)

The colours are intended reflect their story and the bonds of family including purple, which is their shared favourite colour. Elements of the design were taken from the Morrison tartan and the Murray tartan to reflect their family ancestry. The sett incorporates the numbers intended to represent when the couple met and the number of years they have been together.

name: McLaurie, D & C (Personal)

Colours: blue is intended to represent the sea and heritage; red is for courage and passion; black represents strength and endurance; yellow is for honour and light and purple is intended to symbolise dignity and creativity.

name: Neryakhin, A & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was conceived, designed, and woven in 2016 by US-Scots and David McGill (Tartan Designer) to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence. In memory of the designer, this tartan was registered in 2025, ahead of the 260th anniversary. The Atlantic Alliance tartan is intended to be a symbol of connection and mutual respect, friendship and shared ideals. Colours; red is intended to represent courage and valour; white is for purity and honesty and blue is for perseverance and justice. This tartan was created to celebrate the links and the values held in common between the Scotland and the United States.

name: Sparagano, Olivier (Personal)
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Olivier Sparagano and his family. The colours are based on the family’s origins in Sicily: blue is intended to represent the sea; yellow and light brown are for the sun and sand; and green is for the island’s vegetation.

name: Beres, Michal (Personal)

It is intended to be a way for the family to honour their new home, and to embrace the traditions, stories, and landscapes that have become part of their lives. The colours are of personal significance and are intended to represent the family’s shared love of walking and being surrounded by nature.

name: Tomates Farcies

The Tomates Farcies design was inspired by the classic French dish, of tomatoes stuffed with ground meat and herbs, which originated in the Provence region of Southern France. The colours are intended to represent the designer’s favourite ingredients; tomato, minced meat, herbs and garlic.

name: Rovers, L H A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by L H A Rovers and his decendants.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for use by L H A Rovers and his descendants. The colours are of personal significance to the family.

name: Women's Strength

name: Emporium 32 - Salem
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven or reproduced with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Emporium 32, located in Salem, Massachusetts, United States and is intended to celebrate their location in a city with a rich and complex history, known for its maritime heritage and infamous witch trials of 1692. Colours: blue is intended to celebrate the maritime history; brown and black are for their location’s historic architecture; orange is for Halloween and Salem’s autumn foliage and red is to celebrate Salem’s literary history. The threadcount includes references to 1626, the year Salem was incorporated as a town, and 23rd March 1836, the date Salem was incorporated as a city.

name: Cats Protection
restrictions: Yes. Use of this tartan is intended to be restricted by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd. unless prior written consent is given. This tartan can only be woven with prior written consent from Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd. This tartan has been designed by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd, and can only be reproduced with their permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Cats Protection, the UK’s leading cat welfare charity, founded in 1927, dedicated to making a better life for cats and the people who care for them. The tartan was inspired by the Felis Silvestris, the Scottish Wildcat, that features in the belted crest of Clan MacKintosh. Accordingly, the tartan sett was developed from the MacKintosh tartan and references the brand colours of Cats Protection. The purples are intended to be a visual representation of the diverse landscapes and communities across Scotland.

name: Junken, John, United States (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and purchased by descendants from John Junken (1748-1785) and Mary Humphries unless advised otherwise with written confirmation from a member of the family. This design was commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Jason A. Junkens by USA Kilts.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the descendants of John Junken (1748-1785) to preserve their family heritage and keep the family connected. The chosen colours have special meaning to the family and are intended to represent members of the family, including colours which are intended to represent Scottish, Irish, and American themes that track the family's migration to the United States.

name: Glasgow Warriors Laoch
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Slanj Kilts or Glasgow Warriors.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for Glasgow Warriors and was inspired by the Gaelic word ‘Laoch’, meaning warrior, hero or champion. The design incorporates the club’s distinctive colours and is intended to symbolise the strength, pride, and unity that define the team and its supporters. The Laoch tartan represents the enduring spirit of the Warriors, a connection between players, fans, and the city they call home. Designed for a range of official apparel and merchandise, it stands as a proud emblem of the Glasgow Warriors’ identity and heritage.

name: Bomb & Mine Disposal
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to commemorate the bravery and dedication of Bomb & Mine Disposal teams, who have protected the United Kingdom from unexploded ordnance since World War II. From the Royal Engineers tackling land bombs and the Royal Navy's clearance divers addressing sea mines, to vital contributions from the Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve and specialised training schools, these teams have always been at the forefront of danger. Their heroic efforts, highlighted by events like the Chatham Dockyard Incident and their tireless work during The Blitz, continue to this day as modern EDD teams still deal with WWII UXO, ensuring public safety. The tartan's colours were inspired by the flags of the United Kingdom, Scotland, the British Navy, the United States Navy and the Royal Australian Navy, representing the international collaboration and shared sacrifice in bomb and mine disposal efforts. This tartan was commissioned by Fredrick Williams.

name: Lagavulin Islay
restrictions: Yes. Authorisation must be obtained from Lagavulin Distillery to weave/use/reproduce this tartan. Prepared for weaving by Lovat Mill.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate 200 years of Lagavulin distillery’s whisky-making and Scottish roots. The design is intended to pay tribute to the iconic heritage of Islay and the storied distillery. The amber is intended to represent Lagavulin’s copper stills. The alternating lines are intended to echo the tall windows of the distillery, a detail visible from the shore, and mirror both the structure of whisky-making and the natural movement of smoke and sea air.

Ann Davidson Watson / Steplane [email protected] / [email protected]
registrationNotes: The Nantucket tartan was inspired by the island’s history, culture, and natural environment. Colours: brown is intended to symbolise land and echo the island’s Wampanoag name, meaning ‘the faraway land’; blue reflects the surrounding ocean and Nantucket’s maritime and whaling heritage; grey evokes fog, sea salt, and the island’s nickname, ‘The Little Grey Lady of the Sea’; red is intended to honour heritage, the cranberry bogs central to the Wampanoag diet and once the world’s largest contiguous bog and the historic brick architecture, including the famed Three Bricks.

The colours are based on the Ivanti brand’s colours.

name: Verling, A & Family, Cork (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Dr Aran Verling and his family to celebrate their heritage in County Cork, Ireland. The design and colours are intended to unite Irish geography and the Verling family’s history into a singular family identity; green and blue are intended to represent Ireland’s land and sea, as a nod to Gaelic tradition and Cork’s maritime history; yellow is for harp strings and prosperity; white represents faith, peace, and the family’s emigration journeys; orange, representing copper, is for Cork’s 19th-century industrial legacy. The colours were inspired by Cork’s district tartans (County Cork STA#2253 and Munster STA#4061).

name: Edinburgh Medical School
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Edinburgh Medical School.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate 300 years of Edinburgh Medical School. Students were invited to weave that legacy into a contemporary design, one that acknowledges the universities past, while speaking their values, evolution, and enduring commitment to a compassionate, collaborative, and inclusive future. The colours chosen are intended to represent a variety of established University of Edinburgh colours: red for blood and liver and yellow for pus reflecting traditional Edinburgh Medical School colours; purple lines symbolize the acceptance of women in to medical education and the university. Triple red lines are symbols of the influence of the University of Padua in the establishment of Edinburgh Medical School and the success of scientific research and advancement over the last 300 years.

Craig Amner, who resides in Sydney, Australia, and his two daughters are represented by the red lines centred on blue – the broader band for Craig and the narrower ones for his daughters. All the Amners are ardent Rangers fans and the tartan includes the traditional Rangers colours of red, blue and white but with the red and blue to also represent the Melville tartan of Craig’s mother. Craig’s two brothers, who also have two children each, are represented by the red lines on either side of the ‘Rangers’ goal posts’ in white against the green grass of Ibrox. This graphic shows the warp only and not the weft variation.

name: Cancer Card
