registrationNotes: Cancer Card was founded in 2021 by Jen Hardy MBE, a stage 4 cancer patient who experienced firsthand the challenges of navigating a cancer diagnosis. Determined to help others facing similar journeys, Jen established the charity to provide vital support and resources to individuals and families affected by cancer across Scotland. Born a Scott, Jen wanted the charity's identity to reflect her Scottish heritage. The Cancer Card design was inspired by the Scott tartan (STA #1005), reimagined with the charity's distinctive black and yellow colour palette – colours that have become symbolic of the support and hope Cancer Card brings to the cancer community.

name: Inverness Castle
restrictions: Yes. There are no restrictions with regards to who can wear this tartan, however is can only be used as a design by Highlife Higland Ltd in any forms with their instruction and permission. May only be woven with explicit permission granted from Highlife Highland Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 2025 opening of the Inverness Castle Experience. The colours and threadcount were chosen to celebrate the long history of the castle and its position in Inverness. The grey and brown sections are intended to reflect the physical materials used to construct the castle over centuries, the grey stone and rocky base paired with the deep timber colours used latterly within the former courthouse. The threadcount 105 and 35 has been used, representing the latitude and longitude position of the castle. The dark blue section of 43 threads reflects the nearby River Ness and 43 was chosen as the castle is 43 feet above sea level. The 9 light blue threads represent a new chapter of the castle for 2025. The 13 sandstone threads represents the first recorded year of a castle being present, 1057, 1+0+5+7 = 13.

name: Strathcorbie

The tartan is intended to connect traditional farming life and with contemporary rural tourism, capturing the spirit of Newton Farm.

name: Mulhouse
restrictions: Yes. Permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must comply to the contract signed between the City of Mulhouse and Auld Alliance Kiltmakers. (Contact City of Mulhouse team for further details). Prepared for weaving by Auld Alliance Kiltmakers according to the contract signed between them and the City of Mulhouse. Copyright rests with Auld Alliance Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: The tartan was design for the City of Mulhouse, France, to celebrate their textile heritage and connection with Scotland. Mulhouse was the first French city with more than 100,000 inhabitants to adopt an official Scottish tartan. Colours: blue is intended to represent the waterways crossing the city and the ‘Blue Line of the Vosges Mountain’ visible from Mulhouse; green symbolises the city’s parks and natural spaces; red, the city’s emblematic colour, refers to the Mulhouse wheel, seen on the city’s Coat of Arms, and the Andrinople red (or Turkey red) used in textiles woven in the region through the centuries. The white lines form squares of various sizes and are intended to represent the city’s waterwheels and its industrial heritage. The sett of the tartan is made of exactly 360 threads, evoking a full rotation of a wheel (360 degrees).

The colours were derived from the Institute’s emblem: blue is intended to represent the ocean, green is for the living planet and yellow is for the sun and sky that illuminate discovery.

name: Bosworth, A (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for family use only. May only be woven/reproduced with permission from the family.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Andrew Bosworth and his family using colours from a historical Coat of Arms connected to the family.

name: Warped Weavers - Acton Creative Community
restrictions: Yes. Credit to be given to designer is a courtesy.
registrationNotes: The Warped Weavers tartan was designed in honour and recognition of Chris Acton and the Acton Creative Community of weavers she created, supports and fosters, and all the members who make it a fulfilling, active, creative weaving community. This supportive group of weavers exists to share their work, ask and answer questions, and bond over looms & shuttles. The colour palette and thread count were voted on and approved by the community.

name: Clan Kirkpatrick Society
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the Clan Kirkpatrick Society to request permission to weave.
registrationNotes: Designed by Mr Harold A Edington Jr in March 2021 for the Clan Kirkpatrick Society, the tartan is intended to acknowledge the close historical association between the Kirkpatricks of Closeburn and the Colquhouns, through a similarity to the Colquhoun tartan, but also recognising the role in Scottish history played by Sir Roger Kirkpatrick in 1306 at Greyfriars Kirk and his act to ‘Make Sure’ in his support of Robert the Bruce.

name: MacPhedran Dress
registrationNotes: This dress tartan was based on the original MacPhedran tartan. The colours used are intended to reflect nature and the ties that bind the MacPhedrans.

name: Douglas, Rob Roy, Nevada (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Douglas family of Reno, Nevada or anyone with permission of Robert or Yalilet Douglas only. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Douglas family in Reno, Nevada, United States.

name: Afternoon Tea / Black Tea No.45
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Sazaby League ICL Company.
registrationNotes: One of a range of designs for Sazaby League ICL Company's Afternoon Tea brand. This tartan was designed to celebrate Afternoon Tea's 45th anniversary. The colours are intended to evoke the gentle smokiness, rich depth, and smooth, lingering sweetness of premium tea.

name: Afternoon Tea / Almond Green Tea
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Sazaby League ICL Company.
registrationNotes: One of a range of designs for Sazaby League ICL Company's Afternoon Tea brand.

name: Dhanda Singh, J & Kaur, H and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Use and production to be overseen by primary custodians Gurjit K Nijjar, Hardeep K Nijjar & Jujhar S Dhanda, with major decisions requiring two. If only one remains, authority passes to secondary custodians Harveer, Ruben, Simarpreet, Gian Nijjar & future descendants of Jujhar S Dhanda at 21, with decisions ideally agreed by a majority. If no-one can be traced, it can be made public.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for a Scottish Sikh family whose roots in Scotland reach back nearly a century and to reflect the unity of their Scottish and Sikh identities. It intended to be a tribute to generations who have contributed to Scottish society and a legacy for all relatives, and descendants of Jaswinder Singh and Harjinder Kaur Dhanda to wear with pride. Colours: brown represents the family's farming origins in Punjab; blue is for both the Saltire and the uniform of their great-grandfather, Nihang warrior Kanwal Singh Dhanda; orange is intended to reflect the Sikh principles of courage, equality, and service; and black is for balance and structure.

name: Lamanna, A & C and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Antonio Lamanna and his family and those of their friends and supporters they may approve. May only be woven with written permission from Mr Lamanna, or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan designed for Antonio Lamanna and his family. The design was inspired by the Fraser of Struy tartan and the landscapes of the Central Highlands, particularly the area between Inverness and Loch Ness, which hold a special historical and cultural significance for the family. From this geographical and symbolic synthesis, the family refer to the tartan colloquially as ‘Inverloch’. The colours reflect the Mackenzie tradition - deep blues and greens contrasted with black and white - reinterpreted to form a sett that is intended to represent the identity of the Lamanna family.

name: OkieZarks
registrationNotes: The OkieZarks tartan was designed to commemorate the Scottish Highlander and Scots Irish settlers in, and the Cherokee people who were moved to, the Ozark Plateau extending into North Eastern Oklahoma (Okie=Oklahoman, Zarks=Ozark plateau).

name: Ballanti, J & H and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Ballanti family using the colours from the Ballanti-Hanrahan wedding on 7 October 2025 and to commemorate their honeymoon in Scotland and the UK.

name: Institution Saint Pie X
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by all Dominicans of the Holy Spirit within the Institution Saint Pie X, the pupils of the Saint Pie X schools and their families, and in general, all followers and supporters of the causes of the Institution Saint Pie X. May only be woven/reproduced by order of the Institution Saint Pie X authorities and the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Institution Saint Pie X, a French Catholic church community of Mothers in the Dominican Order of the Holy Spirit, and a teaching institution, notably with a school in Saint-Cloud, France.

name: Erskine College
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Erskine College, located in South Carolina, United States. Erskine College was founded in 1839. The design includes the College's colours, gold and garnet.

name: Deakin, B (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of B, Deakin and his family. To use this tartan permission must be obtained from Bryan's relatives or The House of Edgar. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Bryan Deakin to celebrate his 90th birthday. The red and white are intended to represent Arsenal Football Club, Bryan's favourite team.

name: Saunders, M & K and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Saunders family. Colours: black is intended to represent strength in family; red for connectedness; blue for the sky and aspirations and green is intended to represent earth and the act of coming home.

name: Morkus, R & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Morkus family from Rumburk, in the Czech Republic. Colours: blue is intended to represent trust and stability; green reflects the forests and landscape of North Bohemia; purple is for respect, dignity and honour; orange signifies strength and energy, and white is for clarity, truth, and loyalty.

name: Keady, Kevin, Boston (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the family, friends and associates of Col. Kevin Keady of Williamsburg, Virginia, USA.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed to commemorate the life of Col. Kevin Keady of Williamsburg, Virginia USA, by his son-in-law. Kevin Keady was born and raised in Boston Massachusetts of proud Irish heritage. He spent his life in the US army rising to the rank of colonel. The colours are intended to celebrate the important influences and passions of Col. Keady’s life: greens for his Irish ancestry; yellow, representing gold, is drawn from the US army uniform and red for his love for the Boston Red Sox baseball team.

name: Blue Ochils
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Jon Morgan, Jon James Designs, 471 Blair Place, Fife, Glenrothes, KY7 4RE.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan for Jon James Designs.

name: Texas Declaration of Independence
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: On March 2, 1836, delegates gathered at Washington-on-the-Brazos and declared Texas independent from Mexico, adopting the Texas Declaration of Independence. This moment marked the birth of the Republic of Texas and forever shaped its history. This tartan commemorates that fateful day with colours drawn from historic lone star flags and a pattern built on the numbers 3, 2, 18, and 36.

name: Bahanda, Sundeep & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of the Bahanda family. Permission to weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought from Bahanda Family and Araminta Campbell Ltd.
registrationNotes: Anshu Bahanda commissioned this tartan as a gift to her husband Sundeep, from herself and their two daughters Anunya and Amaara. The design is intended to reflect the family’s rich international heritage, blending elements of their roots. The blue-grey and forest green within the tartan pay homage to Sundeep’s ties to London and Glasgow, two cities that hold profound significance in his life. Sundeep and Anshu’s Indian Heritage is celebrated through a diverse palette inspired by the country’s vibrant culture, traditions, and landscapes; saffron red, turmeric yellow, forest green and salmon pink. Anunya and Amaara are represented in the design in the salmon pink and turmeric yellow checks.

name: Auer, Ryan & Connery, Jennie and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Jennie Connery, Ryan Auer and immediate family. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Jennie Connery, Ryan Auer and immediate family; and Araminta Campbell Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Ryan Auer & Jennie Connery and their family. The colours feature a dark ground with checks of ice blue, Dijon yellow, green and red, inspired by the family’s love of Scotland's August hues. Their two daughters are intended to be represented in the two main checks of the design, while the entire family of four is symbolised within the grey and blue checks.

name: Balmoral Group
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Balmoral Group. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Balmoral Group and Araminta Campbell Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate The Balmoral Group’s 45th anniversary. The sett includes a grey check of 45 threads to represent 45 years of the company; grey also reflects Aberdeen’s granite. Colours: blue is intended to represent Balmoral Tanks; the yellow, representing gold, double tram lines symbolise the four original employees and acknowledge the chairman’s knighthood; dark blue reference the founding year, 1980, with each containing 40 threads to form 80. Sir Jim Milne’s birthday is referenced through 12 grey threads for December, framed by 26 black threads for the 26th, and 40 dark blue threads for 1940. Red is included as the group’s core brand colour.

name: Lanfermann, David & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lanfermann family. The sett, featuring grey tones, is intended to represent continuity, clarity and a timeless sense of style, with contrasting accents to symbolise heritage, craftsmanship and the connection between generations.

name: Colvin, Warren & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used with permission from the Colvin family. Please contact registrant before weaving, the family may wish to be included in the order to save costs for all.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Warren Colvin and his family. Colours: the black, blue, red, and orange together are intended to represent the favourite colours and birth order of the four Colvin children; red represents the family’s connection and the fondness shared for each other's company; and black and white are intended to signify a commitment to them from their father, Warren.

name: Magic Of Unicorn
restrictions: Yes. Prior written consent to weave/use/reproduce the tartan is required from the owner and copyright holder of the tartan, Tania Pramschufer, Magic of Unicorn Ltd. All enquiries should be sent to [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan for Magic of Unicorn Ltd inspired by the legendary creature, the unicorn. The colours in this tartan are intended to be vivid and uplifting, with purple, pink, turquoise, green, gold and white, colours chosen to evoke the enchanting nature of this legendary creature. Each colour is intended to reflect aspects of the unicorn’s symbolism; its mystical energy, its protective spirit, and the sense of wonder it inspires. Together, the design celebrates the magic, joy, and unity of the unicorn and Scottish tradition. The sister tartan Auld Magic of Unicorn (SRT # 14592) offers a classic take on the same enchanting theme.

name: Caledonia Dreamin’
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Craig Halley, Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: The Caledonia Dreamin’ tartan was inspired by Scotland’s national football team qualifying for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The tartan is intended to be a vibrant celebration of Scottish spirit, sporting ambition, and eternal hope.

name: Gahn, Martha (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn with permission from the family. This tartan can only be woven by Nicolson Kiltmakers Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the family and descendants of Martha Gahn. The colours were inspired by the Colquhoun tartan, along with yellow and blue from the Swedish flag.

name: Heritage of Khan
restrictions: Yes. Please contact [email protected] for usage.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Heritage of Khan, a project designed to honour the shared history, journeys, and evolving identity associated with the name Khan and those who bear it. Colours: green is intended to represent the landscapes and natural environments that have shaped communities over time; white is for purity, peace, and unity; yellow is for honour, legacy, and the historical significance of the name Khan; black represents resilience and strength and blue was inspired by the Saltire, Scotland’s national flag, as well as the waters that connect homelands across continents. Together, these elements are intended to recognise the historical origins, ongoing journeys, and the shared identity that unites the Heritage of Khan.

name: Bebykh, I & Sobczyk, K and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Bebykh & Sobczyk family and those of their friends and supporters they may approve. Weaving or reproduction of this tartan is only permitted with the explicit written consent of the designer, Kacper Sobczyk.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Bebykh & Sobczyk family to celebrate their heritage and identity. Colours: blue and yellow are intended to represent Ukraine; white and red represent Poland; green symbolises nature, along with happiness, joy, and peace.

name: Prevot, R & C and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used exclusively by the immediate family of the owner.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Romain and Constance Prevot, and their family, using colours of personal significance.

name: McMahon, Gordon and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Gordon McMahon and his family, designed by his daughter and granddaughter.

name: Christie, G and Spear, C & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Christie, G, Spear, C & their family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 21st wedding anniversary of G Christie and C Spear. The colours were inspired by the flowers from their first wedding - hydrangeas of lilacs, purples, and creamy whites. Blue is intended to represent Scotland and red & brown are for Australia and the Outback.

name: Ishga
restrictions: Yes. Tartan use/weaving/reproduction is at the discretion of Ishga Limited.
registrationNotes: The tartan’s colour palette was inspired by Ishga’s brand colours and the natural beauty of the Outer Hebrides, including a seaweed-inspired tone. The design is intended to reflect the purity and simplicity of Ishga’s natural ingredients. Within the threadcount, the sequence 58, 2, 6, 4 reflects the geographic coordinates of Ishga’s head office in Stornoway, creating a connection between place, brand, and design.

name: Lainders, M & C (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Maxime & Claire Lainders, which is a union of their two surnames, Laine and Colders. The design was inspired by the land of Île de Groix in Brittany, France. Colours: the greens are intended to represent the natural textures of Groix including the grass, ferns, and moss; orange and yellow were inspired by the warm tones found on the island and autumn leaves from the season of their wedding and purple can be found in Groix’s land, but also connects to their wedding location in the Beaujolais region.

name: Smith, Alexander and Camp, Mary Elizabeth - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Alexander Smith, Mary Elizabeth Camp and their family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required by Alexander Smith, Mary Elizabeth Camp and Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Alexander Smith and Mary Elizabeth Camp to celebrate their wedding. The colours were inspired by the sunsets in the Teton mountain range in eastern Idaho, United States, a place of love and comfort for the family, where they spend a significant amount of time together.

name: MacGideon, Joseph & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the MacGideon family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce the tartan is required from the MacGideon family & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the union of the MacKoul and Gideon families, forming the MacGideon family, using colours of personal significance.

name: Barbisan-Treffel, Jean-Mary and Christine Dress (Personal)
registrationNotes: A dress version of the ‘Barbisan-Treffel, Jean-Mary and Christine (Personal)’ tartan (SRT #12215).

name: Donnelly-Boyle, Robyn & Chris (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of Robyn & Chris Donnelly Boyle. Prepared for weaving by Taffled Threads. Please contact Taffled threads for any enquiries
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the marriage of Robyn & Chris in Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Clauran Scarf, The - Cairngorms Red
registrationNotes: The Clauran Scarf was designed for NavyGrey and is intended to be a tribute to their heritage, inspired by their founder’s Scottish roots. Clauran, the Scottish Gaelic word for thistle, is intended to reflect both Scotland and the spirit behind the piece.

name: Clauran Scarf, The - Linnhe Blue
registrationNotes: The Clauran Scarf was designed for NavyGrey and is intended to be a tribute to their heritage, inspired by their founder’s Scottish roots. Clauran, the Scottish Gaelic word for thistle, is intended to reflect both Scotland and the spirit behind the piece.

name: Todorovic, Zvonko & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Designed for Mr. Zvonko Todorovic, all rights regarding this tartan are owned by him, transferred to him by Darren Poole, designer.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Zvonko Todorovic and his family. The colours were inspired by a Coat of Arms connected to the family and the flag of the country of their origin, Serbia.

name: Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity
restrictions: Yes. The Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity tartan should not be used in the promotion of any activity/product associated with alcohol, tobacco, and adult entertainment. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of MacNaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created to mark the 25th Anniversary of Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity. As partner charity to Scotland's busiest and largest children's hospital, the charity fundraise to ensure every baby, child and young person treated at the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow, receive the extra special care they deserve.

name: Scotland Can Boogie
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven or replicated by the designers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Scotland Can Boogie and was inspired by Scotland's Men's National Team qualifying for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The tartan design celebrates the designers, located in Canada, travelling to their first World Cup and includes the colours from the Saltire and the Lion Rampant.

name: Creer, Dain and Kala (Personal)
designer: Houston Kiltmakers and Creer, Dain and Kala
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be for use by Dain and Kala Creer only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Dain and Kala Creer. It is intended to celebrate their love and honour Dain Creer’s service in the United States Special Forces, where he served with distinction for over twenty years. Following his retirement from military service, his commitment to others continued through his work as a firefighter. Dain and Kala share a deep love of the outdoors, particularly the mountains. The colours of the tartan are intended to reflect Dain’s service, their connection to nature and enduring love.

name: Lumo
designer: MacDonald, Ken; Scott, Gerry & Salkeld, Richard
registrationNotes: The Lumo tartan was designed to celebrate the innovative all-electric train company Lumo and its sustainable service connecting London, Stevenage, Newcastle, Morpeth, Edinburgh, Falkirk and Glasgow. Colours: the blues are intended to reflect the company’s signature colours and Scotland’s flag; white represents Lumo’s distinctive white logo; red is from England’s flag and the one consistent colour across the tartans of Edinburgh, Glasgow and Stirling’s tartans and black is for Northumberland and London.

name: Kirkpatrick, J & Family, Annandale (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone with the surname Kirkpatrick, Kilpatrick, or any variation of those names or any descendant of James Kirkpatrick. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for John P Kirkpatrick and family from Ellsinore, Missouri, United States, a descendant of the James Kirkpatrick who left Annandale in Scotland, moved to Ireland, and from there settled in South Carolina in the 18th century. Later generations moved to Tennessee, Georgia, Missouri, and across the United States. The colours were inspired by the Douglas tartan recalling the connection between the Douglas and Kirkpatrick families. The design incorporates the Kirkpatrick saltire (blue in a white field) within a St Andrew’s Saltire.

name: T-Uilebheist Dorcha, An
restrictions: Yes. Can only be woven with permission from Radical Weavers Limited.
registrationNotes: The An T-Uilebheist Dorcha tartan (The Dark Monster) was designed during the V&A Dundee’s tartan exhibition by Peter Dickie as part of the Radical Weavers’ “Warp On The Wild Side” residency.

name: Nature, Time, Measure
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Björn Harting and their family. Others may also use this tartan with prior written consent from Björn Harting. Prior approval to weave/reproduce required by Björn Harting Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan inspired by nature, time and historical traditions. Colours: dark green forms the ground colour and is intended to represent nature, continuity, and stability; dark brown evokes connections to land and tradition; white is for clarity; red was inspired by its use in traditional tartans; yellow is for warmth and purple is intended to symbolise creativity, dignity, and individuality.

name: Geraud, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used only by the members of the family who are authorised by Sixtine or Morgan. Copyright rests with the designer, Sixtine Geraud. Contact : [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of Morgan Lagerige and Sixtine Geraud. The colours are intended to be a blend representing Morgan and Sixtine respectively, creating a design for their newly formed family.

name: Weston, Jeffrey and Jennifer (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Weston family to celebrate the history, shared identity and values of the family. The design was inspired by Highlands, using layered greens and blues to reflect forests, hills, and enduring terrain. Five principal bands within the sett represent the five members of the family.

name: Dun, M and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Dun family using colours from a historic Coat of Arms connected to the family.

name: Lippe, M & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lippe family, who reside in north-east Scotland, with roots in Aberdeenshire. The colours are intended to evoke the granite landscape, farmland, coastline, and subdued natural tones of the north-east. This tartan is intended to be a respectful and historically grounded form of family representation.

name: Trujillo-Sebold, G & B and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by members of the Trujillo-Sebold family and those with a personal or familial connection. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Trujillo-Sebold family to symbolize resilience, unity, and the enduring value of hardship. Colours: red and yellow are intended to represent strength and perseverance, drawn from one side of the family; the light and dark blues reflect introspection, loyalty, and balance from the other side.

name: Home of Golf, The
designer: House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Copyright MacNaughton Holdings Ltd. This tartan is produced by House of Edgar for the sole use of St Andrews Links Trust and/or The Home of Golf Ltd. Prepared for weaving by the House of Edgar, a division of MacNaughton Holdings Ltd.
registrationNotes: The Home of Golf tartan was designed as a corporate tartan for use on merchandise for The Home of Golf Ltd (a subsidiary of St Andrews Links Trust). The tartan sett is reflective of the companies’ colour palette, that has been created to celebrate the beauty of the St Andrews natural landscape and landmarks.

name: HeliOffshore
restrictions: Yes. By permission of the CEO or company secretary of HeliOffshore Limited, details can be found at www.helioffshore.org or companies house.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent the branding of the HeliOffshore Limited organisation and to commemorate the founder and first chairman, William E Chiles (Houston, Texas), on his retirement from the role.

name: Bell, Andrew Ronald and Family Dress (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used by the family of Andrew Ronald Ball or those permitted by lineal descendants of the late Sir Ronald Bell and their spouses. This tartan may be woven by any weaver authorised by Andrew Ronald Bell or any appointed agent.
registrationNotes: A dress tartan based on the personal tartan for Andrew Ronald Bell and his family using colours of personal significance.

name: Bell, Andrew Ronald and Family (2025) (Personal)
designer: Bell, Andrew Ronald & Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Andrew Bell and his family. and those of their friends and supporters they may approve. May only be woven with written permission from Mr Bell, or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: A personal design for Andrew Bell and his family inspired by tartans historically used by family members including MacNab, Macallum, MacMillan and Douglas. This tartan commemorates the 2025 celebrations of the 70th birthdays of Andrew and Stephanie Bell and the 40th birthday of their first child Alexandra and the birth of their granddaughter Serena. The dominant red reflects the colour associated with family celebrations – the holly of Christmas and the red envelopes of Chinese New Year which they celebrated while in Hong Kong. This design refers to and was inspired by 18th century tartan fashion.

name: McCuaig-Nishikawa, Ian & Kimiko and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only by members of the McCuaig, Nishikawa and Paisley families. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the wedding of Ian McCuaig and Kimiko Nishikawa. Tartan is based on the McCuaig (Glenelg and the Western Isles) Hunting (SRT #11347) and Paisley tartans.

name: Ailes Françaises, Les
designer: Duclos, Richard & The House of Edgar
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: The Les Ailes Françaises tartan (French: The French Wings) was designed to honour French flying history. It features navy blue which is intended to represent the sky, along with red, white and blue as a nod to the cocardes on the side of some French planes, and the French flag.

name: Baumgärtel, Linus & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the Baumgärtel family only.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Linus Baumgärtel and his family. The binary code for 29 has been incorporated into the design for Linus’ birthday, 2nd September, and his jersey number. The colours are of personal significance and are intended to represent reliability.

name: Andrews, Pauline & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Pauline Andrews and immediate family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Andrews family from Caithness, Inverness and Kirkcaldy. The chosen colours were inspired by a family trip to the Kirkcaldy area; blue for the lochs and brown for the heath.

name: Lefevre, B & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended usage of this tartan is restricted to the designer and their direct descendants or ancestors. Others may wear or use the tartan upon providing proof of lineage or obtaining explicit written permission from the current owner/head of the family. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lefevre family. Colours: black is intended to symbolise continuity and stability; green represents growth and connection; red, white and blue reflect the families broader cultural connections.

name: Black, D (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the family, friends, and associates of Daniel Black (with permission). Weaving can only be conducted if permission is granted by the tartan owner.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Daniel Black, an inventor and engineer. The colours of the tartan are intended to represent and celebrate the influences, passions, and themes which are important to Daniel: black after Daniel’s surname, the vacuum where inspiration forms, and the courage to dive into the unknown; dark blue for deep thought, blue-sky thinking, and multi-disciplined research; dark green for intellect, pride, ambition, and determination; grey, representing silver, for the tools of engineers, prototypes, and clarity of thought; yellow, representing gold, for the rewards of hard work, eureka moments, the optimism in pursuit of ideas, and the ‘gold standard’ in quality.

name: CTSI (Chartered Trading Standards Institute)
registrationNotes: The Chartered Trading Standards Institute (CTSI) commissioned this tartan to commemorate its annual conference, held in Glasgow in 2026. This tartan was designed to serve both marketing and media purposes, to promote the institute and its activities during the event. The colours selected for the tartan are drawn directly from the official CTSI corporate palette, ensuring the design represents the institute's identity and branding.

name: Araminta Campbell – Autumn Woodland Walk
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive the use of Araminta Campbell Ltd. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Drawing inspiration from the beech woodlands surrounding her family home in Aberdeenshire, this tartan is designed by Araminta Campbell and intended to capture the seasonal colours of a walk through woodlands during autumn. The tartan and its colours were inspired by the vibrant hues of the landscape; the moss-covered tree trunks, the fiery reds and oranges of fallen leaves, and the deep greens of the canopy. Using a natural plant dyeing process, Araminta meticulously colour matched each yarn to reflect the shades found in this autumnal landscape.

name: Araminta Campbell – Amber Riverbank
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Araminta Campbell Ltd. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Drawing inspiration from the River Dee and the landscape surrounding her childhood home in Aberdeenshire, this tartan design, by Araminta Campbell, is intended to capture the changing colours of the riverbank in autumn. The colours were inspired by nature: soft oranges of the turning larch trees, deep orange bracken carpeting the woodland floor, deep green of the Scots pines, yellows of autumn leaves, and navy and black reflecting the river’s depths. Using her knowledge of natural dyeing, Araminta meticulously developed each colour from natural materials.

name: Araminta Campbell – West Coast Waters
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Araminta Campbell Ltd. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan and its colours were inspired by walks along the beaches of the west coast of Scotland. Designed by Araminta Campbell, the soft cream evokes the beaches, cool grey reflects the weathered shoreline rocks, deep turquoise mirrors the sea, and vibrant orange depicts flashes of bright lichen clinging to the rocks. Each colour was carefully developed by Araminta using natural dyes to reflect the colours found in the landscape.

name: Araminta Campbell – Cairngorm Frost
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Araminta Campbell Ltd. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan design was inspired by first frost in the Highlands: greys and whites mirror the frost-dusted ridges of the Cairngorms, soft purples reflect the birch trees sparkling lilac in the pale winter sun, and deep green honours the ancient pine forests. Each colour was carefully developed by Araminta Campbell using a natural dye process, to create a palette intended to capture both the landscape and the feeling of being within it.

name: Robinz, R & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This design is intended to represent the divergent background and heritage of the Robinz family and includes colours representing various family branches and other personal meanings.

name: Travelling Wytch, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used by the designer and her authorised representatives under "The Travelling Wytch" brand. Any enquiries for use must be directed to the designer. This tartan is restricted. No person, company or weaving mill may manufacture, sell, or otherwise utilise this design without the express written permission of the designer, Eleanor Marie Dibben.
registrationNotes: A tartan for The Travelling Wytch. It is intended to commemorate the 3,837 individuals accused under the Scottish Witchcraft Act 1563-1736, from the Witches of modern Scotland and a 12 year spiritual journey as ‘The Travelling Witch’ focused on the stories of those accused and offering healing at historic sites. The palette features blue and green intended to represent the Scottish landscape and the Trinity of Earth, Sea and Sky.

name: Cercle de Fermières Neuville
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by members and past members of Cercle de Fermières Neuville or by others with permission. Only members of Cercle de Fermières Neuville can weave this tartan or others with permision. Please contact Cercle de Fermières Neuville to wear/use/weave this tartan. [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the founding of the Cercle de Fermières de Neuville and reflect the women who ensure the transmission of cultural heritage in Québec, Canada. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent the proximity of the St. Lawrence River and the efficiency of the members; green is for the surrounding environment and the dynamism within the Cercle; yellow refers to corn cultivation and creativity; white is for snow and authenticity; blue for the movement of the ice, differences and pride; and red is for fall colours and strength of character.

name: TAF
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn by TAF members. Can only be woven by Ingles Buchan or by permission from Ingles Buchan.
registrationNotes: TAF was founded in 1972 in Glasgow by Colin Findlay and Davie McPhie, the club began with a simple concept: four hillwalking weekends each year and a few beers with the September trip always to an island. Members were given nothing more than a date and grid reference - accommodation a tent or bothy. As popularity grew, brothers Bill Allen and John Allen (Cairngorm John) joined, followed by many more. The tartan colours are intended to reflect Scotland's landscapes and spirit of adventure that has defined TAF - a legacy of hillwalking, camaraderie, and shared memories passed from one generation to the next.

name: Köhler, N (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the family, friends, and associates of J.Noah.K with permission. Weaving can only be conducted if permission is granted by the tartan owner or the tartan designer. IPR rests with Noah which is a gift from the designer, Daniel.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Noah Köhler, a German artist who has spent significant time in Scotland and has a great affinity for its people and culture. The colours are intended to represent the things, themes, and colours which are important to Noah: cream to represent fresh canvas, new beginnings, spring light, and her dog; green for long walks through nature, calm creativity, old trees, and fresh moss; black for inked outlines and sketches, and creative focus; yellow for sunlight, joy, warmth, optimism and the beginning of spring; and brown for familiar trails, tree trunks, soil, and growth.

name: NNEdPro (Scottish Mobile Teaching Kitchen)
restrictions: Yes. Tartan is restricted to NNEdPro only.
registrationNotes: Founded in Cambridge, UK, in 2008, NNEdPro is led by Professor Sumantra (Shumone) Ray and operates through the NNEdPro Global Institute for Food, Nutrition and Health alongside a range of partner initiatives. Together, they work to advance and apply food and nutrition knowledge for the benefit of health and society. Their mission is to improve nutrition-related health outcomes by training professionals, strengthening research, delivering practical solutions, and addressing health inequalities. This tartan was designed specifically for the NNEdPro Scottish Mobile Teaching Kitchen initiative and was woven for their annual summit held in Dundee in 2025. The colours were inspired NNEdPro’s corporate identity, with added yellow and orange to reflect the cultural diversity and character associated with their food and flavour.

name: Plokhov, Igor & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn by those authorised by the copyright holders – the Plokhov family. Cannot be offered for sale or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holders, the Plokhov family. Copyright rests with Igor Plokhov.
registrationNotes: Based on the tartan named after Scottish town of Crieff, first referenced in a letter of 1797, where Igor and Anna Plakhov settled on their arrival from Ukraine in 2020. Blue and yellow from the Ukrainian flag is the focus of the design, flanked by two additional blue lines. Together with the central blue, those are intended to represent Igor & Anna’s three daughters , Khrystyna, Bellakarina and Yeva. Specific thread numbers represent the 21st December 2020, Igor and Anna’s wedding date. The black and white lines symbolise the lines of print in a ‘small book’ which is the translation of Anna’s Jewish father’s surname.

name: Royal Scotsman, A Belmond Train
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Belmond Limited, UK. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Royal Scotsman, A Belmond Train and Araminta Campbell. Copyright rests with The Great Scottish & Western Railway.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for The Royal Scotsman, a Belmond train. The colours are intended to reflect the rugged beauty of the Scottish landscape, with greens and blues inspired by the panoramic views from the window of the train. The three sets of tram lines (double lines) depict the train’s three most illustrious journeys - Scotland's Classic Splendours, Western Scenic Wonders and Taste of the Highlands. Its main check block is made up of 37 threads representing every year the train has been touring the Highlands, reflecting the rich history of The Royal Scotsman. The complete sett is created from 514 threads signifying the number of miles the train travels on one of its routes, whilst the 10 carriages of the train are depicted with 10 threads in the green check.

name: Bogle, J & Family Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and used by anyone of the name or variants such as; Bogle; Boggle; Bogel. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This hunting tartan was designed for Colonel James Stewart Lockhart Bogle and his family. The threadcount was based on the Bogle tartan (STR #11349) registered on 27th August 2015. The sett is based on ancient motifs common to many tartans of the 18th century.

The idea for SDIS 78 to have their own tartan was put forward by Stéphane Millot, Head of Yvelines Fire Brigade. The colours navy, light blue and red are intended to represent the uniforms of the firefighters.

name: Bodart, H & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be restricted to the Bodart family line of the designer, his father, and his brother, including their descendants, and to other bearers of the name with ties to New Caledonia by express permission only.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Bodart family, commemorating their migration from Northern France to New Caledonia. Colours: blue is intended to represent the ocean and seas crossed; white is for the chalky Opal Coast of France and the white sands of their island home; red and dark grey symbolise the transition from the brick and charcoal from their origin in France to the red earth and dark rock of Grande Terre, their new home.

name: BODART & DENIS - Entrelacs
restrictions: Yes. This tartan may only be woven/reproduced/used with the explicit written authorisation from at least one of the designers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for BODART & DENIS as a signature textile for their 2026 fashion collection. The Entrelacs tartan (Interlacing) is intended to explore mathematical series and visual perception, and represent the merging of creative visions during their partnership. The colours are of personal significance for the designers.

name: Brig o Burns
restrictions: Yes. Please contact Robert Burns World Federation regarding use/weaving/reproduction of the tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was commissioned by the Robert Burns World Federation. Inspired by the world famous Burns poem 'A Man's A Man' , it is intended to represents peace, global brotherhood and sisterhood, as Burns said "shall brothers be for a' that". The colours were chosen to best represent the words and sentiments of the poem and were voted for by the members of the Robert Burns World Federation (RBWF) with special thanks to Sir Boyd Tunnock.

name: Free and the Brave, The
restrictions: Yes. May not be woven without express written permission from the tartan's designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the history of the United States. The flag of the United States is intended to be represented by the colours red, white and blue, which have a total six threads for the six military branches. Purple is intended to represent the lyrics ‘purple mountain majesties’ in the song ‘America the Beautiful’, while the brown and dark brown represent the lyrics ‘amber waves of grain’. The thread counts for brown and dark brown represent the fifty-six signatures on the Declaration of Independence.

The threadcount includes the number 24 to reference 2024, the year he became engaged. The colours used are of significance to Nathan and his family.

name: Greenland
restrictions: Yes. Restricted to weaving//use by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd, unless with specific written authorisation.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the long and enduring connection between Scotland and Greenland. From the very first whaling expeditions to Greenland’s coasts in the 1750s, to modern day polar expeditions, Scots men and women have played a key role in both exploration and in furthering our understanding of the Arctic environment and its peoples. Inspired by the Wylie tartan, this tartan pays homage to the Scottish explorer, filmmaker and botanist, Isobel Wylie Hutchison, whose research in Greenland provided a wealth of specimens and seeds for the botanic gardens of Edinburgh and Kew, but she also forged strong friendships with the Greenlanders she met, including the highly respected explorer and anthropologist, Knud Rasmusson - the ‘Father of Inuit Studies’. The red and white of this tartan references the distinctive flag of Greenland, and the pink signifies the hardy ‘Niviarsiaq’, or Dwarf Fireweed, Greenland’s national flower.

name: Douglas, Rob Roy, Nevada Hunting (Personal)
registrationNotes: A hunting tartan for Rob Roy Douglas. It was inspired by hiking and hunting in the Sierra Nevada mountains around Northern Nevada. Colours: green is intended to represent the grass and trees; brown is for the ground above 10,000 feet and the light grey is for light reflecting off the alpine lakes.

name: Mount Royal University
registrationNotes: Mount Royal University (MRU) is a public university located in Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Established in 1910, MRU seeks to solidify its legacy and honour Calgary’s Scottish roots. The tartan is intended to be a symbolic anchor for the institution, incorporating MRU’s signature blues with black and white threads representing the academy’s never-ending quest for truth. An orange thread at the centre of the sett affirms the University’s ongoing work towards truth and reconciliation for Indigenous peoples. In an era of digital change, this tartan is intended to be a timeless nod to the educational traditions that shaped Alberta’s academic landscape, ensuring MRU’s identity is preserved.

name: Puksi
registrationNotes: The Puksi tartan, a term of affection in Hungary, was inspired by the designer’s dogs, two Jack Russell Terrier mix brothers named Jackie and Rusty. The colours within the design also represent their owners/family; green is intended to represent Ticián Máté Balogh and light red is for Judit Rácz-Nagy.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Stirling Centre for Strategic Learning and Innovation. Colours: the blues were inspired by Scotland and the Saltire and blue is often associated with learning, reflection and critical thinking which are core elements of Stirling Centre for Strategic Learning and Innovation; yellow and white are intended to evoke the light and atmosphere of a sunrise over the Scottish Highlands.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Devgun family to celebrate the union of a Sikh & Scottish Family through wedlock, and the heritage of Scotland and Sikh Culture. The colours are intended to represent both families' heritage and culture coming together as one.

name: Goodwin, Robert Preston (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was created as a personal tartan for Robert Preston Goodwin and his family by his daughter, Madeline Goodwin, in recognition of his life and the enduring legacy of adventure, joy, and love he has left with those around him. The colours hold personal significance: dark green is intended to reflect the mountains he so deeply loves; red represents his favourite colour and spirited nature; and white signifies clarity, warmth, and the bonds of family and music that define his life.

name: Fukae, M & Family (2026) (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to reflect the diverse heritage of the Fukae family. Colours: black is for strength and resilience, drawing from the Japanese Fukae line and the German Frey family; green signifies continuity and connection to the land, honouring the family's Scottish Border ancestry through the Nicholson and Hogg Clans; light grey is intended to symbolise clarity and craftsmanship, a nod to their Farrow/Ferrow lineage and red represents the enduring family bloodline that unites these traditions.

name: Heritage of Liberty
restrictions: Yes. Weaving and sale of this tartan are restricted to UTKilts, with permission granted by the registrant.
registrationNotes: The Heritage of Liberty tartan was designed to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and the ties between Scotland and America. The design is intended to reflect continuity, resilience, and shared heritage, acknowledging the influence of Scottish people and traditions on early American settlement, civic life, and concepts of self-governance. The colours are intended to represent shared historical significance: blue for endurance; buff for the land itself and as a reference to its historical use in early American military dress; red for courage & sacrifice; white for balance and clarity and yellow, representing gold, for prosperity and the future.

registrationNotes: This tartan marks the joining of the Stewart and Leader families through marriage. By blending their signature wedding colours with the symbolism of the 'Invisible Golden Thread' (a centuries-old metaphor for the unbreakable bond between two people that represents the idea of a connection that exists outside the constraints of time, distance, or circumstance), this tartan is intended to capture a connection that was always meant to be.

registrationNotes: The No Scotland No Party tartan was designed in collaboration with Slanj Kilts and musician, Nick Morgan, songwriter of the unofficial anthem for fans of Scotland’s Men’s National Football Team. The design is intended to capture the vibrance of the flags of the 3 host nations for the FIFA World Cup 2026; USA, Mexico and Canada.

name: Singleton, The
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: The Singleton’s award-winning Glen Ord Distillery is situated in the heart of the Black Isle near Inverness. This tartan is intended to reflect the brand’s look and was designed in collaboration with Diageo as part of a larger collection. The colours were inspired by the evening sky at the distillery in the Scottish Highlands and uses teal with orange/copper which are the distinctive colours of the brands identity.

name: Talisker Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: The Talisker Distillery is nestled by the sea on the shores of Loch Harport, with the rocky Cuillin Hills as a backdrop. The coastlines surrounding the distillery were the inspiration for the Talisker tartan, intended to capture a small piece of Skye. It was designed in collaboration with Diageo as part of a larger collection. The colours of the sea with copper tones are intended to represent the smokey peat, sea-salt flavours of the whisky.

name: Oban Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: Oban is one of Scotland’s oldest licensed distilleries, the town's sheltered harbour is perfect for seafaring and whisky-making. Founded in 1794 by Hugh Stevenson, a local merchant and entrepreneur, the distillery has formed part of the town’s backbone ever since. This tartan takes its colours from the distillery itself, built in 1794; the grey of its stone walls, the slate of its roof and the prominent red of its iconic chimney – a tribute to the town’s spirit and craftmanship. The Oban Distillery tartan was designed in collaboration with Diageo as part of a larger collection.

name: Lagavulin Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: The Lagavulin distillery is situated in a secluded bay in the Isle of Islay and has been crafted for over two centuries. This tartan was inspired by the windswept landscapes that surround the distillery and the Whisky’s smoky, peaty character. The white is intended to evoke the beaches on Islay’s southern shore, and the copper tones represent rich, smoky whisky. The Lagavulin Distillery tartan was designed in collaboration with Diageo as part of a larger collection.

name: Glenkinchie Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: The Glenkinchie distillery is fifteen miles from the Scottish capital, surrounded by fields of barley and the green Lammermuir Hills rolling north towards the Firth of Forth. This tartan was designed in collaboration with Diageo and was inspired by the malt’s light bodied, floral character with the light grey and cream tones. The dark grey and green are a nod to the Lammermuir hills, and light brown, representing gold, is intended to symbolise the colour of the Glenkinchie whisky.

name: Clynelish Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: The Clynelish distillery is located on the coast across the road from Brora. The barley that makes Clynelish is malted in the Northern Highlands of Scotland and water is pumped down from the Clynemilton Burn to the distillery. The colours in this tartan were inspired by the elusive Scottish Wildcat that appears on every bottle, a nod to its founder, the Duke of Sutherland with a subtle hint of copper to symbolise the rich, waxy whisky. The tartan was designed in collaboration with Diageo as part of a larger collection.

name: Cardhu Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: Cardhu distillery was successfully run by two generations of pioneering women. Helen and Elizabeth Cumming were treasured for their determination, skill, generosity, and loyalty to the community, forever defining Cardhu, named after the Scottish Gaelic for 'Black Rock'. This tartan was designed in collaboration with Diageo and is intended to represent the spirit of Cardhu Single Malt Scotch Whisky. It was inspired by Cardhu's rich history, telling the story of the Cumming family. The design is woven with red and gold intended to represent the whisky’s notes of fruit and spice.

name: Caol Ila Distillery
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and woven with the approval of Diageo/Scotland Brand Homes.
registrationNotes: In 1846, Hector Henderson chose a remote site to build his Caol Ila distillery on the shores of the Sound of Islay, overlooking the Paps of Jura. Craftspeople continue his traditional methods of malt whisky production to ensure the quality of Caol Ila malt whisky is ever-present. The barley used is malted locally at Port Ellen and spring water rises from limestone in nearby Loch Nam Burn, then falls to the sea at Caol Ila. Pronounced 'Cull Eela', it’s the Scottish Gaelic name for the Sound of Islay, which separates the island from Jura. The colours in the Caol Ila tartan are inspired by the distillery’s picturesque location on the rugged eastern coast of Scotland. The charcoal colours in the tartan also link to the Whisky’s smoky flavour, designed in collaboration with Diageo.

name: Moyes, J & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Moyes Family. Colours: blue is intended to represent loyalty, protection, and wisdom; green is for peace, humility, and the sage-covered land; yellow is for light and joy; and red is intended to represent courage, love, and the strength of kinship.

name: Halifax Mussels Inclusive Hockey Society
restrictions: Yes. Intended for members of the Halifax Mussels. May only be woven/reproduced at the team's discretion.
registrationNotes: The Halifax Mussels tartan was designed to honour of the founder’s 50th birthday and the Society’s 10-year anniversary in 2027. The design is intended to celebrate the Queer and Ally players and coaches who make up the Mussels community. The blue, pink, and white reflect the team’s Home and Away jerseys. Together, these elements are intended to represent the Halifax Mussels’ commitment to creating a safe, welcoming space for adults to learn to play hockey, build confidence, and foster inclusion, respect and pride both on and off the ice.

name: Millar, Euan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn with permission from the Euan Millar. This tartan can only be woven by Nicolson Kiltmakers Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Euan Millar to be worn at his wedding and to serve as a lasting family symbol that can be passed to future generations.

name: Deken’s Traveling Dino
restrictions: Yes. The tartan can be worn by anyone who wishes to support Deken's Traveling Dino. Please contact Warren regarding weaving and use at [email protected] or Instagram @DEKENS.DINO
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for Deken's Traveling Dinosaur. In 2011, Deken gave his favourite toy dinosaur to his soldier father before his tour to Afghanistan. A social media page was set up and people are able to follow the dinosaur, which has since travelled the world and has had many adventures, through their webpage.

name: Sciprint
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Sciprint and its employees. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be sought from the owner. Please contact: Sciprint Limited, Unit 7, 12 Easter Inch Road, Easter Inch Industrial Estate, Bathgate, EH48 2FH [email protected]
registrationNotes: A tartan for the company Sciprint Ltd using colours reflecting the company’s logo and brand colours.

name: Simpson, William and Janet & Family, Prince Edward Island (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the descendants of William and Janet Simpson, who left Scotland in 1775 with their young family and shipwrecked on the shores of what would become Prince Edward Island, Canada. The tartan commemorates 250 years of the family’s history and presence on the Island. In 2025, the Simpson family recognised the 250th anniversary through a number of commemorative events and heritage projects, undertaken with the goal of preserving and sharing the family’s history. This tartan is intended to be a visual record of migration, settlement, and community, reflecting both the family’s Scottish origins and the landscape and life established in Prince Edward Island. Colours: red is intended to represent the red earth and cliffs of Prince Edward Island; light blue is for the sky; blue is for Atlantic Ocean; light brown is intended to reflect the dunes and sandy beaches of Cavendish.

name: Teatino, V & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave must be attained by email from Vittorio Teatino and weaving to be arranged through Wales Tartan Centres.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Teatino family, who are connected to the Contrada della Chiocciola, one of the 17 contrade (districts) of Siena, Italy. The colours of the tartan were inspired by the colours of the contrade; red and yellow in equal parts with bands of blue.

name: Thistle and Vine
registrationNotes: The Thistle and Vine tartan was inspired by the designer’s Scottish heritage and his wife's Middle Eastern heritage. The colours are intended to represent; thistle, wheat and grapes.

name: Misiak, Katarzyna (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Katarzyna Misiak by her husband as a symbol of love and commitment. The design is intended to capture Katarzyna’s deep personal connection to Scotland, whose landscapes, traditions, and folklore have long inspired her. The Highlands remind her of the natural beauty and cultural spirit of her homeland. The colours are intended to represent loyalty, love, growth, celebration, and honour. The threadcount incorporates her birth date.

name: Garbo-Yacoubian, Margaret & Jamie (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Margaret & Jamie Garbo-Yacoubian. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Margaret Garbo and Jamie Yacoubian in celebration of their wedding and to be passed to future generations of loved ones. The colours and design draw on themes significant to both their Scottish and Filipino heritage. The threadcount references meaningful milestones and is intended to make the tartan a permanent record of their love.

name: Brownlee, Douglas (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Douglas Brownlee by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. May be woven by anyone who is a descendant of the Lairds of Torfoot, Lanarkshire, Scotland and has familial links to the Brownlee surname. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with Douglas Brownlee
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for the Brownlee family and has been named for Douglas, a name he shared with his late father. The colours in the tartan have personal family meaning; dark blue and black are intended to represent ‘dubh glas’ while the other colours acknowledge a love of the Scottish countryside.

name: Sharkey, R & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with the approval of Ryan Sharkey, or any descendants of Ryan Sharkey. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of Ryan Sharkey by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Fiona Sharkey and Ryan Sharkey's wedding, their love for Scotland and its nature, along with the intent of passing this tartan on to future generations.

name: Illinois State University
restrictions: Yes. Persons may not use this tartan without express permission from Illinois State University. Anyone wishing to produce or weave this tartan must have permission from Illinois State University.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Illinois state University, United States. The tartan is intended to be used to enhance school spirit and serve as part of the University’s brand.

name: Cercle de Fermières Saint-Gilbert
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be exclusive to members of the group Cercle de Fermières Saint-Gilbert. May not be woven/reproduced without permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Association of Cercles de Fermières Saint-Gilbert. The goal of their members is to improve the living conditions for women and families and to promote the transmission of cultural and artisanal heritage. Their members share their knowledge and skills in textile arts: weaving, sewing, knitting, crochet, embroidery, and other techniques.

name: Hancock, M & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to mark the family wedding in June 2027 and to be used by Hancock family and future generations. The tartan was inspired by the Gordon tartan. The orange and white are intended to represent the colours from Blackpool's coat of arms, where the Hancock family originates.

name: Wolfworthy
restrictions: Yes. Intended for Wolfworthy's use and their related commercial activities. This tartan can only be woven or reproduced with prior written consent from Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Wolfworthy, makers of natural, whole-prey inspired dog food. The design reflects Wolfworthy’s branding and its roots in the British countryside. Colours: blue is intended to evoke sky and water; red reflects warmth and vitality; yellow is for energy and nourishment and green represents fields and forests where healthy, well-fed dogs roam. Together, the colours are intended to celebrate the bond between people, their dogs, and the wild ancestry that inspires the Wolfworthy diet.

name: Purewal, N (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Nasdeep Purewal. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Purewal family to commemorate ten years since the family first planted roots in Scotland. The design was influenced by the Baxter tartan, reflecting an association with Dean Village in Edinburgh. The thread count includes numerical references to significant family milestones, including a fortieth birthday and a decade in Scotland. The colours were selected to reflect the family’s heritage and their historical connections to India, Kenya, and Coventry.

name: Anchors Aweigh
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone, past or present, who has honourably served or wishes to honour one who has honourably served in at sea. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The Anchors Aweigh tartan was inspired by those who spend their time at sea, protecting the waters and those on it. Colours: blue and gold were inspired by sailors' uniforms: red is intended to represent lives lost at sea; grey for ship hulls; and blue for the sky and deep oceans.

name: First Troop Philadelphia City Cavalry
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Active Roll, Non-Active Roll, and Honorary Roll members of the First Troop Philadelphia City Cavalry, in good standing, only.
registrationNotes: The tartan was designed for the First Troop Philadelphia City Cavalry, the oldest, continuously serving, mounted unit, in the United States Army, founded in 1774. Colours: red, white and blue are intended to represent the American Flag; brown and gold are the official colours of the First Troop Philadelphia City Cavalry as brown is representative of the uniform the Troop wore during the American Revolution, and gold is representative of the colour of the Markoe Standard, the official and original guidon of the unit.

name: Quinn, R, D & T (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Ryland Quinn and his sons, Danny and Tendai. It is intended to celebrate their weddings in 2026 and to commemorate their Scottish heritage.

registrationNotes: A personal design for John George Wilson of Kilwinnet and family, using colours of personal significance and inspired by the Janet Wilson and Lennox tartans. registrationNotes: The Babcock International Group Tartan features the colours of the Babcock International Group Logo and Branding; shades of blue, aqua, lime green and a light sandy beige. The red represents the hull of the newly launched Royal Navy warships Type 31 general purpose frigates.

name: Mackillop, Carol & Goldberg, Graham - Wedding (Personal)

Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the wedding of Carol Mackillop and Graham Goldberg. It will be known colloquially as MacBerg Tartan, a portmanteau of both surnames, reflecting the joining of their two families.

name: Metric System
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Lisa Petriello, this design is intended to symbolise the Metric System and has stripes of 10 & 100 as the metric system is based on tens. There are 7 colours within the design in reference to the 7 base units of the metric system - Metre, Kilogram, Second, Ampere, Kelvin, Mole & Candela. Based on common tool manufacturing, industry, and organisational standards, the metric system is commonly associated with the colour blue.

name: Modine, R & M and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: Designed for the Modine Family using colours of personal significance.

name: Lawrence, Sebastian & Sterling and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This family tartan was designed for Sebastian & Sterling Lawrence in celebration of their wedding. The colours and design draw on themes significant to them both. The blue is intended to represent their devotion to Christ; the red their passion and home; the yellow the sunshine in Gustine and gorse bushes in Scotland; the white their integrity; and the green representing the Green Fields they come from and will return to. The threadcount includes numbers referencing 2026, the year of their marriage.

name: Seymour, James (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of James Seymour. Permission to weave must be sought from Claire Hunter, Taffled threads. Threadcount to be requested via Claire Hunter, Taffled threads.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for James Seymour and his family. The colours were inspired by a historic Coat of Arms connected to the Seymour family blended with the Montgomery tartan, which is intended to represent bringing the two families together.

name: Gentry, K & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Gentry family and was inspired by the Lowland and Border regions of Scotland. Colours: the near-black charcoal is intended to represent permanence and resilience across generations; green is for the lands and cultivated fields on which families lived and worked; slate grey is for stone, balance and time; yellow, representing antique brass and grey, representing silver, are intended to acknowledge ancestral ties to England and Wales and the blending of cultures carried forward through migration.

name: Amana ® Brand Exclusive Escape – Scotland 2026
restrictions: Yes. May only be used/reproduced with permission from Amana ® Brand. Prepared for weaving by Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Amana ® Brand Exclusive Escape, held in Scotland in 2026. It is intended to celebrate Amana ® brand's journey and connection to Scotland.

name: Konrad, P (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Preston Konrad & Family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce tartan required from Preston Konrad & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Konrad family to celebrate their family heritage and connected families, including Macon, Preston, and Brodie. The design was inspired by the MacKay, Edinburgh District and Brodie Hunting tartans. Colours: green forms the dominant ground to represent heritage and continuity; navy and black are intended to represent strength and structure; red and yellow are for warmth and distinction. The sett includes 84 green threads to mark the designer’s birth year and 26 black threads to represent the year the tartan was designed, embedding personal milestones into the design.

name: Lange, M & C and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is for the exclusive use of Marvin Lange and Claudia Lange, their children Leo and Samuel Lange (+ any future children of their marriage), as well as all direct descendants of their family. Spouses or committed life partners of their direct descendants as well as Marvin and Claudia’s parents, the spouses of their parents, and their siblings are also permitted to wear the tartan. Permission must be sought from Marvin Lange and Claudia Lange during their lifetime, and thereafter from their direct descendants, and Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a 40th birthday gift for Marvin Lange from his close friends, inspired by his decision to celebrate this milestone in Scotland, bringing together the people he holds closest in a spirit of friendship, adventure and togetherness. The tartan is intended to honour Marvin and Claudia’s shared love for travel & adventure, the landscapes explored, and the importance of their family in their lives. A light green check marks his birthday, woven into a green ground to reflect the natural places and journeys that have shaped his story. Blue, chosen by his eldest son, adds a personal touch. Orange is for warmth and light - a reflection of Claudia’s love for sunshine and colour, Marvin’s appreciation for fire and cosy evenings, and their shared belief that warmth and vibrancy should always remain part of life. Within the sett is a tribute to Marvin and Claudia’s wedding anniversary, a reminder that their partnership is the foundation of everything they have built.

name: Grand Casino Bakery
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Grand Casino Bakery, Culver City, California. Prior approval to weave / reproduce the tartan is required from Grand Casino Bakery, Culver City, California & Barry Rosen.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Grand Casino Bakery, an Argentinian bakery and restaurant located in Culver City, California. The colours were inspired by the flag of Argentina.

name: De Luján, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. The use, wearing, and weaving of this tartan are strictly reserved. Authority must be obtained from Sebastián Hernández De Luján.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the De Lujan family. Colours: blue is intended to represent the clear skies of the Ribera region in Spain; red is to honour the Navarro de los Paños family’s, the De Luján family’s ancestors, textile heritage, symbolising strength and artisan tradition; a double white line has been added to represent clarity and light and yellow, representing gold, is intended to represent the family’s future.

name: Heritage Watchmakers
registrationNotes: The Heritage Watchmakers tartan was inspired by the culture of fine mechanical watchmaking and to the generations of artisans whose skill, discipline and precision have shaped the history of horology. The design is intended to reflect the values traditionally associated with watchmaking — balance, structure, accuracy and refinement — and symbolise the continuity between historical craftsmanship and modern horological creation.

name: Douglas, Rob Roy, Nevada Dress (Personal)
registrationNotes: A dress tartan for Rob Roy Douglas. Colours: black is intended to represent the Nevada sky at night; dark purple for the few minutes after sunset and white for the snow-capped peaks of the Sierra Nevada mountains.

name: Cheez-It
