registrationNotes: edit

name: Bosch-Gilst, L & N (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. If intended to be used for commercial purposes it has to be approved by Nick van Gilst or Laura van den Bosch. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the wedding of Laura van den Bosch & Nick van Gilst. The tartan is intended to represent their love of Scotland, where their wedding was held. The colours were chosen to match their wedding palette.

name: Spark of ADHD
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from the designers Beth Hoffmeier and Amel Bashford.
registrationNotes: The ‘Spark of ADHD' tartan was inspired by the core beauty and power of the ADHD Community and is intended to celebrate the values of inclusivity and creativity. The palette was carefully selected; yellow, representing Gold, is for Neurodiversity; blue is for a calming balance and orange is intended to capture the intense spark and rapid-fire energy that can light up the mind. This tartan is intended to be used by The Wee ADHD Tartan Co to promote acceptance, dignity and understanding for ADHD individuals and families.

name: Wiersma, Orion Pascal Coalter (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be restricted for the use of Orion Pascal Coalter Wiersma. Weaving by permission of Orion Pascal Coalter Wiersma.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the graduation and Iron Ring engineering ceremony, a ceremony held in Canada for qualified engineers, of Orion Pascal Coalter Wiersma. Colours: the fine grey lines are intended to represent the constellation Orion’s Belt and the steel of an engineering ring; blue represents the pre-dawn sky; the rose gold colour signifies the light of Easter morning and new beginnings; dark green is intended to honours the Coulter lineage, and red acknowledges his MacDonald ancestry.

name: First (Scots) Presbyterian Church
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Church members and staff. Can only be woven by permission of the Church. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron ordered by Great Scot Intl, Charlotte NC.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for First (Scots) Presbyterian Church, a historic church located at 53 Meeting St, Charleston, South Carolina, United States. The congregation was established in 1731 when a dozen Scottish families formed the church. The original building was destroyed by fire. The current building was built in 1814 making it the 5th oldest church building in Charleston. The designer of the tartan studied the tartans related to the families that formed the church and used those designs as inspiration for this tartan.

name: Veterinary
registrationNotes: This tartan, commissioned for Dr. Don Slaunwhite, Nova Scotia, Canada, was designed to honour the compassion, skill, and unwavering commitment of veterinarians. Each colour is intended to reflect a defining quality of the profession; light red symbolises compassion and empathy; blue is for trust, stability, and professionalism; grey is for calmness, balance, and modern medical practice; purple honours dedication and lifelong service; red signifies urgency, action, and passion, acknowledging the critical decisions, emergency interventions, and courageous advocacy required to protect animal health and white is for the medical profession - ethics, cleanliness, precision, and the guiding principle to care with integrity. Together, these colours are intended to reflect the emotional strength, clinical expertise, and steadfast devotion that define veterinary medicine.

name: Underwood, Nina, Tegan & Dean and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Nina, Tegan & Dean Underwood. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Dean Underwood and his family. The design includes themes and colours of significance them.

name: Grasmere Weavers
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with Grasmere Weavers consent.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Grasmere Weavers and was inspired by the village of Grasmere and its surrounding landscape in the English Lake District. Grasmere has been inhabited since at least the early medieval period, with Norse influence evident in place names and farming traditions. Its character has long been defined by pastoral agriculture, stone-built cottages, and the natural environment of lakes, fells, and woodlands. The colours are intended to reflect these enduring features: greens representing the surrounding hills and woodland; blue symbolising Grasmere Water and the region’s frequent mist and rainfall; grey evoking the local slate and stone architecture; and lighter tones recalling the soft light and traditional cottages of the village. Yellow is intended to reference William Wordsworth’s “I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud”, commonly known as Daffodils, inspired by the flowers growing along the shores of Grasmere and nearby waters.

name: Oranje Veld
restrictions: Yes. Available with the designer's consent. May only be woven with permission from the designer. Enquiries - International Tartans, 11 Market Place, Eyemouth TD14 5HE [email protected] Copyright rests with International Tartans, 11 Market Place, Eyemouth, Berwickshire, Scotland, TD14 5HE [email protected]
registrationNotes: The Oranje Veld (Orange field) tartan is intended to celebrate centuries of economic and cultural exchange between Scotland, the Netherlands, and Flanders, dating as far back as the 15th century. The design was inspired by the iconic orange of the Netherlands and the red, white, and blue of the Dutch national flag. The blue threads are also intended to pay tribute to the Scottish Saltire, symbolising the historical ties between the two nations. Designed in 2013, this tartan was launched in 2017 to coincide with the UEFA Women’s EURO 2017, hosted by the Netherlands.

name: Kadam, S (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Kreya Owens, Sunil Kadam or Keenan Kadam. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the life and legacy of Sunil Kadam, honouring his journey through education, science, and the creation of a lasting family foundation. The tartan was inspired by his journey; from his Indian roots, through Ireland (University College Dublin), Canada (University of Calgary), and the United States, reflecting the scholarship and dedication that shaped both his life and his family. Colours: green is intended to represent growth, renewal, and the foundation of family; red, yellow and black are for scholarly achievement, academia, and intellectual depth; and orange is for hope, prosperity, and the rewards of perseverance.

name: Owens, M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Kreya Owens and Michael Owens. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Michael Owens and his family to celebrate the foundation of their family, honour shared beginnings, growth, and the enduring values passed through generations. It was inspired by experiences at Trinity College, a historical coat of arms connected to the Owens family, and colours intended to symbolise growth, stability, and achievement.

name: Blue Light Sports (BLS)
designer: House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd
restrictions: Yes. The tartan production is restricted to Geoffrey Tailor & Kilt Maker. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings, the copyright holders.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Blue Light Sports Foundation (BLS) to raise awareness of the work that the UK’s emergency, blue light and volunteer services, civil service and armed forces personnel undertake daily, and the unwavering support provided to them by their families. The tartan is intended to be used to raise vital funds to support those who are injured, disabled, sick or suffering from mental illness, and those who are neurodivergent, through the provision of adaptive, accessible and fully inclusive sporting events. Colours: red is intended to be a tribute to the fire service, rescue services and armed forces; blue is all those working within policing; yellow, representing gold, is for all of the volunteers, key workers and families of all those serving in the emergency, blue light, volunteer services and armed forces.

name: Adie, J A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Jonathan Adie & Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Jonathan Adie in celebration of his marriage to Rachel Allan. The thread count incorporates numbers referencing 2026, the year of their marriage. The colours and design draw on themes significant to his family’s heritage, taking inspiration from elements of the Gordon tartan.

name: Banque Populaire du Sud
restrictions: Yes. May only be used/reproduced with permission from Banque Populaire. Prepared for weaving by Nicolson Kiltmakers.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Banque Populaire du Sud to celebrate the spirit of preservation and transmission of heritage. The design is intended to reflect trades and regions and their commitment to local culture, sustainable artisan craftsmanship, and the textile know-how passed down from generation to generation.

name: Sumitomo Electric U.K. Power Cables Ltd

registrationNotes: The tartan’s colour palette was inspired by Sumitomo Electric’s brand Pantone shades, with the inclusion of copper as a symbolic and significant reference to the company’s heritage. The design features a thread count of 20 and 26, marking the opening year of Sumitomo Electric UK Power Cables Ltd, alongside a thread count of 1890 to represent the decade in which the company was founded.

name: Paisley Pirates

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Paisley Pirates, a Scottish based Ice Hockey Club, using the team's colours.

name: Belfast

registrationNotes: The Belfast tartan is intended to celebrate the city's heart and heritage. Colours: yellow is for the iconic Samson and Goliath gantries of Harland & Wolff; black for the ever-present Black Mountain; dark blue for Belfast Lough and the River Lagan; light blue for the petals of the flax flower; white is intended to represent the renowned linen that made Belfast ‘Linenopolis’; and red for the warm red bricks that built the city's terraced streets and warehouses.

name: Dyslexia-Friendly Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be woven with permission from Dyslexia Scotland in the first few years after its registration. Design registered with the UK Intellectual Property Office. Design registration number: 6498903. Date registered: 13 January 2026.
registrationNotes: Commissioned by Dyslexia Scotland, this tartan is intended to represent the pursuit for a dyslexia-friendly Scotland; where people with dyslexia live, learn, work and play as equals in Scottish society.

name: Spirit of Culloden
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used and distributed by the National Trust for Scotland only. May only be woven with permission from the National Trust for Scotland. Threadcount will only be released with permission from the National Trust for Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to reflect the landscape and atmosphere of Culloden Battlefield, and launched to commemorate the 280th anniversary of the Battle of Culloden, 16th April 1746. The colours are intended to represent different aspects of the battlefield, events from the battle, and to convey the atmosphere many visitors feel when they visit: dark grey is for the darkness of the events of the battle and the sombre atmosphere of the battlefield; light grey for the skies and the weaponry used during the battle; green, brown and yellow/green are for the natural landscape, home to a rich variety of wildlife, and the stones marking the graves of those who lost their lives during the battle; blue and white are for the blue bonnets worn by the Jacobites during the Battle of Culloden which had white cockades fixed to them. There are 16 blue threads and 4 white to symbolise the date of the battle 16th April. The tartan repeat has 280 ends to mark the 280 years since the Battle of Culloden.

name: Highlands and Islands Enterprise
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Highlands and Islands Enterprise (HIE), 10 The Campus, Inverness, Scotland, IV2 5NA. Permission to weave/use/reproduce must be obtained from HIE.
registrationNotes: In 2025, Highlands and Islands Enterprise (HIE) and their predecessor, the Highlands and Islands Development Board, celebrated 60 years. As part of this milestone, they launched a competition to design a commemorative tartan, open to all students at the University of the Highlands and Islands (UHI). The winning design by Fiona Helen Lane was chosen for its creativity and visual impact in reflecting the region’s heritage and HIE’s role in shaping progress over six decades. Its use of colour is intended to reflect the land, sea, sky and people of the region, capturing both the strength and gentle beauty of the Highlands and Islands. Bands of HIE’s corporate blue provide a strong link to their brand while symbolising the support offered to businesses and communities across the region. This tartan is intended to serve as a lasting symbol of the connection between people, place and opportunity.

name: Voodoo Violet
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Barry Rosen.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by ‘Goth’ fashion and the colours purple and black.

name: Bayeux Tapestry
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries regarding this tartan should be directed to Michael Lewis [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was based on the colours used in the Bayeux Tapestry, particularly the scene (27) where the dying King Edward (seemingly) promised the kingdom of the English to Earl Harold in early January 1066. The colours have been matched as far as is possible with the original colours of the Bayeux Tapestry. The tartan is intended to honour the return of the Bayeux Tapestry to the United Kingdom in 2026 and was commissioned by Michael Lewis, member of Bayeux Museum’s Bayeux Tapestry Scientific Committee and Curator of the British Museum’s Bayeux Tapestry exhibition (2025-27). The use of Bayeux Tapestry for the name of this tartan was approved by the Mayor of Bayeux on behalf of the City of Bayeux

name: Iliad Institute
restrictions: Yes. Usage and wearing of the Iliad Institute tartan are intended to be reserved for members, partners, and supporters of the Institute. Any third-party commercial use or formal representation requires prior written authorisation from the President of the Institut Iliade. For all enquiries, please contact: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Iliad Institute, France, and is intended to celebrate European civilisational heritage through textile history. The design includes two landmark archaeological references: the ancient Tocharian weaves of the Tarim Basin (c. 1000 BC) and the historic Falkirk sett, Scotland’s oldest checked fragment. The colours are intended to reflect Georges Dumézil’s trifunctional hypothesis of Indo-European societies: red for the bellatores (warriors); white for the oratores (sovereigns and scholars); and black for the laboratores (producers).

name: Porcelli, L (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. The owner of the tartan design should be properly acknowledged and informed of any weaving/use/reproduction.
registrationNotes: A tartan for Luca Porcelli and his family, Lecce, Italy, using colours of personal significance.

name: Legacy of Darkness
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be a tribute to the influence and legacy of heavy metal music and may be worn by anyone who appreciates the culture, music, and artistic spirit it represents. Please contact Warren regarding weaving and use at [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the atmosphere, cultural influence, and theatrical presence associated with heavy metal music. It was inspired by the visual and emotional experience of live arena performances. Colours: black is intended to represent the darkness of the concert arena before and during a performance; grey symbolises the structural elements of the stage environment, including lighting rigs, scaffolding, and the industrial framework that supports large concert productions; red is for the intensity, power, and emotional energy of heavy metal music; yellow is for the spotlight and the enduring legacy of the genre’s most influential performers. Symbolic thread counts were incorporated into the design including a reference to the year 1970, when Black Sabbath released their debut album and helped establish the foundations of heavy metal music.

name: Kane, K & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by anyone with the last name Kane or one of its many variants (O'Kane, McKane, Cain, etc).
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Kevin Kane and his family, and to celebrate the surname Kane. The colours were inspired by the history of the Kane surname and were based on the flags of the countries of the UK and Ireland, along with the United States of America for the many Kanes who have migrated there. The colours also have personal meaning for the family: green is intended to represent Ireland and the forests of Oregon; blue represents Norway and the Oregon flag; red represents Germany; light blue and green represent the Willamette Valley; black commemorates family members who have passed on. The tartan was registered in 2026 to commemorate the 80th birthday of Kevin's father.

name: ScotRail
registrationNotes: The ScotRail tartan was inspired by the rhythm, form and connectivity of the nation’s rail network. The colour palette is rooted in the ScotRail’s brand colours of blue and white. Variations in tones are intended to give the feeling of direction and movement. The double white lines are intended to represent the rail tracks in its physical form and mirror the shape of the iconic Saltire, each one joined to the next, representing the communities connected by Scotland’s Railway.

name: McCourt, J T and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to Terry McCourt.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for J T McCourt MBE and his family. Colours: the Pink lines are remembrance of his late wife Janice; blue is intended to represent his time serving in the 2nd Battalion, Parachute Regiment, which has Scottish Roots.

name: Moorland - Mòinteach, The
restrictions: Yes. Notice of use to the designer is a courtesy.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the vast, open Moorlands of Scotland. The colours are intended to represent the native biodiverse flora and fauna of the ecosystem, and are designed to blend in with the natural environment. It was designed to celebrate all those that serve to protect, preserve, and utilise this valuable resource area and that which lives there.

name: European Renal Association
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn/used with approval of the copyright holders. Cannot be offered for sale or used in any commercial form without the permission of the copyright holders. Copyright rests with the European Renal Association.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to mark and celebrate the 63rd European Renal Association (ERA) Conference which is being held in Glasgow. It’s based on the Glasgow tartan listed in Wilsons’ 1819 Key Pattern Book and incorporates the colours of the ERA logo. The central red square is 63 threads representing the 63rd conference, whilst the adjacent red band of 20 threads, with the yellow band of 26 mark the conference year.

name: Jennings, Zachary & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Zachary Jennings & Family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was designed for Sarah Dewees & Zachary Jennings in celebration of their marriage. The design includes themes & colours of significance to their families and the threadcount references the date of their wedding.

name: Burgess, Zachary & Hinton, Edith - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Zachary Burgess, Edith Hinton & Family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce this tartan required from Zachary Burgess, Edith Hinton & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the wedding of Zachary Burgess and Edith Hinton on December 31, 2026. It features colours of personal significance which were also incorporated throughout the wedding day.

name: American College of Dentists
designer: Martin, Carol A L and Smith, Drew
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be restricted to Fellows of the ACD, family of Fellows, and ACD staff. Special exceptions may be granted by the President of the ACD. This design may be reproduced only with the permission of the ACD. Contact: American College of Dentists, 103 North Adams St, Rockville, Maryland 20850, [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the American College of Dentists and is intended to be a visual emblem of fellowship and service. It was based on the College’s official colours, lilac and American rose, set on a blue ground with red and white to echo the flag of the United States. A red and white houndstooth band references the College’s four pillars - ethics, professionalism, leadership, and excellence - and its eight Regencies, while also intended to suggest ‘teeth’ in the cloth. Two lilac stripes total twenty threads to mark 1920, the year of the College’s founding, and to recall the colours of convocation sashes.

name: Burn, Austin (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be worn with permission from the copyright holder. Cannot be offered for sale, woven or produced in any commercial form without the express permission of the copyright holder. Copyright rests with Austin Burn RVM.
registrationNotes: Based on the Royal Stewart tartan, the inspiration for this tartan for Austin Burn RVM was the medal ribbon of the Royal Victorian Medal, bestowed upon him by Her Late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II for his almost 20 years' service to the Royal Household, his principal position having been Page of the Presence to Her Majesty. A lifelong member of the Salvation Amy, he and his wife Linda spent three weeks working for that organisation in the centre of the Ground Zero site in New York. That event is commemorated by the twin lines in 'Memorial Blue', associated with the 9/11 memorial. Other colours are from Austin's personal Coat of Arms (granted to him by the Late Queen), the Salvation Army, the arms of the Worshipful Company of Fletchers, and the colours of a Freeman of the City of London. Austin & Linda were married in 1998 and that date is referenced with 19 black threads next to the navy blue block of 90 threads – that colour marking their son Ptolemy’s career choice of the Royal Navy.

name: Murray, Jock Alexander George (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Jock Murray & Family. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required from Jock Murray & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed as a special gift to mark Jock Murray’s 60th birthday and reflect both his Scottish heritage and Nova Scotian roots. Based on elements of the Murray of Atholl tartan and combined with colours from the Nova Scotia flag, the design is intended to bring together clan identity and place. Sixty yellow threads have been incorporated throughout the sett to commemorate this milestone birthday.

name: Gladneys in America
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Gladneys in America. Prior Approval to Weave / Reproduce tartan required from Gladneys in America & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.
registrationNotes: Designed for the Gladneys in America, a family association for descendants of Richard II and Jane Gladney, this tartan is intended to reflect both their origins and their journey to South Carolina (SC). The design incorporates 17 stripes and 68 green threads to mark the year their ancestors first arrived in Charleston, SC. Colours: green was inspired by the County Antrim tartan, honouring where the family came from; red was drawn from the Caledonia tartan; and blue is intended to represent indigo, the crop cultivated by the Gladneys following their arrival in SC.

name: St Andrew's Hospice
restrictions: Yes. Use of this tartan is intended to be restricted by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd. unless prior written consent is given. This tartan can only be woven with prior written consent from Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd. This tartan has been designed on behalf of the St Andrew's Hospice, by Great Scot (Scotland) Ltd, and can only be reproduced with their permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lanarkshire-based St Andrew’s Hospice to mark its 40th anniversary in 2026. The Hospice was founded by the Religious Sisters of Charity, and is a specialist palliative care facility offering multidisciplinary, expert care and support to patients, families and carers. A registered charity, it provides care for people living with life-limiting illnesses, funded in part by the NHS and sustained by the generosity of the Lanarkshire community. As a recognised centre of excellence, the Hospice delivers both inpatient and outpatient services, bereavement support for children and adults as well as providing education to help advance end-of-life care across the community. Embraced by people throughout Lanarkshire, the Hospice continues to stand as a symbol of compassion, dignity and unwavering community support.

name: Mogge, René & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Mogge Family, living in the Netherlands, and was inspired by a historic coat of arms connected to the family. The colours are of personal significance intended to represent the fur of their Bernese mountain dog, forestry, rivers and sea.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for MERIX Financial, Toronto, Canada, to celebrate their brand and connection with Scotland. Colours: pink is intended to reflect MERIX’s brand and confidence; blue is for trust, integrity, and longstanding relationships; green reflects growth, prosperity, and connection, inspired by both financial progress and Scotland’s natural landscape; black and white is intended to represent resilience, clarity, and the enduring strength of family and partnership.

name: Manithil, l’esprit de la lune

registrationNotes: This fashion tartan was designed to celebrate the the moon and was inspired by space and the night sky. Colours: the blues and black are intended to represent silent twilight to the first celestial glimmers; purple is for the vast and mysterious galaxy; light grey is intended to reflect the moon.

name: Saturday Morning Shanks

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Saturday Morning Shanks. The group have been brought together by a shared love of golf for four decades, playing every Saturday Morning at 7 or sunrise at Golf Club de Haar, Utrecht, the Netherlands.

name: Rollins, Matthew & Ott, Regan and Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: The Alexandria Presbyterian Church tartan was designed to reflect the church’s corporate colours and is intended to represent the church’s One Foundation and its historical narrative. name: Heart Space

The colours are all shades based on the building’s stained glass windows. The threadcount includes references to the year 1888 and the number of lotus petals at 12.

name: Bingham, Ross, Loch An Eilein (2026) (Personal)

name: Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany Edinburgh
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany Edinburgh. Prior permission to weave / reproduce required by the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany Edinburgh.

The design is intended to reflect the Day of German Unity which commemorates German reunification on 3 October 1990; 3 colours within the design, 10 stripes within the tartan half sett and 90 black threads within the tartan repeat.

name: Rosen, Barry (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Barry Rosen for his own use. The colours feature red, blue and yellow, representing gold, inspired by his ancestral links to the Goldingstones, Fife, and the red bricks manufactured in Fife that were used for ships that brought profits from trade with the Americas.

name: Belladona Nightshade
restrictions: Yes. Prior approval to obtain thread count / weave / reproduce the tartan is required from designer Barry Rosen. Copyright rests with Barry Rosen.
registrationNotes: A fashion tartan inspired by goth style using colours inspired by those of the nightshade plant.

name: Milroy, W H & Family, The Irvine Valley (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/reproduced commercially with permission.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for William Hugh Milroy, born and brought up in the Irvine Valley, Ayrshire. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent Scotland and service in the Royal Air Force; white and black through the blue symbolise service in the Royal Hong Kong Police and the principles of law, order, and integrity; green is for the Ayrshire countryside of the Irvine Valley and red represents over twenty years’ service with a military charity dedicated to supporting homeless veterans of the United Kingdom’s Armed Forces, symbolising continued duty, compassion, and service beyond uniform. The red checks edged with black commemorate the Milroy family’s Covenanter heritage and the Dunnachie connection to Clan Robertson.

name: Cercle de Fermières Ville-Saint-Pierre - 50th Anniversary
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to weave this tartan must consult with Cercle de Fermières Ville-Saint-Pierre Quebec before doing so.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 50th Anniversary of Cercle de Fermières Ville-Saint-Pierre. The colours are intended to evoke the history and values that have united the community for half a century: grey is for the wisdom of the elders, stability of traditions and the memory of gestures passed down from mother to daughter; blue reflects the pride of belonging to a strong community, rooted in the history of the former City of Saint-Pierre; black underlines the depth of heritage, the quiet strength of the women who built, taught and preserved the know-how; red is for the passion, commitment and human warmth that have animated the Cercles de Fermières since 1915 and white is intended to represent the purity of intentions, authenticity of the gestures transmitted and truth shared between generations.

name: Dalgliesh, Euan (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. May only be worn/used/woven with permission of designer - Euan Dalgliesh.
registrationNotes: Designed by Euan Dalgliesh for his wedding.

name: Bourassa
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by employees of Bourassa Transport. May only be woven with permission from Bourassa Transport or Ingles Buchan Textiles.
registrationNotes: Based on the popular 'unofficial' plaid de Quebec and using the Bourassa corporate colours of orange, blue and white. The smallest orange square has 19 threads and the larger square to its right has 56 - marking the year that the company was founded. The grey and white lines represent the highways and roads of Quebec, Ontario and the American East Coast over which Transport Bourassa operates. Finally, the green represents the company's ecological initiatives in pursuit of a greener future in all its operations.

name: Meckenstock, Klaus & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended exclusively for the use of Klaus Meckenstock and family. It may not be offered for sale, woven, reproduced, manufactured, or used in any commercial or personal capacity without the express written permission of Klaus Meckenstock or Family.
registrationNotes: The Meckenstock Family tartan was designed to serve as a visual representation of the family’s diverse ancestral heritage. The colour palette was carefully selected to reflect the principal cultural traditions and historical origins associated with the Meckenstock lineage; red, yellow and black are intended to symbolise the family’s German ancestry, inspired by the German national flag; purple and grey are for the family’s Scandinavian heritage, particularly its ancestral connections to Denmark, Norway, and Sweden and green is intended to reflect the family’s Scottish roots and ties to Scotland.

name: McWittebol, H & P - Wedding (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent the joining of two families and cultures in marriage. The bride's heritage is from the MacKinnon Clan and the groom is from a Dutch family name, Wittebol. The colours are intended to represent each part of that union with pink and teal being the favourite colours of the bride and groom; orange for the Netherlands and blue and white for Scotland.

name: Kucharski, Marcin & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by all persons bearing the surname Kucharski or their heirs, and by all friends of the Kucharski family with their consent.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Kucharski family and was first intended to be worn by Marcin ‘MrBee’ Kucharski whilst attending his first Highland Games in Scotland. The two yellow stripes are intended to represent his beloved daughters, whose birthdates are also referenced in the dark blue threadcount. Colours: dark blue and blue were inspired by Scotland and the union of the sky and sea; yellow references Marcin’s love for bees and his nickname ‘MrBee’; orange is for his closest friends and ochre, capable of withstanding the sea breeze on bare rock, to symbolise resilience in the face of adversity and boundless positive energy.

The threadcount includes references to the years of the family members’ births; 1963, 1977, 2008 and 2010.

name: Bray, David & Family, Cornwall (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for David Bray and his family. Colours: black and white were inspired by the flag of St Piran; yellow is for the 15 bezants; green is intended to reflect the family’s history, traced back to the Withiel parish, deep in the Cornish countryside, in the 1700’s; blue is intended to reflect the family’s move to Wadebridge, on the banks of the Camel Estuary.

name: Eden Park

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Eden Park Trust, as the host for the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo 2026. The colours are intended to represent all facets of New Zealand, the country and its culture, and the variety of events held at the venue.

name: St. Andrew's Society of Baltimore
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by St. Andrew's Society of Baltimore members only. May only be woven with permission from St. Andrew's Society of Baltimore. Copyright rests with St. Andrew's Society of Baltimore, 2345 York Rd, Suite B12, Timonium, MD 21093.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the St. Andrew's Society of Baltimore, United States, founded in 1806, not long after the American Revolution. Its purpose was to raise and keep money available to help Scottish immigrants, seamen and descendants of Scots in times of need; and to maintain Scottish heritage and traditions. The Society has continued to uphold that purpose by contributing to community activities, offering assistance to Scots descendants and by displaying their Scottish traditions and heritage in many forms throughout Maryland and neighbouring states.

name: Stiles, Aaron (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended only for relatives, friends, and associates MAJ Stiles. May not be woven/reproduced without prior approval.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Aaron Stiles, MAJ USA (Ret.), and his friends and family, to celebrate his heritage in the Scottish Borders and his US military and Christian service. Colours: brown is intended to represent Appalachian earth and Scottish ancestry; black is for strength; green is for growth and fruitfulness; red is intended to honour Christ and those who have served and sacrificed; yellow is for glory and justice and white marks redemption through Grace.

Weaving is restricted to those approved by Tartan Manor Ltd. This design was registered with the UK IPO on 29 May 2026, registration number: 6529815.
registrationNotes: The Worshipful Company of Farriers tartan is intended to celebrate the WCo Farriers members and the history of the Farriers. Founded in 1356 in the City of London at the request of the mayor to manage those involved with the craft of farriery and to uphold the welfare of the horse through good practice. Its varied membership consists of craft farriers, veterinary surgeons and an amalgam of individuals committed to the welfare of the horse, farriery and the City of London. The Company is the awarding body for the farriery qualifications of Diploma, Associate and Fellow. In 1674 the Company was granted a Royal Charter and it is number 55 on the register of the City of London Livery Companies. This design features a silvery grey intended to represent the metal of the horseshoe. Black, Creamy/White, Orangey Red, Gold, Pale Blue are all taken from the WCo Farriers Coat of Arms. Red is intended to represent the Company's long association with the City of London.

name: St Margaret's Academy (Scotland)
designer: St Margaret's Academy Pupils & Tartan Caledonia
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by students and staff at Saint Margaret’s Academy in Livingston, Scotland. May not be woven/reproduced without permission.
registrationNotes: Saint Margaret’s Academy in Livingston, Scotland, organised a competition in which pupils were tasked with designing a new tartan specifically for the school. The contest was held in conjunction with the celebration of Saint Margaret of Scotland, whose feast day falls on November 16. The tartan design drew inspiration from the school’s strong connection to Saint Margaret. The chosen colours reflect the school’s official palette, including the maroon shade taken from the school emblem. The winning entry was selected from ten finalists, all created by pupils at Saint Margaret’s Academy. The competition offered students an opportunity to express their creativity and strengthen the school’s identity through a tartan tied to its history and values.

name: Tundra Twilight
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone. It can only be woven/sold/reproduced by request of Tartan Chickadee®.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by family travels into the surrounding mountains in search of lingon berries growing across the tundra. The design is intended to represent gathering the bright red berries from the soft ground, surrounded by the rich colours of autumn, with cranes overhead in air that carries the first hint of snow. This tartan was inspired by quiet moments in Alaska’s backcountry.

name: Scottish Archery
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Scottish Archery to celebrate this historical sport in Scotland. The design incorporates: blue from the Scottish Saltire; colours from archery targets, aligned in a thread count that signifies their score levels; and white, denoting the field layout for an outdoor target competition.

name: Clempson Whisky
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Clempson Whiskey, a small whisky tasting and presentation business ran by Alf Clempson. It was inspired by the journey of Scotch whisky from grain to glass. Colours: brown is intended to reflects the casks in which the spirit matures; yellow is for the whisky itself; black represents the charred interior of the cask and the influence of smoke; light brown denotes malted barley, the foundation of Scotch whisky; orange is for the copper stills used in distillation. The tartan was created as part of ‘Journey into Whisky with Alf Clempson’, celebrating whisky education, storytelling, and shared tasting experiences.

name: Clan del Chiodo
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Clan del Chiodo.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Clan del Chiodo (which translates to ‘of the nail’), Italy. The group was founded by a group of friends, who randomly met at the Montelago Celtic Festival and formed friendship over their shared love of a traditional game of their region, which consists of hammering nails into a stump with a holed hammer. Over the years more members have joined to participate in the game. This tartan is intended to be worn by members.

name: Engelmann, R & Family (Personal)
designer: Engelmann, Robert & James & Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Robert Engelmann or James Engelmann. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the combined Engelmann family lineage between Scottish, Austrian, and Finnish ancestry. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent the oceans crossed by the family’s ancestors; red is for strength and boldness to seek new opportunities; light blue represents the family tradition of metalwork and shipbuilding; green represents the family's ties to agriculture and respect for nature and white is intended to reflect the separate heritages combining into one family.

name: Cask Trade
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave/use/reproduce this tartan must be sought from Cask Trade & Siobhan Mackenzie Limited.
registrationNotes: The Cask Trade tartan is intended to reflect the brand’s identity, heritage, and ambition. Its palette was drawn from the brand guidelines, using deep purple and gold to create a distinctive and recognisable design. The structure is intended to echo the precision and trust at the heart of the business. The founding year, 2018, is subtly embedded in the threadcount, weaving the brand’s origin into the fabric. Together, these elements form a tartan that is intended to connect heritage with whisky commerce.

name: Malik, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of The Malik Family. Can only be woven with the registrant’s permission.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Malik family to celebrate their roots that stretch from Pakistan to Dundee. The colours are intended to reflect the national flags of Pakistan and Scotland, while the tangerine acknowledges the city of Dundee’s heritage - highlighting its historic trade in Seville oranges, its association with marmalade production and the jute industry (the ‘golden fibre’). This vibrant hue also features in the city’s own tartan and is shared by one of Dundee’s two football teams.

name: Bureau Veritas
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the Bureau Veritas. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required by Bureau Veritas & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: Designed for Bureau Veritas, a global leader in testing, inspection and certification, to mark the company’s 200th anniversary. Founded in 1828, the tartan incorporates this date through its thread counts, with three white stripes of six threads (18), alongside purple and green stripes of 18 threads each. Light blue stripes of 28 threads and dark blue stripes of 56 threads further reference ‘28’, the founding year. The colour palette was taken from the company’s branding, combining shades of blue with accents of purple, green and white to reflect its identity.

name: Grande Prairie Legion #54

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Grande Prairie Legion #54, a Veterans organisation located in Canada, to be used by the Grande Prairie Legion #54 and their pipe band. The design is intended to remember all members that have served.

name: McAuley, J (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Jenna McAuley. Prior approval to weave / reproduce required from Jenna McAuley & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.com
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Jenna McAuley to celebrate her Scottish Celtic ancestry and be woven for use as a traditional Jewish Tallit.

name: Fourth Fold Construction
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for Fourth Fold Construction, a company focused on craftsmanship and outdoor construction. Colours: the repeated yellow 4-thread stripe represents the ‘fourth fold’, drawn from the idea that when a worker rolls up their sleeves, it is the fourth fold that lifts the sleeve above the elbow and signals readiness for work; blue is intended to represent trust, planning and long-term reliability; greens is for outdoor spaces, grounded strength and lasting work; red represents labour and perseverance and purple is for an elevated finish quality and careful workmanship.

name: Beamish Museum: Fifty-Five
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by Beamish Museum. May only be woven with permission from Beamish Museum. Designed by Louise Main-Dalziel for Beamish Museum for a bespoke scarf contract order for Eurostick - The Decal Company Limited.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Beamish, The Living Museum of the North to commemorate its fifty-fifth anniversary. Beamish Museum is a tapestry of interwoven stories from the North East of England and this design was inspired by colours and references from its collections.

name: Cricket Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Distribution, wearing and use of the tartan is intended to be restricted to items or merchandise produced or licensed by Cricket Scotland, its staff, players, officials, contracted persons or approved affiliated partners.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Cricket Scotland to mark the national men's team's participation at the 2015 ICC Men's World Cup. The design was based on the Clan tartan of 19th century Scottish international cricketer Gregor MacGregor. The tartan has since been used by Cricket Scotland across a variety of playing, corporate and marketing assets.

name: Rablogan – Living with Hope
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone living with Parkinson's or associated in any way with the disease or wishing to bring attention to it. Prepared for weaving by MacNaughton Holdings Limited. May only be woven with authority in writing from the designer or his descendants.
registrationNotes: The Rablogan - Living with Hope tartan was designed with the intention of raising awareness of those suffering from Parkinson’s Disease and the hope of a brighter future. The colours and threadcount are intended to reflect the various aspects of a life of hope, living with Parkinson’s while also honouring those who lost the battle: three shades of grey categorise Parkinson’s and its various stages, forms and impacts; purple highlights brightness and hope; white is intended to reflect the transition of acceptance to hope; black and red are used to honour those who have succumbed to the disease.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the NATO Industry Advisory Group. The threadcount includes the number 32, referencing the 32 NATO member countries and 68 for the year the NIAG was created, 1968. The shades used are the NATO brand colours.

name: Holloway, Andrew & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Andrew Holloway and his family. The colours are intended to celebrate his Scottish and Cuban identity; blue represents Fife, Scotland; green was inspired by the Scottish landscape; red was drawn from the Cuban flag and yellow, representing gold, is intended to symbolise the bridge between both cultures.

name: Lynde, Charles & Beverly and Family (Personal)
designer: Martin, Carol A L and Nicolucci, Christy
registrationNotes: This tartan was created for the Lynde family and is intended to reflect the family life of Charles and Beverly Lynde and their descendants. Charles and Beverly raised six children within five years and used colours to help identify and organise the children during their upbringing. The eldest daughter, Carrie, was represented by purple; the second daughter, Christy, by pink; and the four sons by light blue, dark blue, red, and yellow. These colours have remained associated with each of the children into adulthood. The sequence of colours in the tartan reflects the birth order of the six children. The eight light blue lines represent the original eight members of the family. The blue ground is intended to symbolise water and sailing, which formed an important part of the family’s shared activities. White represents the medical profession, as Charles Lynde practised as a dermatologist, and the white stripe bordered by pink represents Beverly Lynde’s support of her husband and family.

name: Buisman, H & Schaap, Z, Glen Coe (2026) (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Hannah Buisman & Zachary Schaap. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Restricted. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This family tartan was designed for Hannah Buisman & Zachary Schaap in celebration of their marriage. The design includes themes and colours of significance to them and their families.

name: Speculative Society of Edinburgh
restrictions: Yes. Intended to only be used or worn with the express consent of the Speculative Society of Edinburgh. The Society’s Secretary shall serve as the first point of contact for all future fabric production and for the granting of any necessary permissions.
registrationNotes: This tartan commemorates the two hundred and fiftieth Session of the Speculative Society, instituted in 1764 for the improvement of literary composition and public speaking. The prevailing blue is drawn from the hall in which members assemble upon arrival, a place associated with fellowship and freedom of thought. The scarlet recalls the horsehair benches on which members sit to observe and listen, and embodies the courage required to speak with passionate conviction. Green is taken from the coat worn by Sir Walter Scott, one of the Society’s distinguished members, whose influence did much to shape both Scotland’s literary imagination and the modern expression of tartan itself. Threads of black and white represent ink and paper, through which ideas are formulated, arguments presented, and learning preserved.

name: Black-Capped Chickadee
restrictions: Yes. The tartan is woven exclusively for the brand, Tartan Chickadee®, and created to sell to tourists in Alaska. Weaving may only be done at Tartan Chickadee®'s request.
registrationNotes: The beloved black-capped chickadee, the mascot of Tartan Chickadee, is a year-round resident in Alaska. It’s not uncommon to see a group of these hardy little birds rioting in the alder bushes at -30°F. Influenced by this tiny Alaskan hero, this tartan weaves together black, cream, grey, and tan to reflect the bird’s feathers, soft beauty and resilience.

name: Vincere Ad Astra: Legatum
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced by written permission from the designer. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: A symmetrical version of the Vincere Ad Astra tartan (SRT #14275) inspired by ‘Legatum’, meaning legacy in Latin. Colours: purple is intended to represent Scotland’s engineering and entrepreneurial heritage, and its legacy of applied expertise carried forward into new domains; green is for sustainable stewardship, a human-centred commitment that keeps space activity grounded; light purple is for cybersecurity, leadership, and diplomacy, reworked for space; yellow, representing gold, is for leadership intelligence; white is for integrity and black is for space itself.

name: Abbovitaars
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission from Debra Murray.
registrationNotes: The Abbovitaars tartan was designed for the Craige and Murray family. The word is special to them and was made by combining letters from their names to create their nickname ‘The Abbovitaars’.

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Daniel Albrecht Nüdling & his family, located in Fulda, Germany. The design includes themes and colours of significance to them.

name: Picnics and Pebbles
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of, and commissioned by, Lynne Knox. Intended to be woven by Taffled threads only. Permission to weave must be sought from Claire Hunter of Taffled threads. Thread count should be requested via Claire Hunter of Taffled threads.
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by a childhood picnic rug. It is intended to evoke memories of being young, when a picnic was a grand day out; playing with pebbles, with a picnic rug, salmon sandwiches (tinned on white bread) and tea from a tumbler.

name: Lanyon, K & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Lanyon Family. The name originates in Cornwall and this family branch have lived in Aberdeenshire for more than 30 years. The colours are intended to represent the heathers and woodlands on Bennachie, a touch of blue for the Cornish coast and a slate to represent the granite in both locations.

name: Deeside Kilts
designer: Taylor, Lee Gavin & Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Deeside Kilts Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Deeside Kilts and is intended to represent the company colours and local countryside.

name: Flockhart, J & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the Flockhart family. Use, weaving, reproduction, or commercial use of the tartan should be by permission of the owner/rights holder. Anyone seeking further information or permission should contact the owner/rights holder.
registrationNotes: The Flockhart tartan was designed by James John Flockhart, born in 1944, as a lasting tribute to his name, its Scottish heritage, and the people, places, colours, and traditions that shaped his life. The tartan is being registered with the support and blessing of James John Flockhart’s wife, in remembrance of him and as a lasting legacy for the wider Flockhart family. Together, the colours and pattern are intended to honour the Flockhart family’s Scottish roots, personal memories, sporting loyalties, and enduring connection to Scotland for present and future generations.

name: Young Living
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Young Living Essential Oils, LC. Prior approval to weave / reproduce tartan required by Browne White Ltd t/a ScotlandShop / Young Living Essential Oils, LC.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Young Living to celebrate their 2027 Diamond Retreat in Edinburgh, March 2027. The colours chosen were inspired by their Diamond Retreat core colour accompanied by blues and greens as a reminder of Scotland.

name: Tuxly
restrictions: Yes. Intended for use by the Tuxly community.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Tuxly. It was inspired by penguins: creatures blessed with nature’s finest tuxedo. This design weaves the classic black and white of formal plumage with a yellow highlight to represent the beak.

name: Afonso, F & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from Felipe Raphaeli Afonso. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Portuguese Afonso family. The design and colours were inspired by an historical heraldry shield connected to the family, which reflects the union of three Spanish kingdoms: Castilla, León and Toledo; white and red for León, symbolising purity and victory; green and silver for Castilla, reflecting the green fields and the stable castle; gold and sable for Toledo, a nod to the royal line of the Roman empire and its dual-headed eagle.

name: Genesis Scottish Open
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the use of the European Tour & Genesis and cannot be used, woven or reproduced without their permission.
registrationNotes: A tartan for the European Tour Group designed for the Genesis Scottish Open, a Rolex Series Event co-sanctioned by the DP World Tour and PGA Tour. This tartan is an updated interpretation of the original Scottish Open Golf tartan created in 2017 (SRT #11778).

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Robert Ziembinski and his family, originally from Poland and now living in Austria. The design commemorates over a century of personal connections between the family and Scotland. It is intended to reflect an appreciation of Scotland’s people and shared values. The colours are of personal significance to the family.

registrationNotes: House tartan created for Absolute Garments Ltd, owners of the Balmoral Trademarks, UK Nos. 00001574134; 3086532 and 3086534. This design, along with various colour variants, will form the company’s Balmoral collection.

name: Team Wales Tarw
designer: Tarw Sports; Windsor, A & Lewis, H
restrictions: Yes. Any use/weaving/reproduction of this tartan must be pre-approved by the Commonwealth Games Council for Wales. Copyright rests with Tarw Sports.
registrationNotes: The Team Wales Tarw tartan was commissioned by Tarw Sports to mark the presence of Team Wales at the Commonwealth Games 2026, celebrating both sporting excellence and shared Celtic heritage. The tartan is intended to symbolise the cultural and historical ties between Wales and Scotland. The design reflects the values of Team Wales - strength, unity, and pride - while incorporating colours and structure inspired by Welsh symbolism. Tarw, meaning ‘bull’ in Welsh, represents resilience and determination, qualities embodied by Welsh athletes competing on the international stage. This tartan is intended to be a ceremonial and official garment, but also as a meaningful emblem of friendship between nations, honouring tradition while expressing national identity.

name: Cruickshank, M & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only with the written permission of the designer. This tartan can only be woven with written permission of the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Cruickshank family to celebrate their roots in Aberdeen and the northeast of Scotland. The greys, black, and silver are intended to reflect the enduring spirit of the Granite City, while the red symbolises the family’s historic link to the Stewart of Atholl.

name: Walking Song
restrictions: Yes. The tartan was created as an independent artistic and literary homage. Any resemblance to Tolkien’s works, characters, locations, themes, or imagery is inspirational and does not imply endorsement, sponsorship, licensing, or affiliation with the Tolkien Estate, Middle earth Enterprises, or related rights holders. May only be woven/used/produced with permission from the designer Michael Quigley - [email protected] regarding use. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Walking Song was designed by Michael J. Quigley as a tartan homage inspired by the works of J.R.R. Tolkien, reflecting themes of journey, adventure, homecoming, and the enduring literary tradition of the road and the traveller’s song. The blue, green, black, and white were inspired by Tolkien’s original Hobbit dust jacket artwork, evoking mountains, forests, sky, and a long white road. The symmetrical sett reflects a journey outward and home again. The thread count has 37 black and green threads for the year 1937; 14 white threads for the traveling company; and three black lines within the green for the three trolls turned to stone.

name: Bruel, Nicolas & Rozo, Clemence - Wedding (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the wedding of Nicolas Bruel & Clemence Rozo using colours of personal significance.

It is intended to reflect the sweeping dunes seen from the 9th hole, Hawklaw, while referencing local landmarks including Slains Castle and the mahogany tones of the historic Cruden Bay tram service.

name: Fox, P & Family (Personal)

registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Fox family, Virginia, United States, and was inspired by the family’s ancestry. Each check has the proportional weight of a region of origin disclosed by genetic testing, so the cloth itself is intended to record where the family came from before settling in Virginia. Colours: green was inspired by Munster, Ireland; red is for Northeastern Poland; blue is for a combination of Baltic ancestry from Lithuania, Estonia, and Latvia; charcoal represents Northwestern Germany. At the centre of the sett the design has a pivot of fox rust, to represent the family name, flanked by two checks of blue, for the navy of the Virginia state flag.
