restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with Metropolitan Police Department, Washington, DC, USA.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Metropolitan Police Department (MPD), Washington DC, United States. Colours: navy blue was based on the MPD uniform adopted in 2018 and is intended to represent professionalism and daily commitment of every officer; light blue was based on the historic uniform, worn before the 2018 transition, and the department’s long history and generations of officers who served in light blue; grey represents the earliest MPD uniforms, the streets and neighbourhoods patrolled every day, and more than 160 years of accumulated wisdom and experience; red was drawn from the DC flag, three red stars and two red bars based on George Washington’s family’s Coat of Arms; yellow reflects the gold outline of the U.S. Capitol dome on the MPD patch and the gold border that frames it, and symbolises excellence and leadership; black honours the pipes at memorial services and funerals, represents the mourning of fallen officers and the strength and courage to carry on after loss.

name: Snowball, A & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by anyone bearing the Snowball surname or those wishing to show connection or affinity with the name.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Snowball family. The design was inspired by the name itself, using colours associated with winter landscapes, snow, ice and clear northern skies. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent strength, stability and heritage; white symbolises snow and purity; light blue is for frost and ice and the silver-grey accents are intended to reflect winter light.

name: Order of Saint Stanislas
restrictions: Yes. Intended or the use of the Order of Saint Stanislas.
registrationNotes: The Order of Saint Stanislas was established on the feast of the Bishop and Martyr Saint Stanislas, on the 8th of May 1765, by King Stanislas II Augustus Poniatowski. The Order of Saint Stanislas is a registered non-governmental organisation (NGO) at the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs. This design incorporates elements from their uniform & insignia.

name: Mirza, S & Family, Hyderabad, India (Personal)
designer: Duncan, Lesley A & Lochcarron of Scotland
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven with permission of the family: [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by the Duncan family in Edinburgh, for Dr. Rabeea Mirza in celebration of her wedding in Hyderabad, India to Dr. Anas Siddiqui. The colours are intended to honour the rich and intertwined heritage of the newly married couple. Colours: green and orange pay tribute to the bride and groom’s Indian roots; red, black and white reflect the colours of the U.A.E. flag, a reference to where the groom was raised; white is intended to represent unity, harmony, and the joining of two families; blue represents the bride’s deep love and enduring connection to Scotland.

name: America 250
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be woven/reproduced without permission from America 250. The design rights have been transferred to America250.org by the designer Kaci McEwan, as per agreement with the Scottish Government (USA) and Heriot Watt University.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the United States and the history of the relationship Scotland and the US have had for centuries. The colours are intended to reflect a combination of both the American and Scottish flags. Incorporated are accent colours to represent James Wilson and John Witherspoon, the two Scottish signers of the Declaration of Independence. The design was inspired by significant dates that led up to the signing of the Declaration of Independence including 1607, when the first colony settled in Jamestown, the 13 colonies and the 4th of July, which marks the date on which the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence.

name: Cu, Clarissa Deeia & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This personal family tartan was created to represent continuity, memory, resilience and connection across generations of the Cu family. The design is intended to reflect family legacy, remembrance, discernment, warmth and quiet strength using colours of personal significance.

name: Iwamizawa
registrationNotes: Inspired by Iwamizawa, Japan's history as a vital transportation hub, this tartan is intended to represent the crossing of railways, roads, and people. Selected through a citizen survey, consisting of around 8,000 votes, the design features four colours to symbolise local resources: red is for the city's famous roses, a beloved tourism resource; yellow is for rice ears, representing thriving local agriculture; white is for winter snow, a key part of the local nature and culture and black is for the historic steam locomotives, honouring the railways that drove the city's development.

name: Centennial Nichinara
restrictions: Yes. Cannot be woven or produced in any commercial form without the permission of the Takimoto Co., Ltd of Japan.
registrationNotes: A school uniform tartan produced by Takimoto Co., Ltd of Japan, for Nihon University Narashino Senior High School.

name: Packers of Scotland
designer: House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Packers of Scotland, a fan group dedicated to the Green Bay Packers.

name: Schryver, Todd Albert & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be strictly reserved for Todd Albert Schryver, with entitlement to wear and use the tartan explicitly extending to his spouse, Anna bint Schryver, and their direct descendants. Weaving of this design is strictly limited to commercial or private weavers who have been issued an explicit, written commission or manufacturing license by Todd Albert Schryver or the authorised administrative officers of Mycenae University.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan for Todd Albert Schryver. The design was based on the MacKenzie tartan with the addition of yellow, intended to represent a golden thread. The precise colouration and selection of the specific yellow hue was chosen by Anna bint Schryver, Todd's daughter.

name: Cattani, Antonello & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use by Antonello Cattani, his family and those authorised by them. Permission should be sought before commercial weaving, reproduction or retail use.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Antonello Cattani and his family as a family tartan. The design is intended to capture family memories, their cultural roots and a lifelong attachment to Scotland. Antonello followed Scotland and its men’s national football team from childhood, founded the Italy Tartan Army, and wrote five books on Scottish themes. Colours: dark red is intended to represent pomegranate, as a personal reference to the Reggio Emilia area; brown represents earth, roots and local memory; dark yellow symbolises light and civic memory; dark purple recalls the Scottish thistle; dark green represents guardianship and landscape; dark blue recalls Scotland.

name: Forepaws
registrationNotes: This fashion tartan is intended to celebrate bonds shared with close friends and family. The design is intended to capture the idea of experiences shared and memories to be made with loved ones. The name was inspired by the designer’s love of golf and dogs.

name: Tartan Compass Heritage
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the sole use of the company owners, official guiding staff, and authorized corporate clients or guests of Tartan Compass Tours. Commercial production, weaving, digital printing, reproductions or retail sale of this design, or its likeness, by third parties is strictly prohibited without the express, written authorisation of the brand owners. Permission must be sought directly from the
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Tartan Compass Tours to celebrate their role in the heritage sector. The design is intended to reflect the tones of the land; purple for the vibrant heather found on the summer hills; black for obsidian, found in deep glens and old stone; dark yellow if for the shifting seasonal light and dark green for the land. The design reflects the online identity of Tartan Compass with the threadcount following the exact tracking lines of their digital compass logo.

name: Forand, Michael and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Michael Forand and his family. May only be woven with written permission from Mr Forand, or a nominated agent.
registrationNotes: A personal design for Mick Forand, USA and his immediate family. The colours and proportions are based on his Grant of Arms issued in 2012.

name: City to Coast (ASSC)
restrictions: Yes. The design may only be woven/used/reproduced by Ali Campbell; The Association of Scotland's Self-Caterers or those authorised by either to do so. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: The City to Coast tartan was designed for use as the corporate tartan of the Association of Scotland’s Self-Caterers (ASSC) to celebrate the support they offer for all self-caterers across Scotland, from city properties to those located on the coastline. The greens are based on ASSC branding and are intended to evoke the natural colours of Scotland. White and light purple were inspired by white horses on the waves and heather blossom.

name: Tampalini, Fabio & Ileana and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be reserved for the Tampalini family: Fabio, Ileana, and their children and descendants, or those with permission from Fabio Tampalini, or of his successor as head of the family. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Tampalini Family. The colours are intended to express gravity and rootedness: blue and light grey, representing silver, are based on the heraldic colours of the city of Brescia - d'argento al leone d'azzurro - the city the family are from and continue to return to; green, red and light grey were inspired by the Italian flag; green is intended to represent hope and red is for passion.

name: Tampalini, Fabio & Ileana and Family Hunting (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be reserved for the Tampalini family: Fabio, Ileana, and their children and descendants, and those with express permission from Fabio Tampalini, or of his successor as head of the family. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff.
registrationNotes: A hunting tartan for the Tampalini Family, intended for use in the mountains the family loves, for Celtic gatherings, for outdoor and informal occasions, and for daily family life. Based on the sett of their original family tartan (SRT #15463), the colours are intended to represent the earth and the hills of northern Italy where the family is rooted, and the stability that Fabio and Ileana have chosen to build together.

name: Newell, A (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Newell family to celebrate their longstanding connection with Scotland. The design is intended to represent family, continuity, belonging, and a commitment to preserving a lasting connection with Scotland for descendants of the family.

name: Highland Wanderer, The
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer. THE HIGHLAND WANDERER is a registered trademark with the UK IPO UK00004401877. Design registration pending.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for ‘The Highland Wanderer’ - Iain MacKenzie - and celebrates his memoirs. Colours: dark blue is intended to represent the oceans crossed on various travels; green is for the Scottish highlands and home; purple is for Scottish heather and memories; dark yellow is for whisky casks, the spirit, and good company; off white is for weathered Stone and roads travelled.

name: PSYG Collective
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for PSYG Collective, a group of close friends who met through their professional careers and maintained a strong personal and professional bond. The tartan was created to celebrate their shared journey and the lasting connections formed over time. The colours are intended to reflect shared values and influences meaningful to the group, including references to the French flag, the Order of Liberation, and the Bleuet de France.

name: Knockenhooley
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be used with approval from the owners of Knockenhooley. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to represent Knockenhooley, an old craft cottage owned by the Brierley family, and its history. The colours are intended to represent the cottage itself, its location & surroundings and the family’s connection to their birthplace in the Scottish borders.

name: Bannenberg Van der Stappen, Mark & Natasja (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn only with approval of the Bannenberg Van der Stappen family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Bannenberg Van der Stappen family. The colours chosen are intended to represent one of Mark Bannenberg's favourite painters, Francis Bacon, and his paintings of the Pope, with Natasja Van der Stappen's additional influence on the design.

name: Faraon Spa
restrictions: Yes. Written permission is required for any weaving or reproduction of any kind. For any enquiries, please contact the owner of this tartan at : [email protected]
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Faraon Spa, Québec, Canada, using colours of personal significance to the Owner & President of the Spa.

name: Marylebone Cricket Club
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for Marylebone Cricket Club. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Marylebone Cricket Club. The sett is intended to reference the mowing patterns of the grass on a cricket pitch, the crease markings and cricket stumps. The design uses the MCC brand colours of egg, bacon and indigo.

name: British Transport Police Federation
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the British Transport Police Federation.
registrationNotes: The British Transport Police (BTP) are a National Police Force for policing the railways throughout the UK. In 2026 the British Transport Police Federation held their annual conference in Glasgow and chose to commemorate this with this tartan. The colours are based on the three colours of the BTP Crest and the Federation Crest.

name: Hewage (Wickramarachchi), K & E and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by the family only. It may only be woven or reproduced with the consent of the family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Hewage (Wickramarachchi in Sri Lanka) family using colours of particular significance to celebrate the family settling in Scotland. The colours blend the family's ancestral heritage from Sri Lanka with the medical profession that brought them to the UK and the significant impact that the educational and training institutions have had on their lives & careers: green & red pay homage to the Sri Lankan flag, with green reflecting the country's name as the Emerald Isle; gold merges the Sri Lankan flag with the family's key alma mater, Robert Gordon's College; the navy ground is a reference also to the Royal College of Surgeons Edinburgh; other shades of blue & green represent Queens' College, Cambridge, & Imperial College Medical School.

name: Guinot-Mauchan, Josep & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for members and descendants of the Guinot-Mauchan family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Guinot-Mauchan family to celebrate their heritage. The design combines colours intended to represent family history, cultural roots and continuity between generations.

name: Havranek, J & P and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be a restricted family tartan. The right to wear and use this design is strictly limited to the applicants, their direct descendants, and members of the specific family lineages. Weaving is restricted. No weaver, mill, or manufacturer may weave or reproduce this tartan without the express written consent of the intellectual property right holders.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Jiri and Petr Havranek and their family. The design was inspired by a Coat of Arms connected to the family, using colours and proportions that mirror the Arms.

name: Workmon, Charles & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use by members of the Workmon family and their descendants. Permission for use outside the family may be granted by the family at its discretion.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Workmon family and their descendants using colours of personal significance inspired by Psalm 23.

name: Dedridge, Marilyn & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Marilyn Dedridge, who celebrated her 89th birthday and received a Lifetime Achievement Award from the London Borough of Harrow in recognition of her long and distinguished contribution to public services. The tartan is intended both to acknowledge her service and to celebrate her family. The colours are intended to reflect the Dedridge name which originated in West Lothian; blue represents the Dedridge burns; brown reflects the ridge and valley landscape of West Lothian; black symbolises the shale seams and mining history and green is for the surrounding vegetation.

name: Osborne, C N and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Please contact the designer regarding use of this tartan. This tartan may only be woven/used/reproduced with written permission from the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Osborne family using colours of personal significance.

name: Motyl-Seaman, C & M - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland. It is intended to be used with approval from Claire Motyl Seaman and Matthew Seaman.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate the union of the Motyl and Seaman families in May 2025. The colours are intended to represent the colours chosen for the wedding ceremonies, as well as the colours of the Perthshire countryside in Spring.

name: Sorensen, S & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and used by members and descendants of the Sorensen family. Use/weaving/reproduction only with permission from the registrant or designated family representative. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Sorensen Family to honour their heritage, ancestral journey, and continuing family legacy. The design is intended to reflect the family’s roots in Denmark, later settlement in Nebraska, and the family’s movement westward to California. The colours are intended to symbolise the values of the family: navy for loyalty, wisdom, and service; black for strength, sacrifice, and resilience; dark yellow, representing gold, for honour, legacy, and generosity; white for truth, faith, and integrity; and red for courage, protection, bloodline, and duty.

name: Gerrell, Berkeley & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for use by Berkeley Gerrell, the immediate Gerrell family and persons or organisations authorised by them, including use as the Gerrell family racing colours on classic cars. Please contact Berkeley Gerrell before commercial weaving, manufacture or sale of this tartan.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by Berkeley Gerrell for himself and his immediate family to celebrate the family’s English, Scottish and Italian heritage. It is also intended to be used as the Gerrell family’s racing colours on classic cars.

name: Alvarez-Polyvka, Alberto & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Alberto Alvarez & his family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Alberto Alvarez & his family. The design layout and colours reference themes relating to the family’s Spanish & Ukrainian heritage and the family lineages of Alvarez & Polyvka.

name: Balmoral Escoces
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn with the permission of Balmoral Escoces. May only be woven/reproduced with consent from Balmoral Escoces.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Balmoral Escoces, a preparatory school located in Querétaro, Mexico. The design was inspired by their core values and the spirit of a community built to inspire. The colours are intended to represent the pillars of their vision; educational excellence, holistic growth and leadership & athletic discipline. The tartan is intended to be a symbol of belonging and purpose for the school.

name: RAF Mountain Rescue Service
designer: Blackburn, Scott; Piob Mhor of Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. Permission to use or have this tartan woven must be obtained from the RAF Lossiemouth Team Leader. Or Mr Scott Blackburn, Piob Mhor of Scotland Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for RAF Mountain Rescue Service. Colours: navy blue and maroon were inspired by the traditional knitted RAF Lossiemouth mountain rescue jumpers; yellow is intended to pay homage to previous work with the Sea Kings SAR force; the three silver bands reference the three RAF mountain rescue teams.

name: Georgy, B & C and Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of the Georgy family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Georgy Family incorporating colours of significance as well as the numbers 25 & 27, house numbers the family have lived in, and 3 to represent their children.

name: Krampe, Hendrik & Krampe, Lea - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Hendrik & Lea Krampe and their family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Hendrik and Lea's shared love of Scotland, their wedding and how Scotland that has become a second home through their many travels together. Colours: dark red is one of Hendrik and Lea's favourite shared colours; dark green is intended to reflect Scotland's natural landscapes and the time they have spent exploring them together; yellow is intended to symbolise the bond they share, the good fortune of finding one another, and the golden hues of the whisky they have enjoyed together.

name: Fenix - Umbran
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn freely by individuals. Commercial use, reproduction, or sale of products made from this tartan requires prior written permission from Nita Lipan / Fenix Rising Press. The owner, Nita Lipan / Fenix Rising Press, must be consulted before this tartan is woven commercially. Authorised weaving rights must be obtained in writing from Fenix Rising Press prior to production for sale. Individuals may request weaving rights by contacting [email protected] All commercial rights to this tartan are retained by Nita Lipan / Fenix Rising Press. Royalties or licensing fees apply to any commercial production or sale of products made from this tartan design.
registrationNotes: This tartan designed for the Solasta Trilogy, a book series from Fenix Rising Press, to celebrate the fictional world featured in the book Umbra. The tartan was inspired by the significant role tartan plays in the story and by the author's Scottish wedding with her husband, who the trilogy has been dedicated to.

name: Fielden, Eric and Quintana, Yareli - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Eric Fielden and Yareli Quintana & their family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Yareli and Eric's love and their union in marriage. It is intended to honour their Irish, Scottish, and Mexican heritage while reflecting the families and traditions that have shaped them. Colours: green is intended to represent Ireland; navy blue represents Scotland; yellow reflects their union, celebrating warmth, prosperity, and joy; red represents Mexico, love, passion, courage, and family; ivory is for faith, purity, and grace and light blue reflects the joy, adventure, and shared dreams.

name: Klasse Lucienne Roberts
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by members of the Klasse. Permission to use/weave/reproduce this tartan must be sought by Lucienne Roberts. Prepared for weaving by Auld Alliance Kiltmakers. Copyright rests with Auld Alliance Kiltmakers Kiltmakers and Lucienne Roberts and her students.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by the Communication Design students for Klasse Lucienne Roberts, at ABK, Stuttgart, Germany. The tartan commemorates their trip to Scotland in November 2025 and uses colours relevant to the Klasse.

name: Gloverall 1951
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Gloverall PLC. May only be woven/used with permission for Gloverall PLC.
registrationNotes: This tartan marks Gloverall’s 75th anniversary and their first tartan designed rather than adopted. This design is intended to reflect the brand and the palette is based on Gloverall's signature colours: brown, echoing the iconic Monty duffle coat; navy and racing green, core brand tones; and an orange accent, drawn from naval military insignia, a nod to the coat's origins in seafaring workwear. The structure references the Black Watch tartan.

name: Bluebellgray Coastal
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by and for Bluebellgray, inspired by the colours of the landscape and light of Scotland. Bluebellgray is a Scottish design studio established in 2009 based in Glasgow, creating colourful, nature-inspired design for interiors and beyond. The chosen shades are a range of blues, teals and greens intended to captured the waters off the west coast of Scotland, layered with a deep forest green and soft heather-purple, to echo the hills above the shore.

name: Bluebellgray Ceilidh
restrictions: Yes. May only be woven/used/reproduced with the express approval of Bluebellgray.
registrationNotes: A tartan designed by and for Bluebellgray, inspired by joy and people of Scotland. Bluebellgray is a Scottish design studio established in 2009 based in Glasgow, creating colourful, nature-inspired design for interiors and beyond. The chosen shades are intended to be a joyful mix of celebratory colours inspired by the energy of a traditional Scottish ceilidh: a Scottish blue and deep grass green, highlights of a warm red, whisky gold, soft brown for Highland cattle, and a vibrant pink for the heather on the hills - together capturing the warmth and celebration of a Scottish ceilidh.

name: Girlguiding Scotland
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn by Members of Girlguiding Scotland and those authorised by the organisation. Prepared for weaving by McNaughtons Group.
registrationNotes: This design is intended to reflect the organisation and principles of Girlguiding Scotland using a proportional thread count and the signature colours of its members. The 4 membership groups; Rainbows, Brownies, Guides and Rangers sit within the foundation of Girlguiding blue, used in a band of 40 threads to represent their 40,000 young members. Each group is represented in 4 x 4 threads of their signature colours, with the promises and laws made by members presented as an overcheck of blue threads that connect each group and member.

name: Army Cadet Force
restrictions: Yes. For safeguarding purposes, this tartan can only be worn by Cadets or Instructors of the National Pipes and Drums ACF and this tartan can only be woven with the strict approval of The SO2 or RQMS of the National Pipes and Drums ACF.
registrationNotes: Designed for the specific use of The National Pipes and Drums of the Army Cadet Force, for public and military engagements, and to be worn by Cadets and Adult Volunteers of the Pipes and Drums, or only by the strict permission of The SO2 - National Pipes and Drums ACF.

name: Crimson and Gold
registrationNotes: The name for this tartan ‘Crimson and Gold’ was derived from the principal colours within the design. The tartan was created to celebrate friendship, cultural connection and shared heritage, with each colour carrying symbolic meaning within the sett.

name: Biomar Blue
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for the exclusive use of BioMar employees. Permission is required for any weaving, reproduction, or commercial use. This design was first commissioned for manufacture on behalf of BioMar by MacGregor and MacDuff Kiltmakers. Prepared for weaving by The House of Edgar, a division of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Copyright rests with MacGregor and MacDuff
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Biomar to celebrate the heritage and growth in Scottish Salmon Aquaculture. The tartan highlights the colours found in the BioMar logo.

name: Owen, Ron and Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Ron Owen and his family to honour their Welsh, Southern English, and Norwegian (Møre og Romsdal) ancestry while also celebrating the legacy built by later generations in the United States. Colours: Red, white, and blue are intended to reflect both traditional heraldic meanings and the colours of the American flag, for the family it symbolises loyalty, courage, integrity, and the family’s enduring connection to the United States; yellow, representing gold, is intended to represent opportunity, achievement, wisdom, and prosperity.

name: Lochs and Great Lakes
registrationNotes: This tartan is intended to celebrate the landscapes and traditions of many heritages, and lives that began on different shores and later became intertwined. Inspired by design elements from tartans from Scotland, Ireland, England, Italy, and the United States its colours are intended to reflect the forests, dunes and waters of the Great Lakes while echoing the lochs, mountains, coastal rainforests, and ancient stone ruins of the Scottish Highlands.

name: McNeil, Mark Sanford and Family (Personal)
designer: Blackburn, Scott; Piob Mhor of Scotland Ltd
restrictions: Yes. The weaving/use/reproduction of this tartan can only be authorised by Mr Mark Sanford McNeil and family and Mr Scott Blackburn, Piob Mhor of Scotland Ltd
registrationNotes: Inspired by the MacNeil of Barra tartan and his personal connection thereto, this tartan was designed for Mark Sanford McNeil as a gift from Laura, Lise, and Cathy, incorporating colours of personal significance.

name: Ozturk, Ufuk & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: A tartan for Ufuk Ozturk and his family using colours of personal significance including grey which intended to represent the family, and red and white for the Turkish flag. The tartan was designed to be worn at a family wedding in September 2026.

name: Falkirk Football Club 150th Anniversary
restrictions: Yes. All enquiries to be addressed to Falkirk FC or Slanj Kilts.
registrationNotes: The Falkirk Football Club 150th Anniversary tartan was created to commemorate 150 years of the Club and celebrate its history, identity and enduring relationship with its supporters. The design was developed as a lasting symbol of this milestone and as an official tartan that can remain part of the Club’s heritage beyond the anniversary season. The design uses a predominantly navy and light blue palette, reflecting Falkirk FC’s established colours, with scarlet and ivory detailing.

name: Bosgow
restrictions: Yes. Intended to be worn and used by anyone. Permission should be sought from the owner before weaving the tartan for commercial sale. Copyright rests with the designer.
registrationNotes: Bosgow is a coined name inspired by the cultural friendship between Boston and Glasgow. This design is intended to celebrate that friendship and bring together colours associated with both cities: deep navy and green are intended to represent Glasgow’s civic character and flourishing spirit; Boston blue and buff-gold accents for Boston’s civic identity; red for warmth and celebration and white for friendship and welcome. The navy ground is intended to represent the Atlantic crossing between the two cities, while the layered blue and green sett reflects shared history, humour, music, sport and community.

name: Missouri State University
restrictions: Yes. The Missouri State University Tartan may not be woven or produced in any form without written permission from: Trademark Licensing Office Missouri State University 901 S. National Avenue Springfield, MO 65897 [email protected] The tartan can only be produced under license. The design right for the Missouri State University Tartan is held by Missouri State University under the U.S. Copyright Act- 17 U.S.C. Formal registration is pending.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Missouri State University to celebrate their lasting legacy and contribute to a long-held tradition of pride. Founded in 1905 in the foothills of the Ozarks Highlands, Missouri State is a public university committed to public affairs. Their fight song is ‘The Scotsman’. The institution's name has changed over the decades reflecting growth from a state teacher's college to Missouri's second largest university. One constant throughout the years are the school’s colours, maroon and white. The tartan idea came from Merchandising and Fashion Design faculty J. Roberts, C. Starr and S. Baily. Collegiate Tartan Apparel designed the tartan and student Dylan Lyle helped merchandise. A campus community vote decided the final design.

name: Everage, Clinton & Penny, Caitlin - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Clinton Everage, Caitlin Penny & their family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Clinton Everage and Caitlin Penny to celebrate their wedding. The design uses colours of personal significance intended to represent the stone and land of Scotland and the couple’s life together.

name: Wild Boars Heritage
registrationNotes: This tartan was inspired by the landscape and nature found in the mountains of the Ardennes region, including the wild boar. The design includes the colours of the forests, soil, and stones and is intended to honour the resilience and fraternity in the territory.

name: Royal Shiloh Foundation
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Royal Shiloh Foundation, a nonprofit organisation registered in California, United States. Colours: black is intended to represent dignity, resilience, and steadfastness; red is for leadership, service, and courage; and white is intended to symbolise honour, integrity, and peace.

name: Longden, L and S (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the personal use of Revd Dr Lee and Revd Sally Longden, any to whom they give their permission to wear it, and their descendants. Permission must be sought from the Registrants.
registrationNotes: A personal tartan commissioned for Revd Dr Lee Longden’s 20th anniversary of ordination as a minister of the Church of England. The design was based on the Clergy – Green lines sett and uses colours of special significance to the family: blue is intended to acknowledge Dr Longden’s previous career at sea as a Merchant Naval Officer and their daughter, Abbie’s, love of the sea; yellow for the colour of their daughter’s favourite umbrella; and black for the colour of robes both wear as clergy of the Church of England.

name: Aether Aerospace
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Aether Aerospace to celebrate three companies joining together in January 2026 to provide digital engineering and contract support for the U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force.

name: Multinational Corps Northeast Dress
designer: Lt Col C.M.B Broadbent(RRS)/LCdr D. Matthews (RCN)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended to be worn by any military or civilian members who have served in Multinational Corps Northeast.
registrationNotes: This dress tartan was designed to celebrate the achievements of NATO Multinational Corps Northeast, and its 25th Anniversary in 2024. It was designed in conjunction with MNCNE Tartan (#14623). For 25 years it has been a symbol of cooperation and determination within NATO, while ensuring the security of the Baltic Region, and the eastern flank of the NATO alliance. This tartan incorporates the colours of the three original framework nations: Poland, Germany, and Denmark.

name: Stille, René & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. This tartan is intended for René Stille, his family, and descendants. Other persons or organisations may only wear or use the tartan with the permission of René Stille or a family representative appointed subsequently. This tartan may only be woven with the prior written permission of René Stille or a subsequently appointed family representative. The commercial manufacture, sale, licensing or reproduction of the tartan design requires the prior written authorisation of René Stille or a subsequently appointed family representative.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed by René Stille for himself, his family and future descendants. It was inspired by a heraldic design created for the Stille family: black is intended to reflect the wolf and represents vigilance, steadfastness and family loyalty; yellow refers to the gold field and the architectural capital and symbolises honour, order, responsibility and endurance; red is for the sword and the base of the shield and represents courage and determination.

name: Kearey (Ciardha), T & Family (Personal)
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the Keary family (Ciardha in Irish) to celebrate and honour their family history and Irish roots. The design uses colours of personal significance to the family.

name: 2026 Chevron Brand Ambassador
restrictions: Yes. Permission to weave the material must be obtained from Chevron by contacting 8 Yards. Prepared for weaving by 8 Yards Ltd & Macnaughton Holdings.
registrationNotes: The Chevron Brand Ambassador tartan was designed in 2026 to celebrate the visit of Chevron Brand Ambassadors to Scotland. The tartan was commissioned to mark the occasion and serve as a lasting memento of their time in the country, bringing together the traditions of Scottish tartan with the spirit of the Chevron brand.

name: BMW of North America
restrictions: Yes. Permission should be obtained from BMW North America via 8 Yards Ltd. Prepared for weaving by 8 Yards Ltd & MacNaughton Holdings.
registrationNotes: The BMW of North America tartan was designed to celebrate the connection between BMW of North America and Scotland, reflecting the prestige and heritage of the BMW brand alongside the traditions of Scottish tartan design.

name: Auld Scotland Dark Skies
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the exclusive use of Lochcarron of Scotland and its customers. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: Lochcarron first produced the Auld Scotland tartan in January 2008 to mark the 250th anniversary of the National Bard, Robert Burns, to be celebrated the following year. Inspired by the modern version of his toast to the Haggis, Auld Scotland is quoted in the final verse. The Auld Scotland Dark Skies tartan uses a deeper colour palette intended to evoke the dramatic tones of the Scottish landscape and the enduring legacy of Burns; blue and brown to reflect the Ayrshire countryside, and yellow to symbolise the barley essential for crafting whisky, Scotland’s national drink, traditionally raised in a toast to the haggis.

name: Pieces of Jayde
restrictions: Yes. Prepared for weaving by Lochcarron of Scotland.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for the travel branch of Pieces of Jayde LLC, based in Indiana, United States. The colours include the company’s brand colours, green and purple, which were inspired by the owner’s Irish and Scottish heritage.

name: Portobello High School
restrictions: Yes. Anyone wishing to use this tartan must first seek permission from the leadership team at Portobello High School: https://portobellohighschool.org.uk/
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Portobello High School to celebrates its 150th anniversary in 2026 and the school’s roots and rich history. The design was inspired by the school colours and school crest, and the vibrant local community the school serves.

name: Opila, Krzysztof & Family (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Intended for the use of Krzysztof Opila & their family.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to celebrate Krzysztof's Scottish citizenship, marking an important milestone and reflecting the deep personal connection he has formed with Scotland. Inspired by the colours that hold special significance throughout his life, the design is intended to symbolise his journey, achievements, and the place he now proudly calls home.

name: Bath Caledonian Society
restrictions: Yes. Intended for members, past and present of the Bath Caledonian Society. Prior approval to weave / use this tartan are required from Bath Caledonian Society & Browne White Ltd T/A ScotlandShop.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed to commemorate the community of the Bath Caledonian Society, at the University of Bath, founded in 2020. It is intended to represent all members of the Society, both Scottish and non-Scottish, united by a shared interest in Scottish dancing. The colours were inspired by the colours of the University of Bath and its sporting teams at the time.

name: Whittle, Stephen & Poole, Thea - Wedding (Personal)
restrictions: Yes. Exclusively designed by Kinloch Anderson for the Dr Stephen Whittle & Thea Poole & family. Restricted availability, please contact Kinloch Anderson regarding use. Only to be woven with permission from Kinloch Anderson Ltd.
registrationNotes: This tartan was designed for Dr Stephen Whittle. The design layout, threadcount and colours reference themes & dates of significance to him and his family.

name: Araminta Campbell – Garden Bloom
restrictions: Yes. Intended exclusively for the use of Araminta Campbell Ltd. Permission to weave/reproduce must be sought from Araminta Campbell Ltd. Copyright rests with Araminta Campbell.
registrationNotes: Inspired by the garden when it comes into full bloom in the summer, this tartan is intended to capture the colourful flowers planted to support pollinators. Bumblebees buzzing across a tapestry of colour and greenery: blue of the cornflowers and scabious; white of the lacy ammi and lofty foxgloves; yellow of the echinacea and splashes of reds of the poppies and scabiosa.
